### `__closeNotification`

```js
window.WebToApk.__closeNotification(tag: String): Boolean
```

Notification.close(): removes a notification the page posted, by its tag.

**Example**

Internal plumbing behind `Notification.prototype.close()` - pages use `new Notification(...)` and call `close()` on it. It removes a notification from the shade by its tag.

**Returns:** `true` when the remove request was made (also when nothing had that tag); `false` on an internal error. **Needs:** nothing.

**Use the public API:**

```js
let uploadNote = null;

function showUploading() {
  if (!('Notification' in window) || Notification.permission !== 'granted') return;
  uploadNote = new Notification('Uploading…', { body: 'Keep the app open', tag: 'upload', silent: true });
  uploadNote.onclose = function () { uploadNote = null; };
}

function uploadFinished() {
  if (uploadNote) uploadNote.close();   // removes it from the notification shade
}
```

Open the right chat when the notification is tapped, then remove it from the shade:

```js
function notifyNewMessage(msg) {
  if (!('Notification' in window) || Notification.permission !== 'granted') return;
  const n = new Notification(msg.from, {
    body: msg.text,
    tag: 'chat-' + msg.threadId,          // one notification per chat
    data: { threadId: msg.threadId }
  });
  n.onclick = function () {
    openThread(n.data.threadId);
    n.close();
  };
}
```

Show a short confirmation that removes itself after five seconds:

```js
function confirmCopied() {
  if (!('Notification' in window) || Notification.permission !== 'granted') return;
  const n = new Notification('Link copied', { body: 'Paste it anywhere', tag: 'copied', silent: true });
  setTimeout(function () { n.close(); }, 5000);
}
```

**Notes:** do not call `WebToApk.__closeNotification` directly; the `__` methods may change without notice. `close()` fires the notification's `close` event.

### `__setAppBadge`

```js
window.WebToApk.__setAppBadge(contents: Long): Boolean
```

navigator.setAppBadge(n): n >= 0 is a count (0 clears), -1 the spec's flag badge.

**Example**

Internal transport behind `navigator.setAppBadge(count)` / `clearAppBadge()`. Pages use the standard API; never call this directly - the `__` methods may change without notice.

**Returns:** `true` when the count was applied. **Needs:** nothing to switch on.

**Use the public API:**

```js
if ('setAppBadge' in navigator) navigator.setAppBadge(unreadCount);
```

Keep the icon count in step with the unread count, and clear it at zero:

```js
async function syncBadge(unread) {
  if (!('setAppBadge' in navigator)) return;
  try {
    if (unread > 0) await navigator.setAppBadge(unread);
    else await navigator.clearAppBadge();
  } catch (e) {
    console.warn('badge not applied', e.name);   // NotAllowedError when the launcher refused it
  }
}
syncBadge(messages.filter(function (m) { return !m.read; }).length);
```

Put a flag badge (no number) on the icon while there is unsynced work:

```js
function markPendingSync(hasPending) {
  if (!('setAppBadge' in navigator)) return;
  const p = hasPending
    ? navigator.setAppBadge()      // no argument = flag badge; a count launcher shows 1
    : navigator.clearAppBadge();
  p.catch(function () {});
}
```

**Notes:** `-1` is the spec's flag badge (no number), which a count launcher shows as 1.

### `cancelAllNotifications`

```js
window.WebToApk.cancelAllNotifications(): Boolean
```

Reading and requesting the POST_NOTIFICATIONS grant, and managing notifications the page already scheduled. Posting and scheduling are documented on their own methods.

_Described by its group, Notification permission, cancelling and listing, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Cancels every reminder this app has scheduled.

**Returns:** `true` when done; `false` only on an internal error. **Needs:** nothing extra.

```js
document.getElementById('reset-reminders').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.cancelAllNotifications)) return;
  if (!confirm('Remove all your reminders?')) return;
  const ok = WebToApk.cancelAllNotifications();
  showMessage(ok ? 'All reminders removed' : 'Could not remove reminders');
});
```

On sign-out, stop the previous user's reminders and clear the icon count:

```js
async function signOut() {
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.cancelAllNotifications) {
    WebToApk.cancelAllNotifications();
  }
  if ('clearAppBadge' in navigator) navigator.clearAppBadge().catch(function () {});
  await auth.signOut();
  showLoginScreen();
}
```

Rebuild the whole daily schedule from the saved times (cancel all, then add each one):

```js
function applyMedicineTimes(times) {        // e.g. ['08:00', '20:00']
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.cancelAllNotifications)) return;
  b.cancelAllNotifications();
  times.forEach(function (hhmm, i) {
    const parts = hhmm.split(':');
    const at = new Date();
    at.setHours(Number(parts[0]), Number(parts[1]), 0, 0);
    if (at.getTime() <= Date.now()) at.setDate(at.getDate() + 1);   // next occurrence
    b.scheduleNotification('med-' + i, 'Medicine', 'Time for your ' + hhmm + ' dose',
      String(at.getTime()), 'daily');
  });
}
```

**Notes:** it clears the scheduled list, so nothing fires later and nothing is set again after a restart. Notifications already showing in the tray stay there.

### `cancelNotification`

```js
window.WebToApk.cancelNotification(id: String): Boolean
```

Reading and requesting the POST_NOTIFICATIONS grant, and managing notifications the page already scheduled. Posting and scheduling are documented on their own methods.

_Described by its group, Notification permission, cancelling and listing, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Cancels one scheduled reminder by its id, so it will not fire again.

**Returns:** `true` (also when no reminder had that id); `false` only on an internal error. **Needs:** nothing extra (reminders need **⏰ Reminders** at build time).

```js
function stopWaterReminder() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.cancelNotification)) return;
  WebToApk.cancelNotification('water');   // the id you gave scheduleNotification / scheduleNotificationEx

  // Check it is gone:
  const left = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getScheduledNotifications() || '[]');
  const stillThere = left.some(function (r) { return r.id === 'water'; });
  console.log('water reminder still scheduled?', stillThere);   // false
}
```

A reminder switch in settings that schedules or cancels by the same id:

```js
document.getElementById('water-toggle').addEventListener('change', function (e) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.cancelNotification && b.scheduleNotification)) return;
  if (e.target.checked) {
    b.scheduleNotification('water', 'Drink water', 'Time for a glass of water',
      String(Date.now() + 60 * 60 * 1000), 'hourly');
  } else {
    b.cancelNotification('water');
  }
});
```

When a task is deleted, cancel every reminder that belongs to it:

```js
function cancelTaskReminders(taskId) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.cancelNotification)) return;
  let list = [];
  try { list = JSON.parse(b.getScheduledNotifications() || '[]'); } catch (e) { list = []; }
  list
    .filter(function (r) { return r.id.indexOf('task-' + taskId + '-') === 0; })
    .forEach(function (r) { b.cancelNotification(r.id); });
}
```

**Notes:** this cancels a reminder that has not fired yet (one-off or repeating). It does not remove a notification that is already showing in the tray, and it does not affect notifications posted with `notify()` / `showNotification()`.

### `canOpenAppAtTime`

```js
window.WebToApk.canOpenAppAtTime(): String
```

Whether a scheduled notification may put the APP ITSELF on screen (`openApp`). "granted"  - a full-screen alert will show, over the lock screen. "denied"   - Android 14+ withheld it; call requestOpenAppPermission(). There is no third answer where the app silently launches itself in the background: Android has blocked background activity starts since Android 10, and a full-screen intent is the whole of what remains.

**Example**

Tells you whether a reminder with `openApp: true` may put the app itself on screen (a full-screen alert, also over the lock screen).

**Returns:** a string, synchronously: `'granted'` or `'denied'`. Below Android 14 it is always `'granted'`. **Needs:** turn on **⏰ Reminders** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

```js
function prepareAlarm() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.canOpenAppAtTime)) return;
  if (b.canOpenAppAtTime() === 'denied') {
    showMessage('To open the app at alarm time, allow "full-screen notifications" for this app.');
    b.requestOpenAppPermission();
    return;
  }
  const t = new Date();
  t.setDate(t.getDate() + 1);
  t.setHours(7, 0, 0, 0);                    // tomorrow 07:00
  b.scheduleNotificationEx('wake-up', JSON.stringify({
    at: t.getTime(), repeat: 'daily',
    title: 'Wake up', body: 'Good morning!',
    openApp: true
  }));
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:reminder', function (e) {
  // e.detail.overLockScreen is true when the app was shown as a full-screen alert
  if (e.detail.overLockScreen) showBigAlarmScreen(e.detail.id);
});
```

A settings screen that shows both alarm switches with their current state:

```js
function renderAlarmStatus() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.canOpenAppAtTime && b.getAlarmPrecision)) return;
  const openApp = b.canOpenAppAtTime();       // 'granted' | 'denied'
  const precision = b.getAlarmPrecision();    // 'exact' | 'inexact' | 'unavailable'
  document.getElementById('open-app-state').textContent =
    openApp === 'granted' ? 'Opens over the lock screen' : 'Notification only';
  document.getElementById('open-app-fix').hidden = openApp === 'granted';
  document.getElementById('timing-state').textContent =
    precision === 'exact' ? 'On the minute' : 'May be late';
}

renderAlarmStatus();
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (!document.hidden) renderAlarmStatus();  // back from Settings
});
```

Warn when saved alarms were set to open the app but Android does not allow it right now:

```js
function checkSavedAlarms() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.canOpenAppAtTime && b.getScheduledNotifications)) return;
  if (b.canOpenAppAtTime() === 'granted') return;
  // [{ id, title, body, trigger, repeat, options }] - options is the JSON string you scheduled
  const items = JSON.parse(b.getScheduledNotifications());
  const affected = items.filter(function (r) {
    try { return JSON.parse(r.options || '{}').openApp === true; } catch (e) { return false; }
  });
  if (affected.length) {
    showMessage(affected.length + ' alarm(s) will only show a notification. Tap "Allow" to let them open the app.');
  }
}
```

**Notes:** when it is `'denied'`, an `openApp` reminder still posts a heads-up notification, but the app does not open by itself. Android does not allow any other way for an app to start itself in the background.

### `clearNotificationSounds`

```js
window.WebToApk.clearNotificationSounds(): Int
```

Drops the copied sound files and returns how many were deleted. A file is copied again when a notification (or a scheduled reminder, when it fires) next uses that sound - including on a channel that already exists, which keeps pointing at the same file name (NotificationBridge.restoreBundleSound).

**Example**

Deletes the copies of your custom notification sounds that the app made from your bundle.

**Returns:** a number, synchronously: how many files were deleted. **Needs:** nothing.

**Clear, then put back the sounds you still use:**

```js
document.getElementById('reset-sounds').addEventListener('click', function () {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.clearNotificationSounds)) return;
  const removed = b.clearNotificationSounds();

  // Sounds still in use must be copied again, or they play the default sound:
  ['/audio/alarm.mp3', '/audio/chime.mp3'].forEach(function (path) {
    if (!b.prepareNotificationSound(path)) console.warn('missing sound', path);
  });
  showMessage(removed + ' sound file(s) refreshed');
});
```

A storage screen button that frees the copied sound files and says how many were removed:

```js
document.getElementById('free-space').addEventListener('click', function () {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.clearNotificationSounds)) return;
  const removed = b.clearNotificationSounds();
  showMessage(removed === 0 ? 'No sound files to remove.' : 'Removed ' + removed + ' sound file(s).');
});
```

On sign-out, cancel every reminder and delete the sound copies that belonged to this user:

```js
function signOutAndReset() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (b && b.cancelAllNotifications) b.cancelAllNotifications();
  if (b && b.clearNotificationSounds) b.clearNotificationSounds();
  localStorage.removeItem('alarmSound');
  goToLoginScreen();
}
```

**Notes:** you rarely need this; the copies are small. A sound is copied back the next time anything uses it - `notify()`, a reminder when it fires, `scheduleNotificationEx`, or `prepareNotificationSound(path)` - including on a notification channel that already exists, so the custom sound keeps playing.

### `enableNotifications`

```js
window.WebToApk.enableNotifications(callbackId: String)
```

Brings a user back to notifications: the system dialog while it can still be shown, otherwise the app's notification settings. Resolves `window.__appmintReplies[callbackId]` with {state, changed, openedSettings} (AppMint.enableNotifications() is the promise wrapper).

**Example**

Brings a user who denied or skipped notifications back: shows Android's permission dialog while it can still be shown, otherwise opens this app's notification settings and answers when the user comes back.

**Returns:** nothing directly. The answer `{state, changed, openedSettings}` is delivered to `window.__appmintReplies[callbackId]`; `state` is `'granted' | 'prompt' | 'blocked' | 'unavailable'`, `changed` is `true` when it differs from before the call, `openedSettings` is `true` when the settings screen was used. Already `'granted'` (or `'unavailable'`) answers at once. **Needs:** call it from a button the user tapped; notifications need **Notifications** (or Push / Reminders) in the build.

Prefer the promise wrapper `AppMint.enableNotifications()`. The raw call, for code that manages its own replies:

```js
function enableNotificationsRaw() {
  return new Promise(function (resolve) {
    if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.enableNotifications)) return resolve({ state: 'unavailable', changed: false, openedSettings: false });
    var replies = window.__appmintReplies = window.__appmintReplies || {};
    var id = 'my_notif_' + Date.now();
    replies[id] = resolve;
    WebToApk.enableNotifications(id);
  });
}

document.getElementById('turn-on-btn').onclick = async function () {
  var r = await enableNotificationsRaw();
  if (r.state === 'granted') document.getElementById('notif-banner').hidden = true;
};
```

Every finished flow is also announced, including one started by a push button (`appmint://notifications/enable`):

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:notifications', function (e) {
  // e.detail = { state, changed, openedSettings }
  if (e.detail.state === 'granted') document.getElementById('notif-banner').hidden = true;
});
```

**Notes:** a push or in-app message button whose link is `appmint://notifications/enable` runs this same flow; `appmint://notifications/settings` opens the settings screen. The app's push audience sees the new state at once.

### `getAlarmPrecision`

```js
window.WebToApk.getAlarmPrecision(): String
```

"exact" - reminders fire on the minute. "inexact" - the user (or the OEM) turned exact alarms off for this app, so Doze may batch them by minutes. Ask [requestExactAlarms] to fix it. "unavailable" - Android 12+ and the system alarm service could not be reached, so the precision cannot be read (a reminder scheduled now may not fire either). A page that must be on time should check this instead of assuming. @return `"exact"`, `"inexact"` or `"unavailable"`.

**Example**

Tells you whether reminders will fire on the exact minute, or may be late because the user (or the phone maker) turned exact alarms off for this app.

**Returns:** a string, synchronously: `'exact'`, `'inexact'` (may be batched by battery saving, often by minutes), or `'unavailable'` (the phone has no alarm service). **Needs:** turn on **⏰ Reminders** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

```js
function checkReminderTiming() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getAlarmPrecision)) return;
  const precision = WebToApk.getAlarmPrecision();
  const warn = document.getElementById('timing-warning');
  warn.hidden = precision === 'exact';
  if (precision === 'inexact') {
    warn.textContent = 'Reminders may be a few minutes late. Tap to allow exact alarms.';
    warn.onclick = function () { WebToApk.requestExactAlarms(); };
  }
}
checkReminderTiming();
// Re-check when the user returns from Settings:
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (!document.hidden) checkReminderTiming();
});
```

Check before setting a wake-up alarm, and tell the user if it may be late:

```js
function setWakeUp(atMs) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.getAlarmPrecision && b.scheduleNotificationEx)) return;
  const precision = b.getAlarmPrecision();
  if (precision === 'unavailable') { showMessage('Alarms cannot be set on this phone right now.'); return; }
  b.scheduleNotificationEx('wake', JSON.stringify({ at: atMs, title: 'Wake up', body: 'Good morning', openApp: true }));
  if (precision === 'inexact') {
    showMessage('Alarm set, but it may ring a few minutes late. Allow exact alarms for on-time alarms.');
  }
}
```

Show the reminder timing as a line in a settings screen:

```js
function renderTimingRow() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getAlarmPrecision)) return;
  const labels = {
    exact: 'Reminders arrive on time',
    inexact: 'Reminders may be a few minutes late',
    unavailable: 'Reminders are not available on this phone'
  };
  document.getElementById('timing-row').textContent = labels[WebToApk.getAlarmPrecision()];
}
renderTimingRow();
```

**Notes:** Android 11 and older always answer `'exact'`. An `'inexact'` reminder still fires, just not on the minute.

### `getAlarmSupport`

```js
window.WebToApk.getAlarmSupport(): String
```

Whether `scheduleNotificationEx(id, {alarm: true, ...})` can be scheduled now: "ready" | "not_enabled" (Alarm clock is off in this build) | "needs_exact_alarm" (call requestExactAlarms) | "needs_notification_permission".

**Example**

Tells you whether an alarm clock (`scheduleNotificationEx(id, { alarm: true, ... })`) can be set on this phone right now, and if not, what the user has to allow first.

**Returns:** a string, synchronously: `'ready'`, `'not_enabled'` (the app was built without **🔔 Alarm clock**), `'needs_exact_alarm'` (Android 12+: exact alarms are off for this app - call `requestExactAlarms()`), or `'needs_notification_permission'` (Android 13+: no notification permission, so there would be no Dismiss button - call `requestNotificationPermission()`). **Needs:** turn on **🔔 Alarm clock** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

```js
function prepareAlarms() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.getAlarmSupport)) { showMessage('Alarms work in the installed app only.'); return false; }
  switch (b.getAlarmSupport()) {
    case 'ready': return true;
    case 'needs_exact_alarm':
      showMessage('Allow "Alarms & reminders" for this app, then come back.');
      b.requestExactAlarms();
      return false;
    case 'needs_notification_permission':
      b.requestNotificationPermission();
      return false;
    default:
      showMessage('This app was built without alarm clocks.');
      return false;
  }
}
```

Re-check when the user comes back from Settings:

```js
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (document.hidden || !(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getAlarmSupport)) return;
  document.getElementById('alarm-setup').hidden = WebToApk.getAlarmSupport() === 'ready';
});
```

**Create an alarm only when the phone is ready:**

```js
function setAlarmIn(hours) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.getAlarmSupport)) return false;
  if (b.getAlarmSupport() !== 'ready') { prepareAlarms(); return false; }   // asks for what is missing
  return b.scheduleNotificationEx('wake-up', JSON.stringify({
    at: Date.now() + hours * 3600 * 1000,
    alarm: true,
    title: 'Wake up',
    body: 'Good morning'
  }));
}
```

**Notes:** `scheduleNotificationEx` with `alarm: true` returns `false` whenever this is not `'ready'` - an alarm that could never ring is never stored.

### `getNotificationPermission`

```js
window.WebToApk.getNotificationPermission(): String
```

The CURRENT notification permission, read live from the OS. The polyfill used to hardcode `Notification.permission = 'default'` on every page load, so the overwhelmingly common page pattern if (Notification.permission === 'granted') new Notification(...) never fired - not even for a user who had already granted it, and not on Android 12 and below where notifications need no runtime grant at all.

**Example**

Reads, right now, whether this app may post notifications.

**Returns:** a string, synchronously: `'granted'`; `'denied'` (the user refused for good, or switched this app's notifications off in Settings - a post would not show); or `'default'` (not decided yet, the app can still ask). **Needs:** nothing to call it; posting needs **Notifications** turned on in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

**The standard web API** reads the same live value:

```js
if ('Notification' in window && Notification.permission === 'granted') {
  document.getElementById('alerts-on').hidden = false;
}
```

**The raw call**, for example after the user comes back from Settings:

```js
function refreshAlertSetting() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getNotificationPermission)) return;
  const perm = WebToApk.getNotificationPermission();   // 'granted' | 'denied' | 'default'
  document.getElementById('enable-alerts').hidden = perm !== 'default';   // can still ask
  document.getElementById('open-settings-hint').hidden = perm !== 'denied';
}
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (!document.hidden) refreshAlertSetting();
});
refreshAlertSetting();
```

Decide before scheduling whether to ask, explain, or go ahead:

```js
async function ensureAlerts() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.getNotificationPermission)) return false;
  const perm = b.getNotificationPermission();
  if (perm === 'granted') return true;
  if (perm === 'denied') {
    showMessage('Notifications are off for this app. Turn them on in Settings.');
    return false;
  }
  // 'default': the app can still ask
  return (await Notification.requestPermission()) === 'granted';
}
```

**Notes:** it gives the same answer as `navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'notifications' })`. To ask the user, use `Notification.requestPermission()`.

### `getNotificationState`

```js
window.WebToApk.getNotificationState(): String
```

'granted' | 'prompt' (Android can still ask) | 'blocked' (refused for good or switched off in Settings - only Settings fixes it) | 'unavailable' (Android 13+ and this build does not declare the notification permission). See NotificationOptIn.

**Example**

Reads, right now, whether this app's notifications are on - and if not, whether the app can still ask or only Settings can turn them back on.

**Returns:** a string, synchronously: `'granted'` (notifications reach the phone); `'prompt'` (Android can still show its permission dialog); `'blocked'` (the user refused for good, or switched this app's notifications off in system Settings - only Settings can fix it); or `'unavailable'` (Android 13+ and the app was built without **Notifications** / **Reminders** / **Push**, so nothing can turn them on). **Needs:** nothing to call it.

**The raw call**, to decide whether to show a "Turn on notifications" banner:

```js
function refreshNotifBanner() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getNotificationState)) return;
  var state = WebToApk.getNotificationState();   // 'granted' | 'prompt' | 'blocked' | 'unavailable'
  var banner = document.getElementById('notif-banner');
  banner.hidden = !(state === 'prompt' || state === 'blocked');
  banner.querySelector('.hint').textContent = state === 'blocked'
    ? 'Notifications are off. Tap to open Settings and switch them on.'
    : 'Get order updates. Tap to turn on notifications.';
}
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (!document.hidden) refreshNotifBanner();
});
refreshNotifBanner();
```

**Notes:** `getNotificationPermission()` keeps its own words (`'granted'` / `'default'` / `'denied'`) for older pages. To bring the user back, call `AppMint.enableNotifications()` (it picks the dialog or Settings for you).

### `getScheduledNotifications`

```js
window.WebToApk.getScheduledNotifications(): String
```

Reading and requesting the POST_NOTIFICATIONS grant, and managing notifications the page already scheduled. Posting and scheduling are documented on their own methods.

_Described by its group, Notification permission, cancelling and listing, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Lists the reminders that are still scheduled.

**Returns:** a JSON **string**, synchronously. Parse it. Each item: `{ id, title, body, trigger, repeat, options? }` - `trigger` is the next fire time in epoch ms, `repeat` is `none|minutely|hourly|daily|weekly`, and `options` (only for `scheduleNotificationEx`) is the options as a JSON string. Live fields say how it will really be delivered, read live: `precision` (`"exact"`; `"inexact"` = "Alarms & reminders" is off for the app, so Android delivers it within a 10-minute window while the phone is awake, and may hold it longer while it sleeps; `"alarm_clock"` for `alarm: true`), `windowMs` + `latestAt` (the window Android was given: `0` / `trigger` when exact, `600000` / `trigger + 600000` when inexact) and `notificationsEnabled` (`false` = it fires but Android shows nothing, because the app's notifications are off). `'[]'` when there are none. **Needs:** nothing extra.

```js
function renderReminders() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getScheduledNotifications)) return;
  let list = [];
  try { list = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getScheduledNotifications() || '[]'); } catch (e) { list = []; }

  const ul = document.getElementById('reminders');
  ul.innerHTML = '';
  list.sort(function (a, b) { return a.trigger - b.trigger; }).forEach(function (r) {
    const li = document.createElement('li');
    li.textContent = r.title + ' — ' + new Date(r.trigger).toLocaleString() +
      (r.repeat !== 'none' ? ' (' + r.repeat + ')' : '');
    ul.appendChild(li);
  });
}
```

Show whether one reminder is on, and when it fires next:

```js
function describeReminder(id) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getScheduledNotifications)) return 'Not available';
  let list = [];
  try { list = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getScheduledNotifications() || '[]'); } catch (e) { list = []; }
  const r = list.find(function (x) { return x.id === id; });
  return r ? 'Next: ' + new Date(r.trigger).toLocaleString() : 'Off';
}
document.getElementById('water-status').textContent = describeReminder('water');
```

Read the extra options of reminders made with `scheduleNotificationEx`:

```js
function listAlarmStyleReminders() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getScheduledNotifications)) return [];
  let list = [];
  try { list = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getScheduledNotifications() || '[]'); } catch (e) { list = []; }
  return list.filter(function (r) {
    if (!r.options) return false;                  // made with scheduleNotification
    let o = {};
    try { o = JSON.parse(r.options); } catch (e) { return false; }
    return o.openApp === true;                     // puts the app on screen when it fires
  }).map(function (r) { return r.id; });
}
```

**Notes:** a one-off reminder leaves the list when it fires. A repeating one stays, with `trigger` moved to the next time. A reminder whose time passed while the phone was off or the app was force-stopped is shown once, late, the next time the app or phone starts; a late `alarm: true` is reported as `missed` instead of ringing. A daily, weekly, monthly or yearly reminder keeps its local time when the phone changes time zone.

Warn when reminders will not show up on time:

```js
function reminderHealth() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getScheduledNotifications)) return '';
  let list = [];
  try { list = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getScheduledNotifications() || '[]'); } catch (e) { list = []; }
  if (!list.length) return '';
  if (list.some(function (r) { return r.notificationsEnabled === false; })) return 'Notifications are off for this app: reminders will not appear.';
  if (list.some(function (r) { return r.precision === 'inexact'; })) return 'Reminders may arrive late. Turn on Alarms & reminders.';
  return '';
}
```

### `isAlarmRinging`

```js
window.WebToApk.isAlarmRinging(): Boolean
```

True while an alarm clock is ringing.

**Example**

Tells you whether one of the app's alarm clocks is ringing right now, so the page can show its own stop / snooze screen.

**Returns:** `true` while an alarm rings, otherwise `false` (synchronously). **Needs:** **🔔 Alarm clock** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

```js
function showRingScreenIfNeeded() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;

  document.getElementById('ring-screen').hidden = !ringing;
}
showRingScreenIfNeeded();
```

**Stop the ringing alarm from your own screen** with the matching calls.

```js
document.getElementById('stop').addEventListener('click', function () {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (b && b.isAlarmRinging && b.isAlarmRinging()) b.stopAlarm('');   // '' = whichever is ringing
});
document.getElementById('snooze').addEventListener('click', function () {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (b && b.snoozeAlarm && !b.snoozeAlarm('', 10)) showMessage('Nothing is ringing');
```

**React to the app being opened by a ringing alarm.**

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:reminder', function (e) {
```

**Notes:** when the ringing alarm opens the app, `appmint:reminder` also arrives with `{ action: 'open', ringing: true }`.

### `notify`

```js
window.WebToApk.notify(optionsJson: String): Boolean
```

Rich notification. See NotificationBridge.show for the full option list: channel (urgent|default|quiet|ongoing), image, largeIcon, bigText, ongoing, actions, progress, sound, silent, group, color. Image fetching and decoding happen off the main thread, so a remote image can never block the page.

**Example**

Posts a notification right now, with any mix of options: picture, big text, buttons, progress bar, sticky (ongoing), channel, sound, colour and tag.

**Returns:** `true` when the options were valid JSON and the notification was handed to the system (it is built on a background thread, so a bad image URL does not block the page); `false` for invalid JSON. **Needs:** turn on **Notifications** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build, and the user's permission on Android 13+ (ask with `Notification.requestPermission()`).

**Simple notification.** `tag` is an ID: posting again with the same tag replaces the old one.

```js
async function notifyOrderReady() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.notify)) return;
  if (window.Notification && Notification.permission !== 'granted') {
    const p = await Notification.requestPermission();
    if (p !== 'granted') { showMessage('Notifications are off for this app.'); return; }
  }
  WebToApk.notify(JSON.stringify({
    title: 'Order ready',
    body: 'Your order is ready to collect',
    channel: 'default',            // urgent | default | quiet | ongoing
    tag: 'order-42'
  }));
}
```

**Picture, large icon and long text.** `image` wins over `bigText` when both are given.

```js
WebToApk.notify(JSON.stringify({
  title: 'New photo',
  body: 'Tap to see it',
  image: 'https://example.com/photo.jpg',     // expanded big picture
  largeIcon: 'https://example.com/avatar.png', // round icon on the right
  color: '#00C6FF',
  tag: 'photo-7'
}));

WebToApk.notify(JSON.stringify({
  title: 'Weekly summary',
  body: '3 tasks done, 2 left',
  bigText: 'Done: pay rent, call bank, water plants. Left: tax form, dentist.',
  channel: 'quiet',                            // no sound, low priority
  group: 'summaries'
}));
```

**Buttons** (at most 3). The tap comes back as the `appmint:notification-action` event.

```js
WebToApk.notify(JSON.stringify({
  title: 'Ali sent you a message',
  body: 'Are we still on for 6pm?',
  channel: 'urgent',                           // heads-up banner
  tag: 'chat-ali',
  actions: [
    { id: 'open', label: 'Open chat' },
    { id: 'done', label: 'Mark read' }
  ]
}));

window.addEventListener('appmint:notification-action', function (e) {
  // e.detail = { actionId: 'done', tag: 'chat-ali' }
  if (e.detail.actionId === 'open') openChat(e.detail.tag);
  if (e.detail.actionId === 'done') markRead(e.detail.tag);
});
```

**Sticky progress (ongoing).** Re-post with the same tag to update it. When the job ends, post the final state with `ongoing: false` so the user can swipe it away.

```js
function showUpload(percent) {
  WebToApk.notify(JSON.stringify({
    title: 'Uploading', body: percent + '%',
    ongoing: true,                             // cannot be swiped away
    progress: { current: percent, max: 100 },  // or { indeterminate: true }
    silent: true,
    tag: 'upload'
  }));
}
showUpload(40);
// finished:
WebToApk.notify(JSON.stringify({ title: 'Upload complete', body: '3 photos saved', tag: 'upload' }));
```

**Other options:** `sound` (a file in your bundle like `'/audio/ding.mp3'`, a `data:audio/...` URL, or `'silent'`), `smallIcon` (a drawable name), `when` (epoch ms shown as the time), `openApp: true` (full-screen alert; see `scheduleNotificationEx`).

**Notes:** buttons have no inline reply box, and a button tap reaches the page only while the app is running (it does not open the app); the event also calls `window.onAppMintNotificationAction(detail)` if you define it. `image` and `largeIcon` take an `https://` or `data:` URL, or an image packaged with your app named as your page names it (`'img/logo.png'`, `'/img/logo.png'`, or its full `https://appassets.androidplatform.net/assets/…` address). A bad image is skipped, the notification still shows. `ongoing: true` always uses the quiet "Ongoing" channel. `notify()` has no public "remove" partner: `cancelNotification` only cancels scheduled reminders. A notification you want to remove later from the page should be posted with `new Notification(...)` and removed with its `close()`; a sticky progress card with `Capacitor.AppwrightLiveProgress` (`end`). Android fixes a channel's sound when the channel is created, so a new `sound` value makes a new channel.

### `openNotificationSettings`

```js
window.WebToApk.openNotificationSettings(): Boolean
```

Opens this app's notification settings; true when the screen could be opened.

**Example**

Opens this app's own notification settings screen, where the user can switch notifications (and each channel) on or off.

**Returns:** `true` when the screen was opened, synchronously; `false` when it cannot be (Android 13+ and the build has no notifications). On Android 8+ it is the app's notification page; on older Android, the App info screen. **Needs:** nothing to switch on.

```js
document.getElementById('notif-settings-link').onclick = function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.openNotificationSettings && WebToApk.openNotificationSettings())) {
    showMessage('Open Settings > Apps > this app > Notifications.');
  }
};
```

**Notes:** to bring a user back in one tap, use `AppMint.enableNotifications()` instead: it shows the permission dialog when Android still allows it and opens this screen only when it does not.

### `prepareNotificationSound`

```js
window.WebToApk.prepareNotificationSound(spec: String): Boolean
```

Copies a bundled audio file into place ahead of time and reports whether it is usable as a notification sound. Optional - `notify()` and `scheduleNotificationEx()` do it themselves - but it lets a settings screen verify a sound the moment the user picks it.

**Example**

Checks that an audio file in your app can be used as a notification sound, and copies it into place now. Optional: `notify()` and `scheduleNotificationEx()` do the same by themselves; this lets a settings screen check a sound the moment the user picks it.

**Returns:** `true` if the sound is usable; `false` if the file does not exist or is not a supported audio type. **Needs:** nothing.

```js
function chooseAlarmSound(path) {             // e.g. '/audio/chime.mp3'
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.prepareNotificationSound)) return;
  if (!WebToApk.prepareNotificationSound(path)) {
    showMessage('This sound file is missing from the app: ' + path);
    return;
  }
  localStorage.setItem('alarmSound', path);
  // Use it:
  WebToApk.notify(JSON.stringify({ title: 'Sound test', body: 'This is your alarm sound', sound: path, tag: 'sound-test' }));
}
```

Fill a sound picker with only the sounds that are really usable:

```js
const SOUNDS = [
  { label: 'Chime', path: '/audio/chime.mp3' },
  { label: 'Bell',  path: '/audio/bell.ogg' },
  { label: 'Beep',  path: '/audio/beep.wav' }
];

function renderSoundPicker(select) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.prepareNotificationSound)) return;
  select.innerHTML = '';
  SOUNDS.forEach(function (s) {
    if (!b.prepareNotificationSound(s.path)) return;   // missing or unsupported file
    const opt = document.createElement('option');
    opt.value = s.path; opt.textContent = s.label;
    select.appendChild(opt);
  });
}
```

Let the user pick their own audio file and use it for a daily reminder, passed as a `data:` URL:

```js
document.getElementById('own-sound').addEventListener('change', function (e) {
  const file = e.target.files[0];
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!file || !(b && b.prepareNotificationSound)) return;
  const reader = new FileReader();
  reader.onload = function () {
    const dataUrl = reader.result;                 // 'data:audio/mpeg;base64,...'
    if (!b.prepareNotificationSound(dataUrl)) {
      showMessage('That file cannot be used as a notification sound.');
      return;
    }
    b.scheduleNotificationEx('daily-walk', JSON.stringify({
      at: nextEvening(), repeat: 'daily',
      title: 'Walk time', body: 'Time for your evening walk', sound: dataUrl
    }));
  };
  reader.readAsDataURL(file);
});
```

**Accepted values:** a path in your web bundle (`'/audio/chime.mp3'`, `'audio/chime.mp3'`) or a `data:audio/...;base64,...` URL your page made. Types: mp3, wav, ogg, oga, m4a, aac, flac, opus, mid, midi.

**Notes:** a bare name without a folder or extension (a `res/raw` sound) is not checked here and returns `false`, even though `notify({sound: 'name'})` can use it. Android keeps one sound per channel, so changing the sound creates a new channel and resets the user's settings for that channel.

### `requestExactAlarms`

```js
window.WebToApk.requestExactAlarms(): Boolean
```

Opens the system screen where exact alarms are granted. Android 12+.

**Example**

Opens the Android 12+ system screen where the user allows this app to use exact alarms, so reminders fire on the minute.

**Returns:** `true` when the settings screen was opened (and on Android 11 and older, where nothing is needed); `false` if the screen could not be opened. It does not tell you the user's choice. **Needs:** turn on **⏰ Reminders** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

```js
document.getElementById('allow-exact').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.requestExactAlarms)) return;
  if (WebToApk.getAlarmPrecision() === 'exact') return;   // already fine
  WebToApk.requestExactAlarms();
});

// The user comes back from Settings: read the real answer.
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (document.hidden || !window.WebToApk) return;
  const exact = WebToApk.getAlarmPrecision() === 'exact';
  document.getElementById('allow-exact').hidden = exact;
});
```

Before saving a time-critical reminder, offer the settings screen only when timing is actually off:

```js
function saveMedicineReminder(at) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.scheduleNotificationEx && b.getAlarmPrecision)) return;
  b.scheduleNotificationEx('medicine', JSON.stringify({
    at: at, repeat: 'daily', title: 'Medicine', body: 'Time for your tablet'
  }));
  const precision = b.getAlarmPrecision();   // 'exact' | 'inexact' | 'unavailable'
  if (precision === 'inexact') {
    showBanner('Reminders may arrive a few minutes late.', 'Fix timing', function () {
      b.requestExactAlarms();                // runs from the banner button tap
    });
  } else if (precision === 'unavailable') {
    showBanner('The phone\'s alarm service is not answering; this reminder may not fire.');
  }
}
```

When the settings screen cannot be opened (`false`), tell the user where to find the switch:

```js
document.getElementById('fix-timing').addEventListener('click', function () {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.requestExactAlarms)) return;
  const opened = b.requestExactAlarms();
  if (!opened) {
    showMessage('Open Settings > Apps > this app > "Alarms & reminders" and turn it on.');
  }
  // When it did open, read the answer on return with getAlarmPrecision().
});
```

**Notes:** call it from a button tap and explain why first - it leaves your app. Reminders already scheduled keep working either way; only their timing changes.

### `requestNotificationPermission`

```js
window.WebToApk.requestNotificationPermission(): String
```

Reading and requesting the POST_NOTIFICATIONS grant, and managing notifications the page already scheduled. Posting and scheduling are documented on their own methods.

_Described by its group, Notification permission, cancelling and listing, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Shows the Android 13+ "Allow notifications?" dialog. Pages normally use `Notification.requestPermission()`, which calls this and waits for the user's answer.

**Returns:** a string, synchronously: `'granted'` if already allowed (or on Android 12 and older), otherwise `'default'` while the dialog opens. It cannot return the user's answer. **Needs:** turn on **Notifications** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

**Use the Promise API** - it resolves with the real answer (`'granted'` or `'denied'`):

```js
document.getElementById('enable-alerts').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!('Notification' in window)) return;
  const perm = await Notification.requestPermission();
  if (perm === 'granted') {
    showMessage('Alerts are on');
  } else {
    showMessage('Alerts are off. You can turn them on in Settings.');
  }
});
```

**The raw call**, only to open the dialog without waiting:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.requestNotificationPermission) {
  const now = WebToApk.requestNotificationPermission();  // 'granted' or 'default'
  if (now === 'granted') enableAlertFeatures();
  // otherwise re-check later with WebToApk.getNotificationPermission()
  // ('granted' | 'denied' | 'default')
}
```

Older code that passes a callback to `Notification.requestPermission` gets the same final answer:

```js
document.getElementById('turn-on-reminders').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!('Notification' in window)) return;
  if (Notification.permission !== 'default') { updateReminderUi(Notification.permission); return; }
  Notification.requestPermission(function (perm) {
    updateReminderUi(perm);   // 'granted' or 'denied', once the user answers
  });
});
```

**Notes:** ask from a button tap with a clear reason. After the user refuses twice, Android stops showing the dialog and the answer is `'denied'` at once; the user must then allow it in the app's Settings.

### `requestOpenAppPermission`

```js
window.WebToApk.requestOpenAppPermission(): Boolean
```

Opens the system screen where the full-screen alert is granted. Android 14+.

**Example**

Opens the Android 14+ system screen where the user allows full-screen alerts for this app, so an `openApp: true` reminder can put the app on screen.

**Returns:** `true` when the settings screen was opened (and below Android 14, where nothing is needed); `false` if it could not be opened. It does not tell you the user's choice. **Needs:** turn on **⏰ Reminders** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

```js
document.getElementById('allow-open-app').addEventListener('click', function () {

  if (!(b && b.requestOpenAppPermission)) return;
  if (b.canOpenAppAtTime() === 'granted') return;

// Read the real answer when the user comes back:
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (document.hidden || !window.WebToApk) return;
  const ok = WebToApk.canOpenAppAtTime() === 'granted';
```

Remember the alarm the user was setting, send them to Settings, and finish it when they come back:

```js
let pendingAlarm = null;

function setWakeAlarm(at) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.requestOpenAppPermission)) return;
  if (b.canOpenAppAtTime() === 'denied') {
    pendingAlarm = at;
    b.requestOpenAppPermission();
    return;
  }
  b.scheduleNotificationEx('wake', JSON.stringify({ at: at, title: 'Alarm', body: 'Wake up', openApp: true }));
}

document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (document.hidden || pendingAlarm === null || !window.WebToApk) return;
  if (WebToApk.canOpenAppAtTime() === 'granted') setWakeAlarm(pendingAlarm);
  else showMessage('Without that setting the alarm cannot open the app by itself.');
  pendingAlarm = null;
});
```

When the settings screen cannot be opened (`false`), say where the switch is:

```js
document.getElementById('allow-fullscreen').addEventListener('click', function () {

  if (!(b && b.requestOpenAppPermission)) return;
  if (!b.requestOpenAppPermission()) {
    showMessage('Open Settings > Apps > this app > Notifications and allow full-screen notifications.');
```

**Notes:** call it from a button tap after explaining why - it leaves your app.

### `scheduleNotification`

```js
window.WebToApk.scheduleNotification(id: String, title: String, body: String, triggerAtMillis: String, repeat: String): Boolean
```

Reading and requesting the POST_NOTIFICATIONS grant, and managing notifications the page already scheduled. Posting and scheduling are documented on their own methods.

_Described by its group, Notification permission, cancelling and listing, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Schedules a simple reminder (title and text) for a future time. It fires even when the app is closed and is set again after the phone restarts.

**Returns:** `true` when it was scheduled; `false` when `id` is empty or the time is not a number. **Needs:** turn on **⏰ Reminders** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build (it also turns on Notifications), and the user's notification permission on Android 13+.

```js
function remindToDrinkWater() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.scheduleNotification)) {
    showMessage('Reminders work in the installed app only.');
    return;
  }
  const ok = WebToApk.scheduleNotification(
    'water',                                  // your own id; same id replaces the old reminder
    'Drink water',                            // title
    'Time for a glass of water',              // body
    String(Date.now() + 60 * 60 * 1000),      // epoch milliseconds, AS A STRING
    'daily'                                   // none | minutely | hourly | daily | weekly
  );
  if (!ok) showMessage('Could not schedule the reminder');
}
```

**Know when a reminder opened the app** (the user tapped it):

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:reminder', function (e) {
  // e.detail = { id: 'water', overLockScreen: false }
  if (e.detail.id === 'water') openWaterLog();
});
```

A one-off reminder at 8:00 on the day a task is due:

```js
function remindTask(task) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.scheduleNotification)) return false;
  const at = new Date(task.dueDate);
  at.setHours(8, 0, 0, 0);
  if (at.getTime() <= Date.now()) return false;     // that morning has passed
  return WebToApk.scheduleNotification(
    'task-' + task.id,
    'Due today',
    task.title,
    String(at.getTime()),                           // epoch ms as a string
    'none'
  );
}
```

**Notes:** the reminder uses the "urgent" (heads-up) style and its tag is the id. A repeating reminder that was missed while the phone was off fires at the next step. For a picture, buttons, your own sound or opening the app over the lock screen, use `scheduleNotificationEx`. If exact alarms are off for the app, the time can drift by minutes; check `getAlarmPrecision()`.

### `scheduleNotificationEx`

```js
window.WebToApk.scheduleNotificationEx(id: String, optionsJson: String): Boolean
```

The full form of [scheduleNotification]: everything `notify()` accepts, fired at a future time with the app closed. WebToApk.scheduleNotificationEx('dose-1', JSON.stringify({ at: Date.now() + 3600000,   // epoch millis (alias: triggerAt) repeat: 'daily',            // none|minutely|hourly|daily|weekly|weekdays|monthly|yearly // days: [1, 3, 5],         // with 'weekdays': ISO Mon=1..Sun=7 (default Mon-Fri) // alarm: true,             // ring like an alarm clock (getAlarmSupport()) title: 'Time for your dose', body: 'Vitamin D - 1 tablet', sound: '/audio/chime.mp3',  // a file in YOUR bundle; 'silent' for none openApp: true               // open the app itself, over the lock screen })); A bundled sound is copied into place during this call, so a wrong file name is reported now (false) rather than turning into the default sound days later.

**Example**

Schedules a reminder with every option `notify()` has (picture, buttons, sound, channel, open the app), for a future time. It fires when the app is closed and survives a restart.

**Returns:** `true` when scheduled. `false` when no time is given (`at`, `triggerAt`, `triggerAtMillis` or `inSeconds`), the id is empty, the JSON is bad, or `sound` names a file that is not in your app. **Needs:** turn on **⏰ Reminders** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build, and the user's notification permission on Android 13+.

**A daily reminder with your own sound that opens the app** (over the lock screen):

```js
function scheduleStandup(tomorrowAt9am) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.scheduleNotificationEx)) { showMessage('Reminders work in the installed app only.'); return; }

  // Both are user settings: check, and ask if needed.
  if (b.getAlarmPrecision() === 'inexact') b.requestExactAlarms();
  if (b.canOpenAppAtTime() === 'denied') b.requestOpenAppPermission();

  const ok = b.scheduleNotificationEx('standup', JSON.stringify({
    at: tomorrowAt9am,          // epoch ms (or triggerAt, or inSeconds: 3600)
    repeat: 'daily',            // none | minutely | hourly | daily | weekly | weekdays | monthly | yearly
    title: 'Stand-up',
    body: 'Daily sync starts now',
    sound: '/audio/alarm.mp3',  // a file in YOUR app; 'silent' for none
    openApp: true               // full-screen alert that puts the app on screen
  }));
  if (!ok) showMessage('Check the sound file path — nothing was scheduled.');
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:reminder', function (e) {
  // e.detail = { id: 'standup', overLockScreen: true, action: 'open', ringing: false }
  openMeetingScreen(e.detail.id);
});
```

**Gym days only - Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 18:00** (`days` are ISO: Monday = 1 … Sunday = 7; without `days`, `'weekdays'` means Monday-Friday):

```js
WebToApk.scheduleNotificationEx('gym', JSON.stringify({
  at: nextAt(18, 0),          // epoch ms of the first time; moved to the next listed day if needed
  repeat: 'weekdays',
  days: [1, 3, 5],
  title: 'Gym time',
  body: 'Leg day'
}));

// Rent on the 31st: 'monthly' rings on the last day of shorter months (28/29/30) and on the 31st again when there is one.
WebToApk.scheduleNotificationEx('rent', JSON.stringify({ at: rentDueAt, repeat: 'monthly', title: 'Rent is due' }));
// A birthday: same date every year (29 February rings on the 28th in other years).
WebToApk.scheduleNotificationEx('bday-ana', JSON.stringify({ at: anaBirthdayAt9am, repeat: 'yearly', title: 'Ana\'s birthday' }));
```

**A real alarm clock** (`alarm: true`): rings on the phone's ALARM volume - through silent mode, and through Do Not Disturb when the user allows alarms - and keeps ringing until **Dismiss** / **Snooze** or `ringSeconds`. It shows the alarm icon in the status bar and comes on screen over the lock screen:

```js
function setWakeAlarm(atMs) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.getAlarmSupport)) { showMessage('Alarms work in the installed app only.'); return; }
  const support = b.getAlarmSupport();   // 'ready' | 'not_enabled' | 'needs_exact_alarm' | 'needs_notification_permission'
  if (support === 'needs_exact_alarm') { b.requestExactAlarms(); return; }
  if (support !== 'ready') { showMessage('Alarms are not available: ' + support); return; }

  const ok = b.scheduleNotificationEx('wake', JSON.stringify({
    at: atMs,
    repeat: 'weekdays',          // daily/weekly/weekdays/monthly/yearly keep 07:00 across clock changes
    title: 'Wake up',
    body: 'Good morning',
    alarm: true,
    sound: '',                   // '' = the phone's alarm tone; or '/audio/rooster.mp3'; 'silent' = vibrate only
    vibrate: true,               // needs Vibration on in the build
    ringSeconds: 300,            // stop and count as missed after 5 minutes (default 600, max 3600)
    snoozeMinutes: 9,            // 0 hides the Snooze button (default 10)
    snoozeLabel: 'Snooze', dismissLabel: 'Stop'
  }));
  if (!ok) showMessage('The alarm was not set.');
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:reminder', function (e) {
  const d = e.detail;
  // Opened by the ringing alarm:  { id: 'wake', action: 'open', ringing: true, overLockScreen: true }
  // How a ring ended (also delivered later if the app was closed):
  //   { id: 'wake', action: 'dismiss' | 'snooze' | 'missed' | 'error', alarm: true,
  //     source: 'notification' | 'page' | 'timeout' | 'replaced' | 'system',
  //     snoozeMinutes?, snoozedUntil?, error?, soundError? }
  if (d.action === 'open' && d.ringing) showRingScreen(d.id);   // your Stop / Snooze buttons call stopAlarm / snoozeAlarm
  if (d.action === 'missed') logMissedAlarm(d.id);
});
```

**A reminder with buttons, in 30 minutes:**

```js
WebToApk.scheduleNotificationEx('dose-1', JSON.stringify({
  inSeconds: 30 * 60,
  title: 'Time for your dose',
  body: 'Vitamin D — 1 tablet',
  actions: [{ id: 'taken', label: 'Taken' }, { id: 'snooze', label: 'Snooze' }]
}));

window.addEventListener('appmint:notification-action', function (e) {
  // e.detail = { actionId: 'taken', tag: 'dose-1' }
  if (e.detail.actionId === 'snooze') {
    WebToApk.scheduleNotificationEx(e.detail.tag, JSON.stringify({ inSeconds: 600, title: 'Time for your dose', body: 'Snoozed reminder' }));
  }
});
```

A one-off reminder with a picture when a sale starts, on the normal channel:

```js
function remindSale(sale) {                        // sale.startsAt = epoch ms
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.scheduleNotificationEx)) return false;
  return WebToApk.scheduleNotificationEx('sale-' + sale.id, JSON.stringify({
    at: sale.startsAt,
    title: 'The sale starts now',
    body: sale.name,
    image: 'https://example.com/banners/' + sale.id + '.jpg',   // expanded picture
    channel: 'default'                             // not the heads-up style reminders use by default
  }));
}
```

**Notes:** the same id replaces an older reminder. Defaults: tag = the id, channel = `urgent`, `bigText` = the body. A button tap reaches the page only while the app is running. The sound file is copied when you schedule, so a wrong path fails now and not days later; mp3, wav, ogg, m4a, aac, flac and opus work. `openApp` is the only way an app can come on screen by itself at a set time; on Android 14+ the user must allow it (`canOpenAppAtTime`). `repeat: 'weekdays'` with `days` outside 1-7 returns `false`. `alarm: true` needs **🔔 Alarm clock** in the Access step (Step 4) and returns `false` unless `getAlarmSupport()` is `'ready'`; only one alarm rings at a time (a new one ends the previous as `missed`). If an alarm's own sound file has disappeared by the time it rings (a Remote Update removed it), it rings with the phone's alarm tone and the event carries `soundError: true`.

### `showNotification`

```js
window.WebToApk.showNotification(title: String, body: String, icon: String, tag: String): Boolean
```

The ORIGINAL four-argument form, kept verbatim as an adapter so every app already in the wild and every guide snippet keeps working. It now forwards to the rich builder - which means the `icon` argument, silently discarded by the old implementation, finally does something.

**Example**

The original four-argument notification call. It shows a notification with a title, text, an optional large icon and a tag. New code should use `notify(optionsJson)` or `new Notification(...)`, which do more.

**Returns:** `true` when the notification was handed to the system. **Needs:** turn on **Notifications** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build, and the user's permission on Android 13+.

**The standard web API** (it calls this method for you):

```js
async function tellUser() {
  if (!('Notification' in window)) return;
  const p = Notification.permission === 'granted' ? 'granted' : await Notification.requestPermission();
  if (p === 'granted') new Notification('Saved', { body: 'Your note was saved', tag: 'note' });
}
```

**The raw call.** Arguments: title, body, icon, tag. Pass `''` for no icon or no tag.

```js
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.showNotification) {
  WebToApk.showNotification(
    'Saved',                                  // title
    'Your note was saved',                    // body
    'https://example.com/avatar.png',         // large icon (https://, data:, or 'img/x.png' in your app), or ''
    'note'                                    // tag: same tag replaces the old notification
  );
}
```

Update one status notification in place by reusing its tag:

```js
function showSyncStatus(done, total) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.showNotification)) return;
  if (b.getNotificationPermission() !== 'granted') return;
  b.showNotification(
    'Syncing photos',
    done + ' of ' + total + ' uploaded',
    '',          // no large icon
    'sync'       // same tag every time: the text updates, no new notification
  );
}
```

**Notes:** it forwards to `notify({title, body, largeIcon: icon, tag})` on the default channel. Without a tag every call adds a new notification. For pictures, buttons, progress or a sticky notification use `notify`.

### `snoozeAlarm`

```js
window.WebToApk.snoozeAlarm(id: String, minutes: Int): Boolean
```

Stops the ringing alarm [id] ("" = whichever is ringing) and rings it again in [minutes] (1-1440; 0 = the alarm's own snoozeMinutes). False when it is not ringing.

**Example**

Stops a ringing alarm clock and rings it again after a few minutes, like its **Snooze** button. Only this ring moves: a daily alarm still rings at its usual time tomorrow.

**Returns:** `true` when the alarm was ringing and is snoozed; `false` when it was not ringing. `id` `''` = whichever rings; `minutes` 1-1440, or `0` for the alarm's own `snoozeMinutes` (default 10). **Needs:** **🔔 Alarm clock** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

```js
document.getElementById('snooze').onclick = function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.snoozeAlarm)) return;
  if (WebToApk.snoozeAlarm('', 5)) showMessage('Ringing again in 5 minutes');
  hideRingScreen();
};

window.addEventListener('appmint:reminder', function (e) {
  // { id: 'wake', action: 'snooze', alarm: true, source: 'page', snoozeMinutes: 5, snoozedUntil: 1767340800000 }
  if (e.detail.action === 'snooze') updateNextAlarmLabel(e.detail.snoozedUntil);
});
```

**Schedule an alarm clock, then wire a dismiss button:**

```js
const b = window.WebToApk;
if (b && b.snoozeAlarm && b.getAlarmSupport() === 'ready') {
  b.scheduleNotificationEx('wake', JSON.stringify({
    at: Date.now() + 8 * 3600000, repeat: 'daily', alarm: true,
    title: 'Wake up', body: 'Good morning'
  }));
}
document.getElementById('dismiss').onclick = () => {
  if (WebToApk.isAlarmRinging()) WebToApk.stopAlarm('');
};
```

**Snooze by the alarm's own length, and handle "nothing is ringing":**

```js
document.getElementById('snooze').onclick = () => {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.snoozeAlarm)) return;
  const ok = WebToApk.snoozeAlarm('', 0);   // 0 = the alarm's own snoozeMinutes (default 10)
  if (!ok) showMessage('No alarm is ringing right now.');
};
```

**Notes:** the snoozed ring is listed by `getScheduledNotifications()` as `<id>#snooze`; `cancelNotification(id)` removes it too.

### `stopAlarm`

```js
window.WebToApk.stopAlarm(id: String): Boolean
```

Stops the ringing alarm [id] ("" = whichever is ringing), like its Dismiss button. A repeating alarm stays scheduled for its next time. False when it is not ringing.

**Example**

Stops a ringing alarm clock, exactly like its **Dismiss** button. A repeating alarm stays set for its next time; use `cancelNotification(id)` to remove it.

**Returns:** `true` when that alarm was ringing and is now stopped; `false` when it was not ringing. Pass `''` to stop whichever alarm is ringing. **Needs:** **🔔 Alarm clock** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:reminder', function (e) {
  const d = e.detail;                 // { id, action: 'open', ringing: true, overLockScreen }
  if (d.action === 'open' && d.ringing) showRingScreen(d.id);
});

document.getElementById('stop').onclick = function () {
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.stopAlarm) WebToApk.stopAlarm(currentAlarmId);
  hideRingScreen();
};
```

Offer the stop button only where the bridge exists, and read the answer:

```js
const stopBtn = document.getElementById('stop');
if (window.WebToApk && typeof WebToApk.stopAlarm === 'function') {
  stopBtn.onclick = function () {
    const wasRinging = WebToApk.stopAlarm('');      // '' = whichever alarm is ringing
    if (!wasRinging) showMessage('Nothing was ringing.');
  };
} else {
  stopBtn.hidden = true;                             // plain browser: no alarm clock
}
```

Pair it with `isAlarmRinging()` so the page can show the ring screen for a ring that started while it was away:

```js
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (document.hidden || !window.WebToApk) return;
  if (WebToApk.isAlarmRinging && WebToApk.isAlarmRinging()) showRingScreen();
  else hideRingScreen();
});
```

**Notes:** the page then also receives `appmint:reminder` with `{ id, action: 'dismiss', alarm: true, source: 'page' }`.
