# The push inbox and audience - JavaScript bridge API

> Messages the creator sent from a dashboard, kept on the device so the page can show a history rather than only a tray pop-up - and the signed-in user id and tags that let the send center target one user or a tag, and fire automations such as an abandoned-cart reminder.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/push

### `AppMint.notifyUser`

```js
AppMint.notifyUser(userId, { title, body?, url?, image?, data? })
```

**Example**

> **Send a notification to one user (new order, new like, new message) - two ways:**
> - **Easy - no server:** call `AppMint.notifyUser('seller_7', { title, body })` from your page. AppMint sends it. Its daily limits count notifications SENT, not users or phones: your app can have any number of users and phones (Free: 300 sends a day for the whole app · Starter/Pro: 5,000 · Studio: unlimited).
> - **Advanced - your own server:** your Firebase Cloud Function sends to the user's push token with your own Firebase key. No limits from AppMint. Use this only if you already run a server.
>
> Both reach the user even when the app is closed, look the same, and can be used together. Apps built before AppMint 1.11.63 need a rebuild (Update the App) to get notifyUser.

Sends a notification from this phone to ANOTHER user of your app - on every phone where that user is signed in - even while their app is closed. A tap opens `url` in the app.

**Step 1 - on the receiver's side, once after sign-in** (your own user id, never an email):

```js
AppMint.setPushUser(currentUser.id);   // e.g. 'seller_7'; AppMint.setPushUser('') on sign-out
```

**Step 2 - send.** Real-life cases, copy and change the words:

**Shop app** - a customer places an order, the seller gets "New order #42 · ₹450"; a tap opens the order:

```js
async function placeOrder(order) {
  await saveOrder(order);                                  // your own database
  AppMint.notifyUser(order.sellerId, {
    title: 'New order #' + order.id + ' · ₹' + order.total,
    body: order.items.length + ' items from ' + order.customerName,
    url: '#/orders/' + order.id,
  });
}
```

**Dating app** - someone likes a profile, that person gets "Someone liked your profile":

```js
async function likeProfile(profile) {
  await saveLike(profile.id);
  AppMint.notifyUser(profile.ownerId, { title: 'Someone liked your profile', url: '#/likes' });
}
```

**Chat app** - a message is sent, the receiver gets "Priya: Are you coming?"; a tap opens the chat:

```js
async function sendMessage(chat, text) {
  await saveMessage(chat.id, text);
  AppMint.notifyUser(chat.otherUserId, {
    title: me.name + ': ' + text.slice(0, 80),
    url: '#/chat/' + chat.id,
    data: { chatId: chat.id },
  });
}
```

**Booking app** - a booking is confirmed, the customer gets "Your table is booked for 8 PM":

```js
async function confirmBooking(b) {
  await markConfirmed(b.id);
  AppMint.notifyUser(b.customerId, { title: 'Your table is booked for ' + b.time, body: b.restaurant, url: '#/bookings/' + b.id });
}
```

**Check the answer** - over the day's limit you get `{ ok: false, code: 'rate_limited' }`. The order, like or message is already saved in your database, so simply show nothing (or try again later):

```js
async function tell(userId, note) {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.notifyUser)) return;           // a browser, or an app built before 1.11.63
  const r = await AppMint.notifyUser(userId, note);
  if (r.ok) console.log('sent to', r.sent, 'phone(s)');         // 0 = that user has not signed in on a phone yet
  else if (r.code === 'rate_limited') console.log('daily limit reached, try tomorrow');
  else console.warn('not sent:', r.code, r.detail || '');
}
```

**Returns:** a Promise that never rejects: `{ ok: true, sent }` - `sent` is how many phones it went to (`0` when that user is not signed in on any phone with `setPushUser`); or `{ ok: false, code }`: `rate_limited` (with `limit`: `sender`, `receiver` or `app`), `no_push` (app built without AppMint Push), `bad_request` (with `detail`), `not_registered` (this phone has no push address yet - open the app online once), `no_credentials` (the creator has not added the Firebase key in AppMint's Notifications screen), `foreign_origin` (called from a page outside the app's own address), `network`, `paused`, `unavailable`.

**Rules:** `title` up to 100 characters, `body` up to 500, `url` up to 500 (`#/route`, `/path` or a full address), `image` an `https://` picture, `data` up to 10 keys with short text values - the receiver's page finds it as `message.data` in the push inbox and in the `appmint:push` event. The sender's own phone is skipped; the same user's other phones get it.

**Daily limits** (reset at midnight UTC), by the plan of the app's creator (AppMint Cloud, signed in on the phone that built the app):

| Plan | Notifications one phone can send | Notifications one user can receive | Notifications the whole app can send |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 50 | 100 | 300 |
| Starter, Pro | 200 | 500 | 5,000 |
| Studio | no limit | no limit | no limit |

**What the limits mean:** they count how many notifyUser notifications are sent per day. They never limit how many people use your app, how many phones receive notifications, or how many phones one user has (a user signed in on several phones gets it on each, up to 10). Example: a Free shop app with 50,000 users can send up to 300 "new order" alerts a day. Messages you send from AppMint's Notifications screen (to everyone, a tag or one user) and from your own server are not counted. When a limit is reached, notifyUser answers `{ ok:false, code:'rate_limited' }` until midnight UTC; upgrade the plan to raise it.

**Needs:** **AppMint Push** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) and the Firebase key added in AppMint's Notifications screen. AppMint 1.11.63 and newer.

**Advanced way (your own server)** - the same "order → seller" from a Firebase Cloud Function with your own Firebase key, no AppMint limits: follow the Integration Guide's AppMint Push chapter ("Send from your own server") and the sample in `scripts/push-own-server/functions/`.

**Notes:** any user of your app can notify any user id they know - never put a secret in a notification, and let the receiver's app read the real order or message from your database. Notifications sent this way do not appear in the send center's statistics.

### `AppMint.setPushUser`

```js
AppMint.setPushUser(id)
```

**Example**

> **Send a notification to one user (new order, new like, new message) - two ways:**
> - **Easy - no server:** call `AppMint.notifyUser('seller_7', { title, body })` from your page. AppMint sends it. Its daily limits count notifications SENT, not users or phones: your app can have any number of users and phones (Free: 300 sends a day for the whole app · Starter/Pro: 5,000 · Studio: unlimited).
> - **Advanced - your own server:** your Firebase Cloud Function sends to the user's push token with your own Firebase key. No limits from AppMint. Use this only if you already run a server.
>
> Both reach the user even when the app is closed, look the same, and can be used together. Apps built before AppMint 1.11.63 need a rebuild (Update the App) to get notifyUser.

The same as `WebToApk.setPushUser(id)`, under the `AppMint` name: tells AppMint Push which of YOUR users is signed in on this phone, so `AppMint.notifyUser(id, …)` from another phone - and the send center's "one user" target - reaches it. Call it after sign-in with your own id; call it with `''` on sign-out.

**Returns:** `true` when saved; `false` for an id with anything other than letters, digits and `_ @ . : + -` (up to 128), and in an app built without AppMint Push. **Needs:** AppMint Push turned on when you build; AppMint 1.11.63 and newer (older builds have `WebToApk.setPushUser` only).

```js
// After your own sign-in succeeds:
if (window.AppMint && AppMint.setPushUser) AppMint.setPushUser(user.id);   // e.g. 'seller_7'

// On sign-out, so this phone stops getting that user's notifications:
if (window.AppMint && AppMint.setPushUser) AppMint.setPushUser('');
```

**Notes:** use your database id, never an email address or phone number. The id belongs to this phone until you change it.

### `AppMint.trackEvent`

```js
window.AppMint.trackEvent
```

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.trackEvent` - the example there shows this one too.

Tells the app that something happened ("signed_up", "checkout_done", "level:3"). An in-app message the creator made in the AppMint Push send center with the trigger **"When an event happens"** and the same name shows now (or after the wait the creator picked).

**Returns:** `true` when the event was taken; `false` for a name outside letters, digits and `_ . : -` (up to 64), and in an app built without AppMint Push. `AppMint.trackEvent(name, props)` is the same call with `props` as an object. **Needs:** **AppMint Push** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build. `propsJson` is optional (`''`) and is not stored.

```js
// After a purchase: the creator's "Thanks, rate us?" message is set to trigger on "purchase_done".
function onPurchaseDone(order) {
  if (window.AppMint && AppMint.trackEvent) {
    AppMint.trackEvent('purchase_done', { total: order.total });
  }
}
```

The raw bridge takes the props as a JSON string (pass `''` for none):

```js
function track(name, props) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.trackEvent)) return false;   // a browser: nothing to show
  return WebToApk.trackEvent(name, props ? JSON.stringify(props) : '');
}
track('level:3');
track('tutorial_skipped', { step: 2 });
```

A screen change the address does not show (tabs, a wizard, a modal "page") can be reported as a route, so the creator's **"On a page"** messages see it. The page can also dispatch the `appmint:route` event with the path; the app listens for it:

```js
function showTab(name) {
  document.querySelectorAll('.tab').forEach(function (t) { t.hidden = t.id !== name; });
  if (window.AppMint && AppMint.trackEvent) AppMint.trackEvent('appmint:route', { path: '/' + name });
}

// Same thing, without touching the bridge at all:
window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('appmint:route', { detail: { path: '/cart' } }));
```

**Notes:** route messages already follow real URL changes (page loads, `history.pushState`, `#/hash` routes) on their own; report a route only for views the address does not change. Events are not counted or stored anywhere; they only decide whether a message shows.

### `clearPushInbox`

```js
window.WebToApk.clearPushInbox(): Boolean
```

Empties the push inbox (the tray and server history are untouched).

**Example**

Empties the push inbox on this phone.

**Returns:** `true` when done; `false` on an internal error. **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build.

```js
document.getElementById('clear-inbox').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.clearPushInbox)) return;
  if (!confirm('Delete all messages? This cannot be undone.')) return;
  if (WebToApk.clearPushInbox()) renderInbox();
});
```

Empty the inbox when the user signs out, so the next person on this phone does not see their messages:

```js
async function signOut() {
  await myAuth.signOut();
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.clearPushInbox) {
    WebToApk.clearPushInbox();
  }
  document.getElementById('bell-count').textContent = '';
  showLoginScreen();
}
```

Show a settings row with how many messages are stored, disabled when there is nothing to delete:

```js
function paintClearRow() {
  const btn = document.getElementById('clear-inbox');
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.clearPushInbox)) { btn.hidden = true; return; }
  const count = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getPushInbox() || '[]').length;
  btn.textContent = count ? 'Delete ' + count + ' messages' : 'No messages';
  btn.disabled = count === 0;
}

document.getElementById('clear-inbox').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (WebToApk.clearPushInbox()) paintClearRow();
  else alert('Could not delete the messages. Please try again.');
});

paintClearRow();
```

**Notes:** this is permanent - unlike `dismissPushMessage`, there is no undo. Tray notifications and your send history in AppMint are not touched. New messages still arrive.

### `dismissPushMessage`

```js
window.WebToApk.dismissPushMessage(id: String): Boolean
```

Dismisses ONE message from the inbox - the per-row swipe-away an inbox screen needs (clearPushInbox is all-or-nothing). REVERSIBLE by design: the entry is hidden, not destroyed, so the UI can offer "Undo" for a few seconds after the swipe. Local only: the tray notification and the creator's history are untouched.

**Example**

Hides one message from the push inbox (a swipe-away). It can be undone with `restorePushMessage(id)`.

**Returns:** `true` if the message was hidden; `false` if the id is unknown or it was already hidden. **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build.

**Swipe away with a 5-second Undo:**

```js
function dismissRow(id, rowEl) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.dismissPushMessage)) return;
  if (!WebToApk.dismissPushMessage(id)) return;
  rowEl.remove();

  const bar = document.getElementById('undo-bar');
  bar.hidden = false;
  const timer = setTimeout(function () { bar.hidden = true; }, 5000);
  document.getElementById('undo-btn').onclick = function () {
    clearTimeout(timer);
    bar.hidden = true;
    WebToApk.restorePushMessage(id);         // back in its old place
    renderInbox();
  };
}
```

Tidy the inbox when it opens by hiding messages that are read and older than 30 days:

```js
function hideOldReadMessages() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.dismissPushMessage)) return 0;
  const cutoff = Date.now() - 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
  let hidden = 0;
  JSON.parse(WebToApk.getPushInbox() || '[]').forEach(function (m) {
    if (m.read && m.receivedAt < cutoff && WebToApk.dismissPushMessage(m.id)) hidden++;
  });
  return hidden;
}

if (hideOldReadMessages() > 0) renderInbox();
```

Dismiss a row with a real finger swipe (drag it more than 40% of its width):

```js
function makeSwipeable(rowEl, id) {
  let startX = null;
  rowEl.addEventListener('pointerdown', function (e) { startX = e.clientX; rowEl.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); });
  rowEl.addEventListener('pointermove', function (e) {
    if (startX !== null) rowEl.style.transform = 'translateX(' + (e.clientX - startX) + 'px)';
  });
  rowEl.addEventListener('pointerup', function (e) {
    const dx = startX === null ? 0 : e.clientX - startX;
    startX = null;
    if (Math.abs(dx) > rowEl.offsetWidth * 0.4 && window.WebToApk && WebToApk.dismissPushMessage(id)) {
      rowEl.remove();
    } else {
      rowEl.style.transform = '';            // not far enough: snap back
    }
  });
}
```

**Notes:** only this phone's inbox changes. The tray notification and your send history in AppMint stay. Hidden messages are not returned by `getPushInbox()`.

### `getInAppCampaigns`

```js
window.WebToApk.getInAppCampaigns(): String
```

In-app messages this install holds: JSON [{id, name}] ("[]" without AppMint Push).

**Example**

Lists the in-app messages this install holds right now (the creator's campaigns from the AppMint Push send center that this user is in the audience for) as a JSON string `[{"id": "...", "name": "..."}]`.

**Returns:** a JSON array string; `"[]"` when there are none and in an app built without AppMint Push. **Needs:** **AppMint Push** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build. The list refreshes on each app start (and about every hour in the foreground).

```js
var list = [];
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getInAppCampaigns) {
  try { list = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getInAppCampaigns()); } catch (e) {}
}
console.log('in-app messages on this phone:', list.map(function (c) { return c.name; }));
```

Show a debug list in your own admin screen:

```js
function renderInAppDebug(el) {
  var raw = (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getInAppCampaigns) ? WebToApk.getInAppCampaigns() : '[]';
  var items = JSON.parse(raw);
  el.innerHTML = items.length
    ? items.map(function (c) { return '<li>' + c.name + ' <code>' + c.id + '</code></li>'; }).join('')
    : '<li>No in-app messages for this install</li>';
}
renderInAppDebug(document.getElementById('inapp-debug'));
```

Skip your own welcome hint when the creator already runs a message with that name:

```js
function hasCampaign(name) {
  try { return JSON.parse(WebToApk.getInAppCampaigns()).some(function (c) { return c.name === name; }); }
  catch (e) { return false; }
}
if (!hasCampaign('Welcome tour')) showMyOwnWelcome();
```

**Notes:** only the id and name are exposed; the message itself reaches the page through the `appmint:inapp` event when it shows (see `setInAppPresentation`).

### `getOneSignalIds`

```js
window.WebToApk.getOneSignalIds(): String
```

OneSignal builds: {"externalId","onesignalId","subscriptionId","ready"} as JSON ("" for a value OneSignal does not have yet); "{}" without OneSignal.

**Example**

Reads this install's OneSignal ids: the External ID set with `setOneSignalUser`, OneSignal's own user id and the push subscription id.

**Returns:** a JSON `string`, synchronously: `{"externalId":"u_42","onesignalId":"…","subscriptionId":"…","ready":true}`. A value OneSignal does not have yet is `""` or missing; `{"ready":false}` while OneSignal is still starting; `"{}"` in an app built without OneSignal. **Needs:** turn on **OneSignal** in the Integrate step (Step 3) with your OneSignal App ID when you build.

**Set the user only when it changed** (on every app start):

```js
function syncOneSignalUser(currentUserId) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getOneSignalIds)) return;
  const ids = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getOneSignalIds());
  const want = currentUserId || '';
  if (ids.ready === false) { setTimeout(function () { syncOneSignalUser(currentUserId); }, 1000); return; }
  if ((ids.externalId || '') !== want) WebToApk.setOneSignalUser(want);
}
```

**Save the subscription id with your user**, to send to this one phone from your server:

```js
async function saveSubscription(userId) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getOneSignalIds)) return;
  const ids = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getOneSignalIds());
  if (!ids.subscriptionId) return;               // not registered yet (no notification permission, offline)
  await fetch('/api/devices', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ userId: userId, oneSignalSubscriptionId: ids.subscriptionId })
  });
}
```

**Notes:** The subscription id is empty until the phone has registered with OneSignal (it needs the network, and on Android 13+ the notification permission). It changes after a reinstall or when the app's data is cleared.

### `getPushInbox`

```js
window.WebToApk.getPushInbox(): String
```

AppMint Push inbox (creator-sent messages, newest first, max 50): JSON array of {id, title, body, imageUrl, link, receivedAt, read}. Always the full current truth - an app that mounts late loses nothing by having missed the live `appmint:push` events.

**Example**

Reads the in-app inbox of push messages you sent with AppMint Push: newest first, up to 50, without the ones the user dismissed.

**Returns:** a JSON **string**, synchronously. Parse it. Each item: `{ id, title, body, imageUrl, link, receivedAt, read }` (`receivedAt` in epoch ms; `imageUrl` and `link` are `''` when the message has none), plus optional design fields when you used a template in AppMint: `template`, `accent`, `iconUrl`, `buttons: [{label, link}]`, `badge`, `inapp`, `countdownAt`, `progress`, `lines`, `collapse`. `'[]'` when empty. **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build; without it the inbox is always empty.

**Render the inbox, and refresh it live with `appmint:push`:**

```js
function loadInbox() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getPushInbox)) return [];
  try { return JSON.parse(WebToApk.getPushInbox() || '[]'); } catch (e) { return []; }
}

function renderInbox() {
  const inbox = loadInbox();
  const unread = inbox.filter(function (m) { return !m.read; }).length;
  document.getElementById('bell-count').textContent = unread ? String(unread) : '';
  const ul = document.getElementById('inbox');
  ul.innerHTML = '';
  inbox.forEach(function (m) {
    const li = document.createElement('li');
    li.className = m.read ? 'read' : 'unread';
    li.textContent = m.title + ' — ' + m.body;
    li.onclick = function () {
      WebToApk.markPushRead(m.id);
      if (m.link) location.href = m.link;
      renderInbox();
    };
    ul.appendChild(li);
  });
}

// While the app is open:
window.addEventListener('appmint:push', function (e) {
  // { type: 'received', message: {id, title, body, ...}, presented: true|false }
  // { type: 'revoked', id }  — you retracted the message
  // presented = the app already showed it on screen (see setPushPresentation)
  if (e.detail.type === 'received' && !e.detail.presented) showBanner(e.detail.message.title);
  renderInbox();
});

renderInbox();
```

Update the unread count on your bell whenever the user comes back to the app (messages that arrived while it was in the background are already in the inbox):

```js
function unreadCount() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getPushInbox)) return 0;
  try {
    return JSON.parse(WebToApk.getPushInbox() || '[]').filter(function (m) { return !m.read; }).length;
  } catch (e) { return 0; }
}

function paintBell() {
  const n = unreadCount();
  const badge = document.getElementById('bell-count');
  badge.textContent = n > 9 ? '9+' : (n ? String(n) : '');
  badge.hidden = n === 0;
}

document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (document.visibilityState === 'visible') paintBell();
});
paintBell();
```

Show a message's picture and its buttons (only when you designed it with them), with the time it arrived:

```js
function renderCard(m) {
  const card = document.createElement('article');
  if (m.accent) card.style.borderLeft = '4px solid ' + m.accent;
  if (m.imageUrl) {
    const img = document.createElement('img');
    img.src = m.imageUrl; img.alt = '';
    card.appendChild(img);
  }
  const h = document.createElement('h3');
  h.textContent = m.title;
  const p = document.createElement('p');
  p.textContent = m.body;
  const time = document.createElement('time');
  time.textContent = new Date(m.receivedAt).toLocaleString();
  card.append(h, p, time);
  (m.buttons || []).forEach(function (b) {
    const btn = document.createElement('button');
    btn.textContent = b.label;
    btn.onclick = function () { WebToApk.markPushRead(m.id); if (b.link) location.href = b.link; };
    card.appendChild(btn);
  });
  return card;
}

if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getPushInbox) {
  const list = document.getElementById('inbox');
  JSON.parse(WebToApk.getPushInbox() || '[]').forEach(function (m) { list.appendChild(renderCard(m)); });
}
```

**Notes:** the inbox is kept on the phone, so read it when your screen opens - events only arrive while the app is on screen. A message you retract from AppMint disappears from the inbox and the tray. Messages sent as "push only" (tray) are not added to the inbox. The same detail is also passed to `window.onAppMintPush(detail)` if you define it.

### `getPushTags`

```js
window.WebToApk.getPushTags(): String
```

This install's tags as a JSON object string, e.g. {"plan":"pro"}.

**Example**

Reads this install's AppMint Push tags.

**Returns:** a JSON **string**, synchronously - an object of text values, e.g. `'{"plan":"pro","cart":"open"}'`; `'{}'` when there are none. Parse it. **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build.

**Read one tag:**

```js
function pushTags() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getPushTags)) return {};
  try { return JSON.parse(WebToApk.getPushTags() || '{}'); } catch (e) { return {}; }
}

const plan = pushTags().plan || 'free';
```

**Set a tag only when it changes** - every `setPushTag` call makes the install check in with AppMint Push, so skip the ones that change nothing:

```js
function ensureTag(key, value) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getPushTags)) return;
  const tags = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getPushTags() || '{}');
  if ((tags[key] || '') !== value) WebToApk.setPushTag(key, value);
}

ensureTag('plan', user.isPro ? 'pro' : 'free');
```

**List them on a debug screen** while you test sending to a tag:

```js
const list = document.getElementById('push-tags');
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getPushTags) {
  const tags = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getPushTags() || '{}');
  list.textContent = Object.keys(tags).length
    ? Object.keys(tags).map(function (k) { return k + ' = ' + tags[k]; }).join('\n')
    : 'No tags yet';
}
```

**Notes:** this is what the phone holds; the send center sees it after the install's next check-in, a few seconds after a change when the phone is online.

### `getPushUser`

```js
window.WebToApk.getPushUser(): String
```

The user id last set with setPushUser ("" when signed out or never set).

**Example**

Reads the user id this install last gave AppMint Push with `setPushUser`.

**Returns:** a `string`, synchronously - the saved id, or `''` when nobody is signed in or it was never set. **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build.

**Set the id only when it changed** (on every app start):

```js
function syncPushUser(currentUserId) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getPushUser)) return;
  const want = currentUserId || '';
  if (WebToApk.getPushUser() !== want) WebToApk.setPushUser(want);
}

syncPushUser(localStorage.getItem('userId'));
```

**Clear a stale id** when your own session expired while the app was closed:

```js
async function checkSession() {
  const session = await myBackend.currentSession();       // null when expired
  if (!session && window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getPushUser && WebToApk.getPushUser() !== '') {
    WebToApk.setPushUser('');                              // stop personal messages to this phone
  }
}

checkSession();
```

**Show it on a debug screen** while you test sending to one user:

```js
const info = document.getElementById('push-debug');
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getPushUser) {
  const id = WebToApk.getPushUser();
  info.textContent = id ? 'Push user: ' + id : 'Push user: nobody signed in';
} else {
  info.textContent = 'Not inside the app';
}
```

**Notes:** this is what the phone holds. The send center sees a change after the install's next check-in, a few seconds later when the phone is online.

### `markPushRead`

```js
window.WebToApk.markPushRead(id: String): Boolean
```

Marks one push message read; pass "" to mark every message read.

**Example**

Marks one push inbox message as read, or all of them when you pass `''`.

**Returns:** `true` if a message changed; `false` if nothing changed (unknown id, already read, or AppMint Push not enabled). **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build.

```js
function openMessage(id) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.markPushRead)) return;
  WebToApk.markPushRead(id);                 // one message
  updateBellCount();
}

document.getElementById('mark-all-read').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.markPushRead)) return;
  WebToApk.markPushRead('');                 // every message
  updateBellCount();
});

function updateBellCount() {
  const inbox = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getPushInbox() || '[]');
  const unread = inbox.filter(function (m) { return !m.read; }).length;
  document.getElementById('bell-count').textContent = unread ? String(unread) : '';
}
```

Mark a message read once the user has actually seen it on screen, not just when they tap it:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.markPushRead) {
  const seen = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
    entries.forEach(function (entry) {
      if (!entry.isIntersecting) return;
      const id = entry.target.dataset.msgId;
      seen.unobserve(entry.target);
      if (WebToApk.markPushRead(id)) {       // true only when it was unread
        entry.target.classList.replace('unread', 'read');
        updateBellCount();
      }
    });
  }, { threshold: 0.6 });

  document.querySelectorAll('#inbox li.unread').forEach(function (li) { seen.observe(li); });
}
```

Clear the badge when the inbox screen opens, and only redraw when something was actually unread:

```js
function openInboxScreen() {
  showScreen('inbox');
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.markPushRead)) return;
  const changed = WebToApk.markPushRead('');  // false: nothing was unread
  if (changed) {
    document.getElementById('bell-count').textContent = '';
    renderInbox();
  }
}
```

**Notes:** read state is stored only on this phone. It does not remove the tray notification.

### `notifyUser`

```js
window.WebToApk.notifyUser(callbackId: String, userId: String, optionsJson: String)
```

AppMint Push, user to user (2026-11-25): notifies every install of THIS app whose page called setPushUser(userId) - "new order" to the seller, "someone liked you" to the profile owner - with the app closed too, no creator server. optionsJson = {title, body?, url?, image?, data?}. Resolves `window.__appmintReplies[callbackId]` with {ok:true, sent} or {ok:false, code} (NotifyUser); AppMint.notifyUser() is the promise wrapper. Only from the app's own origin; {code:"no_push"} in an app built without AppMint Push. Every call settles.

**Example**

> **Send a notification to one user (new order, new like, new message) - two ways:**
> - **Easy - no server:** call `AppMint.notifyUser('seller_7', { title, body })` from your page. AppMint sends it. Its daily limits count notifications SENT, not users or phones: your app can have any number of users and phones (Free: 300 sends a day for the whole app · Starter/Pro: 5,000 · Studio: unlimited).
> - **Advanced - your own server:** your Firebase Cloud Function sends to the user's push token with your own Firebase key. No limits from AppMint. Use this only if you already run a server.
>
> Both reach the user even when the app is closed, look the same, and can be used together. Apps built before AppMint 1.11.63 need a rebuild (Update the App) to get notifyUser.

The raw bridge behind `AppMint.notifyUser` - use `AppMint.notifyUser(userId, options)` (a Promise) unless you need the callback form. It notifies every phone of THIS app where the page called `setPushUser(userId)`, even while that app is closed.

**Arguments:** `callbackId` - a key in `window.__appmintReplies` whose function receives the answer; `userId` - the receiver's id as they set it with `setPushUser`; `optionsJson` - `JSON.stringify({ title, body?, url?, image?, data? })`.

**Returns (through the callback):** `{ ok: true, sent }` or `{ ok: false, code }` - `rate_limited` (with `limit`: `sender` | `receiver` | `app`), `no_push`, `bad_request`, `not_registered`, `no_credentials`, `foreign_origin`, `network`, `paused`, `unavailable`. Every call answers.

**Order → seller** (the receiver did `WebToApk.setPushUser('seller_7')` after sign-in):

```js
function notify(userId, options) {
  return new Promise(function (resolve) {
    if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.notifyUser)) return resolve({ ok: false, code: 'no_push' });
    const R = (window.__appmintReplies = window.__appmintReplies || {});
    const id = 'nu_' + Date.now() + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);
    R[id] = resolve;
    WebToApk.notifyUser(id, userId, JSON.stringify(options));
  });
}

notify('seller_7', { title: 'New order #42 · ₹450', body: '2 x Pizza', url: '#/orders/42' })
  .then(function (r) { if (!r.ok) console.warn('not sent', r.code); });
```

**Like → profile owner:**

```js
notify(profile.ownerId, { title: 'Someone liked your profile', url: '#/likes' })
  .then(function (r) {
    if (!r.ok && r.code === 'rate_limited') return;   // the like is saved anyway; skip the notification
  });
```

**Message → receiver, with data for the receiver's page:**

```js
notify(chat.otherUserId, {
  title: me.name + ': ' + text.slice(0, 80),
  url: '#/chat/' + chat.id,
  data: { chatId: chat.id },
});

// On the receiver's side, while the app is open:
window.addEventListener('appmint:push', function (e) {
  const m = e.detail && e.detail.message;
  if (m && m.data && m.data.chatId) refreshChat(m.data.chatId);
});
```

**Daily limits** (midnight UTC), by the app creator's AppMint Cloud plan: Free - up to 50 notifications sent from one phone, 100 received by one user and 300 sent by the whole app per day; Starter and Pro - 200 / 500 / 5,000; Studio - no limit. **Rules:** title up to 100 characters, body up to 500, url up to 500, image `https://` only, data up to 10 short text values. **Needs:** AppMint Push turned on when you build (Integrate step) and the Firebase key added in AppMint's Notifications screen; AppMint 1.11.63 and newer. Only the app's own pages can call it.

**What the limits mean:** they count how many notifyUser notifications are sent per day. They never limit how many people use your app, how many phones receive notifications, or how many phones one user has (a user signed in on several phones gets it on each, up to 10). Example: a Free shop app with 50,000 users can send up to 300 "new order" alerts a day. Messages you send from AppMint's Notifications screen (to everyone, a tag or one user) and from your own server are not counted. When a limit is reached, notifyUser answers `{ ok:false, code:'rate_limited' }` until midnight UTC; upgrade the plan to raise it.

### `restorePushMessage`

```js
window.WebToApk.restorePushMessage(id: String): Boolean
```

Undo a dismiss: puts the message back in its place in the inbox.

**Example**

Undoes `dismissPushMessage(id)`: the message comes back to the push inbox in its old place.

**Returns:** `true` if the message was restored; `false` if the id is unknown or it was not hidden. **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build.

```js
let lastDismissed = null;

function onSwipe(id) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.dismissPushMessage)) return;
  if (WebToApk.dismissPushMessage(id)) {
    lastDismissed = id;
    showUndo();
    renderInbox();
  }
}

document.getElementById('undo-btn').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!lastDismissed || !window.WebToApk) return;
  if (WebToApk.restorePushMessage(lastDismissed)) renderInbox();
  lastDismissed = null;
});
```

Undo several swipes at once: remember every message hidden on this screen and bring them all back:

```js
const hiddenThisVisit = [];

function hide(id) {
  if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.dismissPushMessage(id)) {
    hiddenThisVisit.push(id);
    document.getElementById('undo-all').hidden = false;
    renderInbox();
  }
}

document.getElementById('undo-all').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.restorePushMessage)) return;
  hiddenThisVisit.splice(0).forEach(function (id) { WebToApk.restorePushMessage(id); });
  this.hidden = true;
  renderInbox();
});
```

Offer a "Recently hidden" list the user can restore from later. `getPushInbox()` does not return hidden messages, so keep their ids and titles yourself:

```js
function loadHidden() {
  try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('hiddenMsgs') || '[]'); } catch (e) { return []; }
}

function renderHidden() {
  const ul = document.getElementById('recently-hidden');
  ul.innerHTML = '';
  loadHidden().forEach(function (h) {
    const li = document.createElement('li');
    li.textContent = h.title + ' ';
    const btn = document.createElement('button');
    btn.textContent = 'Restore';
    btn.onclick = function () {
      WebToApk.restorePushMessage(h.id);     // false: retracted, cleared or already back
      const rest = loadHidden().filter(function (x) { return x.id !== h.id; });
      try { localStorage.setItem('hiddenMsgs', JSON.stringify(rest)); } catch (e) {}
      renderHidden();
      renderInbox();
    };
    li.appendChild(btn);
    ul.appendChild(li);
  });
}
```

**Notes:** a message cleared with `clearPushInbox()` or retracted by you from AppMint cannot be restored.

### `setInAppPresentation`

```js
window.WebToApk.setInAppPresentation(mode: String): Boolean
```

In-app message presentation: "auto" (default) lets the shell draw the creator's design; "none" (persisted) hands each message to the page as `appmint:inapp` {type:'shown', presented:false, message} to draw itself.

**Example**

Chooses who draws an in-app message (a campaign from the AppMint Push send center) when its trigger happens: the app (`'auto'`, the default: the creator's banner, centre card, bottom sheet or full-screen design) or your own page (`'none'`).

**Returns:** `true` when the mode was saved (it stays on the phone until changed); `false` for any other value and in an app built without AppMint Push. **Needs:** **AppMint Push** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build.

Every in-app message raises the `appmint:inapp` event (and calls `window.onAppMintInApp(detail)` if you defined it) with `type` `'shown'`, `'clicked'`, `'dismissed'` or `'answered'` (a star or 0-10 score answer, with `question` and `value`):

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:inapp', function (e) {
  var d = e.detail;   // { type, id, name, template?, presented?, message?, button?, link?, question?, value? }
  if (d.type === 'shown') analytics('inapp_shown', d.name);
  if (d.type === 'clicked') analytics('inapp_clicked', d.name + ' #' + d.button);
  if (d.type === 'dismissed') analytics('inapp_closed', d.name);
  if (d.type === 'answered') analytics('inapp_answer', d.name + ' ' + d.question + '=' + d.value);
});
```

Draw the messages yourself; the app hands each one over instead of showing it:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.setInAppPresentation) WebToApk.setInAppPresentation('none');

window.onAppMintInApp = function (d) {
  if (d.type !== 'shown' || d.presented) return;   // presented = the app already drew it
  var m = d.message;                                // { title, body, imageUrl, link, inapp, accent?, buttons?, emoji?, question?, lines? }
  showMyDialog(m.title, m.body, (m.buttons || []).map(function (b) {
    return { label: b.label, onClick: function () { if (b.link) location.href = b.link; } };
  }));
};
```

Give the choice back to the app (for example from a settings switch):

```js
document.getElementById('native-popups').addEventListener('change', function (e) {
  if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.setInAppPresentation) {
    WebToApk.setInAppPresentation(e.target.checked ? 'auto' : 'none');
  }
});
```

**Notes:** with `'none'` a message still counts as shown (its frequency limits apply) the moment it is handed to the page. Setting `'none'` also closes a message the app is showing now. Push messages have their own switch, `setPushPresentation`.

### `setOneSignalUser`

```js
window.WebToApk.setOneSignalUser(id: String): Boolean
```

OneSignal builds: links this install to YOUR user id (OneSignal's external_id, the same as OneSignal.login(id) on the web SDK), so the OneSignal dashboard / REST API can send to that one user. "" signs out (OneSignal.logout()). Support 2026-11: three creators asked; the page had no way to do it. Up to 128 characters, no control characters. Returns false in an app built without OneSignal, or from a page outside the app's own origin. A call made before OneSignal has started is applied once it has.

**Example**

Links this install to YOUR user in OneSignal (OneSignal's External ID, the same as `OneSignal.login(id)` in OneSignal's own SDKs), so the OneSignal dashboard or REST API can send a notification to that one user on every phone they use. Call it after sign-in; call it with `''` on sign-out (`OneSignal.logout()`).

**Returns:** `true` when the id was accepted (applied at once, or as soon as OneSignal has started if the page calls it earlier); `false` in an app built without OneSignal, for an id over 128 characters or with control characters, or from a page outside your app's own site. **Needs:** turn on **OneSignal** in the Integrate step (Step 3) with your OneSignal App ID when you build. Apps built before this method existed do not have it: rebuild.

**After sign-in and on sign-out** - use your database id (a Firebase uid, a Supabase user id):

```js
function oneSignalUser(id) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setOneSignalUser)) return false;   // browser, or an older build
  return WebToApk.setOneSignalUser(id);
}

async function signIn(email, password) {
  const user = await myBackend.signIn(email, password);
  oneSignalUser(user.id);
}

async function signOut() {
  await myBackend.signOut();
  oneSignalUser('');                       // this phone no longer gets that user's notifications
}
```

**Firebase Auth:** follow the auth state, so a restored session counts as well as a fresh sign-in:

```js
firebase.auth().onAuthStateChanged(function (user) {
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setOneSignalUser) {
    WebToApk.setOneSignalUser(user ? user.uid : '');
  }
});
```

**Send to that user from your server** with OneSignal's REST API (your OneSignal REST API key stays on your server, never in the page):

```js
// Node.js, on YOUR server
await fetch('https://api.onesignal.com/notifications?c=push', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: 'Key ' + process.env.ONESIGNAL_REST_KEY },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    app_id: process.env.ONESIGNAL_APP_ID,
    include_aliases: { external_id: ['u_42'] },
    target_channel: 'push',
    headings: { en: 'New order' },
    contents: { en: 'Order #1042 is waiting for you' }
  })
});
```

**Notes:** A user signed in on two phones gets the message on both. Use AppMint Push's `setPushUser` instead when the app is built with AppMint Push rather than OneSignal.

### `setPushPresentation`

```js
window.WebToApk.setPushPresentation(mode: String): Boolean
```

Native in-app presentation of push messages: "auto" (default) lets the shell draw the banner / modal / sheet / full-screen card the creator chose while the app is open; "none" turns it off for good (persisted) - for apps that draw their own. The `appmint:push` event and the inbox are unaffected either way; the received event's `presented` flag says whether the shell showed it.

**Example**

Turns the app's own on-screen display of AppMint Push messages on (`'auto'`, the default) or off (`'none'`) - for apps that draw their own banner from the `appmint:push` event.

**Returns:** `true` when the mode was saved; `false` for any value other than `'auto'` or `'none'`. The choice is saved on the phone and stays until changed. **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build.

**Draw your own banner** instead of the shell's:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushPresentation) {
  WebToApk.setPushPresentation('none');       // 'auto' to give it back to the shell
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:push', function (e) {
  const d = e.detail;
  // { type: 'received', message: {...}, presented: false } — presented = the shell already showed it
  if (d.type === 'received' && !d.presented) showMyBanner(d.message.title, d.message.body, d.message.link);
  if (d.type === 'revoked') hideMyBanner(d.id);
});
```

Let the user switch pop-ups off in your settings screen. There is no getter, so keep your own copy of the choice to draw the switch:

```js
const toggle = document.getElementById('show-popups');
let saved = null;
try { saved = localStorage.getItem('pushPopups'); } catch (e) {}
toggle.checked = saved !== 'none';

toggle.addEventListener('change', function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushPresentation)) return;
  const mode = toggle.checked ? 'auto' : 'none';
  if (WebToApk.setPushPresentation(mode)) {
    try { localStorage.setItem('pushPopups', mode); } catch (e) {}
  }
});
```

With `'auto'`, find out what the user did with a message the app showed on screen: `opened` when they tapped it (`action` is `-1` for the message itself, else the button index), `closed` when they dismissed it without tapping:

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:push', function (e) {
  const d = e.detail;
  if (d.type === 'opened') {
    // the message is already marked read in the inbox
    track('push_opened', { id: d.id, button: d.action, link: d.link });
    updateBellCount();
  } else if (d.type === 'closed') {
    track('push_closed', { id: d.id });
  }
});
```

**Notes:** with `'auto'`, a message you sent with an in-app style is shown over the app while it is open (and then not also put in the tray). With `'none'` the shell never draws it; the inbox (`getPushInbox`) and the `appmint:push` event work the same either way. Setting `'none'` also closes a message the shell is showing now.

### `setPushTag`

```js
window.WebToApk.setPushTag(key: String, value: String): Boolean
```

Sets one AppMint Push tag (key: letters, digits, _ up to 32; value up to 128) - the send center can target "plan = pro", and an automation can fire a set time after a tag is set (an abandoned cart: set cart=open, clear it at checkout). An empty value removes the tag. Up to 50 tags per install.

**Example**

Sets one AppMint Push tag on this install, such as `plan = pro` or `city = pune`. The send center (Home > Notifications) can send to everyone with a tag, and a tag automation can send a message a set time after a tag is set - an abandoned cart, a finished level. An empty value removes the tag.

**Returns:** `true` when saved; `false` when the key is not 1-32 letters, digits or `_`, the value is longer than 128 characters, or the install would have more than 50 tags (nothing is saved then). Tags are kept on the phone and reported to AppMint Push a moment later (or on the next launch when offline). **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build. Tag targeting and automations reach phones running an app built with AppMint from 30 Sep 2026 on.

**Tag what the user bought or chose**, so you can send to "plan = pro" only:

```js
function pushTag(key, value) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushTag)) return false;
  return WebToApk.setPushTag(key, value);
}

pushTag('plan', user.isPro ? 'pro' : 'free');
pushTag('city', user.city.toLowerCase());
```

**Abandoned cart:** set a tag when items are in the cart and clear it at checkout. In the send center, add a tag automation on `cart` with a delay (say 60 minutes); a phone gets the reminder only if `cart` is still set when the time is up:

```js
function onCartChanged(items) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushTag)) return;
  // Setting 'open' again while it is already 'open' does not restart the automation's clock.
  WebToApk.setPushTag('cart', items.length > 0 ? 'open' : '');
}

function onCheckoutComplete() {
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushTag) WebToApk.setPushTag('cart', '');   // bought: no reminder
}
```

**Clear user-specific tags on sign-out**, together with the user id:

```js
function signOutOfPush() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushUser)) return;
  WebToApk.setPushUser('');
  WebToApk.setPushTag('plan', '');
  WebToApk.setPushTag('cart', '');
}
```

**Notes:** tags belong to this install, not to the signed-in user. Setting a tag to the value it already has changes nothing on the server. After a tag is removed, setting it again lets a tag automation send once more. Never put an email address, phone number or anything private in a tag.

### `setPushTags`

```js
window.WebToApk.setPushTags(json: String): Boolean
```

Sets several tags at once from a JSON object string; "" values remove.

**Example**

Sets several AppMint Push tags at once from a JSON object string, e.g. `'{"plan":"pro","team":"red"}'`. A `""` value removes that tag; tags you do not name are kept.

**Returns:** `true` when saved; `false` when the string is not a JSON object, any key is not 1-32 letters, digits or `_`, any value is longer than 128 characters, or the install would end up with more than 50 tags - then nothing at all is saved. **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build. Tag targeting and automations reach phones running an app built with AppMint from 30 Sep 2026 on.

**After sign-in, tag the profile in one call:**

```js
function tagProfile(profile) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushTags)) return false;
  return WebToApk.setPushTags(JSON.stringify({
    plan: profile.plan,                   // 'free' | 'pro'
    level: String(profile.level),         // values are text: turn numbers into strings
    team: profile.team || ''              // '' removes the tag
  }));
}
```

**On sign-out, remove them all** (read the current tags, send each back as `''`):

```js
function clearPushTags() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getPushTags)) return;
  const tags = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getPushTags() || '{}');
  Object.keys(tags).forEach(function (k) { tags[k] = ''; });
  WebToApk.setPushTags(JSON.stringify(tags));
  WebToApk.setPushUser('');
}
```

**Finished a level:** tag it, and let a tag automation on `level_done` (say 10 minutes) send the next challenge:

```js
function onLevelComplete(level, score) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushTags)) return;
  WebToApk.setPushTags(JSON.stringify({
    level_done: String(level),            // a new value each level, so the automation can fire again
    last_score: String(score)
  }));
}
```

**Notes:** one call is one change: all of it is saved or none of it. The install reports the new tags to AppMint Push a moment later (or on the next launch when offline).

### `setPushUser`

```js
window.WebToApk.setPushUser(id: String): Boolean
```

AppMint Push audience: tells the creator's send center WHO this install is, so a message can go to one signed-in user ("u_42") or to everyone with a tag. Call it after sign-in with your own stable account id; pass "" on sign-out. Letters, digits and _ @ . : + - (up to 128). Returns false for anything else, and in an app that does not use AppMint Push (OneSignal / own Firebase: nothing is sent, 2026-10-03). Never pass an email address or phone number - use your database id.

**Example**

> **Send a notification to one user (new order, new like, new message) - two ways:**
> - **Easy - no server:** call `AppMint.notifyUser('seller_7', { title, body })` from your page. AppMint sends it. Its daily limits count notifications SENT, not users or phones: your app can have any number of users and phones (Free: 300 sends a day for the whole app · Starter/Pro: 5,000 · Studio: unlimited).
> - **Advanced - your own server:** your Firebase Cloud Function sends to the user's push token with your own Firebase key. No limits from AppMint. Use this only if you already run a server.
>
> Both reach the user even when the app is closed, look the same, and can be used together. Apps built before AppMint 1.11.63 need a rebuild (Update the App) to get notifyUser. For the easy way, the receiver's phone first says who is signed in, with `setPushUser` below.

Tells AppMint Push which of YOUR users is signed in on this phone, so the send center (Home > Notifications) can send a message to that one user - and so `AppMint.notifyUser(id, …)` from another user's phone reaches it. Call it after sign-in with your own stable account id; call it with `''` on sign-out.

**Returns:** `true` when the id was saved; `false` for an id with anything other than letters, digits and `_ @ . : + -`, or longer than 128 characters (nothing is saved then). The id is kept on the phone until you change it, and this install reports it to AppMint Push a moment later (or on the next launch when it is offline). **Needs:** turn on **AppMint Push** in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build. Sending to a user reaches phones running an app built with AppMint from 30 Sep 2026 on; older builds still get messages sent to Everyone.

**After sign-in and on sign-out** - use your database id, never an email address or phone number:

```js
function pushUser(id) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushUser)) return false;   // browser, or an older build
  return WebToApk.setPushUser(id);
}

async function signIn(email, password) {
  const user = await myBackend.signIn(email, password);   // your own sign-in
  pushUser(user.id);                                      // e.g. 'u_42' or a UUID
}

async function signOut() {
  await myBackend.signOut();
  pushUser('');                                           // this phone is nobody's now
}
```

**Supabase:** follow the session, so a restored session counts as well as a fresh sign-in:

```js
supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange(function (event, session) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushUser)) return;
  const id = session ? session.user.id : '';     // the auth UUID: letters, digits and '-'
  if (WebToApk.getPushUser() !== id) WebToApk.setPushUser(id);
});
```

**Make an id acceptable** when yours may contain other characters (spaces, `/`, `#`), and log the rare one that is still refused:

```js
function pushUserIdFrom(rawId) {
  return String(rawId).trim().replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9_@.:+\-]/g, '_').slice(0, 128);
}

if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setPushUser) {
  const ok = WebToApk.setPushUser(pushUserIdFrom(currentUser.id));
  if (!ok) console.warn('push user id refused', currentUser.id);
}
```

**Notes:** the same user signed in on two phones is reached on both. The id belongs to this install, not to the account - sign-out must clear it, or the phone keeps receiving the previous user's messages. `setPushUser('')` does not clear tags set with `setPushTag`; clear user-specific tags on sign-out too.

### `trackEvent`

```js
window.WebToApk.trackEvent(name: String, propsJson: String): Boolean
```

In-app messages: reports an event the creator's campaigns can trigger on ("event" trigger, same name). propsJson is optional JSON. The name `appmint:route` with {"path":"/x"} reports a view change the URL does not show. False for a name outside [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}, and without AppMint Push.

**Example**

Tells the app that something happened ("signed_up", "checkout_done", "level:3"). An in-app message the creator made in the AppMint Push send center with the trigger **"When an event happens"** and the same name shows now (or after the wait the creator picked).

**Returns:** `true` when the event was taken; `false` for a name outside letters, digits and `_ . : -` (up to 64), and in an app built without AppMint Push. `AppMint.trackEvent(name, props)` is the same call with `props` as an object. **Needs:** **AppMint Push** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build. `propsJson` is optional (`''`) and is not stored.

```js
// After a purchase: the creator's "Thanks, rate us?" message is set to trigger on "purchase_done".
function onPurchaseDone(order) {
  if (window.AppMint && AppMint.trackEvent) {
    AppMint.trackEvent('purchase_done', { total: order.total });
  }
}
```

The raw bridge takes the props as a JSON string (pass `''` for none):

```js
function track(name, props) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.trackEvent)) return false;   // a browser: nothing to show
  return WebToApk.trackEvent(name, props ? JSON.stringify(props) : '');
}
track('level:3');
track('tutorial_skipped', { step: 2 });
```

A screen change the address does not show (tabs, a wizard, a modal "page") can be reported as a route, so the creator's **"On a page"** messages see it. The page can also dispatch the `appmint:route` event with the path; the app listens for it:

```js
function showTab(name) {
  document.querySelectorAll('.tab').forEach(function (t) { t.hidden = t.id !== name; });
  if (window.AppMint && AppMint.trackEvent) AppMint.trackEvent('appmint:route', { path: '/' + name });
}

// Same thing, without touching the bridge at all:
window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('appmint:route', { detail: { path: '/cart' } }));
```

**Notes:** route messages already follow real URL changes (page loads, `history.pushState`, `#/hash` routes) on their own; report a route only for views the address does not change. Events are not counted or stored anywhere; they only decide whether a message shows.
