### `enterPip`

```js
window.WebToApk.enterPip(): Boolean
```

Shrinks the whole app into a floating picture-in-picture window right now - a video or a call the user wants to keep watching while they leave. Android 8+ and only when the build enabled PiP (the manifest flag it needs); returns whether the window opened. Leaving the app with PiP enabled does this by itself; this is the explicit "minimise" button.

**Example**

Shrinks the whole app into a small floating picture-in-picture window right now - a "minimise" button for a video or a call.

**Returns:** `true` if the floating window opened, `false` otherwise (synchronously). **Needs:** **Picture-in-Picture (PiP)** switched on in Step 3 (Integrate), under **Display Options**, when you build. Android 8+.

```js
var pipBtn = document.getElementById('pip-btn');
pipBtn.onclick = function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.enterPip === 'function')) return;
  var ok = window.WebToApk.enterPip();
  if (!ok) pipBtn.hidden = true;   // PiP not enabled in this build, or Android 7 and older
};
```

Make the page fit the small window: the window gets very narrow, so a `resize` listener can hide everything but the video.

```js
window.addEventListener('resize', function () {
  var small = window.innerWidth < 300;
  document.querySelector('nav').style.display = small ? 'none' : '';
});
```

Follow the floating window opening and closing with the `appmint:pip` event (`detail.inPip`), for example to hide a call's controls:

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:pip', function (e) {
  var inPip = !!(e.detail && e.detail.inPip);
  document.body.classList.toggle('pip', inPip);   // CSS: .pip .call-controls { display: none; }
  if (!inPip) {
    document.getElementById('chat-panel').hidden = false;   // back to the full-size screen
  }
});

document.getElementById('minimise').onclick = function () {
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.enterPip === 'function') {
    document.getElementById('chat-panel').hidden = true;
    window.WebToApk.enterPip();
  }
};
```

**Notes:** With PiP enabled, pressing Home already enters the floating window by itself; this method is only for an explicit button. It returns `false` in a build without the PiP switch, because the manifest flag it needs is missing. The PiP window size is chosen by Android. AI-built apps can use `pip` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `isFullscreen`

```js
window.WebToApk.isFullscreen(): Boolean
```

Lets the page hide the status bar (clock/battery) and navigation bar itself - e.g. a game entering its play screen:     WebToApk.setFullscreen(true)   // hide the system bars     WebToApk.setFullscreen(false)  // bring them back     WebToApk.toggleFullscreen()     WebToApk.isFullscreen() The choice is remembered across launches. It is a no-op in apps the creator already locked to fullscreen/kiosk - there is nothing to restore to there. The side-menu "Fullscreen" item is the equivalent for end users and is gated by the creator's enableFullscreenToggle option; this bridge is always available to the app's own page.

_Described by its group, Fullscreen bridge, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Tells you whether the Android status and navigation bars are hidden right now.

**Returns:** `true` / `false`, synchronously. **Needs:** nothing.

```js
function barsHidden() {
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.isFullscreen === 'function') {
    return window.WebToApk.isFullscreen();
  }
  return false;   // in a browser
}

if (barsHidden()) {
  document.getElementById('fs-btn').textContent = 'Exit fullscreen';
}
```

Lay the page out for the remembered choice on start, since it survives restarts:

```js
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
  var hidden = !!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.isFullscreen === 'function' &&
                  window.WebToApk.isFullscreen());
  document.documentElement.classList.toggle('bars-hidden', hidden);
  // CSS: .bars-hidden header { padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top); }
});
```

Drop a "show bars" button when the app was built fullscreen and the bars cannot come back:

```js
function showBars() {
  var W = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(W && typeof W.isFullscreen === 'function')) return;
  W.setFullscreen(false);
  setTimeout(function () {             // the change is applied on the UI thread
    if (W.isFullscreen()) {
      document.getElementById('bars-btn').hidden = true;
    }
  }, 100);
}
```

**Notes:** It returns `true` when the creator built the app with **Fullscreen** or **Immersive Kiosk Mode**, OR when the page called `setFullscreen(true)` / `toggleFullscreen()`. In the first case `setFullscreen(false)` cannot bring the bars back.

### `isSecureScreen`

```js
window.WebToApk.isSecureScreen(): Boolean
```

WebToApk.setSecureScreen(true)   // block screenshots on THIS page   WebToApk.setSecureScreen(false)  // release it early   WebToApk.isSecureScreen()        // -> boolean  Protection belongs to the page that asked for it. It is released the moment the app navigates anywhere else - a new document, a pushState route, a #hash route - so a protected screen cannot leave the rest of the app locked down, and a page that wants protection back after a reload simply asks again.  What it does: screenshots, screen recording, casting and the recents-screen thumbnail all stop while it is on. What it cannot do: stop a camera pointed at the screen. Nothing on Android can, and no bridge here will pretend otherwise.

_Described by its group, Screen-capture protection, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Tells you whether screenshot protection (`setSecureScreen`) is on right now.

**Returns:** a boolean, at once. **Needs:** nothing.

```js
function updateLockIcon() {
  var on = !!window.WebToApk &&
    typeof window.WebToApk.isSecureScreen === 'function' &&
    window.WebToApk.isSecureScreen();
  document.getElementById('shield').hidden = !on;
}
```

Check before showing a card number, and turn protection on first if this page has not asked for it yet:

```js
function revealCardNumber(full) {
  var W = window.WebToApk;
  if (W && typeof W.isSecureScreen === 'function' && !W.isSecureScreen()) {
    W.setSecureScreen(true);   // the new state is committed when this returns
  }
  document.getElementById('card-number').textContent = full;
}
```

A "Hide from screenshots" switch that starts from the real state and flips it:

```js
var toggle = document.getElementById('privacy-toggle');
var W = window.WebToApk;

if (!W || typeof W.isSecureScreen !== 'function') {
  toggle.hidden = true;
} else {
  toggle.checked = W.isSecureScreen();
  toggle.addEventListener('change', function () {
    toggle.checked = W.setSecureScreen(!W.isSecureScreen());
  });
}
```

**Notes:** It goes back to `false` by itself when the app navigates to another page or route, because protection belongs to the page that asked for it.

### `setFullscreen`

```js
window.WebToApk.setFullscreen(enabled: Boolean)
```

Lets the page hide the status bar (clock/battery) and navigation bar itself - e.g. a game entering its play screen:     WebToApk.setFullscreen(true)   // hide the system bars     WebToApk.setFullscreen(false)  // bring them back     WebToApk.toggleFullscreen()     WebToApk.isFullscreen() The choice is remembered across launches. It is a no-op in apps the creator already locked to fullscreen/kiosk - there is nothing to restore to there. The side-menu "Fullscreen" item is the equivalent for end users and is gated by the creator's enableFullscreenToggle option; this bridge is always available to the app's own page.

_Described by its group, Fullscreen bridge, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Hides (`true`) or shows (`false`) the Android status bar and navigation bar, for example when a game enters its play screen.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing - it is always available to your page. The choice is remembered across launches.

```js
function enterPlayScreen() {
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.setFullscreen === 'function') {
    window.WebToApk.setFullscreen(true);    // hide clock/battery and the nav bar
  }
}
function leavePlayScreen() {
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setFullscreen) {
    window.WebToApk.setFullscreen(false);   // bring the bars back
  }
}
```

Keep your content out from under the camera cut-out when the bars are hidden:

```js
document.body.style.paddingTop = 'env(safe-area-inset-top)';
document.body.style.paddingBottom = 'env(safe-area-inset-bottom)';
```

Hide the bars while a video plays and bring them back when it pauses or ends:

```js
var video = document.getElementById('movie');

function hideBars(hidden) {
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.setFullscreen === 'function') {
    window.WebToApk.setFullscreen(hidden);
  }
}

video.addEventListener('play', function () { hideBars(true); });
video.addEventListener('pause', function () { hideBars(false); });
video.addEventListener('ended', function () { hideBars(false); });
```

**Notes:** It does nothing in an app built with **Fullscreen** (or **Immersive Kiosk Mode**) switched on in Step 3 (Integrate) - the creator locked that choice. It only hides the Android bars; the app's own top bar (the one with the side-menu button) is the **Show Top Bar** switch. When turned on, the shell adds `viewport-fit=cover` to your viewport meta so the page lays out into the full screen. See `toggleFullscreen` and `isFullscreen`. AI-built apps can use `fullscreen` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `setNavigationBarColor`

```js
window.WebToApk.setNavigationBarColor(color: String, style: String): Boolean
```

WebToApk.setNavigationBarColor('#FFFFFF', 'dark')   // bottom bar only Paints only the phone's bottom (navigation) bar; [color] and [style] as in [setStatusBarColor]. Holds for the rest of this document, a later setStatusBarColor included. Returns false when the colour does not parse.

**Example**

Paints the phone's bottom bar (the navigation bar with back and home) a colour and chooses light or dark icons on it. The status bar at the top is not changed.

**Returns:** `true`, or `false` when the colour cannot be parsed (synchronously). **Needs:** nothing.

`style` is `'light'` (light icons, for a dark bar), `'dark'` (dark icons, for a light bar), or `''` (the shell picks from the colour's brightness):

```js
function paintBottomBar(color, style) {
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.setNavigationBarColor === 'function') {
    return window.WebToApk.setNavigationBarColor(color, style);
  }
  return false;   // in a browser, or an app built before November 2026
}

paintBottomBar('#FFFFFF', 'dark');    // white bottom bar, dark icons
paintBottomBar('#0B0F1A', 'light');   // dark bottom bar, light icons
```

A different colour at the top and at the bottom, e.g. a coloured header over a white page:

```js
WebToApk.setStatusBarColor('#0E7C86', 'light');
WebToApk.setNavigationBarColor('#FFFFFF', 'dark');
```

Follow the phone's light or dark theme, including a switch while the app is open:

```js
var darkTheme = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)');

function matchTheme() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.setNavigationBarColor === 'function')) return;
  if (darkTheme.matches) {
    window.WebToApk.setNavigationBarColor('#121212', 'light');
  } else {
    window.WebToApk.setNavigationBarColor('#F5F5F5', 'dark');
  }
}

matchTheme();
darkTheme.addEventListener('change', matchTheme);
```

**Notes:** Exists in apps built with AppMint from November 2026. The colour holds until the next page loads, and a later `setStatusBarColor` on the same page leaves it alone (on its own, `setStatusBarColor` paints both bars). Without any call, the bottom bar takes the colour chosen in the app's settings (Bar colour → Bottom bar), which can differ in light and dark mode. Colours are Android colour strings: `#RRGGBB` or `#AARRGGBB` (and names like `red`). While the bars are hidden (fullscreen) the colour is kept for when they come back.

### `setSecureScreen`

```js
window.WebToApk.setSecureScreen(enabled: Boolean): Boolean
```

Sets protection for the CURRENT page and returns the state now in force. The window flag itself is applied on the UI thread, but the state this returns is already committed, so a page can call this and immediately reveal its sensitive content without waiting for a callback.

**Example**

Blocks screenshots, screen recording, casting and the recents-screen preview while the CURRENT page shows something private.

**Returns:** a boolean at once - the state now in force (the value you passed). You can reveal the private content right after the call. **Needs:** nothing.

```js
function showStatement() {
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.setSecureScreen === 'function') {
    window.WebToApk.setSecureScreen(true);
  }
  render(statementView);
}
```

Release it yourself only when you hide the private content WITHOUT navigating (a modal closes, a tab switches inside one page):

```js
function closeCardDetails() {
  hide(cardDetailsModal);
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.setSecureScreen === 'function') {
    window.WebToApk.setSecureScreen(false);
  }
}
```

Show a one-time recovery code only once capture is blocked, since the call answers with the state in force:

```js
function revealRecoveryCode(code) {
  var W = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(W && typeof W.setSecureScreen === 'function')) {
    alert('Open the app to see your recovery code.');
    return;
  }
  if (W.setSecureScreen(true)) {
    document.getElementById('recovery-code').textContent = code;
  }
}
```

**Notes:** Protection belongs to the page that asked. It is released as soon as the app navigates anywhere else - a new page, a `pushState` route or a `#hash` route - so there is nothing to clean up on the way out, and after a reload the page must ask again. Do not re-apply it on a timer: the flag must already be on when the user presses the screenshot buttons. Nothing can stop a camera pointed at the screen.

### `setStatusBarColor`

```js
window.WebToApk.setStatusBarColor(color: String, style: String): Boolean
```

Paints the status and navigation bars [color] and picks the icon tint: [style] 'light' means light icons on a dark bar, 'dark' the reverse, '' lets the luminance decide. [color] is `#RGB`, `#RGBA`, `#RRGGBB`, `#AARRGGBB` (alpha FIRST - CSS's `#RRGGBBAA` order is read as alpha-first too) or a basic colour name ('black', 'navy'…); `rgb()`/`hsl()` are not read. Returns false when the colour does not parse.

**Example**

Paints the Android status bar a colour and chooses light or dark icons on it.

**Returns:** `true`, or `false` when the colour cannot be parsed (synchronously). **Needs:** nothing.

`style` is `'light'` (light icons, for a dark bar), `'dark'` (dark icons, for a light bar), or `''` (the shell picks from the colour's brightness):

```js
function paintBar(color, style) {
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.setStatusBarColor === 'function') {
    return window.WebToApk.setStatusBarColor(color, style);
  }
  return false;   // in a browser
}

paintBar('#0B0F1A', 'light');   // dark bar, light icons
paintBar('#FFFFFF', 'dark');    // white bar, dark icons
paintBar('#0E7C86', '');        // icons chosen automatically
```

Match the bar to each screen:

```js
function showScreen(name) {
  var colors = { home: '#0B0F1A', settings: '#FFFFFF' };
  paintBar(colors[name] || '#0B0F1A', name === 'settings' ? 'dark' : 'light');
}
```

Follow the phone's light or dark theme, including a switch while the app is open:

```js
var darkTheme = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)');

function matchTheme() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.setStatusBarColor === 'function')) return;
  if (darkTheme.matches) {
    window.WebToApk.setStatusBarColor('#121212', 'light');
  } else {
    window.WebToApk.setStatusBarColor('#F5F5F5', 'dark');
  }
}

matchTheme();
darkTheme.addEventListener('change', matchTheme);
```

**Notes:** Colours are Android colour strings: `#RRGGBB` or `#AARRGGBB` (and names like `red`). CSS forms such as `rgb(...)` or `#RGB` return `false`. It works on Android 15+ too, where Capacitor's StatusBar plugin cannot paint the bar. While the bars are hidden (fullscreen) the colour is kept for when they come back. AI-built apps can use `setStatusBar` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `splashHold`

```js
window.WebToApk.splashHold()
```

Keeps the branded launch splash up until [splashReady] is called. By default the splash hides as soon as the body has laid-out children, which for an app that paints a skeleton and then fetches its first screen means "splash, then a skeleton". An app that would rather reveal a finished first screen calls this at import and [splashReady] once that screen is on. Capped at the same 6s backstop as the paint poll, so a page that never reports ready still opens.

**Example**

Keeps the app's launch splash on screen until you call `splashReady()` - so the user sees your finished first screen, not "splash, then a loading skeleton".

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing.

Call it as early as possible (at the top of your first script), then call `splashReady()` once the first screen is drawn:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.splashHold === 'function') {
  window.WebToApk.splashHold();
}

loadFirstScreen()                      // your own async start-up (fetch data, render)
  .catch(function (err) { showError(err); })
  .then(function () {
    if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.splashReady) window.WebToApk.splashReady();
  });
```

Hold the splash until the first screen's hero image has loaded, so the app opens on a finished picture:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.splashHold === 'function') {
  window.WebToApk.splashHold();
}

function releaseSplash() {
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.splashReady) window.WebToApk.splashReady();
}

var hero = document.getElementById('hero');
if (hero.complete) {
  releaseSplash();
} else {
  hero.addEventListener('load', releaseSplash);
  hero.addEventListener('error', releaseSplash);   // a broken image must not keep the splash up
}
```

Hold only when the first screen needs data, and let a screen that paints at once open normally:

```js
var signedIn = !!localStorage.getItem('session');

if (signedIn && window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.splashHold === 'function') {
  window.WebToApk.splashHold();        // the dashboard needs its data before it looks right
}

if (signedIn) {
  loadDashboard().finally(function () {
    if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.splashReady) window.WebToApk.splashReady();
  });
} else {
  showLoginScreen();                   // paints at once; the splash hides by itself
}
```

**Notes:** Without `splashHold()` the splash hides as soon as the page body has visible children. A held splash still hides by itself after a few seconds (the same backstop as the normal paint check), so a page that never calls `splashReady()` still opens. Always call `splashReady()` on the error path too. The creator's minimum splash time still applies. AI-built apps can use `splash` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `splashReady`

```js
window.WebToApk.splashReady()
```

The first screen is on - hide the launch splash now (subject to the creator's minimum splash duration). Idempotent; harmless when nothing was held.

**Example**

Tells the shell your first screen is on, so the launch splash hides now.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing. Safe to call more than once, and harmless when nothing was held.

It pairs with `splashHold()`:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.splashHold) window.WebToApk.splashHold();

async function start() {
  try {
    var res = await fetch('/api/today');
    renderToday(await res.json());
  } catch (e) {
    renderOfflineMessage();
  } finally {
    if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.splashReady === 'function') {
      window.WebToApk.splashReady();   // hide the splash in every case
    }
  }
}
start();
```

Reveal the screen only after the browser has painted what you just rendered (two animation frames):

```js
renderApp(document.getElementById('root'));

requestAnimationFrame(function () {
  requestAnimationFrame(function () {
    if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.splashReady === 'function') {
      window.WebToApk.splashReady();
    }
  });
});
```

Wait for several start-up jobs, and hide the splash even when one of them fails:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.splashHold) window.WebToApk.splashHold();

Promise.allSettled([
  loadProfile(),          // your own start-up requests
  loadFeed(),
  document.fonts.ready    // no flash of the wrong font
]).then(function (results) {
  results.forEach(function (r) { if (r.status === 'rejected') console.warn(r.reason); });
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.splashReady === 'function') {
    window.WebToApk.splashReady();
  }
});
```

**Notes:** The creator's minimum splash duration is still honoured. If you never call `splashHold()`, the splash hides on its own when the page paints, and `splashReady()` does nothing extra.

### `toggleFullscreen`

```js
window.WebToApk.toggleFullscreen()
```

Lets the page hide the status bar (clock/battery) and navigation bar itself - e.g. a game entering its play screen:     WebToApk.setFullscreen(true)   // hide the system bars     WebToApk.setFullscreen(false)  // bring them back     WebToApk.toggleFullscreen()     WebToApk.isFullscreen() The choice is remembered across launches. It is a no-op in apps the creator already locked to fullscreen/kiosk - there is nothing to restore to there. The side-menu "Fullscreen" item is the equivalent for end users and is gated by the creator's enableFullscreenToggle option; this bridge is always available to the app's own page.

_Described by its group, Fullscreen bridge, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Switches the Android status and navigation bars between hidden and shown.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing. The new state is remembered across launches.

A "fullscreen" button that also updates its own label:

```js
var btn = document.getElementById('fs-btn');
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.toggleFullscreen === 'function') {
  btn.onclick = function () {
    window.WebToApk.toggleFullscreen();
    // The change is applied on the UI thread; read the state a moment later.
    setTimeout(function () {
      btn.textContent = window.WebToApk.isFullscreen() ? 'Exit fullscreen' : 'Fullscreen';
    }, 100);
  };
} else {
  btn.hidden = true;   // in a browser
}
```

Double-tap a photo or a reading view to hide or show the bars:

```js
var viewer = document.getElementById('photo-viewer');

viewer.addEventListener('dblclick', function () {
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.toggleFullscreen === 'function') {
    window.WebToApk.toggleFullscreen();
  }
});
```

Toggle with the F key on a hardware keyboard, but not while the user types in a field:

```js
document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
  if (e.key !== 'f' || e.target.closest('input, textarea, [contenteditable]')) return;
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.toggleFullscreen === 'function') {
    e.preventDefault();
    window.WebToApk.toggleFullscreen();
  }
});
```

**Notes:** It does nothing in an app built with **Fullscreen** or **Immersive Kiosk Mode** on (the bars stay hidden). The side-menu "Fullscreen" item for end users is a separate build switch (**Fullscreen Button** in Step 3, under **Display Options**); this bridge method works without it.

# Share, clipboard and print - JavaScript bridge API

> The Android share sheet, the system clipboard, text another app shared into yours, and the print dialogue.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/share

### `AppMint.pdf`

```js
AppMint.pdf.fromPage(options) / fromHtml(html, options)
```

**Example**

Makes a real PDF (selectable text, vector graphics) with no print dialog: `fromPage` saves the page as it is on screen, laid out with your `@media print` CSS; `fromHtml` renders HTML you pass in an invisible page at the app's own address - so relative images, stylesheets and fonts load as in your page - waits for the fonts and every image, then saves it. `window.print()` still opens the normal print dialog.

**Returns:** a Promise of `{ok: true, fileName, pages, bytes, saved, uri?, base64?}` or `{ok: false, code, message}` - `code` is `busy` (one PDF at a time), `bad-options`, `failed`, `too-large` (base64 over 25 MB) or `permission-denied` (storage refused on Android 7-9). **Needs:** nothing - every build has it. Saving to Downloads needs no permission on Android 10+.

**Options:** `fileName` (".pdf" is added; default: the page title), `pageSize` `'A4'` (default) | `'Letter'` | `'Legal'` | `'A3'` | `'A5'`, `landscape` (`true`/`false`), `margins` in millimetres (one number, or `{top, right, bottom, left}`; left out = your own `@page` rule), `save` `'downloads'` (default) | `'share'` | `'base64'`.

**Save the current page to Downloads:**

```js
async function saveInvoice() {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.pdf)) { window.print(); return; }   // in a browser
  var r = await AppMint.pdf.fromPage({ fileName: 'invoice-1042', pageSize: 'A4', margins: 12 });
  if (r.ok) console.log('Saved ' + r.fileName + ' (' + r.pages + ' pages)');
  else alert('Could not make the PDF: ' + r.message);
}
```

**A receipt built from HTML, straight to the share sheet** (images and fonts are loaded before the PDF is made):

```js
async function shareReceipt(order) {
  var html = '<style>body{font-family:sans-serif} td{padding:4px 8px}</style>' +
    '<img src="img/logo.png" width="120"><h1>Receipt #' + order.id + '</h1><table>' +
    order.items.map(function (i) { return '<tr><td>' + i.name + '</td><td>' + i.price + '</td></tr>'; }).join('') +
    '</table><p><b>Total ' + order.total + '</b></p>';
  var r = await AppMint.pdf.fromHtml(html, { fileName: 'receipt-' + order.id, pageSize: 'Letter', save: 'share' });
  if (!r.ok) console.warn(r.code, r.message);
}
```

**Get the bytes back** to upload them yourself:

```js
async function uploadReport() {
  var r = await AppMint.pdf.fromPage({ landscape: true, margins: { top: 10, right: 8, bottom: 10, left: 8 }, save: 'base64' });
  if (!r.ok) return;
  var bin = atob(r.base64), buf = new Uint8Array(bin.length);
  for (var i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) buf[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
  await fetch('/api/reports', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/pdf' }, body: buf });
}
```

The raw calls take the options as JSON text and a callback id; use the helper above instead:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.pdfFromPage === 'function') {
  // AppMint.pdf.fromPage wraps: WebToApk.pdfFromPage(JSON.stringify(options), callbackId)
  // and AppMint.pdf.fromHtml wraps: WebToApk.pdfFromHtml(html, JSON.stringify(options), callbackId)
  AppMint.pdf.fromPage({ save: 'downloads' }).then(function (r) { console.log(r); });
}
```

**Notes:** Hide buttons and menus from the PDF with `@media print { .no-print { display: none } }`. A downloaded PDF shows "Downloaded <name> · Open" like any download. `fromHtml` runs the HTML's scripts (charts drawn by script appear) but it has no access to the app's native features. Pages longer than one sheet are split as Chrome would; use `break-before: page` to control where.

### `navigator.clipboard`

```js
navigator.clipboard.writeText / readText (and write / read)
```

**Example**

The standard Clipboard API, answered by the phone's real clipboard inside the app.

**Returns:** `writeText(text)` → a Promise that resolves when copied and rejects with a `NotAllowedError` otherwise. `readText()` → a Promise with the clipboard text (`""` when empty). `write([item])` / `read()` → Promises, as in the standard. **Needs:** nothing. Installed at document start, so a check made while your page parses already sees it.

**Copy:**

```js
async function copyLink(link) {
  if (!(navigator.clipboard && navigator.clipboard.writeText)) { alert('Copy is not available'); return; }
  try {
    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(link);
    showMessage('Link copied');
  } catch (e) {
    showMessage('Could not copy');
  }
}
```

**Paste** - from a tap:

```js
document.getElementById('paste').onclick = async function () {
  try {
    var text = await navigator.clipboard.readText();
    document.getElementById('input').value = text;
  } catch (e) {
    showMessage('Could not read the clipboard');
  }
};
```

**Copy an image** (for example a QR code drawn on a canvas) with `ClipboardItem`:

```js
async function copyCanvas(canvas) {
  if (!(navigator.clipboard && navigator.clipboard.write && window.ClipboardItem)) {
    alert('Copying images is not available here');
    return;
  }
  var blob = await new Promise(function (r) { canvas.toBlob(r, 'image/png'); });
  try {
    await navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({ 'image/png': blob })]);
    showMessage('Image copied');
  } catch (e) {
    showMessage('Could not copy the image');
  }
}
```

**Notes:** In the app, `writeText`/`readText` call `WebToApk.copyToClipboard` and `WebToApk.readClipboard`. `write()` takes the first `ClipboardItem` only and supports `text/plain`, `text/html` and one image (up to 16 MB; an image wins over text in the same item). `read()` resolves to `[item]` with the clipboard's text, HTML or image (`[]` when it is empty). Only the app's own pages can read it: a foreign website opened inside the app is refused (`NotAllowedError`). Read it on a user tap - Android 12+ shows a "pasted from clipboard" notice. In a browser the same code works with the browser's own permission rules.

### `navigator.share`

```js
navigator.share(data) / navigator.canShare(data)
```

**Example**

The standard Web Share API, made to work inside the app: text and links open the Android share sheet, and `files` are shared as real files (WhatsApp, Gmail, Drive…).

**Returns:** `navigator.share` → a Promise that resolves when the sheet opens (it does not tell you which app was picked). `navigator.canShare` → `true`/`false`. **Needs:** nothing. Installed at document start, so a check made while your page parses already sees it.

**Text and a link:**

```js
async function shareItem(item) {
  if (!navigator.share) { alert('Sharing is not available here'); return; }
  try {
    await navigator.share({ title: item.name, text: 'Look at this', url: item.link });
  } catch (e) { /* in a browser: AbortError when the user closes the sheet */ }
}
```

**Files** - check with `canShare` first:

```js
async function sharePdf(blob) {
  var file = new File([blob], 'invoice.pdf', { type: 'application/pdf' });
  var data = { files: [file], title: 'Invoice', text: 'Invoice for March' };
  if (!(navigator.canShare && navigator.canShare(data))) {
    alert('File sharing is not available here');
    return;
  }
  try {
    await navigator.share(data);
  } catch (e) { console.log('Share failed', e); }
}
```

**Several files** the user picked - photos of one type share with that type:

```js
document.getElementById('photos').onchange = async function (e) {
  var files = Array.from(e.target.files);
  if (!files.length) return;
  var data = { files: files, title: 'Trip photos' };
  if (!(navigator.canShare && navigator.canShare(data))) {
    alert('File sharing is not available here');
    return;
  }
  try {
    await navigator.share(data);
  } catch (err) { console.log('Share failed', err); }
};
```

**Notes:** In the app `title` becomes the subject, and `text` + `url` are sent as one text. With `files`, each file is read in the page and sent as base64 (`WebToApk.shareFiles`), so keep files to a few MB. If the share sheet cannot open, the files are saved as downloads instead and the promise still resolves. `canShare` returns `true` for any text share. AI-built apps can use `share` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `window.print`

```js
window.print()
```

**Example**

The standard print call, made to work inside the app: it opens Android's print screen, where the user prints on paper or saves a PDF.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing.

```js
document.getElementById('print-receipt').onclick = function () {
  window.print();
};
```

Hide the app's controls on paper with a print stylesheet:

```html
<style>
  @media print {
    nav, .toolbar, button { display: none !important; }
    body { background: #fff; color: #000; }
  }
</style>
```

Print a shipping label without the page around it - a same-origin `srcdoc` iframe prints only its own document:

```js
function esc(s) {
  return String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, function (c) {
    return { '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;' }[c];
  });
}
function printLabel(name, address) {
  var frame = document.createElement('iframe');
  frame.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;width:0;height:0;border:0';
  frame.srcdoc = '<title>Label</title><style>body{font:18px sans-serif;margin:24px}</style>' +
                 '<b>' + esc(name) + '</b><br>' + esc(address).replace(/\n/g, '<br>');
  frame.onload = function () {
    frame.contentWindow.print();
    setTimeout(function () { frame.remove(); }, 1000);
  };
  document.body.appendChild(frame);
}
```

**Notes:** `window.print()` prints the main page as it is drawn now. A same-origin `<iframe>` - the hidden iframe a print library fills with a receipt and calls `iframe.contentWindow.print()` on, or an iframe page calling its own `window.print()` - prints THAT iframe's document (see `__printHtml`). A cross-origin iframe cannot be printed from the page. The replacement exists before the page's first script. `beforeprint` cannot be cancelled (in any browser).

### `__clipboardRead`

```js
window.WebToApk.__clipboardRead(): String
```

navigator.clipboard.read(): `{parts:[{type, text|base64}]}`. Same reach as readClipboard() in this shell (which has no origin gate).

**Example**

Internal transport behind `navigator.clipboard.read()`. Pages use the standard API; never call this directly - the `__` methods may change without notice.

**Returns:** `{parts:[{type, text|base64}]}` - the same reach as `readClipboard()` in this app. **Needs:** nothing to switch on.

**Use the public API:**

```js
canvas.toBlob(async (png) => {
  await navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({ 'image/png': png })]);
});
const [item] = await navigator.clipboard.read();
if (item && item.types.includes('image/png')) preview(await item.getType('image/png'));
```

Paste formatted text into an editor, keeping the formatting when the clipboard has HTML:

```js
async function pasteRich(editor) {
  try {
    var items = await navigator.clipboard.read();
    if (!items.length) { showMessage('The clipboard is empty'); return; }
    var item = items[0];
    if (item.types.includes('text/html')) {
      editor.insertHtml(sanitize(await (await item.getType('text/html')).text()));
    } else if (item.types.includes('text/plain')) {
      editor.insertText(await (await item.getType('text/plain')).text());
    }
  } catch (e) {
    showMessage('Could not read the clipboard');
  }
}
```

Paste any copied picture (PNG, JPEG, WebP…) as a profile photo, and tell a refused read apart:

```js
document.getElementById('paste-photo').onclick = async function () {
  try {
    var items = await navigator.clipboard.read();
    var item = items[0];
    var type = item && item.types.find(function (t) { return t.indexOf('image/') === 0; });
    if (!type) { showMessage('Copy a picture first'); return; }
    uploadAvatar(await item.getType(type));   // a Blob of that type
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.name === 'NotAllowedError') showMessage('This page cannot read the clipboard');
    else showMessage('Could not paste the picture');
  }
};
```

**Notes:** Android 12+ shows its own "pasted from your clipboard" message when an app reads the clipboard.

### `__clipboardWrite`

```js
window.WebToApk.__clipboardWrite(partsJson: String): Boolean
```

navigator.clipboard.write(): [partsJson] is `[{type, text}|{type, base64}]` for one ClipboardItem - text/plain, text/html, or an image that is copied as a content URI.

**Example**

Internal transport behind `navigator.clipboard.write([ClipboardItem])`. Pages use the standard API; never call this directly - the `__` methods may change without notice.

**Returns:** `true` when the clip was placed. **Needs:** nothing to switch on.

**Use the public API:**

```js
canvas.toBlob(async (png) => {
  await navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({ 'image/png': png })]);
});
const [item] = await navigator.clipboard.read();
if (item && item.types.includes('image/png')) preview(await item.getType('image/png'));
```

Copy formatted text and its plain version in one item, so rich editors get the table and plain fields get the text:

```js
async function copyTable(table) {
  if (!(navigator.clipboard && navigator.clipboard.write && window.ClipboardItem)) return;
  try {
    await navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({
      'text/html': new Blob([table.outerHTML], { type: 'text/html' }),
      'text/plain': new Blob([table.innerText], { type: 'text/plain' })
    })]);
    showMessage('Table copied');
  } catch (e) {
    showMessage('Could not copy (' + e.name + ')');   // NotAllowedError when the write fails
  }
}
```

Copy an image the page shows, such as a QR code, so it can be pasted into a chat:

```js
async function copyImage(img) {
  try {
    var blob = await (await fetch(img.src)).blob();   // an image/* type, up to 16 MB
    await navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({ [blob.type]: blob })]);
    showMessage('Image copied');
  } catch (e) {
    showMessage('Could not copy the image');
  }
}
```

**Notes:** Text, HTML and one image per item. The image is copied as a content URI through the app's FileProvider, so it pastes into WhatsApp, Gmail or Keep.

### `__printHtml`

```js
window.WebToApk.__printHtml(html: String, baseUrl: String, title: String)
```

Prints [html] - a same-origin iframe's serialised document, sent by the `window.print()` shim ([PrintShim]) - through an offscreen WebView at [baseUrl], because the main WebView's print adapter can only print the whole page. [title] names the print job ("<App name> Document" when blank).

**Example**

Internal transport behind printing an iframe: `iframe.contentWindow.print()` (and an iframe page's own `window.print()`) sends that iframe's document here, and the app prints it through Android's print screen. Pages use the standard calls; never call this directly.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing.

The receipt pattern this makes work - a hidden iframe filled with just the receipt:

```js
function printReceipt(order) {
  var frame = document.createElement('iframe');
  frame.style.display = 'none';
  document.body.appendChild(frame);
  var doc = frame.contentWindow.document;
  doc.open();
  doc.write('<html><head><title>Receipt ' + order.id + '</title>' +
            '<style>body{font:14px sans-serif} td{padding:2px 8px}</style></head><body>' +
            '<h2>Receipt ' + order.id + '</h2><table>' +
            order.lines.map(function (l) { return '<tr><td>' + l.name + '</td><td>' + l.price + '</td></tr>'; }).join('') +
            '</table></body></html>');
  doc.close();
  frame.contentWindow.print();   // prints the RECEIPT, not the page behind it
  setTimeout(function () { frame.remove(); }, 1000);
}
```

A ticket page of your own, loaded into a hidden iframe from the same origin - its CSS and images load, and its `<title>` names the print job:

```js
function printTicket(id) {
  var frame = document.createElement('iframe');
  frame.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;width:0;height:0;border:0';
  frame.src = 'ticket.html?id=' + encodeURIComponent(id);
  frame.onload = function () {
    frame.contentWindow.print();   // prints ticket.html's DOM as it stands now
    setTimeout(function () { frame.remove(); }, 1000);
  };
  document.body.appendChild(frame);
}
```

Adjust the iframe's document just before the snapshot with `beforeprint` on the iframe's window:

```js
function printWithTimestamp(frame) {
  var w = frame.contentWindow;
  w.addEventListener('beforeprint', function () {
    var p = w.document.createElement('p');
    p.textContent = 'Printed ' + new Date().toLocaleString();
    w.document.body.appendChild(p);
  }, { once: true });
  w.print();   // the printed copy includes the line added above
}
```

**Notes:** Arguments are `(html, baseUrl, title)`: the iframe's serialised document, the address its relative links resolve against (the page's own address for an `about:blank` iframe), and the print job name (the iframe's `<title>`, else the page's). The snapshot is taken when `print()` is called - scripts inside it do not run again - and `beforeprint` / `afterprint` fire on the iframe's window around it. A cross-origin iframe cannot be printed from the page.

### `__shareWithResult`

```js
window.WebToApk.__shareWithResult(id: String, title: String, text: String, url: String)
```

navigator.share for text: the share sheet with Android's chosen-target callback, so the page's promise settles on the user's real answer (see [settleShare]).

**Example**

Internal transport behind `navigator.share()` for text and links. Pages use the standard API; never call this directly - the `__` methods may change without notice.

**Returns:** nothing; the page's `navigator.share()` promise settles later - resolved when the user picks an app in the share sheet, rejected with `AbortError` when they close it without choosing one (as in Chrome). **Needs:** nothing to switch on.

**Use the public API:**

```js
document.getElementById('share').onclick = async function () {
  try {
    await navigator.share({ title: 'My list', text: 'Groceries for Sunday', url: location.href });
    showMessage('Thanks for sharing!');
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.name === 'AbortError') return;   // the user closed the share sheet
    showMessage('Could not share');
  }
};
```

Reward a share only when it really happened:

```js
async function shareForBonus(code) {
  try {
    await navigator.share({ text: 'Join me with code ' + code });
    grantBonus();                 // runs only after an app was chosen
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.name !== 'AbortError') console.warn('share failed', e);
  }
}
```

Fall back to copying the link where sharing is not possible:

```js
async function shareOrCopy(url) {
  if (navigator.share) {
    try { await navigator.share({ url }); return; }
    catch (e) { if (e.name === 'AbortError') return; }
  }
  await navigator.clipboard.writeText(url);
  showMessage('Link copied');
}
```

**Notes:** Files go through `navigator.share({ files })`, which keeps its own path (`shareFiles`).

### `clearSharedText`

```js
window.WebToApk.clearSharedText()
```

Clears the kept share once the page has consumed it.

**Example**

Forgets the text or link that was shared into the app, once your page has used it.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing (the share itself needs **Receive Shares From Other Apps** with **Text and links** ticked).

Read the kept share, use it, then clear it so it is not handled again after a reload:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.getSharedText === 'function') {
  var raw = window.WebToApk.getSharedText();
  if (raw) {
    var shared = JSON.parse(raw);          // { text, subject, url, receivedAt }
    saveNote(shared.subject, shared.text);
    window.WebToApk.clearSharedText();     // getSharedText() now returns ""
  }
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:shared', function (e) {
  saveNote(e.detail.subject, e.detail.text);
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.clearSharedText) window.WebToApk.clearSharedText();
});
```

Ask first, and clear the share whichever button the user taps:

```js
function askAboutShare(s) {
  var dialog = document.getElementById('share-dialog');
  document.getElementById('share-preview').textContent = s.text;
  dialog.hidden = false;
  function done() {
    dialog.hidden = true;
    if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.clearSharedText === 'function') {
      window.WebToApk.clearSharedText();
    }
  }
  document.getElementById('share-save').onclick = function () { saveNote(s.subject, s.text); done(); };
  document.getElementById('share-discard').onclick = done;
}
```

Clear it only once it is safely saved, so a failed upload can be retried:

```js
async function importShare() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.getSharedText === 'function')) return;
  var raw = window.WebToApk.getSharedText();
  if (!raw) return;
  var s = JSON.parse(raw);
  try {
    var res = await fetch('/api/bookmarks', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ url: s.url || s.text, title: s.subject })
    });
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + res.status);
    window.WebToApk.clearSharedText();
  } catch (e) {
    showMessage('Could not save the link — tap Retry');   // Retry calls importShare() again
  }
}
```

**Notes:** Clearing only affects `getSharedText()`. A new share replaces the kept one and fires `appmint:shared` again. Files shared into the app are released separately with `AppMint.releaseOpenedFile()`.

### `copyToClipboard`

```js
window.WebToApk.copyToClipboard(text: String): Boolean
```

Use the promise wrapper:     const r = await AppMint.requestReview();                 // {result, openedStore}     const r = await AppMint.requestReview({ openStore: true }); // listing if no sheet r.result: 'shown' | 'not_from_play' | 'quota' | 'error'. See RatePrompt.

_Described by its group, Google Play's in-app review sheet, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Copies plain text to the phone's clipboard. Pages normally use the standard `navigator.clipboard.writeText(text)`, which the shell routes here.

**Returns:** `true` on success, `false` on failure (synchronously). **Needs:** nothing.

The standard API first:

```js
document.getElementById('copy-btn').onclick = async function () {
  try {
    await navigator.clipboard.writeText('PROMO-2026');
    showMessage('Copied');
  } catch (e) {
    showMessage('Could not copy');
  }
};
```

The raw call:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.copyToClipboard === 'function') {
  var ok = window.WebToApk.copyToClipboard('PROMO-2026');
  showMessage(ok ? 'Copied' : 'Could not copy');
}
```

A "Copy" button on every code block, using the synchronous answer to update the label:

```js
document.querySelectorAll('pre').forEach(function (pre) {
  var btn = document.createElement('button');
  btn.textContent = 'Copy';
  btn.onclick = function () {
    var ok = !!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.copyToClipboard === 'function' &&
                window.WebToApk.copyToClipboard(pre.innerText));
    btn.textContent = ok ? 'Copied' : 'Copy failed';
    setTimeout(function () { btn.textContent = 'Copy'; }, 1500);
  };
  pre.parentNode.insertBefore(btn, pre);
});
```

**Notes:** Plain text only (no images or HTML). Android 13+ shows its own small "Copied" preview, so you may not need your own message there.

### `getSharedText`

```js
window.WebToApk.getSharedText(): String
```

Text or a link another app shared INTO this one ("Share to <app>" - a YouTube video shared from the YouTube app arrives as its link), as JSON `{text, subject, url, receivedAt}` or "" when nothing was shared. Kept until read, so an app that mounts after the share still sees it; a share arriving while the app runs also fires `appmint:shared`. A photo or video shared with a caption delivers the file through AppMint.getOpenedFile() and the caption here. Requires the build's "Receive shares from other apps" option with "Text and links" ticked, which registers the share-sheet entry.

**Example**

Text or a link that another app shared INTO your app ("Share → your app"), as a JSON string - `JSON.parse` it - or `""` when nothing was shared.

**Returns:** a JSON string `{text, subject, url, receivedAt}` or `""` (synchronously). `url` is the first `http(s)://` link found in `text` (or `""`); `receivedAt` is a time in milliseconds. **Needs:** **Receive Shares From Other Apps** switched on when you build, with **Text and links** ticked - that puts your app in other apps' Share menu.

The share is kept until you clear it, so read it on start, and listen for shares that arrive while the app runs:

```js
function handleShare(s) {
  addBookmark(s.url || s.text, s.subject);
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.clearSharedText) window.WebToApk.clearSharedText();
}

// 1. On start (the app may have been opened by the share).
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.getSharedText === 'function') {
  var raw = window.WebToApk.getSharedText();
  if (raw) handleShare(JSON.parse(raw));
}

// 2. While running: detail has the same keys { text, subject, url, receivedAt }.
window.addEventListener('appmint:shared', function (e) {
  handleShare(e.detail);
});
```

A global hook receives the same object, if you prefer one:

```js
window.onAppMintShared = function (s) { handleShare(s); };
```

Open a YouTube video that was shared into the app, using the `url` field:

```js
function openSharedVideo() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.getSharedText === 'function')) return;
  var raw = window.WebToApk.getSharedText();
  if (!raw) return;
  var s = JSON.parse(raw);
  var m = /(?:youtu\.be\/|[?&]v=)([\w-]{11})/.exec(s.url || s.text);
  if (m) {
    showVideo(m[1]);
    window.WebToApk.clearSharedText();
  } else {
    showMessage('That share is not a video link');
  }
}
```

**Notes:** It is filled on a cold start (the app was opened by the share) and on a warm start (the app was already open: `appmint:shared` fires too). A link from Chrome arrives here even though Chrome attaches a preview picture to the share - that picture is not delivered as a file. A YouTube video shared from the YouTube app arrives as its link. A photo or video shared WITH a caption delivers the file through `AppMint.getOpenedFile()` and the caption here. Clear the share after you use it, or you will see it again on the next start. AI-built apps can use `sharedText()` / `onShared()` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `pdfFromHtml`

```js
window.WebToApk.pdfFromHtml(html: String, optionsJson: String, callbackId: String)
```

Renders [html] offscreen at the app's origin and saves it as a PDF - use `AppMint.pdf.fromHtml(html, options)`.

**Example**

Documented together with `AppMint.pdf` - the example there shows this one too.

Makes a real PDF (selectable text, vector graphics) with no print dialog: `fromPage` saves the page as it is on screen, laid out with your `@media print` CSS; `fromHtml` renders HTML you pass in an invisible page at the app's own address - so relative images, stylesheets and fonts load as in your page - waits for the fonts and every image, then saves it. `window.print()` still opens the normal print dialog.

**Returns:** a Promise of `{ok: true, fileName, pages, bytes, saved, uri?, base64?}` or `{ok: false, code, message}` - `code` is `busy` (one PDF at a time), `bad-options`, `failed`, `too-large` (base64 over 25 MB) or `permission-denied` (storage refused on Android 7-9). **Needs:** nothing - every build has it. Saving to Downloads needs no permission on Android 10+.

**Options:** `fileName` (".pdf" is added; default: the page title), `pageSize` `'A4'` (default) | `'Letter'` | `'Legal'` | `'A3'` | `'A5'`, `landscape` (`true`/`false`), `margins` in millimetres (one number, or `{top, right, bottom, left}`; left out = your own `@page` rule), `save` `'downloads'` (default) | `'share'` | `'base64'`.

**Save the current page to Downloads:**

```js
async function saveInvoice() {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.pdf)) { window.print(); return; }   // in a browser
  var r = await AppMint.pdf.fromPage({ fileName: 'invoice-1042', pageSize: 'A4', margins: 12 });
  if (r.ok) console.log('Saved ' + r.fileName + ' (' + r.pages + ' pages)');
  else alert('Could not make the PDF: ' + r.message);
}
```

**A receipt built from HTML, straight to the share sheet** (images and fonts are loaded before the PDF is made):

```js
async function shareReceipt(order) {
  var html = '<style>body{font-family:sans-serif} td{padding:4px 8px}</style>' +
    '<img src="img/logo.png" width="120"><h1>Receipt #' + order.id + '</h1><table>' +
    order.items.map(function (i) { return '<tr><td>' + i.name + '</td><td>' + i.price + '</td></tr>'; }).join('') +
    '</table><p><b>Total ' + order.total + '</b></p>';
  var r = await AppMint.pdf.fromHtml(html, { fileName: 'receipt-' + order.id, pageSize: 'Letter', save: 'share' });
  if (!r.ok) console.warn(r.code, r.message);
}
```

**Get the bytes back** to upload them yourself:

```js
async function uploadReport() {
  var r = await AppMint.pdf.fromPage({ landscape: true, margins: { top: 10, right: 8, bottom: 10, left: 8 }, save: 'base64' });
  if (!r.ok) return;
  var bin = atob(r.base64), buf = new Uint8Array(bin.length);
  for (var i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) buf[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
  await fetch('/api/reports', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/pdf' }, body: buf });
}
```

The raw calls take the options as JSON text and a callback id; use the helper above instead:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.pdfFromPage === 'function') {
  // AppMint.pdf.fromPage wraps: WebToApk.pdfFromPage(JSON.stringify(options), callbackId)
  // and AppMint.pdf.fromHtml wraps: WebToApk.pdfFromHtml(html, JSON.stringify(options), callbackId)
  AppMint.pdf.fromPage({ save: 'downloads' }).then(function (r) { console.log(r); });
}
```

**Notes:** Hide buttons and menus from the PDF with `@media print { .no-print { display: none } }`. A downloaded PDF shows "Downloaded <name> · Open" like any download. `fromHtml` runs the HTML's scripts (charts drawn by script appear) but it has no access to the app's native features. Pages longer than one sheet are split as Chrome would; use `break-before: page` to control where.

### `print`

```js
window.WebToApk.print()
```

Hands the page as it currently stands to Android's print dialogue, which can print on paper or save a PDF. Nothing to configure - the WebView renders the document.

_Described by its group, Printing, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Opens Android's print screen for the page as it looks now - print on paper or "Save as PDF". Pages normally use the standard `window.print()`, which the shell routes here.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing.

The standard API first:

```js
document.getElementById('print-btn').onclick = function () {
  window.print();   // in the app: the Android print screen
};
```

The raw call does the same:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.print === 'function') {
  window.WebToApk.print();
}
```

Print one invoice out of a list by marking it for a print stylesheet (leave the mark on - the print screen lays the page out after `print()` returns):

```js
// CSS: @media print { .invoice:not(.print-me), nav, button { display: none !important; } }
function printInvoice(id) {
  document.querySelectorAll('.invoice.print-me').forEach(function (el) {
    el.classList.remove('print-me');
  });
  document.getElementById('invoice-' + id).classList.add('print-me');
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.print === 'function') {
    window.WebToApk.print();
  } else {
    window.print();   // a normal browser
  }
}
```

**Notes:** It prints the whole WebView - the main page. A same-origin iframe's own `print()` prints just that iframe (see `window.print`). Use a `@media print` stylesheet to hide buttons and menus. The job is named "<App name> Document". Errors are only logged.

### `readClipboard`

```js
window.WebToApk.readClipboard(): String
```

Use the promise wrapper:     const r = await AppMint.requestReview();                 // {result, openedStore}     const r = await AppMint.requestReview({ openStore: true }); // listing if no sheet r.result: 'shown' | 'not_from_play' | 'quota' | 'error'. See RatePrompt.

_Described by its group, Google Play's in-app review sheet, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Reads the text that is on the phone's clipboard now. Pages normally use the standard `navigator.clipboard.readText()`, which the shell routes here.

**Returns:** the text, or `""` when the clipboard is empty or cannot be read (synchronously). **Needs:** nothing.

The standard API first - for example a "Paste code" button:

```js
document.getElementById('paste-btn').onclick = async function () {
  try {
    var text = await navigator.clipboard.readText();
    if (text) document.getElementById('code').value = text.trim();
    else showMessage('The clipboard is empty');
  } catch (e) {
    showMessage('Could not read the clipboard');
  }
};
```

The raw call:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.readClipboard === 'function') {
  var text = window.WebToApk.readClipboard();
  if (text) document.getElementById('code').value = text;
}
```

A "Paste link" button that takes the first web address out of whatever was copied:

```js
document.getElementById('paste-link').onclick = function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.readClipboard === 'function')) return;
  var text = window.WebToApk.readClipboard();
  var m = /https?:\/\/\S+/.exec(text);
  if (m) document.getElementById('link').value = m[0];
  else showMessage('There is no link on the clipboard');
};
```

**Notes:** Only your own app's pages can read it: a foreign website opened inside the app gets `""`. Android only lets the app read the clipboard while it is on screen, and Android 12+ shows a "pasted from clipboard" notice - read it on a user tap, not on page load.

### `shareFiles`

```js
window.WebToApk.shareFiles(filesJson: String, title: String, text: String): Boolean
```

TRUE native file share for navigator.share({files:[...]}). Android WebView has no Web Share API, and text/plain ACTION_SEND can't carry a file - so before this a shared image was merely SAVED, not shared. filesJson is [{name, mimeType, base64}, ...]; we write each to cache, expose it via the app's FileProvider, and fire ACTION_SEND / ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE so the real Android share sheet (WhatsApp, Gmail, …) opens. Returns true if the sheet opened.

**Example**

Shares one or more real files (an image, a PDF…) through the Android share sheet. Pages normally use the standard `navigator.share({ files: [...] })`, which the shell routes here.

**Returns:** `true` if the share sheet opened, `false` otherwise (synchronously). **Needs:** nothing.

The standard API first:

```js
async function shareCanvas(canvas) {
  var blob = await new Promise(function (r) { canvas.toBlob(r, 'image/png'); });
  var file = new File([blob], 'drawing.png', { type: 'image/png' });
  if (!(navigator.canShare && navigator.canShare({ files: [file] }))) {
    alert('File sharing is not available here');
    return;
  }
  try {
    await navigator.share({ files: [file], title: 'My drawing', text: 'Made in my app' });
  } catch (e) { /* in a browser: the user closed the sheet */ }
}
```

The raw call takes a JSON string of `[{name, mimeType, base64}]` (base64 without the `data:` prefix), then `title` and `text`:

```js
function shareBase64Png(base64) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.shareFiles === 'function')) return false;
  var files = [{ name: 'receipt.png', mimeType: 'image/png', base64: base64 }];
  return window.WebToApk.shareFiles(JSON.stringify(files), 'Receipt', 'Your receipt');
}
```

Export a table as a CSV file (text is UTF-8 encoded before base64):

```js
function shareCsv(rows) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.shareFiles === 'function')) return;
  var csv = rows.map(function (r) {
    return r.map(function (c) { return '"' + String(c).replace(/"/g, '""') + '"'; }).join(',');
  }).join('\n');
  var base64 = btoa(unescape(encodeURIComponent(csv)));
  var files = [{ name: 'expenses.csv', mimeType: 'text/csv', base64: base64 }];
  if (!window.WebToApk.shareFiles(JSON.stringify(files), 'Expenses', '')) {
    showMessage('Could not open the share sheet');
  }
}
```

**Notes:** Files are written to the app's cache and shared through its FileProvider. Unsafe characters in `name` become `_`. Several files of one type share with that type; mixed types share as `*/*`. The whole file travels as base64 over the bridge, so keep it to a few MB. When `navigator.share({files})` cannot open the sheet, the shell saves the files as downloads instead and the promise still resolves.

### `shareNative`

```js
window.WebToApk.shareNative(title: String, text: String, url: String)
```

The Android share sheet, the system clipboard, and closing a window the page opened. These are the plain-web equivalents (navigator.share, navigator.clipboard, window.close) answered natively so they behave the same inside the app.

_Described by its group, Share, clipboard and window, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Opens the Android share sheet with a title, text and link. Pages normally use the standard `navigator.share({title, text, url})`, which the shell routes here.

**Returns:** nothing (it cannot tell you which app the user picked). **Needs:** nothing.

The standard API first - it also works in a mobile browser:

```js
document.getElementById('share-btn').onclick = async function () {
  if (!navigator.share) { alert('Sharing is not available here'); return; }
  try {
    await navigator.share({ title: 'My app', text: 'Look at this', url: 'https://mysite.com/item/42' });
  } catch (e) {
    // in a browser: AbortError when the user closes the sheet
  }
};
```

The raw call, all three arguments are strings (use `''` to leave one out):

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.shareNative === 'function') {
  window.WebToApk.shareNative('My app', 'Look at this', 'https://mysite.com/item/42');
}
```

Text only, no link - for example a game score:

```js
function shareScore(score) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.shareNative === 'function')) return;
  window.WebToApk.shareNative('My score', 'I scored ' + score + ' points. Can you beat it?', '');
}
```

**Notes:** The shared text is `text` + a new line + `url` (or just one of them). `title` becomes the email subject and the share sheet's heading. Text and links only - to share a file, use `navigator.share({files})` (see `shareFiles`).

**`share:` button links in in-app messages.** A button whose link is `share:<text>` opens this same share sheet with that text, with no page code. The **Invite friends** template uses `share:Try {app}: {store}`; the app fills in its own name and Play address. Your page can tell it happened:

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:inapp', function (e) {
  var d = e.detail;
  if (d.type === 'clicked' && d.link && d.link.indexOf('share:') === 0) analytics('invite_shared', d.name);
});
```

If you draw in-app messages yourself (`setInAppPresentation('none')`), run a `share:` button the same way:

```js
function runInAppButton(link) {
  if (link.indexOf('share:') === 0 && window.WebToApk && WebToApk.shareNative) {
    WebToApk.shareNative('', link.slice(6), '');   // text only
  }
}
```

A `copy:<text>` link copies instead of sharing, for example a coupon code from a promo message:

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:inapp', function (e) {
  var d = e.detail;
  if (d.type === 'clicked' && d.link === 'copy:SAVE20') showToast('Code SAVE20 copied');
});
```
