# Launch, shortcuts and the back button - JavaScript bridge API

> How the app was opened, long-press shortcuts on the icon, the in-app review prompt, and telling the shell the page wants the back press.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/navigation

### `AppMint.requestReview`

```js
AppMint.requestReview(options)
```

**Example**

Asks Google Play to show its own rating sheet inside the app (Play In-App Review) and tells you what happened.

**Returns:** a Promise that always resolves `{result, openedStore, message?}`. `result` is `'shown'` (Play put its sheet up - it never says whether the user rated), `'not_from_play'` (this install did not come from Google Play: a sideloaded APK or a test install, where Play never shows the sheet), `'quota'` (Play chose not to show it now: its quota for this user, or they already reviewed) or `'error'` (Play could not be asked: no Play Store, offline). With `{openStore: true}` the app's Play listing opens when the sheet did not show, and `openedStore` is `true`. **Needs:** nothing to switch on.

**Any code:**

```js
// A "Rate us" button: the sheet when Play shows it, the Play listing otherwise.
document.getElementById('rate-btn').onclick = async function () {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.requestReview)) { location.href = 'https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.example.app'; return; }
  var r = await AppMint.requestReview({ openStore: true });
  if (r.result === 'shown' || r.openedStore) showToast('Thank you!');
};
```

Ask after a success moment instead of from a button, without ever leaving the app:

```js
async function onOrderDelivered(count) {
  if (count !== 3 || !(window.AppMint && AppMint.requestReview)) return;
  var r = await AppMint.requestReview();      // no openStore: nothing opens if Play says no
  if (r.result === 'not_from_play') console.log('Test install: Play only shows the sheet for Play installs');
}
```

When the creator switched on **Ask users to rate the app** (Display step), the app asks by itself at a calm moment and tells the page what happened:

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:review', function (e) {
  // e.detail = { result, openedStore: false, source: 'auto' }
  analytics.track('rate_prompt', { result: e.detail.result });
});
```

**Notes:** Google Play rate-limits the sheet and decides by itself whether it appears; never reward a review or promise the sheet on a button. Test it with an internal-testing track install from Play - a sideloaded APK always answers `not_from_play`.

**Without code: the `appmint://review` link.** A button or link with this address asks for the same sheet (and opens the Play listing when Play will not show it, because the user asked to rate). In an in-app message, put it on a button in the send center (the **Rate us** template does); on a page, use it as a plain link:

```html
<a href="appmint://review" class="rate-link">Rate us on Google Play</a>
```

From script, for example after the third finished order:

```js
function maybeAskForRating(ordersDone) {
  if (ordersDone === 3) location.href = 'appmint://review';   // the app runs it; nothing is loaded
}
```

Hear what the user picked in a "Rate us" in-app message before the sheet opens:

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:inapp', function (e) {
  var d = e.detail;
  if (d.type === 'answered' && d.question === 'stars' && d.value <= 3) showFeedbackForm();
  if (d.type === 'clicked' && d.link === 'appmint://review') console.log('Opening the Play review sheet');
});
```

### `AppMint.setBackHandler`

```js
AppMint.setBackHandler(handler)
```

**Example**

Gives your page the first say when the user presses the phone's Back button (or uses the back gesture). Needed by apps that change screens by showing and hiding elements, where Android's history is empty and Back would exit the app.

**Returns:** nothing. Your `handler` must return `true` (handled, stay here) or `false` (let the app go back / exit). **Needs:** nothing. Installed at document start, so you can register it in your first script.

```js
if (window.AppMint && AppMint.setBackHandler) {
  AppMint.setBackHandler(function () {
    if (isMenuOpen)               { closeMenu();  return true; }   // consumed
    if (currentScreen !== 'home') { goTo('home'); return true; }
    return false;   // nothing to undo: normal Back (history back, exit dialog, exit)
  });
}

// Remove it again, for example when the screen that needed it closes:
// AppMint.setBackHandler(null);
```

**The `appmint:back` event** - cancelable. Call `e.preventDefault()` to consume the press. It runs before the handler, and any number of listeners can use it:

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:back', function (e) {
  var sheet = document.querySelector('.bottom-sheet.open');
  if (sheet) {
    sheet.classList.remove('open');
    e.preventDefault();   // consumed: the handler and the shell do nothing more
  }
});
```

Keep a half-written note from being lost: Back shows your own "Discard changes?" bar instead of leaving (a blocking `confirm()` would miss the 350 ms answer window, so the shell would go back anyway):

```js
if (window.AppMint && AppMint.setBackHandler) {
  var noteDirty = false;
  document.getElementById('note').addEventListener('input', function () { noteDirty = true; });

  AppMint.setBackHandler(function () {
    if (!noteDirty) return false;        // nothing to lose: normal Back
    showDiscardBar();                    // your in-page "Discard changes? / Keep editing" bar
    return true;                         // stay here while the user decides
  });

  document.getElementById('discard-btn').onclick = function () {
    noteDirty = false;                   // the next Back press passes straight through
    hideDiscardBar();
    closeEditor();
  };
}
```

**Notes:** The answer must be synchronous: returning a Promise counts as "not handled". Answer quickly - if the page does not answer within about 350 ms, the shell goes back by itself. Order on each press: an open side menu (the app's own drawer) closes first and the page is not asked; then `appmint:back` listeners → your handler → the shell's built-in dialog closer (it closes an open `<dialog>`, ARIA dialog or full-screen modal) → history back / exit confirmation / exit. Apps that use `history.pushState` for every screen (React Router and similar) do not need this. AI-built apps can use `onBackGesture` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `__pullRefreshEligible`

```js
window.WebToApk.__pullRefreshEligible(eligible: Boolean)
```

See [pullPageEligible] / [pullProbeJs]. Called on every touchstart.

**Example**

Internal plumbing behind **pull-to-refresh**: the shell's own touch probe calls it on every touch to say whether a downward pull there should refresh the page. Pages never call it - they control pull-to-refresh with standard CSS and touch events.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** **Enable Pull-to-Refresh** switched on in Step 3 (Integrate), under **Display Options**, when you build (without it the probe is not installed).

The public way to stop a pull from refreshing in part of your page - claim the gesture:

```html
<style>
  /* A map, drawing canvas or slider: this element owns vertical drags. */
  #map, #canvas { touch-action: none; }
  /* A horizontal carousel: pan-x also tells the shell "not a refresh". */
  .carousel { touch-action: pan-x; }
</style>
```

Or claim it from a touch handler, the standard way:

```js
document.getElementById('canvas').addEventListener('touchstart', function (e) {
  e.preventDefault();   // the page took this gesture: no pull-to-refresh
}, { passive: false });
```

Keep a pan-and-zoom surface from refreshing the page by claiming vertical drags with CSS only:

```html
<div id="board" style="touch-action: none; height: 60vh"></div>
<script>
  // Dragging on #board moves the board; a pull from the top of the rest of the page still refreshes.
  document.getElementById('board').addEventListener('pointermove', function (e) { moveBoard(e); });
</script>
```

**Notes:** A pull only refreshes when the nearest scrollable box under the finger (or the page itself) is scrolled to the top, only one finger is down, and neither of the claims above applies. A touch inside a cross-origin iframe never refreshes. Do not call this method yourself.

### `getAppIcon`

```js
window.WebToApk.getAppIcon(): String
```

The launcher icon in use: "default" or one of the names from getAvailableIcons().

**Example**

The launcher icon in use: `'default'` or one of the names from `getAvailableIcons()`.

**Returns:** a string. `'default'` in a build without alternate icons.

```js
if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getAppIcon) {
  const current = WebToApk.getAppIcon();          // 'default', 'Dark', …
  document.querySelectorAll('[data-icon]').forEach(el => {
    el.classList.toggle('selected', el.dataset.icon === current);
  });
}
```

**Switch to the next icon from a settings screen:**

```js
function nextIcon() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getAvailableIcons && WebToApk.setAppIcon)) return;
  const names = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getAvailableIcons());
  if (names.length < 2) return;                                  // no alternate icons in this build
  const next = names[(names.indexOf(WebToApk.getAppIcon()) + 1) % names.length];
  if (!WebToApk.setAppIcon(next)) alert('Could not change the icon.');
}
```

**Show the icon name in a label, or hide it outside the app:**

```js
const label = document.getElementById('icon-label');
if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getAppIcon) {
  const name = WebToApk.getAppIcon();
  label.textContent = name === 'default' ? 'Classic icon' : name + ' icon';
} else {
  label.hidden = true;           // in a browser there is no launcher icon
}
```

### `getAvailableIcons`

```js
window.WebToApk.getAvailableIcons(): String
```

JSON array of the icon names setAppIcon accepts: "default" first, then the build's alternates.

**Example**

The icon names `setAppIcon` accepts, as a JSON array string: `'default'` first, then the alternate icons from the build wizard in the order you added them.

**Returns:** `'["default","Dark","Gold"]'`, or `'["default"]'` in a build without alternate icons.

**Build an icon picker:**

```js
function iconPicker(container) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getAvailableIcons)) return;
  const names = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getAvailableIcons());
  if (names.length < 2) { container.hidden = true; return; }   // nothing to choose
  const current = WebToApk.getAppIcon();
  container.innerHTML = '';
  names.forEach(name => {
    const b = document.createElement('button');
    b.textContent = name === 'default' ? 'Classic' : name;
    b.className = name === current ? 'selected' : '';
    b.onclick = () => { if (WebToApk.setAppIcon(name)) iconPicker(container); };
    container.appendChild(b);
  });
}
iconPicker(document.querySelector('#iconPicker'));
```

**Hide the picker in a build without alternate icons:**

```js
const picker = document.getElementById('iconPicker');
let names = ['default'];
if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getAvailableIcons) names = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getAvailableIcons());
picker.hidden = names.length < 2;      // only 'default' means there is nothing to choose
```

**Switch the icon with the theme:**

```js
function matchIconToTheme(dark) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getAvailableIcons && WebToApk.setAppIcon)) return;
  const names = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getAvailableIcons());
  const wanted = dark ? 'Dark' : 'default';
  if (names.includes(wanted) && WebToApk.getAppIcon() !== wanted) WebToApk.setAppIcon(wanted);
}
matchIconToTheme(matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches);
```

### `getLaunchUrl`

```js
window.WebToApk.getLaunchUrl(): String
```

The deep link that launched or resumed this app, or "" if it was opened normally. Read it whenever your app mounts and route on it yourself: const u = window.WebToApk?.getLaunchUrl?.(); if (u) router.navigate(new URL(u).pathname); The value is KEPT, not consumed, so a late-mounting app still sees it; a later link arriving while the app runs replaces it and also fires 'appmint:deep-link'.

**Example**

The deep link that opened (or reopened) the app, as a string, or `""` when the app was opened normally.

**Returns:** a string, synchronously. **Needs:** nothing. The value is kept, not consumed, so it is safe to read whenever your app mounts.

A link can arrive in three shapes: `https://yoursite.com/path`, the shell's own `appmint-shortcut://<package>/<route>` (launcher shortcuts, the home-screen widget), or your custom scheme `myapp://segment/path`. This helper turns all three into a route:

```js
function routeOf(link) {
  var m = /^([a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*):\/\/([^\/?#]*)([^#]*)/i.exec(link || '');
  if (!m) return '/';
  var scheme = m[1].toLowerCase(), host = m[2], rest = m[3] || '';
  if (scheme === 'http' || scheme === 'https' || scheme === 'appmint-shortcut') return rest || '/';
  return '/' + host + rest;               // myapp://product/42 -> /product/42
}

// 1. On start: the link that launched the app.
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.getLaunchUrl === 'function') {
  var link = window.WebToApk.getLaunchUrl();
  if (link) goTo(routeOf(link));
}

// 2. While running: a new link replaces the old one and fires 'appmint:deep-link'.
window.addEventListener('appmint:deep-link', function (e) {
  goTo(routeOf(e.detail.url));            // detail: { url }
});
```

The same announcement is also passed to a global hook, if you prefer one:

```js
window.onAppMintDeepLink = function (detail) { goTo(routeOf(detail.url)); };
```

Read a referral code from a link such as `https://yoursite.com/invite?code=AB12` or `myapp://invite?code=AB12`, once per link (it uses `routeOf` from above):

```js
function applyInvite(link) {
  if (!link) return;
  var done = '';
  try { done = sessionStorage.getItem('handledLink') || ''; } catch (e) {}
  if (link === done) return;                      // the same url is announced again after a reload
  try { sessionStorage.setItem('handledLink', link); } catch (e) {}
  var code = null;
  try { code = new URL(link).searchParams.get('code'); } catch (e) { return; }
  if (code && routeOf(link).indexOf('/invite') === 0) showInviteBanner(code);
}

if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.getLaunchUrl === 'function') {
  applyInvite(window.WebToApk.getLaunchUrl());
  window.addEventListener('appmint:deep-link', function (e) { applyInvite(e.detail.url); });
}
```

**Notes:** `appmint:deep-link` is also fired after every page load while a link is kept, so the same `url` can arrive more than once. Ignore a link you already handled.

**Website-mode apps are different:** the shell itself loads an incoming `https://` link (on a cold start and while running), and a custom-scheme link `myapp://product/42` is first rewritten onto your site's address (`https://yoursite.com/product/42`), so `getLaunchUrl()` returns the `https://` form and your page usually has nothing to route. A launcher shortcut or widget tap opens its route on your site (`/today` loads `https://yoursite.com/today`), and `getLaunchUrl()` still returns the `appmint-shortcut://` form (see `setAppShortcuts`). In HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps (served from inside the app) the shell never navigates: your page gets the link and routes on it. A custom-scheme link stays as it arrived there, because there is no site address to map it onto. AI-built apps can use `launchUrl()` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `rateApp`

```js
window.WebToApk.rateApp(): String
```

Opens the Play listing's rating flow. `rateApp()` already existed but only the native drawer entry could reach it, so an app that draws its own UI - every AI build, where the drawer is off - had no way to ask for a rating. It is the one store action a page genuinely cannot perform for itself: `market://` is an intent, not a navigable URL. Gated on the creator's own "Rate App Button" switch, exactly like the drawer entry and the bottom-nav Share item: turning Rate off must mean no rating surface anywhere, or the toggle looks broken.

**Example**

Opens the app's Google Play page so the user can rate it.

**Returns:** `'opened'` when the listing was opened, `'off'` when the creator switched Rate App off (then nothing happens). **Needs:** the **Rate App Button** switch in Step 5 (Menu) when you build (it is on by default; it also adds a "Rate App" item to the side menu). With it off, the call does nothing and returns `'off'`. For Google Play's in-app rating sheet use `AppMint.requestReview()`.

```js
var rateBtn = document.getElementById('rate-btn');
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.rateApp === 'function') {
  rateBtn.onclick = function () { window.WebToApk.rateApp(); };
} else {
  rateBtn.hidden = true;   // in a browser
}
```

Offer the rating once, after the user has finished five workouts, from a card they tap:

```js
function maybeOfferRating(completedCount) {
  if (!window.WebToApk || typeof window.WebToApk.rateApp !== 'function') return;
  var asked = false;
  try { asked = localStorage.getItem('rateAsked') === '1'; } catch (e) {}
  if (asked || completedCount < 5) return;

  var card = document.getElementById('rate-card');   // "Enjoying the app? Rate it on Google Play"
  card.hidden = false;
  card.querySelector('.rate-yes').onclick = function () {
    window.WebToApk.rateApp();                         // opens the Play listing
    try { localStorage.setItem('rateAsked', '1'); } catch (e) {}
    card.hidden = true;
  };
  card.querySelector('.rate-later').onclick = function () { card.hidden = true; };
}
```

A "Rate us" row on your settings screen that says thank you when the user comes back from Google Play (the page's return to the foreground is the only signal that the user came back):

```js
document.getElementById('settings-rate').onclick = function () {
  if (!window.WebToApk || typeof window.WebToApk.rateApp !== 'function') return;
  window.WebToApk.rateApp();
  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function onBack() {
    if (document.visibilityState !== 'visible') return;
    document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', onBack);
    showToast('Thanks for taking a look!');           // your own toast; the user may not have rated
  });
};
```

**Notes:** It opens the Play Store listing (`market://details?id=<package>`), or the Play website when the Play Store app is missing. It is not the in-app review card. A page cannot open `market://` itself - it is an Android intent, not a web address. Only ask after the user did something they liked, and from a tap.

### `requestReview`

```js
window.WebToApk.requestReview(optionsJson: String, callbackId: String)
```

Asks Play for its review sheet; [optionsJson] `{openStore?}`. Resolves AppMint.requestReview [callbackId].

**Example**

Internal plumbing behind `AppMint.requestReview()` - pages use that Promise helper, which asks Google Play for its in-app review sheet and resolves with what happened.

**Returns:** nothing directly; the outcome resolves the `AppMint.requestReview()` promise. **Needs:** nothing to switch on. The sheet only ever appears for an app installed from Google Play.

The public API:

```js
async function askForRating() {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.requestReview)) return;          // a browser: no store here
  var r = await AppMint.requestReview();
  console.log(r.result);   // 'shown' | 'not_from_play' | 'quota' | 'error'
}
```

**Ask after a good moment, and ask for the store page when the sheet does not appear:**

```js
async function afterHappyMoment() {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.requestReview)) return;
  const r = await AppMint.requestReview({ openStore: true });   // {result, openedStore, message?}
  if (r.result === 'shown') thankUser();
  else if (r.openedStore) console.log('Opened the Play listing instead');
}
```

**Listen for the automatic prompt and report an error:**

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:review', (e) => {
  if (e.detail.source === 'auto') console.log('Rate prompt result:', e.detail.result);
});

AppMint.requestReview().then((r) => {
  if (r.result === 'error') console.warn(r.message);
  if (r.result === 'not_from_play') showMessage('Rating is available once the app is installed from Google Play.');
});
```

### `setAppIcon`

```js
window.WebToApk.setAppIcon(name: String): Boolean
```

Changes the app's launcher icon to one of the alternate icons added in the build wizard, by the name given there ("default" = the normal icon). Returns false for a name this build does not have. The launcher redraws in its own time (a few seconds on some phones), and some launchers close the app or move its home-screen icon when it changes - switch from a settings screen, not in the middle of a task.

**Example**

Changes the app's launcher icon to one of the **alternate icons** you added in the build wizard (Basic step, "Alternate app icons"), by the name you gave it there. `'default'` is your normal icon.

**Returns:** `true` when the switch was made (or it is already that icon), `false` for a name this build does not have. **Needs:** alternate icons added in the wizard (up to 4). Some launchers take a few seconds to redraw the icon, and a few close the app or move its home-screen shortcut when it changes: switch from a settings screen, not in the middle of a task. Your launcher shortcuts (`setAppShortcuts`) are republished under the new icon automatically.

```js
function useIcon(name) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setAppIcon)) return false;
  const ok = WebToApk.setAppIcon(name);
  if (!ok) console.warn('no icon called', name);
  return ok;
}

document.querySelector('#darkIcon').addEventListener('click', () => useIcon('Dark'));
document.querySelector('#normalIcon').addEventListener('click', () => useIcon('default'));
```

**Build the picker from the icons this build has:**

```js
if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getAvailableIcons) {
  const names = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getAvailableIcons());   // 'default' first, then your alternates
  const current = WebToApk.getAppIcon();
  names.forEach((n) => addRadio('icon', n, n === current, () => WebToApk.setAppIcon(n)));
}
```

**Check the answer for a name the build does not have:**

```js
function pickIcon(name) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.setAppIcon)) return showMessage('Icons can be changed in the app only');
  if (!WebToApk.setAppIcon(name)) {
    showMessage('Unknown icon "' + name + '". Choose one of: ' + JSON.parse(WebToApk.getAvailableIcons()).join(', '));
  } else {
    showMessage('Done. Your launcher may take a few seconds to redraw the icon.');
  }
}
```

**Notes:** the first update that ADDS alternate icons moves the launcher entry to a new component, so a home-screen shortcut made before that update may have to be placed again.

### `setAppShortcuts`

```js
window.WebToApk.setAppShortcuts(itemsJson: String)
```

Launcher shortcuts (long-press the app icon). Up to four entries: `[{id, title, route}]`, where `route` is a path in the app ('/new-note'). A tap opens the app with that route as its launch deep link (`appmint-shortcut://<package><route>`), which the page reads through `getLaunchUrl()` and routes on exactly like any other deep link. In a Website-mode app the shell itself opens the route on the website (`/new-note` → `https://<site>/new-note`). Pass `[]` to remove them. Android 7.1+; a no-op below that.

**Example**

Sets the launcher shortcuts that appear when the user touches and holds the app icon.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing. Android 7.1+ (a no-op below that).

`itemsJson` is a JSON string: an array of up to four `{id, title, route}` objects. `route` is a path inside your app. A tap opens the app with `appmint-shortcut://<package><route>` as its launch link:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.setAppShortcuts === 'function') {
  window.WebToApk.setAppShortcuts(JSON.stringify([
    { id: 'new-note', title: 'New note', route: '/new-note' },
    { id: 'search',   title: 'Search',   route: '/search' }
  ]));
}
```

Read the tap the same way as any other deep link, on start and while running:

```js
function shortcutRoute(link) {
  var m = /^appmint-shortcut:\/\/[^\/?#]*([^#]*)/i.exec(link || '');
  return m ? (m[1] || '/') : null;
}
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getLaunchUrl) {
  var r = shortcutRoute(window.WebToApk.getLaunchUrl());
  if (r) goTo(r);
}
window.addEventListener('appmint:deep-link', function (e) {
  var r = shortcutRoute(e.detail.url);
  if (r) goTo(r);
});
```

Remove all shortcuts:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.setAppShortcuts) window.WebToApk.setAppShortcuts('[]');
```

**Notes:** Each call replaces the whole list. Entries without a `title` are skipped; the label is cut to 25 characters (50 for the long label). `id` defaults to `appmint-<index>`. A route without a leading `/` gets one. The icon is the app icon. A malformed list is ignored (logged), never thrown. AI-built apps can use `shortcuts` from `@/lib/appmintNative`. **Website-mode apps:** a tap opens the route on your website - `/new-note` loads `https://<your site>/new-note` - and `getLaunchUrl()` still returns the `appmint-shortcut://` link, so a page that routes itself keeps working.

# Contacts - JavaScript bridge API

> Reading, searching, picking and writing - the picker needs no permission at all.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/contacts

### `navigator.contacts`

```js
navigator.contacts.select(properties, options) — Contact Picker
```

**Example**

The standard Contact Picker API: the phone's own contact picker opens, and the page gets only the person the user chose - no contacts permission.

**Returns:** a Promise of an array: `[{ name: [string], tel: [string] }]`, or `[]` when the user closes the picker. **Needs:** nothing to switch on; call it from a tap (a user gesture is required, else `SecurityError`).

```js
document.getElementById('pick').addEventListener('click', async () => {
  if (!('contacts' in navigator)) { showManualEntry(); return; }
  const props = await navigator.contacts.getProperties();   // ['name', 'tel']
  const [person] = await navigator.contacts.select(props, { multiple: false });
  if (!person) return;                                       // closed without choosing
  document.getElementById('name').value = person.name[0] || '';
  document.getElementById('phone').value = person.tel[0] || '';
});
```

Fill a "Send to" box with only the number, and show a message for each way the picker can refuse:

```js
document.getElementById('choose-number').addEventListener('click', async () => {
  if (!('contacts' in navigator)) return;
  try {
    const [person] = await navigator.contacts.select(['tel']);
    if (person && person.tel.length) document.getElementById('to').value = person.tel[0];
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.name === 'InvalidStateError') showMessage('The contact picker is already open or not available.');
    else if (err.name === 'SecurityError') showMessage('Tap the button to choose a contact.');
    else showMessage('Could not pick a contact: ' + err.message);
  }
});
```

Build a guest list one tap at a time (one person per pick), skipping a number already on the list:

```js
const guests = [];

document.getElementById('add-guest').addEventListener('click', async () => {
  if (!('contacts' in navigator)) { showManualEntry(); return; }
  const [person] = await navigator.contacts.select(['name', 'tel']);
  if (!person || !person.tel.length) return;   // closed, or no number

  const number = person.tel[0];
  if (guests.some((g) => g.number === number)) { showMessage('Already invited'); return; }
  guests.push({ name: person.name[0] || number, number });
  renderGuests(guests);
});
```

**Notes:** the app supports `name` and `tel` - the number the user tapped. `email`, `address` and `icon` would need the full contacts permission, so they are not offered and asking for them rejects with `TypeError`. One person per pick (`multiple` is allowed but the Android picker returns one). Works in the top page only. For listing or searching all contacts use `WebToApk.listContacts` (needs the Contacts switch).

### `addContact`

```js
window.WebToApk.addContact(requestId: String, contactJson: String)
```

The system picker (no permission needed) and writing a new contact (WRITE_CONTACTS). The read side - listing and searching - is under the Contacts group above.

_Described by its group, Contacts: pick and add, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Saves a new contact straight into the phone's address book, without opening the Contacts app.

**Returns:** nothing now. The answer is the `appmint:contacts` event (and `window.onAppMintContacts`) with `detail = { requestId, ok: true, id: '123' }` on success, `{ requestId, ok: false, id: null }` when the save failed, or `{ requestId, error }`. **Needs:** turn on **Edit Contacts** in Step 4 (Access) when you build; the user is asked for permission on the first call.

**Save a customer.** The contact is passed as a JSON string.

```js
function saveCustomer(name, phone, email) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.addContact)) return;
  var id = 'add-' + Date.now();

  window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);

    if (e.detail.error === 'not_enabled') { showMessage('Turn on Edit Contacts when you build'); return; }
    if (e.detail.error) { showMessage('Not saved: ' + e.detail.error); return; }
    showMessage(e.detail.ok ? 'Saved to contacts' : 'Could not save the contact');
  });

  WebToApk.addContact(id, JSON.stringify({
    displayName: name,
    phones: [{ number: phone, type: 'mobile' }],   // type: mobile | home | work
    emails: [email]
  }));
}
```

**Short form.** Single values are accepted too: `{ name: 'Ali', phone: '+911234567890', email: 'ali@example.com' }`.

A "Save to contacts" button on a business card page, using the short form and a Promise:

```js
function addOne(contact) {
  return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {
    var id = 'card-' + Date.now() + '-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);
    window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
      if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
      window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);
      if (e.detail.error) reject(new Error(e.detail.error));
      else if (!e.detail.ok) reject(new Error('save_failed'));
      else resolve(e.detail.id);
    });
    WebToApk.addContact(id, JSON.stringify(contact));
  });
}

document.getElementById('save-card').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.addContact)) return;
  addOne({ name: 'Priya Sharma', phone: '+919876543210', email: 'priya@example.com' })
    .then(function () { showMessage('Priya is in your contacts now'); })
    .catch(function (err) {
      showMessage(err.message === 'permission_denied' ? 'Allow Contacts to save this card.' : 'Not saved: ' + err.message);
    });
});
```

Import a team list one person at a time, with work and home numbers, and report how many were saved:

```js
async function importTeam(team) {   // [{ name, work, home, email }]
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.addContact)) return;
  var saved = 0;
  for (var i = 0; i < team.length; i++) {
    var m = team[i];
    try {
      await addOne({   // addOne() from the example above
        displayName: m.name,
        phones: [{ number: m.work, type: 'work' }, { number: m.home, type: 'home' }],
        emails: m.email ? [m.email] : []
      });
      saved++;
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.message === 'not_enabled' || err.message === 'permission_denied') break;   // the rest would fail too
    }
  }
  showMessage(saved + ' of ' + team.length + ' saved');
}
```

**Notes:** Errors: `not_enabled`, `permission_denied`. The returned `id` is the new raw-contact id. A phone `type` other than `home` or `work` is saved as `mobile`. The contact is saved on the device (no account). Writing contacts is a sensitive permission: your Play Store listing must declare it in the Data safety form and privacy policy.

### `getContact`

```js
window.WebToApk.getContact(requestId: String, contactId: String)
```

All async: cursor reads can be thousands of rows, and a blocking @JavascriptInterface return would run that on the JS thread - an ANR. Results arrive as `appmint:contacts` / window.onAppMintContacts({requestId,...}). requestId: pass a STRING ('pick-' + Date.now()). A raw NUMBER also works - the bridge coerces it through a double ("1.787491234567E12"), and every reply canonicalizes it back (BridgeRequestId), so `res.requestId === Date.now()` strict-compares true either way.    WebToApk.listContacts(id, limit, offset)   WebToApk.searchContacts(id, query, limit)   WebToApk.getContact(id, contactId)   WebToApk.pickContact(id)      <- NO permission needed (system picker)   WebToApk.addContact(id, json) <- needs the Contacts-write permission

_Described by its group, Contacts, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Reads one contact again by its `id` (the `id` from `listContacts` or `searchContacts`).

**Returns:** nothing now. The answer is the `appmint:contacts` event (and `window.onAppMintContacts`) with `detail = { requestId, contact: { id, displayName, photoUri, phones: [{ number, type }], emails: [...] } }`. `contact` is `null` when that contact no longer exists. On failure: `{ requestId, error }`. **Needs:** turn on **Contacts** in Step 4 (Access) when you build.

**Refresh a saved contact** using the page hook instead of an event listener.

```js
var pendingId = '';

window.onAppMintContacts = function (detail) {
  if (detail.requestId !== pendingId) return;
  if (detail.error) { showMessage('Could not read the contact: ' + detail.error); return; }
  if (!detail.contact) { showMessage('This contact was deleted.'); return; }

  var c = detail.contact;
  document.getElementById('name').textContent = c.displayName;
  document.getElementById('phones').textContent =
    c.phones.map(function (p) { return p.type + ': ' + p.number; }).join(', ');
  document.getElementById('emails').textContent = c.emails.join(', ');
};

function openContact(contactId) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getContact)) return;
  pendingId = 'one-' + Date.now();
  WebToApk.getContact(pendingId, String(contactId));
}
```

Refresh a saved list of favourite contact ids and drop the ones deleted from the phone since:

```js
function getOne(contactId) {
  return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {
    var id = 'fav-' + contactId + '-' + Date.now();
    window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
      if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
      window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);
      if (e.detail.error) reject(new Error(e.detail.error)); else resolve(e.detail.contact);
    });
    WebToApk.getContact(id, String(contactId));
  });
}

async function loadFavourites() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getContact)) return;
  var ids = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('favIds') || '[]');
  var people = [];
  for (var i = 0; i < ids.length; i++) {
    var c = await getOne(ids[i]);
    if (c) people.push(c);   // null = deleted from the phone
  }
  localStorage.setItem('favIds', JSON.stringify(people.map(function (c) { return c.id; })));
  renderFavourites(people);
}
```

Check whether the number your app stored for a customer is still on their contact card:

```js
function checkStoredNumber(customer) {   // { contactId, phone }
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.getContact)) return;
  var id = 'check-' + Date.now();

  window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);
    if (e.detail.error) { showMessage('Could not check: ' + e.detail.error); return; }
    if (!e.detail.contact) { showMessage('This customer is no longer in your contacts.'); return; }

    var digits = function (s) { return String(s).replace(/\D/g, ''); };
    var still = e.detail.contact.phones.some(function (p) {
      return digits(p.number).slice(-10) === digits(customer.phone).slice(-10);
    });
    if (!still) showMessage('The number for ' + e.detail.contact.displayName + ' has changed.');
  });

  WebToApk.getContact(id, String(customer.contactId));
}
```

**Notes:** `window.onAppMintContacts` receives every contacts answer (list, search, pick, add), so always check `requestId`. You can use it or `addEventListener('appmint:contacts', ...)` - both fire. Errors: `not_enabled`, `permission_denied`, `foreign_origin`. The `id` from `pickContact` is a phone-row id, not a contact id, so it does not work here. Contacts is personal data: your Play Store listing must declare it in the Data safety form and privacy policy.

### `listContacts`

```js
window.WebToApk.listContacts(requestId: String, limit: Int, offset: Int)
```

All async: cursor reads can be thousands of rows, and a blocking @JavascriptInterface return would run that on the JS thread - an ANR. Results arrive as `appmint:contacts` / window.onAppMintContacts({requestId,...}). requestId: pass a STRING ('pick-' + Date.now()). A raw NUMBER also works - the bridge coerces it through a double ("1.787491234567E12"), and every reply canonicalizes it back (BridgeRequestId), so `res.requestId === Date.now()` strict-compares true either way.    WebToApk.listContacts(id, limit, offset)   WebToApk.searchContacts(id, query, limit)   WebToApk.getContact(id, contactId)   WebToApk.pickContact(id)      <- NO permission needed (system picker)   WebToApk.addContact(id, json) <- needs the Contacts-write permission

_Described by its group, Contacts, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Reads the phone's address book, page by page, sorted A to Z by name.

**Returns:** nothing now. The answer comes later as the `appmint:contacts` event (and `window.onAppMintContacts`) with `detail = { requestId, contacts: [{ id, displayName, photoUri, phones: [{ number, type }], emails: ['a@b.com'] }] }`, or `{ requestId, error }`. **Needs:** turn on **Contacts** in Step 4 (Access) when you build; the user is asked for permission on the first call.

**Load the first 100 contacts.** Match the answer on your own `requestId`.

```js
function loadContacts() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.listContacts)) {
    showMessage('Contacts work only inside the app.');
    return;
  }
  var id = 'contacts-' + Date.now();

  window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;   // another call's answer
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);

    if (e.detail.error) { showMessage('Could not read contacts: ' + e.detail.error); return; }

    var list = document.getElementById('list');
    list.innerHTML = '';
    e.detail.contacts.forEach(function (c) {
      var li = document.createElement('li');
      var num = c.phones.length ? c.phones[0].number + ' (' + c.phones[0].type + ')' : '';
      li.textContent = c.displayName + ' ' + num;
      list.appendChild(li);
    });
  });

  WebToApk.listContacts(id, 100, 0);   // limit 100, start at 0
}
```

**Next page.** Pass the number you already have as `offset`: `WebToApk.listContacts(id, 100, 100)`.

Load the whole address book in pages of 500 until a short page says you reached the end:

```js
function listPage(limit, offset) {
  return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {
    var id = 'page-' + offset + '-' + Date.now();
    window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
      if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
      window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);
      if (e.detail.error) reject(new Error(e.detail.error));
      else resolve(e.detail.contacts);
    });
    WebToApk.listContacts(id, limit, offset);
  });
}

async function loadEveryContact() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.listContacts)) return [];
  var all = [];
  while (true) {
    var page = await listPage(500, all.length);
    all = all.concat(page);
    if (page.length < 500) return all;   // last page
  }
}
```

Build an "Invite friends" list from mobile numbers only, and tell the user what to do when reading is refused:

```js
function showInviteList() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.listContacts)) return;
  var id = 'invite-' + Date.now();

  window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);

    if (e.detail.error === 'permission_denied') { showMessage('Allow Contacts to invite friends.'); return; }
    if (e.detail.error) { showMessage('Contacts are not available: ' + e.detail.error); return; }

    var mobiles = [];
    e.detail.contacts.forEach(function (c) {
      c.phones.forEach(function (p) {
        if (p.type === 'mobile') mobiles.push({ name: c.displayName, number: p.number });
      });
    });
    renderInviteList(mobiles);   // your own list UI
  });

  WebToApk.listContacts(id, 500, 0);
}
```

**Notes:** `limit` is clamped to 1-2000. Errors: `not_enabled` (Contacts was off at build time), `permission_denied` (the user said No), `foreign_origin` (called from a page that is not your app's own). Phone `type` is `home`, `mobile`, `work`, `main`, `work_fax`, `home_fax` or `other`. `photoUri` is a `content://` address, not an image URL a page can load. To let the user choose just one person, use `pickContact` instead - it needs no permission. Contacts is personal data: your Play Store listing must declare it in the Data safety form and privacy policy.

### `pickContact`

```js
window.WebToApk.pickContact(requestId: String)
```

System contact picker - needs NO permission, and is the right choice whenever the page just wants the user to choose one person. Picks from the PHONE table, not the contact table: the picker grants read access only to the row it returns, so picking a phone row is what makes the number readable without READ_CONTACTS. Picking a bare contact would return a row with a name and no number, and reading the number from it would need the permission this method exists to avoid.

**Example**

Opens Android's own contact picker so the user chooses one phone number. No permission is needed.

**Returns:** nothing now. The answer is the `appmint:contacts` event (and `window.onAppMintContacts`) with `detail = { requestId, contact: { id, displayName, photoUri, phones: [{ number, type: 'picked' }], emails: [] } }`. If the user closes the picker: `{ requestId, error: 'cancelled' }`. **Needs:** nothing - no build switch, no permission prompt.

**Fill a form with the chosen person.**

```js
function chooseContact() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.pickContact)) {
    showMessage('Open this page in the app to pick a contact.');
    return;
  }
  var id = 'pick-' + Date.now();

  window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);

    if (e.detail.error === 'cancelled') return;              // user closed the picker
    if (e.detail.error) { showMessage('Could not open contacts'); return; }
    if (!e.detail.contact) { showMessage('Could not read that contact'); return; }

    var c = e.detail.contact;
    document.getElementById('name').value = c.displayName;
    document.getElementById('phone').value = c.phones.length ? c.phones[0].number : '';
  });

  WebToApk.pickContact(id);
}
```

Keep a short list of emergency contacts. Save the name and number, not the `id`, so the list does not depend on the address book:

```js
function pickOne() {
  return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {
    var id = 'sos-' + Date.now();
    window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
      if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
      window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);
      if (e.detail.error === 'cancelled') resolve(null);
      else if (e.detail.error) reject(new Error(e.detail.error));
      else resolve(e.detail.contact);
    });
    WebToApk.pickContact(id);
  });
}

document.getElementById('add-sos').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.pickContact)) return;
  var c = await pickOne();
  if (!c || !c.phones.length) return;   // closed, or nothing readable
  var list = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('sos') || '[]');
  list.push({ name: c.displayName, number: c.phones[0].number });
  localStorage.setItem('sos', JSON.stringify(list));
  renderSosList(list);
});
```

Disable the button while the picker is open, and show the typing fields when the phone has no contacts app:

```js
var pickBtn = document.getElementById('pick');

pickBtn.addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.pickContact)) { showManualEntry(); return; }
  var id = 'recipient-' + Date.now();
  pickBtn.disabled = true;   // one picker at a time

  window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);
    pickBtn.disabled = false;

    if (e.detail.error === 'no_picker') { showManualEntry(); return; }
    if (e.detail.error) return;   // 'cancelled'
    if (e.detail.contact && e.detail.contact.phones.length) {
      document.getElementById('to').value = e.detail.contact.phones[0].number;
    }
  });

  WebToApk.pickContact(id);
});
```

**Notes:** You get the name and the ONE number the user tapped - never emails, never the rest of the book. `emails` is always empty. Errors: `cancelled`, `no_picker` (no contacts app on the phone). If the read fails after a pick, `contact` is `null`. Because nothing is read without the user's choice, this is the Play-friendly way to get a phone number; prefer it over `listContacts` when you only need one person. For AI-built apps and Google AI Studio imports the build scans your code; a `pickContact(` call does not tick **Contacts** - only `listContacts`, `searchContacts` and `getContact` do - so the picker adds no contacts-read permission.

### `searchContacts`

```js
window.WebToApk.searchContacts(requestId: String, query: String, limit: Int)
```

All async: cursor reads can be thousands of rows, and a blocking @JavascriptInterface return would run that on the JS thread - an ANR. Results arrive as `appmint:contacts` / window.onAppMintContacts({requestId,...}). requestId: pass a STRING ('pick-' + Date.now()). A raw NUMBER also works - the bridge coerces it through a double ("1.787491234567E12"), and every reply canonicalizes it back (BridgeRequestId), so `res.requestId === Date.now()` strict-compares true either way.    WebToApk.listContacts(id, limit, offset)   WebToApk.searchContacts(id, query, limit)   WebToApk.getContact(id, contactId)   WebToApk.pickContact(id)      <- NO permission needed (system picker)   WebToApk.addContact(id, json) <- needs the Contacts-write permission

_Described by its group, Contacts, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Finds contacts whose name matches a search word, without loading the whole address book.

**Returns:** nothing now. The answer is the `appmint:contacts` event (and `window.onAppMintContacts`) with `detail = { requestId, contacts: [...] }` - the same contact shape as `listContacts` - or `{ requestId, error }`. **Needs:** turn on **Contacts** in Step 4 (Access) when you build; the user is asked for permission on the first call.

**Search as the user types.** Only the answer to the latest search is shown.

```js
var lastSearchId = '';

function searchPeople(word) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.searchContacts)) return;
  lastSearchId = 'search-' + Date.now();
  WebToApk.searchContacts(lastSearchId, word, 20);   // at most 20 results
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function (e) {
  if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== lastSearchId) return;   // old or other request
  if (e.detail.error) { showMessage('Search failed: ' + e.detail.error); return; }

  var names = e.detail.contacts.map(function (c) {
    return c.displayName + (c.phones.length ? ' - ' + c.phones[0].number : '');
  });
  document.getElementById('results').textContent = names.join('\n') || 'No match';
});

document.getElementById('q').addEventListener('input', function (e) {
  searchPeople(e.target.value);
});
```

Wrap the search in a Promise and wait until the user stops typing, so fast typing does not start a search per key:

```js
function searchOnce(word, limit) {
  return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {
    var id = 'find-' + Date.now() + '-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);
    window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
      if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
      window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);
      if (e.detail.error) reject(new Error(e.detail.error)); else resolve(e.detail.contacts);
    });
    WebToApk.searchContacts(id, word, limit);
  });
}

var timer = null;
document.getElementById('q').addEventListener('input', function (e) {
  clearTimeout(timer);
  var word = e.target.value.trim();
  timer = setTimeout(function () {
    if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.searchContacts) || !word) return;
    searchOnce(word, 10)
      .then(function (people) { renderSuggestions(people); })
      .catch(function (err) { showMessage('Search failed: ' + err.message); });
  }, 300);
});
```

Fill the email box from the address book when the typed name matches one person who has an email:

```js
function suggestEmail(name) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.searchContacts) || name.length < 2) return;
  var id = 'email-' + Date.now();

  window.addEventListener('appmint:contacts', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:contacts', handler);
    if (e.detail.error) return;   // leave the box for the user to type

    var withEmail = e.detail.contacts.filter(function (c) { return c.emails.length > 0; });
    if (withEmail.length === 1) {
      document.getElementById('email').value = withEmail[0].emails[0];
    }
  });

  WebToApk.searchContacts(id, name, 5);
}

document.getElementById('name').addEventListener('change', function (e) {
  suggestEmail(e.target.value.trim());
});
```

**Notes:** An empty search word returns contacts from the start of the list (like `listContacts`). `limit` is clamped to 1-2000 and there is no offset. Errors: `not_enabled`, `permission_denied`, `foreign_origin`. Contacts is personal data: your Play Store listing must declare it in the Data safety form and privacy policy.

# Phone, SMS and the call log - JavaScript bridge API

> Placing a call, sending or drafting a message, and reading history. Every one of these is permission-gated and Play asks about them.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/telephony

### `composeSms`

```js
window.WebToApk.composeSms(phoneNumber: String, message: String): Boolean
```

Opens the user's SMS app with the message prefilled. Needs no permission and cannot be rejected by Play - the right default for anything non-automated. Returns false when the phone has no SMS app (or it could not be opened).

**Example**

Opens the user's SMS app with the number and the text already filled in. The user presses send.

**Returns:** `true` when the SMS app opened, `false` when the phone has no SMS app or it could not be opened (synchronous). **Needs:** nothing - no build switch, no permission.

**A "Text us" button.**

```js
document.getElementById('textUs').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.composeSms) {
    var ok = WebToApk.composeSms('+911234567890', 'Hello, I need help with my order');
    if (!ok) showMessage('Could not open the SMS app.');
  } else {
    // In a normal browser the standard sms: link does the same job.
    location.href = 'sms:+911234567890?body=' + encodeURIComponent('Hello, I need help with my order');
  }
});
```

A "Remind" button on each appointment row, prefilling a reminder to that customer's number:

```js
document.getElementById('appointments').addEventListener('click', function (e) {
  var row = e.target.closest('[data-phone]');
  if (!row || !(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.composeSms === 'function')) return;
  var when = new Date(Number(row.getAttribute('data-time')));
  var text = 'Hi ' + row.getAttribute('data-name') + ', a reminder of your appointment on ' +
             when.toLocaleDateString() + ' at ' +
             when.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' }) + '.';
  if (!WebToApk.composeSms(row.getAttribute('data-phone'), text)) {
    showMessage('This phone has no SMS app.');
  }
});
```

A "Send by SMS" form: when the phone has no SMS app (`false`), copy the text so the user can paste it elsewhere:

```js
document.getElementById('smsForm').addEventListener('submit', function (e) {
  e.preventDefault();
  var number = document.getElementById('to').value.trim();
  var text = document.getElementById('message').value;
  if (!number || !text) return;

  var opened = window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.composeSms === 'function' &&
               WebToApk.composeSms(number, text);
  if (!opened && navigator.clipboard) {
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(function () {
      showMessage('No SMS app here. The message was copied instead.');
    });
  }
});
```

**Notes:** Nothing is sent until the user taps send in their own SMS app, so this method itself needs no SMS permission. Use this for every message the user writes or approves; use `sendSms` only when the app really must send by itself. For AI-built apps and Google AI Studio imports the build scans your code; a `composeSms(` call does not tick **SMS (read & send)** - only `sendSms` and `listSms` do - so a "Text us" button adds no Play-restricted permission.

### `listCallLog`

```js
window.WebToApk.listCallLog(requestId: String, limit: Int, offset: Int, sinceMillis: String)
```

WebToApk.listCallLog(id, limit, offset, sinceMillis) Delivered as `appmint:calllog` / window.onAppMintCallLog.

_Described by its group, Call log, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Reads the phone's call history, newest call first.

**Returns:** nothing now. The answer is the `appmint:calllog` event (and `window.onAppMintCallLog`) with `detail = { requestId, calls: [{ number, name, type, date, duration }] }` or `{ requestId, error }`. `date` is milliseconds since 1970; `duration` is seconds. **Needs:** turn on **Call log (read)** in Step 4 (Access) when you build; the user is asked for permission on the first call.

**Show the last 50 calls.**

```js
function loadCalls() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.listCallLog)) return;
  var id = 'calls-' + Date.now();

  window.addEventListener('appmint:calllog', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:calllog', handler);
    if (e.detail.error) { showMessage('Call log: ' + e.detail.error); return; }

    e.detail.calls.forEach(function (c) {
      // c.type: incoming | outgoing | missed | voicemail | rejected | blocked | other
      addRow((c.name || c.number) + ' - ' + c.type + ' - ' +
             new Date(c.date).toLocaleString() + ' - ' + c.duration + 's');
    });
  });

  WebToApk.listCallLog(id, 50, 0, '0');   // limit, offset, since (string)
}
```

**Only calls from the last 24 hours**, using the page hook. `sinceMillis` is a STRING because the number is too big for the bridge's int.

```js
window.onAppMintCallLog = function (detail) {
  if (detail.requestId !== 'today') return;
  if (detail.error) return;
  document.getElementById('count').textContent = detail.calls.length + ' calls today';
};

if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.listCallLog) {
  WebToApk.listCallLog('today', 500, 0, String(Date.now() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
}
```

A call-history screen with a "Load more" button, fetching 25 calls at a time with `offset`:

```js
var PAGE = 25, loaded = 0;

function loadMoreCalls() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.listCallLog === 'function')) return;
  var id = 'page-' + loaded;

  window.addEventListener('appmint:calllog', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:calllog', handler);
    if (e.detail.error) { showMessage('Call log: ' + e.detail.error); return; }

    e.detail.calls.forEach(function (c) { addRow(c.name || c.number, c.type, c.date); });
    loaded += e.detail.calls.length;
    document.getElementById('more').hidden = e.detail.calls.length < PAGE;   // last page
  });

  WebToApk.listCallLog(id, PAGE, loaded, '0');   // skip the calls already shown
}

document.getElementById('more').addEventListener('click', loadMoreCalls);
loadMoreCalls();
```

**Notes:** `limit` is clamped to 1-2000. Errors: `not_enabled`, `permission_denied`, `foreign_origin`. Call log is a Google Play restricted permission: you must file an approved Permissions Declaration in Play Console, or the app is rejected.

### `listSms`

```js
window.WebToApk.listSms(requestId: String, box: String, limit: Int, offset: Int)
```

WebToApk.composeSms(number, message)   <- NO permission, opens the SMS app   WebToApk.sendSms(id, number, message, wantDelivery)   WebToApk.listSms(id, "inbox"|"sent"|"draft", limit, offset) Send results: `appmint:sms` / window.onAppMintSms   {requestId, status:"sent"|"delivered"|"failed", ok, reason?} Inbound messages: `appmint:sms-received` / window.onAppMintSmsReceived.

_Described by its group, SMS, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Reads SMS messages from the phone's inbox, sent box or drafts, newest first. This file also shows how to receive new messages as they arrive.

**Returns:** nothing now. The answer is the `appmint:sms` event (and `window.onAppMintSms`) with `detail = { requestId, messages: [{ id, address, body, date, read, box }] }`. On failure: `{ requestId, status: 'failed', ok: false, reason }`. **Needs:** turn on **SMS (read & send)** in Step 4 (Access) when you build; the user is asked for permission on the first call.

**Read the latest 30 inbox messages.**

```js
function loadInbox() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.listSms)) return;
  var id = 'inbox-' + Date.now();

  window.addEventListener('appmint:sms', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:sms', handler);
    if (e.detail.status === 'failed') { showMessage('Cannot read SMS: ' + e.detail.reason); return; }

    e.detail.messages.forEach(function (m) {
      addRow(m.address + ': ' + m.body + (m.read ? '' : ' (new)') +
             ' - ' + new Date(m.date).toLocaleString());
    });
  });

  WebToApk.listSms(id, 'inbox', 30, 0);   // box: 'inbox' | 'sent' | 'draft'
}
```

**New messages as they arrive** (`appmint:sms-received`, also `window.onAppMintSmsReceived`). Messages that arrive while the app is closed are kept (the last 50) and given to your page when the app opens again.

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:sms-received', function (e) {
  // e.detail = { address: '+91...', body: 'Your OTP is 4821', date: 1737000000000 }
  var code = (e.detail.body.match(/\b\d{4,6}\b/) || [])[0];
  if (code) document.getElementById('otp').value = code;
});

// or, as a page hook:
window.onAppMintSmsReceived = function (sms) {
  console.log('SMS from ' + sms.address);
};
```

An expense tracker that scans the last 200 inbox messages for bank debits and adds up the amounts:

```js
function scanSpending() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.listSms === 'function')) return;
  var id = 'spend-' + Date.now();

  window.addEventListener('appmint:sms', function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    window.removeEventListener('appmint:sms', handler);
    if (e.detail.status === 'failed') { showMessage('Cannot read SMS: ' + e.detail.reason); return; }

    var total = 0;
    e.detail.messages.forEach(function (m) {
      if (!/debited/i.test(m.body)) return;
      var amount = m.body.match(/(?:Rs\.?|INR)\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d{1,2})?)/i);
      if (amount) total += parseFloat(amount[1].replace(/,/g, ''));
    });
    document.getElementById('spent').textContent = 'Spent: Rs ' + total.toFixed(2);
  });

  WebToApk.listSms(id, 'inbox', 200, 0);
}
```

**Notes:** `limit` is clamped to 1-500. Any unknown box name reads the inbox. `reason` values: `not_enabled`, `permission_denied`, `foreign_origin`. Received messages still reach the user's normal SMS app too. SMS is a Google Play restricted permission: you must file an approved Permissions Declaration in Play Console (usually only default SMS apps qualify), or the app is rejected.

### `makePhoneCall`

```js
window.WebToApk.makePhoneCall(phoneNumber: String)
```

Calls [phoneNumber]. - Phone permission ON in the build: places the call directly. The first time, Android asks the user for the Phone permission; if they refuse, the dialer opens with the number filled in so they can still place it themselves. - Phone permission OFF: opens the dialer with the number filled in (the dialer needs no permission) and the user taps Call. - A page that is not the app's own (an external site open in the app) always gets the dialer, never a direct call. A plain `tel:` link in your HTML also opens the dialer and is often enough.

**Example**

Starts a phone call to a number, or opens the dialer with the number filled in.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing to open the dialer. Turn on **Phone** in Step 4 (Access) when you build if the call should start directly.

**A "Call the shop" button.**

```js
document.getElementById('callShop').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.makePhoneCall) {
    WebToApk.makePhoneCall('+911234567890');
  }
});
```

**No switch needed: a plain `tel:` link** opens the dialer with the number, in the app and in a browser. This is often all you need.

```html
<a href="tel:+911234567890">Call the shop</a>
```

One handler for a whole staff directory, where each row carries its number in a `data-phone` attribute:

```js
document.getElementById('staffList').addEventListener('click', function (e) {
  var btn = e.target.closest('[data-phone]');
  if (!btn) return;
  var number = btn.getAttribute('data-phone').replace(/[^\d+]/g, '');   // keep digits and +
  if (!number) return;
  if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.makePhoneCall === 'function') {
    WebToApk.makePhoneCall(number);
  } else {
    location.href = 'tel:' + number;   // a normal browser
  }
});
```

**Notes:** With **Phone** off, the dialer opens with the number and the user presses call. With **Phone** on, the call starts directly; the first time, Android asks the user for the phone-call permission, and if they refuse, the dialer opens instead so they can still place the call. A page that is not the app's own (an external site open inside the app) always gets the dialer. Pass the number as a plain string. Nothing is reported back - you cannot know if the call was placed. The Phone switch adds the CALL_PHONE permission to your Play listing; declare it in the Data safety form and only turn it on if you need it.

### `sendSms`

```js
window.WebToApk.sendSms(
```

WebToApk.composeSms(number, message)   <- NO permission, opens the SMS app   WebToApk.sendSms(id, number, message, wantDelivery)   WebToApk.listSms(id, "inbox"|"sent"|"draft", limit, offset) Send results: `appmint:sms` / window.onAppMintSms   {requestId, status:"sent"|"delivered"|"failed", ok, reason?} Inbound messages: `appmint:sms-received` / window.onAppMintSmsReceived.

_Described by its group, SMS, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Sends an SMS directly from the app, without opening the SMS app, and reports what really happened.

**Returns:** nothing now. The answer is the `appmint:sms` event (and `window.onAppMintSms`) with `detail = { requestId, status: 'sent' | 'delivered' | 'failed', ok, reason? }`. With a delivery report you get TWO answers on success: `sent`, then `delivered`. **Needs:** turn on **SMS (read & send)** in Step 4 (Access) when you build; the user is asked for permission on the first call.

**Send a code and follow its status.** Do not remove the listener after the first answer when you asked for a delivery report.

```js
function sendCode(phone, code) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.sendSms)) {
    showMessage('Sending SMS works only inside the app.');
    return;
  }
  var id = 'sms-' + Date.now();

  function handler(e) {
    if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
    var d = e.detail;
    if (d.status === 'sent' && d.reason === 'no_delivery_report') {
      showStatus('Sent (the network gave no delivery report)');
      window.removeEventListener('appmint:sms', handler);
    } else if (d.status === 'sent') {
      showStatus('Sent');
    } else if (d.status === 'delivered') {
      showStatus('Delivered');
      window.removeEventListener('appmint:sms', handler);
    } else {                                   // 'failed'
      showStatus('Failed: ' + d.reason);
      window.removeEventListener('appmint:sms', handler);
    }
  }
  window.addEventListener('appmint:sms', handler);

  WebToApk.sendSms(id, phone, 'Your code is ' + code, true);   // true = delivery report
}
```

**No delivery report.** Pass `false` as the last value: you get exactly one answer, `sent` or `failed`.

```js
window.onAppMintSms = function (d) {
  if (d.requestId === 'alert-1') showStatus(d.ok ? 'Alert sent' : 'Failed: ' + d.reason);
};
if (window.WebToApk && window.WebToApk.sendSms) {
  WebToApk.sendSms('alert-1', '+911234567890', 'Gate opened at ' + new Date().toLocaleTimeString(), false);
}
```

The same notice to a short list of numbers, one after another, collecting each result (and stopping when SMS is off or refused, because every other number would fail the same way):

```js
function sendToAll(numbers, text, done) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.sendSms === 'function')) { done(null); return; }
  var results = [], i = 0;

  function next() {
    if (i >= numbers.length) { done(results); return; }
    var number = numbers[i++];
    var id = 'notice-' + Date.now() + '-' + i;

    window.addEventListener('appmint:sms', function handler(e) {
      if (!e.detail || e.detail.requestId !== id) return;
      window.removeEventListener('appmint:sms', handler);
      results.push({ number: number, ok: e.detail.ok, reason: e.detail.reason });
      var r = e.detail.reason;
      if (r === 'not_enabled' || r === 'permission_denied' || r === 'foreign_origin') done(results);
      else next();
    });
    WebToApk.sendSms(id, number, text, false);   // one answer per number
  }
  next();
}

sendToAll(['+911234567890', '+919876543210'], 'Practice moved to 6 pm today.', function (results) {
  if (!results) return showMessage('Sending SMS works only inside the app.');
  showStatus(results.filter(function (r) { return r.ok; }).length + ' of ' + results.length + ' sent');
});
```

**Notes:** Long text is split into parts and sent as one message. If no delivery report arrives within 60 seconds you get `status: 'sent'` with `reason: 'no_delivery_report'` - the message was still sent. `reason` values: `not_enabled`, `permission_denied`, `foreign_origin`, `invalid_arguments` (empty number or text), `no_service`, `radio_off`, `generic_failure`, `null_pdu`, `not_delivered`, and others. Use a string `requestId`. Each SMS may cost the user money. SMS is a Google Play restricted permission: you must file an approved Permissions Declaration in Play Console (usually only default SMS apps qualify), so prefer `composeSms` when the user can press send.
