# Web Bluetooth - JavaScript bridge API

> The navigator.bluetooth shape, answered natively so a page written for Chrome works unchanged.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/webbluetooth

### `navigator.bluetooth`

```js
navigator.bluetooth — Web Bluetooth
```

**Example**

Standard Web Bluetooth: the same `navigator.bluetooth` code you would write for Chrome works in the installed app, for any Bluetooth Low Energy device.

**Returns:** Promises, as in the web standard. Values are `DataView`s. **Needs:** Bluetooth. There is no switch: when you build from a ZIP or an HTML page, the build turns it on by itself if your code mentions `navigator.bluetooth` (or `BluetoothUUID`). A website (URL) build cannot turn it on. Without it, `navigator.bluetooth` does not exist. The first `requestDevice()` asks for the Nearby devices permission (Location on Android 11 and older). If Bluetooth is switched off, the app asks the user to turn it on and then opens the device list by itself; on Android 6 to 11 it does the same for the Location setting, because those versions find no Bluetooth device while Location is off.

**Heart-rate strap, from a button tap.** `navigator.bluetooth` exists before your first script runs, so feature detection at the top of the page works; checking inside the handler, as here, is still the safest habit:

```js
var hrDevice = null;

document.getElementById('connect').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!navigator.bluetooth) { showStatus('Bluetooth is not available in this app.'); return; }
  try {
    hrDevice = await navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice({
      filters: [{ services: ['heart_rate'] }],        // or { name: 'Polar H10' } / { namePrefix: 'Polar' }
      optionalServices: ['battery_service']
    });
    hrDevice.addEventListener('gattserverdisconnected', function () {
      showStatus('Strap disconnected');
    });
    var server = await hrDevice.gatt.connect();
    var hr = await server.getPrimaryService('heart_rate');
    var chr = await hr.getCharacteristic('heart_rate_measurement');
    chr.addEventListener('characteristicvaluechanged', function (e) {
      var v = e.target.value;                                   // DataView
      var bpm = (v.getUint8(0) & 1) ? v.getUint16(1, true) : v.getUint8(1);
      document.getElementById('bpm').textContent = bpm;
    });
    await chr.startNotifications();

    var battery = await server.getPrimaryService('battery_service');
    var level = await (await battery.getCharacteristic('battery_level')).readValue();
    document.getElementById('battery').textContent = level.getUint8(0) + '%';
  } catch (err) {
    // NotFoundError: user cancelled the chooser, Bluetooth is off, or no such service.
    // SecurityError: permission denied.  NetworkError: connection lost.
    showStatus(err.name + ': ' + err.message);
  }
});

document.getElementById('disconnect').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (hrDevice && hrDevice.gatt.connected) hrDevice.gatt.disconnect();
});
```

**Writing.** `writeValue` and `writeValueWithResponse` wait for the device to confirm; `writeValueWithoutResponse` does not:

```js
async function sendCommands(server) {
  // Heart Rate Control Point: 0x01 = reset energy expended
  var hr = await server.getPrimaryService('heart_rate');
  var ctrl = await hr.getCharacteristic('heart_rate_control_point');
  await ctrl.writeValueWithResponse(new Uint8Array([0x01]));

  // A custom UART-style service (full 128-bit UUIDs work everywhere)
  var uart = await server.getPrimaryService('6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e');
  var rx = await uart.getCharacteristic('6e400002-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e');
  await rx.writeValueWithoutResponse(new TextEncoder().encode('LED ON\n'));
}
```

**Device explorer.** Pick any nearby device and list every service and characteristic it has, with what each one can do:

```js
document.getElementById('explore').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!navigator.bluetooth) { showStatus('Bluetooth is not available in this app.'); return; }
  try {
    var device = await navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice({ acceptAllDevices: true });
    var server = await device.gatt.connect();
    var lines = [];
    for (var service of await server.getPrimaryServices()) {
      lines.push(service.uuid === BluetoothUUID.getService('battery_service') ? 'Battery' : service.uuid);
      var chars = await service.getCharacteristics().catch(function () { return []; });
      chars.forEach(function (c) {
        var can = Object.keys(c.properties).filter(function (k) { return c.properties[k]; });
        lines.push('  ' + c.uuid + '  ' + can.join(', '));
      });
    }
    document.getElementById('tree').textContent = lines.join('\n');
    device.gatt.disconnect();
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus(err.name + ': ' + err.message);
  }
});
```

**Cycling speed and cadence sensor.** One sensor (or a separate speed and cadence pair) on the standard CSC service. The values are running totals, so speed and cadence come from the difference between two notifications:

```js
var WHEEL_MM = 2105;                       // 700x25c; set your own wheel circumference
var last = null;

async function connectCsc() {
  var device = await navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice({
    filters: [{ services: ['cycling_speed_and_cadence'] }]      // same as { services: [0x1816] }
  });
  device.addEventListener('gattserverdisconnected', function () { showStatus('Sensor disconnected'); });
  var server = await device.gatt.connect();
  var csc = await server.getPrimaryService('cycling_speed_and_cadence');
  var chr = await csc.getCharacteristic('csc_measurement');
  chr.addEventListener('characteristicvaluechanged', function (e) {
    var v = e.target.value, flags = v.getUint8(0), i = 1, now = {};
    if (flags & 1) { now.wheels = v.getUint32(i, true); now.wheelTime = v.getUint16(i + 4, true); i += 6; }
    if (flags & 2) { now.cranks = v.getUint16(i, true); now.crankTime = v.getUint16(i + 2, true); }
    if (last) {
      if (now.wheels !== undefined && now.wheelTime !== last.wheelTime) {
        var dt = ((now.wheelTime - last.wheelTime) & 0xffff) / 1024;          // seconds
        var kmh = (now.wheels - last.wheels) * WHEEL_MM / 1e6 / (dt / 3600);
        document.getElementById('speed').textContent = kmh.toFixed(1) + ' km/h';
      }
      if (now.cranks !== undefined && now.crankTime !== last.crankTime) {
        var ct = ((now.crankTime - last.crankTime) & 0xffff) / 1024;
        var rpm = ((now.cranks - last.cranks) & 0xffff) / ct * 60;
        document.getElementById('cadence').textContent = Math.round(rpm) + ' rpm';
      }
    }
    last = Object.assign({}, last, now);
  });
  await chr.startNotifications();
}
```

**Showing every failure on screen.** Each step rejects with a named error, so the page can tell the user what to do instead of staying silent:

```js
async function connectWithMessage(connect) {
  try {
    await connect();
    showStatus('Connected');
  } catch (err) {
    var msg = {
      NotFoundError: 'No sensor chosen, Bluetooth was left off, or the sensor lacks that service.',
      SecurityError: 'Bluetooth permission was refused. Allow "Nearby devices" in the app settings.',
      NetworkError: 'The sensor went out of range or is connected to another app or watch. Try again.',
      TypeError: 'Programming error: ' + err.message
    }[err.name] || err.message;
    showStatus(err.name + ': ' + msg);
  }
}
document.getElementById('scan-hr').addEventListener('click', function () { connectWithMessage(connectHeartRate); });
document.getElementById('scan-csc').addEventListener('click', function () { connectWithMessage(connectCsc); });
```

**Notes:** The device chooser is drawn by the app and scans for 30 seconds, then offers "Scan again"; a page can only reach a device the user picked. `getAvailability()` answers whether the phone has Bluetooth at all (as in Chrome), not whether it is switched on: `requestDevice()` asks to turn it on. A sensor that sends its name only in its scan response is still listed by name and matches `namePrefix`. A first connection that Android drops at once is retried before `connect()` rejects. A misspelt service name in `filters` or `optionalServices` rejects with `TypeError`. A `services` filter matches only services the device advertises. After `connect()` every service the device has can be used, even ones not in `optionalServices` (keep them anyway, Chrome needs them). Also available: `getAvailability()`, `getPrimaryServices()`, `getCharacteristics()`, `stopNotifications()`, `characteristic.properties`, `device.forget()`, `BluetoothUUID.getService/getCharacteristic/canonicalUUID`. `getDevices()`, `requestLEScan()`, `watchAdvertisements()` and descriptors reject with `NotSupportedError`. For the standard fitness sensors with the numbers already parsed, see `bleStartScan`.

### `wbConnect`

```js
window.WebToApk.wbConnect(requestId: String, deviceId: String)
```

Raw transport for WebBluetoothPolyfill. A page never calls these directly - it calls navigator.bluetooth, exactly as it would in a browser.

_Described by its group, Web Bluetooth (navigator.bluetooth), rather than on its own._

**Example**

Internal transport behind `device.gatt.connect()`. Pages use `navigator.bluetooth`; do not call this directly.

**Returns:** (through `gatt.connect()`) a Promise of the `BluetoothRemoteGATTServer`, after the device's services are discovered. **Needs:** Bluetooth (turned on by a ZIP or HTML build when your code mentions `navigator.bluetooth`).

```js
async function connectAndList(device) {
  try {
    var server = await device.gatt.connect();
    var services = await server.getPrimaryServices();
    services.forEach(function (s) { console.log('service', s.uuid); });
    return server;
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus('Could not connect: ' + err.message);    // NetworkError, NotFoundError
    return null;
  }
}
```

**Reconnect when the device drops.** Calling `connect()` again on the same device works:

```js
device.addEventListener('gattserverdisconnected', async function () {
  showStatus('Reconnecting...');
  try { await connectAndList(device); showStatus('Connected'); } catch (e) {}
});
```

Connect to two sensors at the same time, for example a heart-rate strap and a power meter:

```js
async function connectBoth(hrDevice, powerDevice) {
  var servers = await Promise.all([hrDevice.gatt.connect(), powerDevice.gatt.connect()]);
  var hr = await servers[0].getPrimaryService('heart_rate');
  var power = await servers[1].getPrimaryService('cycling_power');
  return {
    heartRate: await hr.getCharacteristic('heart_rate_measurement'),
    power: await power.getCharacteristic('cycling_power_measurement')
  };
}
```

**Notes:** Raw signature `wbConnect(requestId, deviceId)`. Connecting to a device that is already connected resolves again at once. `getPrimaryService(s)` rejects with `NetworkError` before `connect()` has finished. Several devices can be connected at the same time.

### `wbDisconnect`

```js
window.WebToApk.wbDisconnect(deviceId: String)
```

Raw transport for WebBluetoothPolyfill. A page never calls these directly - it calls navigator.bluetooth, exactly as it would in a browser.

_Described by its group, Web Bluetooth (navigator.bluetooth), rather than on its own._

**Example**

Internal transport behind `device.gatt.disconnect()` (and `device.forget()`). Pages use `navigator.bluetooth`; do not call this directly.

**Returns:** nothing (`disconnect()` is synchronous, as in the web standard). The device then fires `gattserverdisconnected`. **Needs:** Bluetooth (turned on by a ZIP or HTML build when your code mentions `navigator.bluetooth`).

```js
var device = null;   // from navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice(...)

document.getElementById('stop').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (device && device.gatt.connected) device.gatt.disconnect();
});

// Fires for your own disconnect() and when the device goes away by itself.
function watch(dev) {
  dev.addEventListener('gattserverdisconnected', function () {
    showStatus('Disconnected from ' + (dev.name || dev.id));
  });
}
```

Tell your own Stop apart from the sensor going out of range, and reconnect only in the second case:

```js
var userStopped = false;

function stopSession(device) {
  userStopped = true;
  if (device.gatt.connected) device.gatt.disconnect();
}

function watchDrops(device) {
  device.addEventListener('gattserverdisconnected', function () {
    if (userStopped) { userStopped = false; showStatus('Session ended'); return; }
    showStatus('Sensor out of range, reconnecting...');
    device.gatt.connect()
      .then(resubscribe)                 // your code: get the characteristics, startNotifications()
      .catch(function () { showStatus('Could not reconnect'); });
  });
}
```

A "Remove sensor" button: `forget()` disconnects and drops the device, and no `gattserverdisconnected` follows it:

```js
var device = null;   // from navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice(...)

document.getElementById('forget').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!device) return;
  await device.forget();
  device = null;
  showStatus('Sensor removed. Tap Connect to pick one again.');
});
```

**Notes:** Raw signature `wbDisconnect(deviceId)`. After a disconnect the old service and characteristic objects stop receiving notifications; after the next `connect()`, get them again and call `startNotifications()` again. The app drops every connection when it closes.

### `wbGetCharacteristics`

```js
window.WebToApk.wbGetCharacteristics(requestId: String, deviceId: String, service: String)
```

Raw transport for WebBluetoothPolyfill. A page never calls these directly - it calls navigator.bluetooth, exactly as it would in a browser.

_Described by its group, Web Bluetooth (navigator.bluetooth), rather than on its own._

**Example**

Internal transport behind `service.getCharacteristic(uuid)` and `service.getCharacteristics()`. Pages use `navigator.bluetooth`; do not call this directly.

**Returns:** (through the service) a Promise of one `BluetoothRemoteGATTCharacteristic`, or of an array of them, each with `uuid` and `properties` (`read`, `write`, `writeWithoutResponse`, `notify`, `indicate`, `broadcast`, `authenticatedSignedWrites`). **Needs:** Bluetooth (turned on by a ZIP or HTML build when your code mentions `navigator.bluetooth`).

```js
async function describe(server) {
  var service = await server.getPrimaryService('heart_rate');

  // One characteristic, by standard name, 16-bit number or full UUID:
  var measurement = await service.getCharacteristic('heart_rate_measurement'); // same as 0x2a37

  // All of them:
  var list = await service.getCharacteristics();
  list.forEach(function (c) {
    var p = c.properties;
    console.log(c.uuid, p.read ? 'read' : '', p.write ? 'write' : '', p.notify ? 'notify' : '');
  });
  return measurement;
}
```

Find the characteristics of a custom service by what they can do, instead of hard-coding their UUIDs:

```js
async function findSerialPipes(server) {
  var svc = await server.getPrimaryService('0000ffe0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb');
  var list = await svc.getCharacteristics();
  var incoming = list.find(function (c) { return c.properties.notify || c.properties.indicate; });
  var outgoing = list.find(function (c) { return c.properties.write || c.properties.writeWithoutResponse; });
  if (!incoming || !outgoing) throw new Error('This device does not look like a serial adapter');
  return { incoming: incoming, outgoing: outgoing };
}
```

Read an optional characteristic and treat `NotFoundError` as "this device does not have it":

```js
var LOCATIONS = ['Other', 'Chest', 'Wrist', 'Finger', 'Hand', 'Ear lobe', 'Foot'];

async function sensorLocation(server) {
  var hr = await server.getPrimaryService('heart_rate');
  try {
    var chr = await hr.getCharacteristic('body_sensor_location');   // 0x2a38, optional in the spec
    var v = await chr.readValue();
    return LOCATIONS[v.getUint8(0)] || 'Unknown';
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.name === 'NotFoundError') return null;                   // this strap does not report it
    throw err;
  }
}
```

**Notes:** Raw signature `wbGetCharacteristics(requestId, deviceId, service)`. A UUID the service does not have rejects with `NotFoundError`; an unknown name throws `TypeError` (pass a full UUID for custom characteristics). The list is fetched once per service and then reused.

### `wbIsAvailable`

```js
window.WebToApk.wbIsAvailable(): Boolean
```

getAvailability(): whether the phone HAS Bluetooth (Chrome's answer), not whether it is switched on. requestDevice() asks the user to turn it on; answering false while it was merely off made pages that check first ("if (!await getAvailability())") say "Bluetooth not supported" and never reach that prompt (fitness report 2026-10-03).

**Example**

Internal transport behind `navigator.bluetooth.getAvailability()`. Pages use `navigator.bluetooth`; do not call this directly.

**Returns:** (through `getAvailability()`) a Promise of `true` when the build has Bluetooth and the phone's Bluetooth is on, else `false`. **Needs:** Bluetooth (turned on by a ZIP or HTML build when your code mentions `navigator.bluetooth`).

```js
async function updateBluetoothHint() {
  var hint = document.getElementById('bt-hint');
  if (!navigator.bluetooth) { hint.textContent = 'Bluetooth is not available in this app.'; return; }
  var on = await navigator.bluetooth.getAvailability();
  hint.textContent = on ? '' : 'Turn on Bluetooth to connect your sensor.';
}
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (!document.hidden) updateBluetoothHint();
});
```

Enable the Connect button only while Bluetooth is on, checking again whenever the user comes back to the app:

```js
async function refreshConnectButton() {
  var btn = document.getElementById('connect');
  if (!navigator.bluetooth) { btn.hidden = true; return; }
  btn.disabled = !(await navigator.bluetooth.getAvailability());
}
window.addEventListener('load', refreshConnectButton);
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (!document.hidden) refreshConnectButton();
});
```

Give a clear "Bluetooth is off" message before opening the chooser, instead of a NotFoundError afterwards:

```js
document.getElementById('scan').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!navigator.bluetooth) { showStatus('Bluetooth is not available in this app.'); return; }
  if (!(await navigator.bluetooth.getAvailability())) {
    showStatus('Bluetooth is off. Turn it on, then tap Scan again.');
    return;
  }
  try {
    var device = await navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice({ acceptAllDevices: true });
    showStatus('Picked ' + (device.name || device.id));
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus(err.name === 'NotFoundError' ? 'No device chosen.' : err.message);
  }
});
```

**Notes:** Raw signature `wbIsAvailable(): Boolean` (synchronous). It checks the adapter only - it does not ask for any permission. The `availabilitychanged` event of the web standard is not fired, so check again when the page becomes visible.

### `wbNotify`

```js
window.WebToApk.wbNotify(
```

Raw transport for WebBluetoothPolyfill. A page never calls these directly - it calls navigator.bluetooth, exactly as it would in a browser.

_Described by its group, Web Bluetooth (navigator.bluetooth), rather than on its own._

**Example**

Internal transport behind `characteristic.startNotifications()` and `stopNotifications()`. Pages use `navigator.bluetooth`; do not call this directly.

**Returns:** (through the characteristic) a Promise of the characteristic itself. Each new value fires `characteristicvaluechanged` on it, with the value in `event.target.value` (a `DataView`). **Needs:** Bluetooth (turned on by a ZIP or HTML build when your code mentions `navigator.bluetooth`).

```js
var cadenceChr = null;

async function startCadence(server) {
  var svc = await server.getPrimaryService('running_speed_and_cadence');
  cadenceChr = await svc.getCharacteristic('rsc_measurement');
  cadenceChr.addEventListener('characteristicvaluechanged', onRsc);
  await cadenceChr.startNotifications();
}

function onRsc(e) {
  var v = e.target.value;
  var kmh = v.getUint16(1, true) / 256 * 3.6;
  var spm = v.getUint8(3);
  show('run', kmh.toFixed(1) + ' km/h, ' + spm + ' steps/min');
}

async function stopCadence() {
  if (!cadenceChr) return;
  cadenceChr.removeEventListener('characteristicvaluechanged', onRsc);
  try { await cadenceChr.stopNotifications(); } catch (e) {}
}
```

A thermometer whose measurement only supports indications is subscribed the same way, here through the `oncharacteristicvaluechanged` property:

```js
async function watchThermometer(server) {
  var svc = await server.getPrimaryService('health_thermometer');
  var chr = await svc.getCharacteristic('temperature_measurement');
  chr.oncharacteristicvaluechanged = function (e) {
    var v = e.target.value;
    var mantissa = v.getUint32(1, true) & 0x00ffffff;          // IEEE-11073 FLOAT
    if (mantissa & 0x800000) mantissa -= 0x1000000;
    var fahrenheit = v.getUint8(0) & 1;
    show('temp', (mantissa * Math.pow(10, v.getInt8(4))).toFixed(1) + (fahrenheit ? ' °F' : ' °C'));
  };
  await chr.startNotifications();
}
```

Receive text lines from a serial-style device, joining notifications that split a line in the middle:

```js
async function listenForLines(server, onLine) {
  var uart = await server.getPrimaryService('6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e');
  var tx = await uart.getCharacteristic('6e400003-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e');
  if (!tx.properties.notify && !tx.properties.indicate) throw new Error('This device does not stream data');
  var decoder = new TextDecoder(), buffer = '';
  tx.addEventListener('characteristicvaluechanged', function (e) {
    buffer += decoder.decode(e.target.value, { stream: true });
    var lines = buffer.split('\n');
    buffer = lines.pop();
    lines.forEach(onLine);
  });
  await tx.startNotifications();
  return tx;
}
```

**Notes:** Raw signature `wbNotify(requestId, deviceId, service, characteristic, enable)`. A characteristic that only supports indications is subscribed with indications automatically. A characteristic that cannot notify rejects with `NotSupportedError`. `oncharacteristicvaluechanged = fn` works too. After a disconnect, subscribe again.

### `wbRead`

```js
window.WebToApk.wbRead(requestId: String, deviceId: String, service: String, characteristic: String)
```

Raw transport for WebBluetoothPolyfill. A page never calls these directly - it calls navigator.bluetooth, exactly as it would in a browser.

_Described by its group, Web Bluetooth (navigator.bluetooth), rather than on its own._

**Example**

Internal transport behind `characteristic.readValue()`. Pages use `navigator.bluetooth`; do not call this directly.

**Returns:** (through `readValue()`) a Promise of a `DataView`; `characteristic.value` is updated too. **Needs:** Bluetooth (turned on by a ZIP or HTML build when your code mentions `navigator.bluetooth`).

```js
async function readInfo(server) {
  try {
    var battery = await server.getPrimaryService('battery_service');
    var level = await (await battery.getCharacteristic('battery_level')).readValue();
    show('battery', level.getUint8(0) + '%');

    var info = await server.getPrimaryService('device_information');
    var maker = await (await info.getCharacteristic('manufacturer_name_string')).readValue();
    show('maker', new TextDecoder().decode(maker));
  } catch (err) {
    // NotFoundError: the device has no such service/characteristic
    // NotSupportedError: read rejected by the device   NetworkError: not connected / read failed
    show('info', err.message);
  }
}
```

Poll a sensor that can only be read, here the standard Temperature characteristic (0x2a6e, in hundredths of a degree):

```js
var pollTimer = null;

async function startTemperaturePolling(server) {
  var env = await server.getPrimaryService('environmental_sensing');
  var temp = await env.getCharacteristic(0x2a6e);
  pollTimer = setInterval(async function () {
    try {
      var v = await temp.readValue();
      show('temp', (v.getInt16(0, true) / 100).toFixed(1) + ' °C');
    } catch (err) {
      clearInterval(pollTimer);          // NetworkError once the sensor is gone
      show('temp', err.message);
    }
  }, 5000);
}
```

Fill an "About this device" panel by starting several reads at once; they run one after another for you:

```js
async function readDeviceInfo(server) {
  var info = await server.getPrimaryService('device_information');
  var names = ['model_number_string', 'serial_number_string', 'firmware_revision_string'];
  var decoder = new TextDecoder();
  var results = await Promise.allSettled(names.map(async function (name) {
    var chr = await info.getCharacteristic(name);
    return decoder.decode(await chr.readValue());
  }));
  results.forEach(function (r, i) {
    show(names[i], r.status === 'fulfilled' ? r.value : '-');   // missing ones reject with NotFoundError
  });
}
```

**Notes:** Raw signature `wbRead(requestId, deviceId, service, characteristic)`. Reads, writes and notification changes on one device run one after another in the order you call them, so you can fire several without waiting in between.

### `wbRequestDevice`

```js
window.WebToApk.wbRequestDevice(requestId: String, optionsJson: String)
```

Raw transport for WebBluetoothPolyfill. A page never calls these directly - it calls navigator.bluetooth, exactly as it would in a browser.

_Described by its group, Web Bluetooth (navigator.bluetooth), rather than on its own._

**Example**

Internal transport behind `navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice(options)`: it shows the app's device chooser. Pages use `navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice`; do not call this directly.

**Returns:** (through `requestDevice`) a Promise of a `BluetoothDevice` `{id, name, gatt}`. **Needs:** Bluetooth (turned on by a ZIP or HTML build when your code mentions `navigator.bluetooth`) and the Nearby devices permission, asked on first use.

```js
document.getElementById('pick').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!navigator.bluetooth) { showStatus('Bluetooth is not available in this app.'); return; }
  try {
    var device = await navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice({
      filters: [{ services: ['cycling_power'] }, { namePrefix: 'KICKR' }],
      optionalServices: ['battery_service']
    });
    showStatus('Picked ' + (device.name || device.id));
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.name === 'NotFoundError') showStatus('No device chosen.');   // also: Bluetooth off
    else showStatus(err.name + ': ' + err.message);                     // SecurityError = permission
  }
});
```

To list every nearby device instead of filtering: `requestDevice({ acceptAllDevices: true })`.

Pick a custom device by its exact name or name prefix, listing its own 128-bit service so it can be used after connecting:

```js
async function pickLamp() {
  try {
    return await navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice({
      filters: [{ name: 'Desk Lamp' }, { namePrefix: 'LAMP-' }],   // either one matches
      optionalServices: ['0000ffe0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb']
    });
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.name === 'SecurityError') showStatus('Allow Nearby devices to find your lamp.');
    else if (err.name !== 'NotFoundError') showStatus(err.message);  // NotFoundError = cancelled
    return null;
  }
}
```

Ask for the device once per session and reuse it on later taps (`getDevices()` is not available, so keep the object you got):

```js
var scale = null;

document.getElementById('weigh').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!navigator.bluetooth) { showStatus('Bluetooth is not available in this app.'); return; }
  try {
    if (!scale) {
      scale = await navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice({
        filters: [{ services: ['weight_scale'], namePrefix: 'MI' }]   // both keys must match
      });
    }
    var server = await scale.gatt.connect();
    var svc = await server.getPrimaryService('weight_scale');
    var chr = await svc.getCharacteristic('weight_measurement');
    chr.addEventListener('characteristicvaluechanged', onWeight);
    await chr.startNotifications();
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus(err.name + ': ' + err.message);
  }
});
```

**Notes:** Raw signature `wbRequestDevice(requestId, optionsJson)`; the answer comes back to the polyfill, not to the page. Call `requestDevice` from a tap. Filters use `services` (must be advertised), `name` (exact) and `namePrefix`; a filter matches when all its keys match, and the device matches when any filter matches. Neither `filters` nor `acceptAllDevices` → `TypeError`. Cancelling the chooser rejects with `NotFoundError`. The chooser scans for 30 seconds. `device.id` is the device's Bluetooth address.

### `wbWrite`

```js
window.WebToApk.wbWrite(
```

Raw transport for WebBluetoothPolyfill. A page never calls these directly - it calls navigator.bluetooth, exactly as it would in a browser.

_Described by its group, Web Bluetooth (navigator.bluetooth), rather than on its own._

**Example**

Internal transport behind `characteristic.writeValue()`, `writeValueWithResponse()` and `writeValueWithoutResponse()`. Pages use `navigator.bluetooth`; do not call this directly.

**Returns:** (through the characteristic) a Promise of `undefined`. **Needs:** Bluetooth (turned on by a ZIP or HTML build when your code mentions `navigator.bluetooth`).

**With response** (`writeValue` is the same): resolves when the device confirms the write.

```js
async function setTargetPower(server, watts) {
  var ftms = await server.getPrimaryService('fitness_machine');
  var cp = await ftms.getCharacteristic('00002ad9-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb'); // FTMS control point
  await cp.writeValueWithResponse(new Uint8Array([0x00]));                       // request control
  var cmd = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(3));
  cmd.setUint8(0, 0x05);                 // set target power
  cmd.setInt16(1, watts, true);
  await cp.writeValueWithResponse(cmd);
}
```

**Without response:** faster, for streams where a lost packet does not matter.

```js
async function sendText(characteristic, text) {
  if (!characteristic.properties.writeWithoutResponse) throw new Error('This characteristic needs writeValue');
  await characteristic.writeValueWithoutResponse(new TextEncoder().encode(text));
}
```

Send a long text command in 20-byte pieces. The app does not ask the device for a larger packet size, so 20 bytes is what fits in one write:

```js
async function sendLine(rx, text) {
  var bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(text + '\n');
  for (var i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 20) {
    await rx.writeValueWithoutResponse(bytes.subarray(i, i + 20));
  }
}
// sendLine(rxCharacteristic, 'SET COLOR 255 120 0 BRIGHTNESS 80');
```

**Notes:** Raw signature `wbWrite(requestId, deviceId, service, characteristic, valueBase64, withResponse)`. The value can be an `ArrayBuffer`, any typed array, a `DataView` or a plain array of bytes; anything else throws `TypeError`. Errors: `NotSupportedError` (write rejected), `NetworkError` (write failed or not connected), `NotFoundError`.

# Home-screen widget - JavaScript bridge API

> A small Android card on the home screen that your page fills with a title, a value and a few lines - AppMint.widget.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/widget

### `AppMint.widget`

```js
AppMint.widget.set(card) / update(partial) / clear() / placedCount() / requestPin()
```

**Example**

Fills your app's home-screen widget: a native card with a title, one big value, a caption, up to twelve lines (each with its own colour, marker and tap route if you like), your colours, and a route that a tap opens. When the user makes the widget bigger it shows more lines, and with `textSize: 'auto'` the text grows to fill it - as far as every line still fits, a long line taking two rows rather than being cut. A widget cannot show HTML - you send it the text.

**Returns:** every method returns a Promise. `set(card)` → `{ok: true, placed}` (`placed` = how many copies are on the home screen) or `{ok: false, error}`. `clear()` → `undefined`. `placedCount()` → a number. `requestPin()` → `true` if the launcher's "Add" sheet opened. **Needs:** nothing - every build has the widget.

**Set the card** - once at start, and again every time the data it shows changes:

```js
async function updateWidget(events) {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) return;          // in a browser
  var r = await AppMint.widget.set({
    title: 'Today',
    value: events.length + ' events',
    lines: events.slice(0, 6).map(function (ev) { return ev.time + ' ' + ev.name; }),
    route: '/calendar',      // a tap opens the app at this route
    bg: '#0E7C86',           // background
    ink: '#FFFFFF',          // title and lines
    accent: '#FFE08A'        // the big value
  });
  if (!r.ok) console.log('Widget not updated: ' + r.error);
}
```

**An agenda that fills the widget** - see-through background, text that grows when the widget is resized, coloured lines with a marker, an overdue line in red, and a tap on a line that opens that day:

```js
AppMint.widget.set({
  title: 'Agenda',
  value: 'Sun 18 Oct',
  caption: '5 events, 1 overdue',          // small text under the value
  bg: 'rgba(20, 38, 74, 0.6)',             // 60 % opaque — the wallpaper shows through
  ink: '#FFFFFF', accent: '#FFE08A',
  textSize: 'auto',                        // 'auto' | 'small' | 'normal' | 'large' | 'xl' | a number 0.6–3
  align: 'start',                          // 'start' (left) | 'center' | 'end'
  lines: [
    { text: '09:00 Stand-up', marker: '#29B6F6', route: '/#/day/2026-10-18' },
    { text: '10:30 Dentist, Dr Rao', marker: '#43A047', route: '/#/day/2026-10-18' },
    { text: 'Overdue: renew the car insurance', color: '#FF5252', marker: '#FF5252', bold: true, route: '/#/tasks/overdue' },
    { text: 'Tue 20: Team lunch', route: '/#/day/2026-10-20' },
    'Wed 21: Gym'                           // a plain string is still a line
  ],
  route: '/#/today'                         // a tap anywhere else on the card
});
```

A line is a string or `{ text, color?, marker?, bold?, wrap?, route? }`; `marker` puts a coloured `●` in front of the text, `wrap: true` on one line (or on the card) lets a long line take two rows at any text size; with `textSize: 'auto'` lines already do, and `wrap: false` keeps a line on one row. Up to six lines always show; lines seven to twelve show when the widget is tall enough.

**Richer widgets** - a list, a big number with a progress bar, a background picture and buttons. A card is drawn this way only when it has one of these keys; a card without them looks exactly as before:

```js
AppMint.widget.set({
  layout: 'list',                 // 'list' | 'progress' | 'card'
  title: 'Today', subtitle: 'Tue 30 Sep',
  items: [                         // up to 5 rows; a row tap opens its own route
    { text: '09:00 Dentist', secondary: 'Dr Rao, 2nd floor', image: 'img/tooth.png', route: '/event/41' },
    { text: '13:30 Lunch with Sam', image: 'https://example.com/sam.jpg', route: '/event/42' }
  ],
  buttons: [{ label: 'Add', route: '/new' }, { label: 'Week', route: '/week' }],   // up to 2
  bgImage: 'img/widget-bg.jpg', bg: '#101820', ink: '#FFFFFF', accent: '#FFB000'
});

AppMint.widget.set({
  layout: 'progress', title: 'Steps', value: '8 214',
  progress: { value: 8214, max: 10000, label: '82% of today's goal' }
});

AppMint.widget.update({ value: '8 950', progress: { value: 8950, max: 10000 } });   // change only these keys
```

**Your own font** - put the font file in your app (`.ttf` or `.otf`, e.g. from Google Fonts' "Download family") and give its path, as you would an `<img>`; every text on the card is drawn in it:

```js
AppMint.widget.set({
  title: 'Score', value: '1 250',
  font: 'fonts/RocknRollOne-Regular.ttf',   // a file in your app, an https address, or a data: URL
  lines: ['Level 7', { text: 'New record!', bold: true }]
}).then(function (r) { if (!r.ok) console.log(r.error); });   // e.g. "font file not found in the app: …"
```

A font NAME such as `'RocknRoll One'` cannot work: the home screen draws widgets, and it has only the phone's own fonts - `set()` answers `{ok: false, error}` saying so. Those built-in families need no file: `'serif'`, `'monospace'`, `'sans-serif-condensed'`, `'sans-serif-light'`, `'sans-serif-medium'`, `'sans-serif-black'`, `'casual'`, `'cursive'`, `'sans-serif-smallcaps'`. WOFF / WOFF2 files are refused (Android cannot read them) - use the `.ttf`. With a font file the card is drawn as a picture at the widget's size and redrawn when it is resized; taps on lines, rows and buttons and screen readers work as on any card.

**Refresh with the app closed** - give a https address that returns the same JSON; Android fetches it every `refreshMinutes` (30 or more, default 60) while a widget is on the home screen, even after a restart:

```js
AppMint.widget.set({
  title: 'Orders', value: '…',
  refreshUrl: 'https://api.example.com/widget.json?user=42',
  refreshMinutes: 30
}).then(function (r) { console.log('refreshing every ' + r.refreshMinutes + ' min'); });
// widget.json answers e.g. {"title":"Orders","value":"12 new","layout":"list","items":[{"text":"#1042 paid"}]}
```

Images: a path in your app (resolved like an `<img src>` in the page), an https address, or a `data:image/…` URL; they are scaled down and kept on the phone. In the refresh JSON a relative path means a file of the app. `refreshUrl: ''` stops the refresh; `clear()` stops it too. Android decides the exact moment of each refresh (it batches background work to save battery).

**An "Add to home screen" button:**

```js
async function addWidget() {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) return;
  if ((await AppMint.widget.placedCount()) > 0) { alert('The widget is already on your home screen'); return; }
  var opened = await AppMint.widget.requestPin();
  if (!opened) alert('Touch and hold your home screen, tap Widgets, and pick this app.');
}
```

**Empty it** (for example after the user signs out):

```js
if (window.AppMint && AppMint.widget) AppMint.widget.clear();   // shows "Nothing to show yet"
```

**A tap on the widget** opens the app with `appmint-shortcut://<package><route>` as its launch link - read it with `WebToApk.getLaunchUrl()` on start and the `appmint:deep-link` event while running:

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:deep-link', function (e) {
  var m = /^appmint-shortcut:\/\/[^\/?#]*([^#]*)/i.exec(e.detail.url);
  if (m) goTo(m[1] || '/');
});
```

**Colours:** `#RRGGBB`, `#RGB`, `rgb(20, 38, 74)`, `rgba(20, 38, 74, 0.6)` (also `rgb(20 38 74 / 60%)`), `transparent` and plain names such as `red`. **Eight-digit hex is Android order, alpha FIRST: `#AARRGGBB`.** `#9914264A` is 60 % opaque; CSS's `#14264A99` reads here as alpha `14` (8 %), an almost invisible card. For see-through backgrounds `rgba()` avoids the confusion. Line colours (`color`, `marker`) take the same forms; a bad line colour is refused with `{ok: false, error: 'lines[2].color is not a colour'}`, a bad card colour uses the default.

**Notes:** All card fields are optional: an empty `title` shows the app name; empty `value`, `caption` or lines are hidden; lines after the twelfth are dropped. `textSize` and `align` apply to every text on the card; an unknown value is refused with `{ok: false, error}`. A card without the new keys (`caption`, `textSize`, `align`, `wrap`, styled lines) looks exactly as before. The widget keeps the last card, even after a restart, and changes only when your page calls `set()` again. `requestPin()` needs Android 8+ and a launcher that supports it. AI-built apps can use `widget` from `@/lib/appmintNative`. Styled lines, `caption`, `textSize`, `align`, `wrap` and `rgba()` need an app built with AppMint 1.11.38 or newer - rebuild the app before you send line objects, because an older build would show them as raw text. `font` needs an app built with AppMint 1.11.41 or newer (an older build ignores it). **Website-mode apps:** a tap opens the route on your website - `/#/today` loads `https://<your site>/#/today` - and `getLaunchUrl()` still returns the `appmint-shortcut://` link.

### `widgetClear`

```js
window.WebToApk.widgetClear()
```

Removes the card; placed widgets go back to their empty state.

**Example**

Internal plumbing behind `AppMint.widget.clear()` - removes the widget's card; every placed widget goes back to "Nothing to show yet".

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing.

The public API first:

```js
async function onSignOut() {
  if (window.AppMint && AppMint.widget) await AppMint.widget.clear();
}
```

The raw call:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.widgetClear === 'function') {
  window.WebToApk.widgetClear();
}
```

Tie the widget to a "Show on home screen" switch in your settings - off empties it, on fills it again:

```js
document.getElementById('widget-toggle').onchange = async function (e) {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) return;
  if (e.target.checked) {
    await AppMint.widget.set(buildWidgetCard()); // your own card builder
  } else {
    await AppMint.widget.clear();
  }
};
```

After deleting the account, empty the widget and tell the user if a copy is still on their home screen:

```js
function afterAccountDeleted() {
  var W = window.WebToApk;
  if (!W || typeof W.widgetClear !== 'function') return;
  W.widgetClear();
  if (W.widgetPlacedCount() > 0) {
    showMessage('Your widget is now empty. You can remove it from your home screen.');
  }
}
```

**Notes:** The widget stays on the home screen; only its content is removed. Call `AppMint.widget.set()` to fill it again.

### `widgetPlacedCount`

```js
window.WebToApk.widgetPlacedCount(): Int
```

How many copies of the widget the user has placed on the home screen.

**Example**

Internal plumbing behind `AppMint.widget.placedCount()` - how many copies of your widget the user has put on the home screen.

**Returns:** a number, synchronously (`0` when none). **Needs:** nothing.

The public API first - show an "Add widget" button only when the widget is not placed yet:

```js
async function showAddWidgetButton() {
  var btn = document.getElementById('add-widget');
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) { btn.hidden = true; return; }
  btn.hidden = (await AppMint.widget.placedCount()) > 0;
}
```

The raw call:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.widgetPlacedCount === 'function') {
  var n = window.WebToApk.widgetPlacedCount();
  console.log('Widgets on the home screen: ' + n);
}
```

Check again each time the user comes back from the launcher, and thank them once the widget is there:

```js
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', async function () {
  if (document.visibilityState !== 'visible') return;
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) return;
  var n = await AppMint.widget.placedCount();
  document.getElementById('widget-promo').hidden = n > 0;
  if (n > 0) document.getElementById('widget-thanks').hidden = false;
});
```

Show the widget's status on a settings page with the synchronous raw call:

```js
var status = document.getElementById('widget-status');
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.widgetPlacedCount === 'function') {
  var n = window.WebToApk.widgetPlacedCount();
  status.textContent = n === 0 ? 'Not on your home screen'
    : n === 1 ? 'On your home screen' : 'On your home screen ' + n + ' times';
} else {
  status.textContent = 'Available in the installed app';
}
```

**Notes:** Check it again when the app comes back to the front (`visibilitychange`), since the user adds widgets from the launcher, outside your app.

### `widgetRequestPin`

```js
window.WebToApk.widgetRequestPin(): Boolean
```

Opens the launcher's "Add to home screen" sheet for the widget (Android 8+). False where the launcher cannot.

**Example**

Internal plumbing behind `AppMint.widget.requestPin()` - opens the launcher's "Add to home screen" sheet for your widget.

**Returns:** `true` if the sheet opened, `false` where the launcher cannot (synchronously). **Needs:** Android 8+ and a launcher that supports pinning widgets.

The public API first, from a button tap:

```js
document.getElementById('add-widget').onclick = async function () {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) return;
  var opened = await AppMint.widget.requestPin();
  if (!opened) {
    alert('Touch and hold your home screen, tap Widgets, then pick this app.');
  }
};
```

The raw call:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.widgetRequestPin === 'function') {
  if (!window.WebToApk.widgetRequestPin()) showManualSteps();
}
```

Fill the card first, then open the sheet, so the widget shows real content the moment it lands:

```js
document.getElementById('add-widget').onclick = async function () {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) return;
  await AppMint.widget.set({ title: 'Streak', value: '12 days', lines: ['Best 30'], route: '/streak' });
  if (!(await AppMint.widget.requestPin())) {
    document.getElementById('widget-help').hidden = false; // manual steps
  }
};
```

Find out whether the user accepted: compare the placed count before the sheet and after they come back:

```js
document.getElementById('add-widget').onclick = function () {
  var W = window.WebToApk;
  if (!W || typeof W.widgetRequestPin !== 'function') return;
  var before = W.widgetPlacedCount();
  if (!W.widgetRequestPin()) { showManualSteps(); return; }
  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function check() {
    if (document.visibilityState !== 'visible') return;
    document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', check);
    if (W.widgetPlacedCount() > before) showToast('Widget added');
  });
};
```

**Notes:** `true` only means the sheet opened - the user can still cancel it. Use `AppMint.widget.placedCount()` later to see whether it was added. Fill the card with `AppMint.widget.set()` first, so the new widget is not empty.

### `widgetSet`

```js
window.WebToApk.widgetSet(cardJson: String): String
```

Saves the widget card [cardJson] `{title?, value?, lines?, route?, bg?, ink?, accent?}` and redraws every placed widget. Returns `{ok, placed}`.

**Example**

Internal plumbing behind `AppMint.widget.set(card)` - pages use that helper to fill the home-screen widget.

**Returns:** a JSON string `{"ok":true,"placed":<number>}` or `{"ok":false,"error":"…"}` (synchronously). **Needs:** nothing - every build has the widget.

The public API first:

```js
if (window.AppMint && AppMint.widget) {
  AppMint.widget.set({ title: 'Steps', value: '8 214', lines: ['Goal 10 000'], route: '/' })
    .then(function (r) { if (!r.ok) console.log(r.error); });
}
```

The raw call takes the card as a JSON string and returns JSON text:

```js
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.widgetSet === 'function') {
  var card = { title: 'Steps', value: '8 214', lines: ['Goal 10 000'], route: '/',
               bg: '#15161A', ink: '#FFFFFF', accent: '#22D3EE' };
  var r = JSON.parse(window.WebToApk.widgetSet(JSON.stringify(card)));
  console.log(r.ok ? 'on ' + r.placed + ' home screen(s)' : r.error);
}
```

Keep the widget in step with a to-do list - the open count as the value, the first six tasks as lines, and a tap opens the tasks screen:

```js
async function syncTaskWidget(tasks) {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) return;
  var open = tasks.filter(function (t) { return !t.done; });
  var r = await AppMint.widget.set({
    title: 'To do',
    value: open.length ? open.length + ' left' : 'All done',
    lines: open.slice(0, 6).map(function (t) { return '• ' + t.title; }),
    route: '/tasks'
  });
  if (!r.ok) console.warn('Widget not updated: ' + r.error);
}
```

Write the latest state when the user leaves the app; the raw call is synchronous, so it finishes before the page is paused:

```js
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (document.visibilityState !== 'hidden') return;
  if (!window.WebToApk || typeof window.WebToApk.widgetSet !== 'function') return;
  var s = getTodayStats(); // your app's own numbers
  window.WebToApk.widgetSet(JSON.stringify({
    title: 'Today', value: s.spent + ' spent',
    lines: ['Budget ' + s.budget, 'Left ' + (s.budget - s.spent)], route: '/budget'
  }));
});
```

**Notes:** Card keys: `title`, `value`, `caption`, `lines` (up to twelve; a line is a string or `{text, color, marker, bold, wrap, route}`), `route` (a `/` is added if missing), `bg`, `ink`, `accent`, `textSize`, `align`, `wrap`, `font` (a .ttf/.otf file in your app or a system family such as `serif`), plus the rich-layout keys - see `AppMint.widget`. Colours: `#RRGGBB`, `#AARRGGBB` (alpha first), `rgba()`. Every placed widget redraws at once. `placed` is `0` when the user has not added the widget yet - the card is still saved and appears when they do.

### `widgetUpdate`

```js
window.WebToApk.widgetUpdate(partialJson: String): String
```

Merges [partialJson] into the saved widget card (named keys replace, the rest stay) and redraws. Returns `{ok, placed}`.

**Example**

Changes part of the home-screen widget: the keys you pass replace the saved ones, everything else stays. Pages normally call `AppMint.widget.update(partial)`.

**Returns:** a JSON string `{"ok":true,"placed":<n>}` or `{"ok":false,"error":"…"}`. **Needs:** nothing - every build has the widget.

```js
// Only the number and the progress bar change; title, rows and buttons stay as they were.
if (window.AppMint && AppMint.widget) {
  AppMint.widget.update({ value: '7 420', progress: { value: 7420, max: 10000, label: '74% of goal' } });
}

// Raw form:
if (window.WebToApk && typeof window.WebToApk.widgetUpdate === 'function') {
  var r = JSON.parse(window.WebToApk.widgetUpdate(JSON.stringify({ subtitle: 'Updated ' + new Date().toLocaleTimeString() })));
  if (!r.ok) console.warn(r.error);
}
```

Clear the card on sign-out and report an error from `update`:

```js
async function onSignOut() {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) return;
  await AppMint.widget.clear();
}

async function bumpCount(n) {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) return;
  const r = await AppMint.widget.update({ value: String(n) });
  if (!r.ok) console.warn('Widget not updated: ' + r.error);
}
```

Combine it with the placement check: only refresh the card while a copy is on the home screen.

```js
async function refreshWidget(stats) {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.widget)) return;
  if (await AppMint.widget.placedCount() === 0) return;
  AppMint.widget.update({ value: stats.total + ' today', subtitle: 'Updated ' + new Date().toLocaleTimeString() });
}
```

**Notes:** With no saved card, `update()` behaves like `set()`. See `AppMint.widget` for every card key.

# NFC - JavaScript bridge API

> Reading a tag through window.AndroidNFC, and the write side behind the NDEFReader polyfill.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/nfc

### `NDEFReader`

```js
new NDEFReader() — Web NFC
```

**Example**

Standard Web NFC: `new NDEFReader()` reads, writes and locks NFC tags in the installed app, with the same code Chrome on Android accepts.

**Returns:** Promises and `reading` / `readingerror` events, as in the web standard. Records are `NDEFRecord`s: `recordType` (`'text'`, `'url'`, `'absolute-url'`, `'mime'`, `'smart-poster'`, `'empty'`, `'unknown'` or an external type such as `'example.com:thing'`), `mediaType` (mime records), `id`, `encoding` and `lang` (text records) and `data` as a `DataView`. **Needs:** turn on **Web NFC Support** in Step 4 (Access) when you build. Without it `NDEFReader` does not exist. No runtime permission prompt; `navigator.permissions.query({name:'nfc'})` answers `granted`.

**Read tags.** Decode `data` with `TextDecoder`, exactly as in Chrome:

```js
function describe(record) {
  if (record.recordType === 'text') return new TextDecoder(record.encoding).decode(record.data);
  if (record.recordType === 'url' || record.recordType === 'absolute-url') return new TextDecoder().decode(record.data);
  if (record.recordType === 'mime') return record.mediaType + ' (' + record.data.byteLength + ' bytes)';
  return record.recordType;
}

var scanStop = null;

document.getElementById('read').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  var reader = new NDEFReader();
  scanStop = new AbortController();
  reader.onreading = function (e) {
    showStatus('Tag ' + e.serialNumber + ': ' + e.message.records.map(describe).join(' | '));
  };
  reader.onreadingerror = function () { showStatus('That tag holds no NFC data this phone can read.'); };
  try {
    await reader.scan({ signal: scanStop.signal });
    showStatus('Hold a tag to the back of the phone.');
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus('NFC error: ' + err.name + ' ' + err.message);   // NotReadableError = NFC switched off
  }
});

document.getElementById('stop').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (scanStop) scanStop.abort();   // the standard way to stop scanning
});
```

**Write text or a link.** The Promise resolves after the user taps a tag:

```js
async function writeTag(kind, value) {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  var reader = new NDEFReader();
  showStatus('Tap a tag to write it...');
  try {
    if (kind === 'text') await reader.write(value);   // same as { records: [{ recordType: 'text', data: value }] }
    else await reader.write({ records: [{ recordType: 'url', data: value }] }, { overwrite: false });
    showStatus('Tag written.');
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus('Write failed: ' + err.name + ' ' + err.message);   // NotAllowedError: read-only, or overwrite:false on a used tag
  }
}
```

**Lock a tag for ever.** `makeReadOnly()` cannot be undone - ask first:

```js
async function lockTag() {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) return;
  if (!confirm('Lock the next tag you tap? It can never be changed again.')) return;
  try { await new NDEFReader().makeReadOnly(); showStatus('Tag locked.'); }
  catch (err) { showStatus('Lock failed: ' + err.message); }
}
```

**Notes:** Record types for `write`: `text` (string, or bytes with `encoding`), `url` and `absolute-url` (string), `mime` (bytes + `mediaType`), `smart-poster` (`{records: [...]}`), an external type `'domain:thing'` (bytes or `{records: [...]}`), `unknown` (bytes) and `empty`. A plain string writes a text record; plain bytes write an `application/octet-stream` mime record. Only readers that called `scan()` get `reading` events; `AbortController.abort()` on the `signal` stops that reader (there is no `stop()` in the standard). `readingerror` fires for a tag that cannot hold NFC data. The phone waits for ONE tag operation at a time: a new `write()` or `makeReadOnly()` while one waits replaces it, and the replaced call rejects with `AbortError` (Chrome would queue it). A `signal` on `write()` / `makeReadOnly()` cancels the wait. Errors: `NotSupportedError` (no NFC, or the tag cannot hold NDEF, or it is too small), `NotReadableError` (NFC switched off), `NotAllowedError` (read-only tag, or `overwrite: false` on a tag with records), `NetworkError` (the tag moved away), `TypeError` (a record the standard does not allow). `NDEFReader` exists in the main page, not inside iframes.

### `__nfcCancelWrite`

```js
window.WebToApk.__nfcCancelWrite()
```

Cancels the waiting write/lock (the polyfill calls it when the operation's `signal` aborts).

**Example**

Drops a queued NFC write or lock so the next tag tap is read normally. Pages cancel through the web standard - an `AbortController` `signal` - and the `NDEFReader` polyfill calls this for them.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** **Web NFC Support** turned on in Step 4 (Access) when you build.

The standard way, which the app honours - the waiting `write()` rejects with `AbortError`:

```js
var controller = null;

async function writeWithCancel(text) {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  controller = new AbortController();
  showStatus('Tap a tag to write it... (or press Cancel)');
  try {
    await new NDEFReader().write(text, { signal: controller.signal });
    showStatus('Tag written.');
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus(err.name === 'AbortError' ? 'Cancelled.' : 'Write failed: ' + err.message);
  }
}

document.getElementById('cancel').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (controller) controller.abort();
});
```

Give up by itself when no tag arrives in time; a timer that aborts the signal cancels the same way:

```js
async function writeWithTimeout(url, ms) {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  var controller = new AbortController();
  var timer = setTimeout(function () { controller.abort(); }, ms);
  showStatus('Tap a tag within ' + Math.round(ms / 1000) + ' seconds...');
  try {
    await new NDEFReader().write({ records: [{ recordType: 'url', data: url }] }, { signal: controller.signal });
    showStatus('Tag written.');
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus(err.name === 'AbortError' ? 'Timed out. Tap Write to try again.' : 'Write failed: ' + err.message);
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}
```

Cancel a waiting lock (or write) when the user leaves the screen, so a later tap does not change a tag:

```js
var pendingTagOp = null;

window.addEventListener('hashchange', function () {
  if (pendingTagOp) { pendingTagOp.abort(); pendingTagOp = null; }
});

document.getElementById('lock').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  if (pendingTagOp) pendingTagOp.abort();
  var controller = pendingTagOp = new AbortController();
  showStatus('Tap the tag to lock it...');
  new NDEFReader().makeReadOnly({ signal: controller.signal })
    .then(function () { showStatus('Tag locked.'); })
    .catch(function (err) { if (err.name !== 'AbortError') showStatus('Lock failed: ' + err.message); })
    .finally(function () { if (pendingTagOp === controller) pendingTagOp = null; });
});
```

**Notes:** Do not call `WebToApk.__nfcCancelWrite()` yourself: called directly it drops the native wait but cannot settle the page's Promise. The `signal` does both. Cancelling also drops a queued `makeReadOnly()`.

### `__nfcMakeReadOnly`

```js
window.WebToApk.__nfcMakeReadOnly(): String
```

Queues a permanent lock (`NDEFReader.makeReadOnly()`) for the next tag tap; returns its op id, "" when NFC is off in this app.

**Example**

Internal transport behind `NDEFReader.makeReadOnly()`. Pages use `new NDEFReader().makeReadOnly()`; never call this directly.

**Returns:** (through `makeReadOnly`) a Promise that resolves after the user taps a tag and it is locked, or rejects with a `DOMException`. **Needs:** **Web NFC Support** turned on in Step 4 (Access) when you build.

Locking is permanent. Write the tag first, then lock it, and ask the user before both:

```js
document.getElementById('publish-tag').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  if (!confirm('Write and lock this tag? A locked tag can never be changed.')) return;
  var reader = new NDEFReader();
  try {
    showStatus('Tap the tag to write it...');
    await reader.write({ records: [{ recordType: 'url', data: 'https://example.com/item/42' }] });
    showStatus('Now tap the same tag again to lock it...');
    await reader.makeReadOnly();
    showStatus('Tag written and locked.');
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus('Failed: ' + err.message);
  }
});
```

Lock a tag that is already written, and give up if no tag arrives within 20 seconds:

```js
async function lockTag() {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  if (!confirm('Lock this tag for good? It can never be changed again.')) return;
  var controller = new AbortController();
  var timer = setTimeout(function () { controller.abort(); }, 20000);
  showStatus('Tap the tag to lock it...');
  try {
    await new NDEFReader().makeReadOnly({ signal: controller.signal });
    showStatus('Tag locked.');
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.name === 'AbortError') showStatus('No tag was tapped. Try again when ready.');
    else if (err.name === 'NotAllowedError') showStatus('This kind of tag cannot be locked.');
    else showStatus('Lock failed: ' + err.message);
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}
```

Read a tag first and only offer to lock it when it holds the expected link:

```js
async function checkThenLock(expectedUrl) {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  var reader = new NDEFReader();
  var scanning = new AbortController();
  var lockBtn = document.getElementById('lock-btn');
  reader.onreading = function (e) {
    var rec = e.message.records.find(function (r) { return r.recordType === 'url'; });
    var url = rec ? new TextDecoder().decode(rec.data) : null;
    showStatus(url ? 'Tag points to ' + url : 'This tag holds no link.');
    lockBtn.disabled = url !== expectedUrl;
  };
  await reader.scan({ signal: scanning.signal });
  showStatus('Hold the tag to the phone to check it.');

  lockBtn.onclick = async function () {
    if (!confirm('Lock this tag? It can never be changed again.')) return;
    scanning.abort();
    showStatus('Tap the tag again to lock it...');
    try { await reader.makeReadOnly(); showStatus('Tag locked.'); }
    catch (err) { showStatus('Lock failed: ' + err.message); }
  };
}
```

**Notes:** Each step needs its own tap. The call returns an operation id and the result arrives through `window.__appmintNfcDone`. Rejections: `NotSupportedError` "Tag does not support NDEF", `NotAllowedError` "This tag cannot be made read-only" (many tags cannot be locked), `NetworkError` when the tag moves away. Starting a `write()` while a lock waits replaces the lock, which then rejects with `AbortError`. A `signal` passed to `makeReadOnly({ signal })` cancels the wait.

### `__nfcState`

```js
window.WebToApk.__nfcState(): String
```

"on", "off" (NFC switched off in the phone's settings) or "none" (no NFC, or not enabled in this app) - what `NDEFReader.scan()` checks first.

**Example**

Internal check behind `NDEFReader.scan()`: whether this app can use NFC right now. Pages call `scan()` and read its rejection instead.

**Returns:** `'on'`, `'off'` (NFC is switched off in the phone's settings) or `'none'` (the phone has no NFC, or the app was built without Web NFC Support). **Needs:** **Web NFC Support** turned on in Step 4 (Access) when you build.

The standard way - `scan()` rejects with the same answer:

```js
async function startReading() {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  try {
    await new NDEFReader().scan();
    showStatus('Hold a tag to the back of the phone.');
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.name === 'NotReadableError') showStatus('Turn on NFC in the phone settings, then try again.');
    else if (err.name === 'NotSupportedError') showStatus('This phone has no NFC.');
    else showStatus('NFC error: ' + err.message);
  }
}
```

Check once when the screen opens, to choose between the NFC panel, a "turn on NFC" hint and hiding NFC altogether. Aborting the probe's scan right away leaves nothing running:

```js
async function nfcStatus() {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) return 'none';
  var probe = new AbortController();
  try {
    await new NDEFReader().scan({ signal: probe.signal });
    return 'on';
  } catch (err) {
    return err.name === 'NotReadableError' ? 'off' : 'none';
  } finally {
    probe.abort();
  }
}

async function refreshNfcUi() {
  var state = await nfcStatus();
  document.getElementById('nfc-panel').hidden = state !== 'on';
  document.getElementById('nfc-off-hint').hidden = state !== 'off';
}

refreshNfcUi();
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (document.visibilityState === 'visible') refreshNfcUi(); // back from the phone settings
});
```

Read tags only while one screen is open, and tell an empty or unreadable tag apart from NFC being off:

```js
var tagScreen = null;

async function openTagScreen() {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  tagScreen = new AbortController();
  var reader = new NDEFReader();
  reader.onreading = function (e) {
    var n = e.message.records.length;
    showStatus(n ? 'Tag ' + e.serialNumber + ' holds ' + n + ' record(s).' : 'This tag is empty.');
  };
  reader.onreadingerror = function () { showStatus('This tag cannot be read. Try another one.'); };
  try {
    await reader.scan({ signal: tagScreen.signal });
    showStatus('Hold a tag to the back of the phone.');
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus(err.name === 'NotReadableError' ? 'NFC is off. Turn it on in the phone settings.' : 'NFC error: ' + err.message);
  }
}

function closeTagScreen() {
  if (tagScreen) { tagScreen.abort(); tagScreen = null; }
}
```

**Notes:** Plumbing for the polyfill; use `scan()`. `window.AndroidNFC.startScan()` answers the same question as a boolean and shows a "Please enable NFC" message when NFC is off.

### `__nfcWrite`

```js
window.WebToApk.__nfcWrite(messageJson: String): String
```

Queues [messageJson] (`{records:[…], overwrite}`, built by `NDEFReader.write()`) for the next tag tap and returns its op id; "" when NFC is not enabled in this app.

**Example**

Internal transport behind `NDEFReader.write(message)`. Pages use `new NDEFReader().write(...)`; never call this directly.

**Returns:** (through `write`) a Promise that resolves after the user taps a tag and it is written, or rejects with a `DOMException`. **Needs:** **Web NFC Support** turned on in Step 4 (Access) when you build.

```js
document.getElementById('write-table-tag').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  showStatus('Tap a tag to write it...');
  try {
    await new NDEFReader().write({
      records: [
        { recordType: 'url', data: 'https://example.com/menu' },
        { recordType: 'text', data: 'Table 12', lang: 'en' },
        { recordType: 'mime', mediaType: 'application/json',
          data: new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({ table: 12 })) }
      ]
    });
    showStatus('Tag written.');
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus('Write failed: ' + err.message);
  }
});
```

Write only to a blank tag, so a tag that already holds data is never replaced by mistake:

```js
async function writeToBlankTag(url) {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  showStatus('Tap a blank tag...');
  try {
    await new NDEFReader().write(
      { records: [{ recordType: 'url', data: url }] },
      { overwrite: false }
    );
    showStatus('Tag written.');
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.name === 'NotAllowedError') showStatus('That tag already holds data or is locked. Use a blank tag.');
    else if (err.name === 'NetworkError') showStatus('Hold the tag still until it is written.');
    else showStatus('Write failed: ' + err.message);
  }
}
```

Write a smart poster, a link together with its title, as one record:

```js
document.getElementById('write-poster').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!('NDEFReader' in window)) { showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.'); return; }
  showStatus('Tap a tag to write the poster...');
  try {
    await new NDEFReader().write({
      records: [{
        recordType: 'smart-poster',
        data: { records: [
          { recordType: 'url', data: 'https://example.com/events/spring-fair' },
          { recordType: 'text', data: 'Spring Fair tickets', lang: 'en' }
        ] }
      }]
    });
    showStatus('Poster tag written.');
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus(err.name === 'NotSupportedError' ? 'This tag is too small or cannot hold NFC data.' : 'Write failed: ' + err.message);
  }
});
```

**Notes:** The polyfill checks the records, turns them into `{records:[{recordType, id, data(base64), encoding, lang, mediaType, records?}], overwrite}` and passes the JSON string here. The call returns an operation id; the result comes back to the page through `window.__appmintNfcDone(id, errorName, message)`, so an answer for a replaced write never settles a newer one. Unformatted tags are formatted first. Rejections: `NotAllowedError` ("Tag is read-only", or a tag with records when `overwrite` is false), `NotSupportedError` ("Tag does not support NDEF", "Tag too small (N bytes available)"), `NetworkError` (the tag moved away), `SyntaxError` (a record the tag format cannot hold). The app also shows its own short "Ready to write" and "NFC tag written" messages.

### `startScan`

```js
window.AndroidNFC.startScan(): Boolean
```

Legacy availability probe, present only when the creator enabled NFC. Real NFC work goes through the standard NDEFReader polyfill (window.WebToApk.__nfc*), which is what a page should use; this only reports whether the adapter is on.

_Described by its group, Web NFC, rather than on its own._

**Example**

Tells you whether the phone's NFC is switched on. It lives on `window.AndroidNFC`, not on `window.WebToApk`, and it does not read a tag - reading is done with `NDEFReader`.

**Returns:** `true` (synchronously) when the phone has NFC and it is on; `false` when the phone has no NFC, or when NFC is off (then the app also shows a short "Please enable NFC" message). **Needs:** **Web NFC Support** turned on in Step 4 (Access) when you build; without it `window.AndroidNFC` does not exist.

Check before showing an NFC button:

```js
function nfcReady() {
  if (!window.AndroidNFC || typeof window.AndroidNFC.startScan !== 'function') return false;
  return window.AndroidNFC.startScan();
}

document.getElementById('scan-tag').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!nfcReady()) { showStatus('Turn on NFC in the phone settings, then try again.'); return; }
  var reader = new NDEFReader();
  reader.addEventListener('reading', function (e) { showStatus('Tag ' + e.serialNumber); });
  await reader.scan();
  showStatus('Hold a tag to the back of the phone.');
});
```

Check right before a write: with NFC switched off the write would wait for a tap that never comes, while `startScan()` answers at once and shows the app's "Please enable NFC" message:

```js
document.getElementById('write-pass').addEventListener('click', async function () {
  if (!window.AndroidNFC || typeof window.AndroidNFC.startScan !== 'function') {
    showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.');
    return;
  }
  if (!window.AndroidNFC.startScan()) { showStatus('NFC is off, or this phone has no NFC.'); return; }
  showStatus('Tap a tag to write it...');
  try {
    await new NDEFReader().write('Visitor pass #1042');
    showStatus('Tag written.');
  } catch (err) {
    showStatus('Write failed: ' + err.message);
  }
});
```

Re-check when the user comes back and taps "I've turned it on":

```js
var retry = document.getElementById('nfc-retry');
retry.addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (!window.AndroidNFC || typeof window.AndroidNFC.startScan !== 'function') {
    showStatus('NFC is not available in this app.');
    return;
  }
  if (window.AndroidNFC.startScan()) {
    retry.hidden = true;
    document.getElementById('nfc-panel').hidden = false;
    startReading(); // your own NDEFReader.scan() code
  } else {
    showStatus('NFC is still off, or this phone has no NFC.');
  }
});
```

**Notes:** `window.AndroidNFC` exists from the first script on the page. After the user turns NFC on in settings and comes back, tag reading starts by itself.
