# Running in the background - JavaScript bridge API

> A foreground service the page starts and stops, location that keeps arriving with the app in the background, geofences that fire with the app closed, and your own code run periodically after a restart. Each needs its switch in the build and a Play Console declaration.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/background

### `AppMint.background`

```js
AppMint.background.register(name, options) / unregister / list / runNow / done / isBackgroundRun / currentRun / onRun
```

**Example**

Runs your page's OWN code periodically with the app closed - refresh data, check a price, post a notification. Each run loads your page invisibly (same origin, same localStorage/IndexedDB, no screen, no ads) with `?appmint_background=1&appmint_task=<name>&appmint_run=<runId>`, fires `appmint:background { name, runId }` once it has loaded, and waits for `done(runId, { ok })`. A run is cut off after about 9 minutes.

**Returns:** every method returns a Promise. `register` → `{ ok: true, name, intervalMinutes }` or `{ ok: false, reason }` (`not_enabled`, `invalid_name`, `interval_below_15_minutes`, `invalid_interval`, `schedule_failed`). `unregister` → `true` / `false`. `list` → `[{ name, intervalMinutes, requiresNetwork, requiresCharging, registeredAt, lastRunAt, lastResult }]` (`lastResult`: `ok`, `retry`, `failed`, `timeout`, `unsupported_mode`, `page_load_failed`, …). `runNow` → `{ ok }` (one run as soon as the conditions allow - for testing). `done` → `true` when the run was ended. `isBackgroundRun()` and `currentRun()` are synchronous. **Needs:** tick **Run page code while closed** (Access step → Background). Website and offline/ZIP apps; document and media apps have no page code to run.

**One page, two roles:**

```js
function startApp() {
  const bg = window.AppMint && AppMint.background;
  if (bg && bg.isBackgroundRun()) return;          // a background run: no UI work
  renderUi();
  if (bg) bg.register('prices', { intervalMinutes: 60, requiresNetwork: true }).then(function (r) {
    if (!r.ok) console.warn('background task not scheduled:', r.reason);
  });
}

// Runs only in the background copy of the page.
window.addEventListener('appmint:background', async function (e) {
  const run = e.detail;                              // { name: 'prices', runId: '…' }
  try {
    const price = await fetch('https://api.example.com/price').then(function (r) { return r.json(); });
    const last = Number(localStorage.getItem('lastPrice') || 0);
    if (price.value < last) {
      WebToApk.notify(JSON.stringify({ title: 'Price dropped', body: 'Now ' + price.value, tag: 'price' }));
    }
    localStorage.setItem('lastPrice', String(price.value));
    AppMint.background.done(run.runId, { ok: true });
  } catch (err) {
    AppMint.background.done(run.runId, { ok: false, retry: true });   // retried with backoff
  }
});
startApp();
```

**Late-mounting pages** (React, a lazy route) use `onRun`, which also fires if the run already started, or the page hook:

```js
if (window.AppMint && AppMint.background) {
  AppMint.background.onRun(function (run) { syncInbox().then(function () { AppMint.background.done(run.runId, { ok: true }); }); });
}
window.onAppMintBackground = function (run) { console.log('background run', run.name, run.runId, AppMint.background.currentRun()); };
```

**Manage:**

```js
AppMint.background.list().then(function (tasks) { console.table(tasks); });
AppMint.background.runNow('prices');
AppMint.background.unregister('prices');
```

**Notes:** Android decides the exact moment; 15 minutes is the shortest interval and battery saving can delay runs. With **Start after phone restart** every task also runs once after a restart. A run's `WebToApk` has only `notify`, `showNotification`, the location buffer, geofences, `workEnqueueOnline`, `isBackgroundServiceRunning` and these task methods; anything else is absent (feature-detect).

### `addGeofence`

```js
window.WebToApk.addGeofence(json: String): String
```

Adds a geofence {id, lat, lng, radiusM, events, dwellMs?, notify?} → JSON {ok, status:'adding'} or {ok:false, reason}; the result is appmint:geofence-added.

**Example**

A circle that fires `enter`, `exit` and/or `dwell` with the app closed, optionally posting a notification. Geofences survive a phone restart (they are added back automatically).

**Returns:** `addGeofence` → a JSON string `{ ok: true, status: 'adding', id }` or `{ ok: false, reason }` - `not_enabled`, `invalid_id`, `invalid_position`, `invalid_radius` (1 m … 100 km), `invalid_events`, `location_permission_required`, `background_permission_required`, `foreign_origin`. Play services' answer arrives as `appmint:geofence-added` (`window.onAppMintGeofenceAdded`) = `{ id, ok, reason? }` (`location_off`, `too_many_geofences` - 100 per app, `play_services_unavailable`). A transition arrives as `appmint:geofence` (`window.onAppMintGeofence`) = `{ id, event: 'enter' | 'exit' | 'dwell', time, lat, lng, queued? }` - `queued: true` when it happened while the app was closed and is handed over at the next start. `removeGeofence` → `true` if it existed; `getGeofences` → a JSON array of what you added. **Needs:** tick **Geofences** in the build, and "Allow all the time" (`requestBackgroundLocation()`).

```js
function watchOffice() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.addGeofence)) return;
  const r = JSON.parse(b.addGeofence(JSON.stringify({
    id: 'office', lat: 51.5033, lng: -0.1196, radiusM: 150,
    events: ['enter', 'exit', 'dwell'], dwellMs: 5 * 60000,
    notify: {
      enter: { title: 'At the office', body: 'Tap to check in' },
      exit: { title: 'Left the office', body: 'Tap to check out' }
    }
  })));
  if (!r.ok && r.reason === 'background_permission_required') b.requestBackgroundLocation();
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:geofence-added', function (e) {
  if (!e.detail.ok) showMessage('Geofence ' + e.detail.id + ' not added: ' + e.detail.reason);
});
window.addEventListener('appmint:geofence', function (e) {
  logVisit(e.detail.id, e.detail.event, e.detail.time);
});

console.log(JSON.parse(WebToApk.getGeofences()).map(function (g) { return g.id; }));
WebToApk.removeGeofence('office');
```

**Feature-detect and report every refusal:**

```js
function addCircle(id, lat, lng, radiusM) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.addGeofence)) { showMessage('Place alerts need the app'); return false; }
  const r = JSON.parse(b.addGeofence(JSON.stringify({ id: id, lat: lat, lng: lng, radiusM: radiusM, events: ['enter'] })));
  if (r.ok) return true;
  if (r.reason === 'not_enabled') showMessage('Geofences are not switched on in this build');
  else if (r.reason === 'background_permission_required') b.requestBackgroundLocation();
  else if (r.reason === 'invalid_radius') showMessage('Pick a radius between 1 m and 100 km');
  else showMessage('Could not add the place: ' + r.reason);
  return false;
}
```

**List what is registered and remove one:**

```js
const mine = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getGeofences());          // [] when none
mine.forEach(function (g) { addRow(g.id); });
document.getElementById('forget').onclick = function () {
  const existed = WebToApk.removeGeofence('office');       // true if it was there
  if (!existed) showMessage('That place was not registered');
};
```

### `backgroundDone`

```js
window.WebToApk.backgroundDone(runId: String, resultJson: String): Boolean
```

AppMint.background.done(runId, result): ends a background run; always false in the app itself.

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.backgroundRegister` - the example there shows this one too.

The raw methods behind `AppMint.background` - use `AppMint.background.register(...)` (it returns promises and handles the run event). Listed here so every bridge method has an example.

**Returns:** `backgroundRegister` → JSON `{ ok: true, name, intervalMinutes }` or `{ ok: false, reason }` (`not_enabled`, `invalid_name` - letters, digits, `_`, `-`, up to 64 - `interval_below_15_minutes`, `invalid_interval`, `schedule_failed`). `backgroundUnregister` → `true` if it existed. `backgroundList` → JSON array. `backgroundRunNow` → JSON `{ ok, name }` or `{ ok: false, reason: 'not_registered' }`. `backgroundDone(runId, resultJson)` → `true` in a background run, always `false` in the app. `isBackgroundRun()` → `false` in the app, `true` in a background run. **Needs:** tick **Run page code while closed**.

```js
const b = window.WebToApk;
if (b && b.backgroundRegister) {
  const r = JSON.parse(b.backgroundRegister('refresh', JSON.stringify({ intervalMinutes: 60, requiresNetwork: true })));
  if (!r.ok) console.warn('not scheduled:', r.reason);
  console.log(JSON.parse(b.backgroundList()));
  console.log(b.isBackgroundRun());               // false here: this is the app on screen
  // b.backgroundRunNow('refresh');  b.backgroundUnregister('refresh');
  // In a run: b.backgroundDone(runId, JSON.stringify({ ok: true }))
}
```

**Feature-detect and tell the app run from the background run:**

```js
const b = window.WebToApk;
if (!(b && b.backgroundRegister)) {
  console.log('background tasks are only in the app');
} else if (b.isBackgroundRun()) {
  // the invisible copy: do the work, no UI
} else {
  const r = JSON.parse(b.backgroundRegister('sync', JSON.stringify({ intervalMinutes: 5 })));
  if (!r.ok) console.warn(r.reason);                // 'interval_below_15_minutes'
}
```

**Test a task and clean up:**

```js
const run = JSON.parse(WebToApk.backgroundRunNow('sync'));
if (!run.ok && run.reason === 'not_registered') WebToApk.backgroundRegister('sync', JSON.stringify({ intervalMinutes: 30 }));
JSON.parse(WebToApk.backgroundList()).forEach(function (t) { console.log(t.name, t.intervalMinutes, t.lastResult); });
WebToApk.backgroundUnregister('old-task');           // true if it existed
```

### `clearBufferedLocations`

```js
window.WebToApk.clearBufferedLocations(): Boolean
```

Empties the buffer getBufferedLocations reads (call it after you saved the points).

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.getBufferedLocations` - the example there shows this one too.

The fixes recorded while your page was away (app in the background or closed), oldest first, up to 10,000.

**Returns:** `getBufferedLocations()` → a JSON string array of `{ type: 'fix', lat, lng, accuracy, time, …, background: true }`; `'[]'` when Background location is off. `clearBufferedLocations()` → `true` when emptied. **Needs:** **Background location** in the build.

```js
function syncTrack() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getBufferedLocations)) return;
  const points = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getBufferedLocations());
  if (!points.length) return;
  points.forEach(function (p) { drawPoint(p.lat, p.lng); });
  saveTrack(points).then(function () { WebToApk.clearBufferedLocations(); });
}
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () { if (!document.hidden) syncTrack(); });
```

**Start tracking, then handle a refusal.** The start call answers with a JSON string.

```js
function startTracking() {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.startLocationUpdates)) return;
  const r = JSON.parse(WebToApk.startLocationUpdates(JSON.stringify({
    intervalMs: 15000, accuracy: 'balanced', background: true
  })));
  if (!r.ok) showMessage('Tracking not started: ' + r.reason);   // not_enabled, location_permission_required, ...
}
```

**Live fixes while the page is open** arrive as `appmint:location`; the buffer holds the rest.

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:location', function (e) {
  drawPoint(e.detail.lat, e.detail.lng);
});
document.getElementById('stop').addEventListener('click', function () {
  if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.stopLocationUpdates) WebToApk.stopLocationUpdates();
  if (WebToApk.getBufferedLocations) {
    const left = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getBufferedLocations());
    console.log(left.length + ' fixes still buffered');
  }
});
```

### `clearGeofenceEvents`

```js
window.WebToApk.clearGeofenceEvents(): Boolean
```

Empties the transition history getGeofenceEvents reads.

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.getGeofenceEvents` - the example there shows this one too.

The last 100 geofence transitions, oldest first - including the ones that happened while the app was closed. Read it on start if your page mounts late and might miss the queued `appmint:geofence` events.

**Returns:** `getGeofenceEvents()` → a JSON string array of `{ id, event, time, lat, lng }`; `clearGeofenceEvents()` → `true`. **Needs:** **Geofences** in the build.

```js
if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.getGeofenceEvents) {
  JSON.parse(WebToApk.getGeofenceEvents()).forEach(function (ev) {
    logVisit(ev.id, ev.event, ev.time);
  });
  WebToApk.clearGeofenceEvents();
}
```

**Add a geofence, then watch for transitions** while the page is open.

```js
if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.addGeofence) {
  const r = JSON.parse(WebToApk.addGeofence(JSON.stringify({
    id: 'shop-1', lat: 12.9716, lng: 77.5946, radiusM: 150, events: ['enter', 'exit']
  })));
  if (!r.ok) showMessage('Geofence refused: ' + r.reason);   // not_enabled, invalid_radius, ...
}
window.addEventListener('appmint:geofence', function (e) {
  logVisit(e.detail.id, e.detail.event, e.detail.time);
});
```

**List what is registered and remove one** when the user leaves a feature.

```js
function dropGeofence(id) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.removeGeofence)) return false;
  const known = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getGeofences()).length;
  const removed = WebToApk.removeGeofence(id);
  console.log(removed ? 'removed' : 'not found', 'of', known, 'registered');
  return removed;
}
```

### `getGeofences`

```js
window.WebToApk.getGeofences(): String
```

JSON array of the geofences this app has added (they survive restarts).

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.addGeofence` - the example there shows this one too.

A circle that fires `enter`, `exit` and/or `dwell` with the app closed, optionally posting a notification. Geofences survive a phone restart (they are added back automatically).

**Returns:** `addGeofence` → a JSON string `{ ok: true, status: 'adding', id }` or `{ ok: false, reason }` - `not_enabled`, `invalid_id`, `invalid_position`, `invalid_radius` (1 m … 100 km), `invalid_events`, `location_permission_required`, `background_permission_required`, `foreign_origin`. Play services' answer arrives as `appmint:geofence-added` (`window.onAppMintGeofenceAdded`) = `{ id, ok, reason? }` (`location_off`, `too_many_geofences` - 100 per app, `play_services_unavailable`). A transition arrives as `appmint:geofence` (`window.onAppMintGeofence`) = `{ id, event: 'enter' | 'exit' | 'dwell', time, lat, lng, queued? }` - `queued: true` when it happened while the app was closed and is handed over at the next start. `removeGeofence` → `true` if it existed; `getGeofences` → a JSON array of what you added. **Needs:** tick **Geofences** in the build, and "Allow all the time" (`requestBackgroundLocation()`).

```js
function watchOffice() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.addGeofence)) return;
  const r = JSON.parse(b.addGeofence(JSON.stringify({
    id: 'office', lat: 51.5033, lng: -0.1196, radiusM: 150,
    events: ['enter', 'exit', 'dwell'], dwellMs: 5 * 60000,
    notify: {
      enter: { title: 'At the office', body: 'Tap to check in' },
      exit: { title: 'Left the office', body: 'Tap to check out' }
    }
  })));
  if (!r.ok && r.reason === 'background_permission_required') b.requestBackgroundLocation();
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:geofence-added', function (e) {
  if (!e.detail.ok) showMessage('Geofence ' + e.detail.id + ' not added: ' + e.detail.reason);
});
window.addEventListener('appmint:geofence', function (e) {
  logVisit(e.detail.id, e.detail.event, e.detail.time);
});

console.log(JSON.parse(WebToApk.getGeofences()).map(function (g) { return g.id; }));
WebToApk.removeGeofence('office');
```

**Feature-detect and report every refusal:**

```js
function addCircle(id, lat, lng, radiusM) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.addGeofence)) { showMessage('Place alerts need the app'); return false; }
  const r = JSON.parse(b.addGeofence(JSON.stringify({ id: id, lat: lat, lng: lng, radiusM: radiusM, events: ['enter'] })));
  if (r.ok) return true;
  if (r.reason === 'not_enabled') showMessage('Geofences are not switched on in this build');
  else if (r.reason === 'background_permission_required') b.requestBackgroundLocation();
  else if (r.reason === 'invalid_radius') showMessage('Pick a radius between 1 m and 100 km');
  else showMessage('Could not add the place: ' + r.reason);
  return false;
}
```

**List what is registered and remove one:**

```js
const mine = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getGeofences());          // [] when none
mine.forEach(function (g) { addRow(g.id); });
document.getElementById('forget').onclick = function () {
  const existed = WebToApk.removeGeofence('office');       // true if it was there
  if (!existed) showMessage('That place was not registered');
};
```

### `getLocationPermissionState`

```js
window.WebToApk.getLocationPermissionState(): String
```

JSON {foreground:'granted'|'denied', background:'granted'|'denied', precise: boolean}.

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.requestBackgroundLocation` - the example there shows this one too.

Asks for location, then for "Allow all the time" (Android 10+ asks for them separately; on Android 11+ the second step opens the app's location settings page). Geofences need it; so does restarting location tracking after a phone restart.

**Returns:** nothing directly; the answer arrives as `appmint:location-permission` (and `window.onAppMintLocationPermission(detail)`) = `{ foreground: 'granted' | 'denied', background: 'granted' | 'denied', precise: boolean, error?: 'not_enabled' }`. `getLocationPermissionState()` → the same object as a JSON string, without asking. **Needs:** **Background location** or **Geofences** in the build.

```js
function askAlways() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.requestBackgroundLocation)) return;
  const now = JSON.parse(b.getLocationPermissionState());
  if (now.background === 'granted') { enableGeofences(); return; }
  // Explain first: Play requires an in-app disclosure before this request.
  if (!confirm('Allow location "all the time" so we can remind you when you arrive?')) return;
  b.requestBackgroundLocation();
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:location-permission', function (e) {
  if (e.detail.background === 'granted') enableGeofences();
  else showMessage('Choose "Allow all the time" in the location settings to use arrival reminders.');
});
```

**Check the state first and explain what the user must tap:**

```js
const b = window.WebToApk;
if (b && b.getLocationPermissionState) {
  const s = JSON.parse(b.getLocationPermissionState());
  if (s.foreground !== 'granted') showMessage('Location is off for this app.');
  else if (s.background !== 'granted') showMessage('Tap "Allow all the time" to enable arrival reminders.');
  else if (!s.precise) showMessage('Precise location is off; arrival alerts may be late.');
}
```

**Request the permission, then add a geofence once it is granted:**

```js
window.addEventListener('appmint:location-permission', function (e) {
  if (e.detail.error === 'not_enabled') return showMessage('This build has no background location.');
  if (e.detail.background !== 'granted') return;
  const r = JSON.parse(WebToApk.addGeofence(JSON.stringify({
    id: 'home', lat: 51.5033, lng: -0.1196, radiusM: 120, events: ['enter']
  })));
  if (!r.ok) showMessage('Could not add the place: ' + r.reason);
}, { once: true });
WebToApk.requestBackgroundLocation();
```

### `isBackgroundRun`

```js
window.WebToApk.isBackgroundRun(): Boolean
```

False here: the app's own page is never a background run (a headless run answers true).

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.backgroundRegister` - the example there shows this one too.

The raw methods behind `AppMint.background` - use `AppMint.background.register(...)` (it returns promises and handles the run event). Listed here so every bridge method has an example.

**Returns:** `backgroundRegister` → JSON `{ ok: true, name, intervalMinutes }` or `{ ok: false, reason }` (`not_enabled`, `invalid_name` - letters, digits, `_`, `-`, up to 64 - `interval_below_15_minutes`, `invalid_interval`, `schedule_failed`). `backgroundUnregister` → `true` if it existed. `backgroundList` → JSON array. `backgroundRunNow` → JSON `{ ok, name }` or `{ ok: false, reason: 'not_registered' }`. `backgroundDone(runId, resultJson)` → `true` in a background run, always `false` in the app. `isBackgroundRun()` → `false` in the app, `true` in a background run. **Needs:** tick **Run page code while closed**.

```js
const b = window.WebToApk;
if (b && b.backgroundRegister) {
  const r = JSON.parse(b.backgroundRegister('refresh', JSON.stringify({ intervalMinutes: 60, requiresNetwork: true })));
  if (!r.ok) console.warn('not scheduled:', r.reason);
  console.log(JSON.parse(b.backgroundList()));
  console.log(b.isBackgroundRun());               // false here: this is the app on screen
  // b.backgroundRunNow('refresh');  b.backgroundUnregister('refresh');
  // In a run: b.backgroundDone(runId, JSON.stringify({ ok: true }))
}
```

**Feature-detect and tell the app run from the background run:**

```js
const b = window.WebToApk;
if (!(b && b.backgroundRegister)) {
  console.log('background tasks are only in the app');
} else if (b.isBackgroundRun()) {
  // the invisible copy: do the work, no UI
} else {
  const r = JSON.parse(b.backgroundRegister('sync', JSON.stringify({ intervalMinutes: 5 })));
  if (!r.ok) console.warn(r.reason);                // 'interval_below_15_minutes'
}
```

**Test a task and clean up:**

```js
const run = JSON.parse(WebToApk.backgroundRunNow('sync'));
if (!run.ok && run.reason === 'not_registered') WebToApk.backgroundRegister('sync', JSON.stringify({ intervalMinutes: 30 }));
JSON.parse(WebToApk.backgroundList()).forEach(function (t) { console.log(t.name, t.intervalMinutes, t.lastResult); });
WebToApk.backgroundUnregister('old-task');           // true if it existed
```

### `isBackgroundServiceRunning`

```js
window.WebToApk.isBackgroundServiceRunning(): Boolean
```

Whether the app's foreground service is running (for either keep-running or background location).

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.startBackgroundService` - the example there shows this one too.

Keeps your app running while the user is away: a real Android foreground service with a notification. While it runs the page is not paused, so its JavaScript, `<audio>` and the app's background music carry on (Android still slows the timers of a page nobody can see).

**Returns:** `startBackgroundService` → a JSON string `{ ok: true, status: 'starting', type, notificationShown }` or `{ ok: false, reason }` - reason `not_enabled`, `invalid_options`, `type_not_declared`, `invalid_progress`, `location_permission_required`, `start_not_allowed`. `updateBackgroundService` → `{ ok: true }` or `{ ok: false, reason: 'not_running' }`. `stopBackgroundService` / `isBackgroundServiceRunning` → `true` / `false`. State changes arrive as `appmint:background-service` (and `window.onAppMintBackgroundService(detail)`): `{ state: 'running' | 'stopped' | 'failed' | 'not_restarted', reason?, types?, restored?, queued? }`. **Needs:** tick **Keep running in background** (Access step → Background) and pick the service type. On Android 13+ the notification is only visible once the user allowed notifications (`notificationShown: false` otherwise - the service still runs).

```js
function startWorkout() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.startBackgroundService)) return;             // browser
  const r = JSON.parse(b.startBackgroundService(JSON.stringify({
    title: 'Workout in progress',
    text: '00:00 elapsed',
    stopLabel: 'Stop',                  // a Stop button on the notification
    progress: { value: 0, max: 100 }
  })));
  if (!r.ok) showMessage('Could not keep running: ' + r.reason);
}

function tick(seconds) {
  if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.isBackgroundServiceRunning()) {
    WebToApk.updateBackgroundService(JSON.stringify({
      title: 'Workout in progress', text: seconds + ' s elapsed', stopLabel: 'Stop',
      progress: { value: Math.min(100, seconds / 18), max: 100 }
    }));
  }
}

function finishWorkout() {
  if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.stopBackgroundService) WebToApk.stopBackgroundService();
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:background-service', function (e) {
  // reason: 'user' (Stop button), 'page', 'timeout' (Android 15 dataSync 6-hour limit),
  // 'task_removed' (app swiped away); after a phone restart, state 'not_restarted' with
  // 'android_forbids_type_at_boot' | 'background_permission_required' | 'start_not_allowed'
  if (e.detail.state === 'stopped') showMessage('Stopped (' + e.detail.reason + ')');
});
```

Handle the answers that mean the build or the phone cannot do it:

```js
function startKeepAlive() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && typeof b.startBackgroundService === 'function')) return;
  const r = JSON.parse(b.startBackgroundService(JSON.stringify({ title: 'Syncing', text: 'Uploading photos' })));
  if (r.ok) return;
  if (r.reason === 'not_enabled') showMessage('Keep running in background is not on in this build.');
  else if (r.reason === 'type_not_declared') showMessage('This build declares no service type.');
  else showMessage('Could not start: ' + r.reason);
}
```

Combine it with an upload loop: keep running only while the queue has work.

```js
async function uploadAll(files) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  const keep = b && b.startBackgroundService &&
    JSON.parse(b.startBackgroundService(JSON.stringify({ title: 'Uploading', text: '0 of ' + files.length }))).ok;
  for (let i = 0; i < files.length; i++) {
    await upload(files[i]);
    if (keep) b.updateBackgroundService(JSON.stringify({ title: 'Uploading', text: (i + 1) + ' of ' + files.length }));
  }
  if (keep) b.stopBackgroundService();
}
```

**Notes:** the type must be one the build declared (the one picked in the wizard, plus `location` when Background location is on). Swiping the app away stops a keep-running service unless you pass `keepAfterSwipe: true` (the page itself is gone then). Play Console asks for a foreground-service declaration with a short video for every declared type.

### `isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations`

```js
window.WebToApk.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations(): Boolean
```

Whether the user exempted this app from battery optimisation (Doze app standby).

**Example**

Checks and asks for the battery-optimisation exemption, so Doze does not defer your background work.

**Returns:** `isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations()` → `true` / `false`. `requestIgnoreBatteryOptimizations()` → `'already_ignoring'`, `'dialog_opened'` (the system's Allow/Deny dialog - only when the build ticked **Ask to skip battery optimisation directly**), `'settings_opened'` (the battery-optimisation list; no permission, no Play declaration) or `'unavailable'`. **Needs:** nothing for the settings list. The direct dialog declares REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS, which Play accepts only when it is the app's core function.

```js
document.getElementById('reliable').addEventListener('click', function () {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations)) return;
  if (b.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations()) { showMessage('Already unrestricted'); return; }
  const how = b.requestIgnoreBatteryOptimizations();
  if (how === 'settings_opened') showMessage('Find this app in the list and choose "Not optimised".');
});
```

**Say what happened** for each answer.

```js
function askBatteryExemption() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.requestIgnoreBatteryOptimizations)) { showMessage('Only available in the app'); return; }
  const how = b.requestIgnoreBatteryOptimizations();
  const text = {
    already_ignoring: 'Already unrestricted',
    dialog_opened: 'Please tap Allow',
    settings_opened: 'Choose "Not optimised" for this app',
    unavailable: 'This phone has no such setting'
  };
  showMessage(text[how] || how);
}
```

**Pair it with background tracking**, since Doze would pause it.

```js
if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.startLocationUpdates) {
  const r = JSON.parse(WebToApk.startLocationUpdates(JSON.stringify({ intervalMs: 30000 })));
  if (r.ok && !WebToApk.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations()) {
    showMessage('For steady tracking, turn off battery optimisation for this app.');
  }
}
```

### `removeGeofence`

```js
window.WebToApk.removeGeofence(id: String): Boolean
```

Removes the geofence with this id; false when there was none.

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.addGeofence` - the example there shows this one too.

A circle that fires `enter`, `exit` and/or `dwell` with the app closed, optionally posting a notification. Geofences survive a phone restart (they are added back automatically).

**Returns:** `addGeofence` → a JSON string `{ ok: true, status: 'adding', id }` or `{ ok: false, reason }` - `not_enabled`, `invalid_id`, `invalid_position`, `invalid_radius` (1 m … 100 km), `invalid_events`, `location_permission_required`, `background_permission_required`, `foreign_origin`. Play services' answer arrives as `appmint:geofence-added` (`window.onAppMintGeofenceAdded`) = `{ id, ok, reason? }` (`location_off`, `too_many_geofences` - 100 per app, `play_services_unavailable`). A transition arrives as `appmint:geofence` (`window.onAppMintGeofence`) = `{ id, event: 'enter' | 'exit' | 'dwell', time, lat, lng, queued? }` - `queued: true` when it happened while the app was closed and is handed over at the next start. `removeGeofence` → `true` if it existed; `getGeofences` → a JSON array of what you added. **Needs:** tick **Geofences** in the build, and "Allow all the time" (`requestBackgroundLocation()`).

```js
function watchOffice() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.addGeofence)) return;
  const r = JSON.parse(b.addGeofence(JSON.stringify({
    id: 'office', lat: 51.5033, lng: -0.1196, radiusM: 150,
    events: ['enter', 'exit', 'dwell'], dwellMs: 5 * 60000,
    notify: {
      enter: { title: 'At the office', body: 'Tap to check in' },
      exit: { title: 'Left the office', body: 'Tap to check out' }
    }
  })));
  if (!r.ok && r.reason === 'background_permission_required') b.requestBackgroundLocation();
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:geofence-added', function (e) {
  if (!e.detail.ok) showMessage('Geofence ' + e.detail.id + ' not added: ' + e.detail.reason);
});
window.addEventListener('appmint:geofence', function (e) {
  logVisit(e.detail.id, e.detail.event, e.detail.time);
});

console.log(JSON.parse(WebToApk.getGeofences()).map(function (g) { return g.id; }));
WebToApk.removeGeofence('office');
```

**Feature-detect and report every refusal:**

```js
function addCircle(id, lat, lng, radiusM) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.addGeofence)) { showMessage('Place alerts need the app'); return false; }
  const r = JSON.parse(b.addGeofence(JSON.stringify({ id: id, lat: lat, lng: lng, radiusM: radiusM, events: ['enter'] })));
  if (r.ok) return true;
  if (r.reason === 'not_enabled') showMessage('Geofences are not switched on in this build');
  else if (r.reason === 'background_permission_required') b.requestBackgroundLocation();
  else if (r.reason === 'invalid_radius') showMessage('Pick a radius between 1 m and 100 km');
  else showMessage('Could not add the place: ' + r.reason);
  return false;
}
```

**List what is registered and remove one:**

```js
const mine = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getGeofences());          // [] when none
mine.forEach(function (g) { addRow(g.id); });
document.getElementById('forget').onclick = function () {
  const existed = WebToApk.removeGeofence('office');       // true if it was there
  if (!existed) showMessage('That place was not registered');
};
```

### `requestBackgroundLocation`

```js
window.WebToApk.requestBackgroundLocation()
```

Asks for location, then "Allow all the time"; the result arrives as appmint:location-permission.

**Example**

Asks for location, then for "Allow all the time" (Android 10+ asks for them separately; on Android 11+ the second step opens the app's location settings page). Geofences need it; so does restarting location tracking after a phone restart.

**Returns:** nothing directly; the answer arrives as `appmint:location-permission` (and `window.onAppMintLocationPermission(detail)`) = `{ foreground: 'granted' | 'denied', background: 'granted' | 'denied', precise: boolean, error?: 'not_enabled' }`. `getLocationPermissionState()` → the same object as a JSON string, without asking. **Needs:** **Background location** or **Geofences** in the build.

```js
function askAlways() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.requestBackgroundLocation)) return;
  const now = JSON.parse(b.getLocationPermissionState());
  if (now.background === 'granted') { enableGeofences(); return; }
  // Explain first: Play requires an in-app disclosure before this request.
  if (!confirm('Allow location "all the time" so we can remind you when you arrive?')) return;
  b.requestBackgroundLocation();
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:location-permission', function (e) {
  if (e.detail.background === 'granted') enableGeofences();
  else showMessage('Choose "Allow all the time" in the location settings to use arrival reminders.');
});
```

**Check the state first and explain what the user must tap:**

```js

  else if (!s.precise) showMessage('Precise location is off; arrival alerts may be late.');
```

### `startLocationUpdates`

```js
window.WebToApk.startLocationUpdates(optionsJson: String): String
```

Location updates {intervalMs, minDistanceM, accuracy, background, uploadUrl?, headers?} → JSON {ok, background, backgroundPermission, precise} or {ok:false, reason}; fixes arrive as appmint:location.

**Example**

Location updates that keep coming while the app is in the background (a run tracker, a delivery app). With `background: true` (the default) they run inside the app's foreground service. Each fix goes to the page as `appmint:location` while the page is there, into a buffer (`getBufferedLocations()`) while it is not, and - when you give an `uploadUrl` - to your server as a JSON POST from native code, so tracking works with the page gone.

**Returns:** a JSON string `{ ok: true, background, backgroundPermission, precise }` or `{ ok: false, reason }` - `not_enabled`, `invalid_options`, `invalid_interval` (1 s … 24 h), `invalid_distance`, `invalid_accuracy`, `invalid_upload_url`, `location_permission_required`, `start_not_allowed`, `foreign_origin`. `stopLocationUpdates()` → `true` if something was running. Fixes: `appmint:location` / `window.onAppMintLocation(detail)` = `{ type: 'fix', lat, lng, accuracy, altitude?, speed?, bearing?, time, provider, background }`, or `{ type: 'error', reason: 'play_services_unavailable' | 'location_unavailable' | 'location_permission_required' }`. **Needs:** tick **Background location** (Access step → Background) and the user's location permission first.

```js
function startTracking(token) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.startLocationUpdates)) return;
  navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(function () {       // asks for location first
    const r = JSON.parse(b.startLocationUpdates(JSON.stringify({
      intervalMs: 10000, minDistanceM: 10, accuracy: 'high', background: true,
      uploadUrl: 'https://api.example.com/track',
      headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + token }
    })));
    if (!r.ok) showMessage('Tracking not started: ' + r.reason);
  });
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:location', function (e) {
  if (e.detail.type === 'fix') drawPoint(e.detail.lat, e.detail.lng);
  else showMessage('Location stopped: ' + e.detail.reason);
});

function stopTracking() { if (window.WebToApk) WebToApk.stopLocationUpdates(); }
```

Report a bad option or a missing permission with the answer's `reason`:

```js
function tryTrack() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && typeof b.startLocationUpdates === 'function')) {
    showMessage('Background tracking needs the installed app.');
    return;
  }
  const r = JSON.parse(b.startLocationUpdates(JSON.stringify({ intervalMs: 500 })));
  if (!r.ok && r.reason === 'invalid_interval') showMessage('Interval must be 1 second or more.');
  if (!r.ok && r.reason === 'location_permission_required') showMessage('Allow location first.');
}
```

A natural pair with the buffer: stop at the end of a shift and upload what was recorded while the page was away.

```js
async function endShift() {
  if (!window.WebToApk) return;
  WebToApk.stopLocationUpdates();
  const points = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getBufferedLocations());
  if (points.length) {
    await fetch('/api/shift/points', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(points) });
    WebToApk.clearBufferedLocations();
  }
}
```

**Notes:** a location service started from the app keeps getting fixes in the background without "Allow all the time"; restarting it after a phone restart needs it (`requestBackgroundLocation()`). A POST that fails is handed to WorkManager and sent when the network is back. Phones without Google Play services answer `play_services_unavailable`. Play Console needs a background-location declaration.

### `stopBackgroundService`

```js
window.WebToApk.stopBackgroundService(): Boolean
```

Stops the service started by startBackgroundService (background location, if running, continues).

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.startBackgroundService` - the example there shows this one too.

Keeps your app running while the user is away: a real Android foreground service with a notification. While it runs the page is not paused, so its JavaScript, `<audio>` and the app's background music carry on (Android still slows the timers of a page nobody can see).

**Returns:** `startBackgroundService` → a JSON string `{ ok: true, status: 'starting', type, notificationShown }` or `{ ok: false, reason }` - reason `not_enabled`, `invalid_options`, `type_not_declared`, `invalid_progress`, `location_permission_required`, `start_not_allowed`. `updateBackgroundService` → `{ ok: true }` or `{ ok: false, reason: 'not_running' }`. `stopBackgroundService` / `isBackgroundServiceRunning` → `true` / `false`. State changes arrive as `appmint:background-service` (and `window.onAppMintBackgroundService(detail)`): `{ state: 'running' | 'stopped' | 'failed' | 'not_restarted', reason?, types?, restored?, queued? }`. **Needs:** tick **Keep running in background** (Access step → Background) and pick the service type. On Android 13+ the notification is only visible once the user allowed notifications (`notificationShown: false` otherwise - the service still runs).

```js
function startWorkout() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.startBackgroundService)) return;             // browser
  const r = JSON.parse(b.startBackgroundService(JSON.stringify({
    title: 'Workout in progress',
    text: '00:00 elapsed',
    stopLabel: 'Stop',                  // a Stop button on the notification
    progress: { value: 0, max: 100 }
  })));
  if (!r.ok) showMessage('Could not keep running: ' + r.reason);
}

function tick(seconds) {
  if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.isBackgroundServiceRunning()) {
    WebToApk.updateBackgroundService(JSON.stringify({
      title: 'Workout in progress', text: seconds + ' s elapsed', stopLabel: 'Stop',
      progress: { value: Math.min(100, seconds / 18), max: 100 }
    }));
  }
}

function finishWorkout() {
  if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.stopBackgroundService) WebToApk.stopBackgroundService();
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:background-service', function (e) {
  // reason: 'user' (Stop button), 'page', 'timeout' (Android 15 dataSync 6-hour limit),
  // 'task_removed' (app swiped away); after a phone restart, state 'not_restarted' with
  // 'android_forbids_type_at_boot' | 'background_permission_required' | 'start_not_allowed'
  if (e.detail.state === 'stopped') showMessage('Stopped (' + e.detail.reason + ')');
});
```

Handle the answers that mean the build or the phone cannot do it:

```js
function startKeepAlive() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && typeof b.startBackgroundService === 'function')) return;
  const r = JSON.parse(b.startBackgroundService(JSON.stringify({ title: 'Syncing', text: 'Uploading photos' })));
  if (r.ok) return;
  if (r.reason === 'not_enabled') showMessage('Keep running in background is not on in this build.');
  else if (r.reason === 'type_not_declared') showMessage('This build declares no service type.');
  else showMessage('Could not start: ' + r.reason);
}
```

Combine it with an upload loop: keep running only while the queue has work.

```js
async function uploadAll(files) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  const keep = b && b.startBackgroundService &&
    JSON.parse(b.startBackgroundService(JSON.stringify({ title: 'Uploading', text: '0 of ' + files.length }))).ok;
  for (let i = 0; i < files.length; i++) {
    await upload(files[i]);
    if (keep) b.updateBackgroundService(JSON.stringify({ title: 'Uploading', text: (i + 1) + ' of ' + files.length }));
  }
  if (keep) b.stopBackgroundService();
}
```

**Notes:** the type must be one the build declared (the one picked in the wizard, plus `location` when Background location is on). Swiping the app away stops a keep-running service unless you pass `keepAfterSwipe: true` (the page itself is gone then). Play Console asks for a foreground-service declaration with a short video for every declared type.

### `stopLocationUpdates`

```js
window.WebToApk.stopLocationUpdates(): Boolean
```

Stops the location updates started by startLocationUpdates; false when none were running.

**Example**

Documented together with `WebToApk.startLocationUpdates` - the example there shows this one too.

Location updates that keep coming while the app is in the background (a run tracker, a delivery app). With `background: true` (the default) they run inside the app's foreground service. Each fix goes to the page as `appmint:location` while the page is there, into a buffer (`getBufferedLocations()`) while it is not, and - when you give an `uploadUrl` - to your server as a JSON POST from native code, so tracking works with the page gone.

**Returns:** a JSON string `{ ok: true, background, backgroundPermission, precise }` or `{ ok: false, reason }` - `not_enabled`, `invalid_options`, `invalid_interval` (1 s … 24 h), `invalid_distance`, `invalid_accuracy`, `invalid_upload_url`, `location_permission_required`, `start_not_allowed`, `foreign_origin`. `stopLocationUpdates()` → `true` if something was running. Fixes: `appmint:location` / `window.onAppMintLocation(detail)` = `{ type: 'fix', lat, lng, accuracy, altitude?, speed?, bearing?, time, provider, background }`, or `{ type: 'error', reason: 'play_services_unavailable' | 'location_unavailable' | 'location_permission_required' }`. **Needs:** tick **Background location** (Access step → Background) and the user's location permission first.

```js
function startTracking(token) {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && b.startLocationUpdates)) return;
  navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(function () {       // asks for location first
    const r = JSON.parse(b.startLocationUpdates(JSON.stringify({
      intervalMs: 10000, minDistanceM: 10, accuracy: 'high', background: true,
      uploadUrl: 'https://api.example.com/track',
      headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + token }
    })));
    if (!r.ok) showMessage('Tracking not started: ' + r.reason);
  });
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:location', function (e) {
  if (e.detail.type === 'fix') drawPoint(e.detail.lat, e.detail.lng);
  else showMessage('Location stopped: ' + e.detail.reason);
});

function stopTracking() { if (window.WebToApk) WebToApk.stopLocationUpdates(); }
```

Report a bad option or a missing permission with the answer's `reason`:

```js
function tryTrack() {
  const b = window.WebToApk;
  if (!(b && typeof b.startLocationUpdates === 'function')) {
    showMessage('Background tracking needs the installed app.');
    return;
  }
  const r = JSON.parse(b.startLocationUpdates(JSON.stringify({ intervalMs: 500 })));
  if (!r.ok && r.reason === 'invalid_interval') showMessage('Interval must be 1 second or more.');
  if (!r.ok && r.reason === 'location_permission_required') showMessage('Allow location first.');
}
```

A natural pair with the buffer: stop at the end of a shift and upload what was recorded while the page was away.

```js
async function endShift() {
  if (!window.WebToApk) return;
  WebToApk.stopLocationUpdates();
  const points = JSON.parse(WebToApk.getBufferedLocations());
  if (points.length) {
    await fetch('/api/shift/points', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(points) });
    WebToApk.clearBufferedLocations();
  }
}
```

**Notes:** a location service started from the app keeps getting fixes in the background without "Allow all the time"; restarting it after a phone restart needs it (`requestBackgroundLocation()`). A POST that fails is handed to WorkManager and sent when the network is back. Phones without Google Play services answer `play_services_unavailable`. Play Console needs a background-location declaration.

# Health Connect - JavaScript bridge API

> Reading and writing steps, distance, calories, heart rate, sleep, weight and exercise through Android’s Health Connect, for exactly the types the build ticked.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/health

### `AppMint.health`

```js
AppMint.health.isAvailable() / requestPermissions() / read() / write() / openHealthConnect()
```

**Example**

Reads and writes the user's health data through Health Connect: steps, distance, active calories, heart rate, sleep, weight and exercise sessions. Turn on **Health data (Health Connect)** in the wizard's Access step and tick the types and whether the app reads or writes each one - only those can be asked for.

**Returns:** every method returns a Promise. `isAvailable()` → `{ok: true, available, status, read, write}` (`status`: `available`, `not_installed`, `update_required`, `unsupported` = Android below 8.0, `disabled` = option off). The others → `{ok: true, …}` or `{ok: false, code, message}` with `code` `disabled`, `unsupported`, `not_installed`, `update_required`, `not_declared` (type not ticked in the wizard), `permission` (the user has not granted it), `bad-input`, `blocked` (a page from another site), `failed`. **Needs:** the wizard option, Android 8.0+, and Health Connect (built into Android 14+, an app from Play before that).

Types: `steps`, `distance`, `calories`, `heartRate`, `sleep`, `weight`, `exercise`. Times are milliseconds (`Date.now()`), `Date` objects or ISO strings; answers use ISO strings.

**Check, then ask:**

```js
async function connectHealth() {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.health)) return false;          // browser or option off
  var s = await AppMint.health.isAvailable();
  if (s.status === 'not_installed') { await AppMint.health.openHealthConnect(); return false; }
  if (!s.available) return false;
  var r = await AppMint.health.requestPermissions({ read: ['steps', 'heartRate'], write: ['weight'] });
  return r.ok && r.denied.read.length === 0;
}
```

**Today's steps** (totals with `aggregate: true`, the records themselves without it):

```js
async function stepsToday() {
  var start = new Date(); start.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
  var r = await AppMint.health.read('steps', { start: start, end: new Date(), aggregate: true });
  if (!r.ok) { console.warn(r.code, r.message); return 0; }
  return r.aggregate.count;
}

async function lastNightHeartRate() {
  var end = Date.now(), start = end - 12 * 3600 * 1000;
  var r = await AppMint.health.read('heartRate', { start: start, end: end });
  // r.records = [{start, end, id, samples: [{time, bpm}]}]
  return r.ok ? r.records.flatMap(function (x) { return x.samples; }) : [];
}
```

**Write** - one record or an array:

```js
await AppMint.health.write('weight', { time: Date.now(), kilograms: 72.4 });
await AppMint.health.write('exercise', [{
  start: Date.now() - 45 * 60000, end: Date.now(), exerciseType: 'running', title: 'Evening run'
}]);
await AppMint.health.write('steps', { start: Date.now() - 3600000, end: Date.now(), count: 4200 });
```

**Record fields:** steps `{start, end, count}` · distance `{start, end, meters}` · calories `{start, end, kilocalories}` · heartRate `{start, end, samples: [{time, bpm}]}` · sleep `{start, end, title?, stages?: [{start, end, stage}]}` (`awake`, `sleeping`, `out_of_bed`, `light`, `deep`, `rem`) · weight `{time, kilograms}` · exercise `{start, end, exerciseType, title?}` (Health Connect names such as `running`, `walking`, `biking`, `swimming_pool`, `yoga`, `strength_training`, `other_workout`). Aggregates: steps `{count}`, distance `{meters}`, calories `{kilocalories}`, heartRate `{avg, min, max}`, sleep / exercise `{minutes}`, weight `{avg, min, max}` (kg).

**Notes:** Health Connect shows your privacy policy from its permission screen - the address from the Finish step, or the generated policy. Before publishing on Google Play, fill in **App content → Health apps** in Play Console with the same data types and why the app needs each one; Play reviews health permissions. Health Connect gives an app the last 30 days of history from before its first grant. The raw bridge methods behind it (`healthIsAvailable`, `healthRequestPermissions`, `healthRead`, `healthWrite`, `healthOpen`) take JSON text and a callback id - use the helper.

```js
async function stepsToday() {
  var start = new Date(); start.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
  var r = await AppMint.health.read('steps', { start: start, end: new Date(), aggregate: true });
  if (!r.ok) { console.warn(r.code, r.message); return 0; }
  return r.aggregate.count;
}

async function lastNightHeartRate() {
  var end = Date.now(), start = end - 12 * 3600 * 1000;
  var r = await AppMint.health.read('heartRate', { start: start, end: end });
  // r.records = [{start, end, id, samples: [{time, bpm}]}]
  return r.ok ? r.records.flatMap(function (x) { return x.samples; }) : [];
}
```

**Write** - one record or an array:

```js
await AppMint.health.write('weight', { time: Date.now(), kilograms: 72.4 });
await AppMint.health.write('exercise', [{
  start: Date.now() - 45 * 60000, end: Date.now(), exerciseType: 'running', title: 'Evening run'
}]);
await AppMint.health.write('steps', { start: Date.now() - 3600000, end: Date.now(), count: 4200 });
```

**Record fields:** steps `{start, end, count}` · distance `{start, end, meters}` · calories `{start, end, kilocalories}` · heartRate `{start, end, samples: [{time, bpm}]}` · sleep `{start, end, title?, stages?: [{start, end, stage}]}` (`awake`, `sleeping`, `out_of_bed`, `light`, `deep`, `rem`) · weight `{time, kilograms}` · exercise `{start, end, exerciseType, title?}` (Health Connect names such as `running`, `walking`, `biking`, `swimming_pool`, `yoga`, `strength_training`, `other_workout`). Aggregates: steps `{count}`, distance `{meters}`, calories `{kilocalories}`, heartRate `{avg, min, max}`, sleep / exercise `{minutes}`, weight `{avg, min, max}` (kg).

**Notes:** Health Connect shows your privacy policy from its permission screen - the address from the Finish step, or the generated policy. Before publishing on Google Play, fill in **App content → Health apps** in Play Console with the same data types and why the app needs each one; Play reviews health permissions. Health Connect gives an app the last 30 days of history from before its first grant. The raw bridge methods behind it (`healthIsAvailable`, `healthRequestPermissions`, `healthRead`, `healthWrite`, `healthOpen`) take JSON text and a callback id - use the helper.

### `healthRequestPermissions`

```js
window.WebToApk.healthRequestPermissions(requestJson: String, callbackId: String)
```

Opens Health Connect's permission screen for [requestJson] `{read:[…], write:[…]}`; resolves with `{granted, denied}`.

**Example**

Documented together with `AppMint.health` - the example there shows this one too.

Reads and writes the user's health data through Health Connect: steps, distance, active calories, heart rate, sleep, weight and exercise sessions. Turn on **Health data (Health Connect)** in the wizard's Access step and tick the types and whether the app reads or writes each one - only those can be asked for.

**Returns:** every method returns a Promise. `isAvailable()` → `{ok: true, available, status, read, write}` (`status`: `available`, `not_installed`, `update_required`, `unsupported` = Android below 8.0, `disabled` = option off). The others → `{ok: true, …}` or `{ok: false, code, message}` with `code` `disabled`, `unsupported`, `not_installed`, `update_required`, `not_declared` (type not ticked in the wizard), `permission` (the user has not granted it), `bad-input`, `blocked` (a page from another site), `failed`. **Needs:** the wizard option, Android 8.0+, and Health Connect (built into Android 14+, an app from Play before that).

Types: `steps`, `distance`, `calories`, `heartRate`, `sleep`, `weight`, `exercise`. Times are milliseconds (`Date.now()`), `Date` objects or ISO strings; answers use ISO strings.

**Check, then ask:**

```js
async function connectHealth() {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.health)) return false;          // browser or option off
  var s = await AppMint.health.isAvailable();
  if (s.status === 'not_installed') { await AppMint.health.openHealthConnect(); return false; }
  if (!s.available) return false;
  var r = await AppMint.health.requestPermissions({ read: ['steps', 'heartRate'], write: ['weight'] });
  return r.ok && r.denied.read.length === 0;
}
```

**Today's steps** (totals with `aggregate: true`, the records themselves without it):

```js
async function stepsToday() {
  var start = new Date(); start.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
  var r = await AppMint.health.read('steps', { start: start, end: new Date(), aggregate: true });
  if (!r.ok) { console.warn(r.code, r.message); return 0; }
  return r.aggregate.count;
}

async function lastNightHeartRate() {
  var end = Date.now(), start = end - 12 * 3600 * 1000;
  var r = await AppMint.health.read('heartRate', { start: start, end: end });
  // r.records = [{start, end, id, samples: [{time, bpm}]}]
  return r.ok ? r.records.flatMap(function (x) { return x.samples; }) : [];
}
```

**Write** - one record or an array:

```js

await AppMint.health.write('exercise', [{
  start: Date.now() - 45 * 60000, end: Date.now(), exerciseType: 'running', title: 'Evening run'
}]);

```

**Record fields:** steps `{start, end, count}` · distance `{start, end, meters}` · calories `{start, end, kilocalories}` · heartRate `{start, end, samples: [{time, bpm}]}` · sleep `{start, end, title?, stages?: [{start, end, stage}]}` (`awake`, `sleeping`, `out_of_bed`, `light`, `deep`, `rem`) · weight `{time, kilograms}` · exercise `{start, end, exerciseType, title?}` (Health Connect names such as `running`, `walking`, `biking`, `swimming_pool`, `yoga`, `strength_training`, `other_workout`). Aggregates: steps `{count}`, distance `{meters}`, calories `{kilocalories}`, heartRate `{avg, min, max}`, sleep / exercise `{minutes}`, weight `{avg, min, max}` (kg).

**Notes:** Health Connect shows your privacy policy from its permission screen - the address from the Finish step, or the generated policy. # Facebook, Meta events and Firebase Analytics - JavaScript bridge API

> Facebook Login, Meta App Events and Firebase Analytics under the creator’s own keys, set in the build. Analytics collects nothing until the user has consented.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/growth

### `AppMint.analytics`

```js
AppMint.analytics — one event to Firebase and Meta
```

**Example**

Logs an event to every analytics service the build connected: Firebase Analytics (your own google-services.json) and Meta App Events. Names are cleaned to each service's rules and the answer says what was sent.

**Returns:** `log(name, params)` → `{ok, providers: {firebase?, meta?}}`, each `{ok, name, dropped}` or `{ok: false, error}`. `setUserId(id)`, `setUserProperty(name, value)`, `screenView(name, class)`, `setEnabled(on)` → Promises; `providers()` → `{firebase, meta}`. **Needs:** Integrate step → **Firebase Analytics** (upload google-services.json in the Push card) and/or **Meta App Events**.

```js
if (window.AppMint && AppMint.analytics) {
  AppMint.analytics.setUserId(currentUser.id);
  AppMint.analytics.setUserProperty('plan', 'pro');
  var r = await AppMint.analytics.log('add_to_cart', { item_id: 'sku-42', value: 19.99, currency: 'USD' });
  if (!r.ok) console.warn('not logged', r.providers);   // e.g. {firebase: {ok:false, error:'no_consent'}}
}

// Your own consent screen: nothing is collected while this is off (persisted).
document.getElementById('optOut').onchange = (e) => AppMint.analytics.setEnabled(!e.target.checked);
```

**Sign-in and sign-out keep the user id in step:**

```js
async function onAuthChange(user) {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.analytics)) return;
  if (user) {
    await AppMint.analytics.setUserId(user.id);
    await AppMint.analytics.setUserProperty('country', user.country);
  } else {
    await AppMint.analytics.setUserId('');           // clears it
  }
}
```

**See which services are connected before relying on them:**

```js
if (window.AppMint && AppMint.analytics) {
  const p = await AppMint.analytics.providers();     // { firebase, meta }
  if (!p.firebase && !p.meta) console.warn('no analytics service is connected in this build');
  await AppMint.analytics.screenView('Settings', 'SettingsPage');
  const r = await AppMint.analytics.log('first_open_tip', { shown: true });
  if (!r.ok) console.warn('not logged', r.providers);
}
```

**Notes:** Consent: when the app shows ads, Google's consent form decides for analytics too - nothing is collected before it has an answer, and where the GDPR applies purpose 1 must be granted; the page's `setEnabled(false)` always wins. While collection is off, calls answer `no_consent` (nothing is queued). Firebase names: letters, digits and `_`, up to 40 characters, at most 25 parameters, string values up to 100 characters; reserved names (`first_open`, `session_start`, `firebase_…`, `google_…`, `ga_…`) answer `reserved_name` / `reserved_prefix`. `params.value` (a number) becomes Meta's value-to-sum. With **Log a screen view for every page change** on, route changes log `screen_view` automatically. Errors: `not_configured`, `missing_google_app_id`, `params_not_json`, `invalid_name`.

### `AppMint.facebook`

```js
AppMint.facebook — Facebook Login and Meta App Events
```

**Example**

"Continue with Facebook" on your OWN Facebook app. Sign-in opens Facebook in a browser tab (Custom Tab): it uses the facebook.com login of that browser, NOT the Facebook app, and returns to the app when the user confirms. Also logs Meta App Events when you switched them on.

**Returns:** `login(permissions)` → a Promise that always resolves: `{ok: true, accessToken, userId, expires, grantedPermissions, declinedPermissions}` or `{ok: false, cancelled?, error}`. `getAccessToken()` → the same token object, or `null` when signed out. `logEvent(name, valueToSum, params)` → `{ok, name, dropped}` (queued and sent in batches) or `{ok: false, error}`. **Needs:** the build's Integrate step → **Facebook Login** with your Facebook App ID and Client Token (and **Meta App Events** for `logEvent`).

**Sign in, then use the token with your backend:**

```js
async function facebookSignIn() {
  if (!(window.AppMint && AppMint.facebook)) { alert('Open this page in the app'); return; }
  var r = await AppMint.facebook.login(['public_profile', 'email']);
  if (!r.ok) {
    if (r.cancelled) return;                          // the user backed out
    alert('Facebook sign-in failed: ' + (r.message || r.error));
    return;
  }
  // Firebase: firebase.auth().signInWithCredential(firebase.auth.FacebookAuthProvider.credential(r.accessToken))
  await fetch('/api/login/facebook', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ token: r.accessToken }) });
  console.log('Signed in as', r.userId, 'until', new Date(r.expires));
}

var existing = AppMint.facebook.getAccessToken();   // null when signed out
if (existing) showSignedIn(existing.userId);

document.getElementById('logout').onclick = () => AppMint.facebook.logout();
```

**Meta App Events:**

```js
AppMint.facebook.logEvent('fb_mobile_purchase', 9.99, { fb_currency: 'USD', fb_content_id: 'sku-42' });
AppMint.facebook.logEvent('Level Complete', null, { level: 3 });
```

**Show the Facebook button only inside the app, and handle a missing setup:**

```js
const fb = window.AppMint && AppMint.facebook;
document.getElementById('fb-button').hidden = !fb;
if (fb) {
  document.getElementById('fb-button').onclick = async function () {
    const r = await fb.login(['public_profile']);
    if (r.ok || r.cancelled) return;
    if (r.error === 'not_configured') alert('Facebook sign-in is not set up in this build');
    else if (r.error === 'busy') console.log('a login is already open');
    else alert('Facebook sign-in failed: ' + (r.message || r.error));
  };
}
```

**Notes:** Facebook Developers → your app → Facebook Login → Settings → Valid OAuth Redirect URIs: add `https://freewebtoapk.com/fb-return/` (the wizard has a Copy button). No key hash or Android platform setup is needed. The token is checked with Facebook (it must belong to your App ID) before the promise resolves. If Android closed the app while the user was in the browser, the result is not delivered to a promise - the token is stored and `getAccessToken()` returns it when the page starts. Errors: `not_configured`, `busy` (a login is already open), `cancelled` (also when the user closes the tab), `state_mismatch`, `wrong_app`, `failed`, `no_token`, `foreign_origin` (a page that is not the app's own). App Events (sent from the app to Facebook's App Events API with your client token) start only after consent (see `AppMint.analytics`) and answer `no_consent` until then. Web sign-in through Supabase or Firebase redirects keeps working as before.

### `analyticsLogEvent`

```js
window.WebToApk.analyticsLogEvent(name: String, paramsJson: String): String
```

Firebase event; the name is cleaned to Firebase's rules. Returns {ok, name, dropped} or {ok:false, error}.

**Example**

The raw Firebase Analytics methods behind `AppMint.analytics` - prefer the wrapper. Each returns its answer as JSON text: `{ok, name, dropped}` or `{ok: false, error}`.

**Returns:** JSON text (`analyticsSetEnabled` returns nothing). **Needs:** Integrate step → Firebase Analytics, with your google-services.json uploaded in the Push Notifications card.

```js
var r = JSON.parse(WebToApk.analyticsLogEvent('share', JSON.stringify({ method: 'whatsapp', content_type: 'post' })));
if (!r.ok) console.warn(r.error);                        // 'no_consent', 'reserved_name', …
WebToApk.analyticsLogScreenView('/checkout', 'CheckoutPage');
WebToApk.analyticsSetUserId('user-123');                 // '' clears it
WebToApk.analyticsSetUserProperty('favorite_food', 'pizza');
WebToApk.analyticsSetEnabled(false);                     // stops every analytics provider
```

**Feature-detect, then log a purchase and a screen view:**

```js
if (window.WebToApk && WebToApk.analyticsLogEvent) {
  WebToApk.analyticsLogScreenView(location.pathname, 'ProductPage');
  document.getElementById('buy').onclick = function () {
    WebToApk.analyticsLogEvent('purchase', JSON.stringify({ value: 19.99, currency: 'USD', transaction_id: orderId }));
  };
}
```

**Handle a refused event and a consent switch:**

```js
function track(name, params) {
  if (!(window.WebToApk && WebToApk.analyticsLogEvent)) return;      // browser, or option off
  const r = JSON.parse(WebToApk.analyticsLogEvent(name, JSON.stringify(params || {})));
  if (!r.ok) console.warn('analytics dropped', name, r.error);       // 'no_consent', 'invalid_name', ...
}

document.getElementById('analytics-toggle').onchange = function (e) {
  WebToApk.analyticsSetEnabled(e.target.checked);
};
track('tutorial_complete', { step_count: 5 });
```

**Notes:** `analyticsSetEnabled` is the page's consent switch for Firebase and Meta App Events together; see `AppMint.analytics` for the consent rules.

```js
track('tutorial_complete', { step_count: 5 });
```

**Notes:** `analyticsSetEnabled` is the page's consent switch for Firebase and Meta App Events together; see `AppMint.analytics` for the consent rules.

Meta App Event; [valueToSum] a number as text or ""; [paramsJson] a flat JSON object. Returns {ok, name, dropped} or {ok:false, error}.

**Example**
