# Capacitor plugins - JavaScript bridge API

> The Capacitor plugins the app hosts. A hand-written page reaches them as window.Capacitor.Plugins.<Name>; an AI-built app uses the @/lib/appmintNative wrapper each example names.

- **Applies to:** AppMint
- **Source:** extracted from the app runtime and its per-method example files; this page is generated from them.
- **HTML:** https://freewebtoapk.com/docs/api/capacitor

### `Capacitor.ActionSheet`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.ActionSheet — showActions({ title, message, options })
```

**Example**

Shows a native bottom sheet with a list of choices and tells you which one was tapped (`@capacitor/action-sheet` 8.1.1).

**Returns:** Promise `{ index, canceled }` - `index` is the tapped option; when the sheet is dismissed `canceled` is `true` and `index` is outside the list (`-1`). **Needs:** nothing to switch on - every app hosts the plugin. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

Each option is `{ title, style? }` with `style` `'DEFAULT'`, `'DESTRUCTIVE'` or `'CANCEL'`.

```js
var ActionSheet = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.ActionSheet;

async function photoMenu() {
  if (!ActionSheet) return;
  var opts = [
    { title: 'Share', style: 'DEFAULT' },
    { title: 'Edit', style: 'DEFAULT' },
    { title: 'Delete', style: 'DESTRUCTIVE' }
  ];
  var r = await ActionSheet.showActions({ title: 'Photo', message: 'Choose an action', options: opts });
  if (r.canceled || r.index < 0 || r.index >= opts.length) return;   // dismissed
  if (opts[r.index].title === 'Delete') deletePhoto();
}
```

**In an AI-built app** the Capacitor-shaped wrapper returns `{ index: -1 }` on dismiss; the short form `actionSheet()` returns `null`:

```ts
import { ActionSheet, actionSheet } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

const { index } = await ActionSheet.showActions({
  title: 'Photo',
  options: [{ title: 'Share' }, { title: 'Delete', destructive: true }],
});
if (index === 1) deletePhoto();

const i = await actionSheet('Sort by', [{ title: 'Name' }, { title: 'Date' }]);   // number | null
```

**Delete confirmation that also works in a plain browser:**

```js
async function confirmDelete(name) {
  const AS = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.ActionSheet;
  if (!AS) return window.confirm('Delete ' + name + '?');
  const r = await AS.showActions({
    title: 'Delete ' + name + '?',
    options: [{ title: 'Delete', style: 'DESTRUCTIVE' }, { title: 'Keep it', style: 'CANCEL' }]
  });
  return !r.canceled && r.index === 0;
}
```

**Notes:** Always check the index bound - never treat any index as a real choice. The wrapper's option shape is `{ title, destructive? }`; it maps `destructive` to the plugin's `'DESTRUCTIVE'` style.

### `Capacitor.App`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.App — getInfo(), getState(), exitApp(), minimizeApp(), addListener(...)
```

**Example**

App identity and lifecycle: name, package id, version, whether the app is in front, and pause/resume events (`@capacitor/app` 8.1.0).

**Returns:** `getInfo()` → `{ name, id, build, version }`; `getState()` → `{ isActive }`; `getLaunchUrl()` → `{ url }` or nothing; `getAppLanguage()` → `{ value }`; `exitApp()` / `minimizeApp()` → `void`. `addListener()` → a Promise of a handle with `remove()`, as in Capacitor’s own API - `await` it or chain `.then()`; the returned value also has `remove()` itself. **Needs:** nothing to switch on - every app hosts the plugin. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
var App = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.App;
if (App) {
  App.getInfo().then(function (i) {
    document.getElementById('about').textContent = i.name + ' ' + i.version + ' (' + i.build + ')';
  });
}
```

**Pause and resume** - save a draft when the user leaves, refresh when they come back:

```js
if (App) {
  App.addListener('appStateChange', function (s) {
    if (!s.isActive) saveDraft();      // went to the background
    else refreshInbox();               // back in front
  });
  App.addListener('pause', function () { console.log('paused'); });
  App.addListener('resume', function () { console.log('resumed'); });
}
```

**In an AI-built app:**

```ts
import { App } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

const info = await App.getInfo();   // { name, id, build, version }
App.exitApp();                      // closes the app on Android
```

**Notes:** The `backButton` event never fires: the shell keeps the back button (the plugin runs with `disableBackButtonHandler`). Handle back with `AppMint.setBackHandler(fn)` or the `onBackGesture` wrapper. For deep links use `WebToApk.getLaunchUrl()` / the `appmint:deep-link` event (or `launchUrl()` / `onDeepLink()` in AI-built apps). `minimizeApp()` is Android-only. Never make an Exit button the only way forward.

### `Capacitor.AppLauncher`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.AppLauncher — canOpenUrl({ url }), openUrl({ url })
```

**Example**

Opens another app by link (`whatsapp://send?text=…`, `tel:`, `geo:`, an https link) and asks whether one can handle it (`@capacitor/app-launcher` 8.0.1).

**Returns:** `canOpenUrl()` → Promise `{ value: boolean }`. `openUrl()` → Promise `{ completed: boolean }` (`false` when no app took the link). **Needs:** nothing to switch on - every app hosts the plugin. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
var AL = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppLauncher;

async function chatOnWhatsApp(text) {
  if (!AL) return;
  var url = 'whatsapp://send?text=' + encodeURIComponent(text);
  var can = await AL.canOpenUrl({ url: url });
  if (!can.value) { alert('WhatsApp is not installed'); return; }
  var r = await AL.openUrl({ url: url });
  if (!r.completed) alert('Could not open WhatsApp');
}
```

**In an AI-built app:**

```ts
import { appLauncher } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

if (await appLauncher.canOpen('tel:+15551234567')) await appLauncher.open('tel:+15551234567');
```

**Open a map link without asking first:**

```js
async function openMap(query) {
  const AL = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppLauncher;
  if (!AL) { window.open('https://maps.google.com/?q=' + encodeURIComponent(query)); return; }
  const r = await AL.openUrl({ url: 'geo:0,0?q=' + encodeURIComponent(query) });
  if (!r.completed) alert('No maps app could open this');
}
```

**Notes:** On Android 11+ an app can only "see" other apps it declares. Generated apps declare `https`, `geo`, `google.navigation`, `tel`, `mailto`, `sms`, `whatsapp`, `intent` and `upi` links, so `canOpenUrl` answers `false` for other schemes (for example `spotify:`) even when the app is installed. `openUrl` still works for them - call it and check `completed`. On Android `canOpenUrl` also accepts a package name (`'com.whatsapp'`), with the same visibility limit.

### `Capacitor.AppUpdate`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.AppUpdate — getAppUpdateInfo(), performImmediateUpdate(), startFlexibleUpdate(), completeFlexibleUpdate(), openAppStore()
```

**Example**

Checks Google Play for a newer version of the app and starts Play's in-app update. Vendored `@capawesome/capacitor-app-update` (`template/plugins/app-update`).

**Returns:** `getAppUpdateInfo()` → `{ currentVersionName, currentVersionCode, availableVersionCode, updateAvailability, updatePriority, immediateUpdateAllowed, flexibleUpdateAllowed, clientVersionStalenessDays?, installStatus }` (version codes are strings; `updateAvailability` `2` = an update is available). `performImmediateUpdate()` / `startFlexibleUpdate()` → `{ code }`: `0` OK, `1` cancelled, `2` failed, `3` not available, `4` not allowed, `5` call `getAppUpdateInfo()` first. `openAppStore()` → `void`. **Needs:** nothing to switch on; the app must be installed from Google Play. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
var AU = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppUpdate;

async function checkForUpdate() {
  if (!AU) return;
  try {
    var info = await AU.getAppUpdateInfo();          // must come first
    if (info.updateAvailability !== 2) return;       // up to date
    if (info.immediateUpdateAllowed) {
      var r = await AU.performImmediateUpdate();     // Play's full-screen update
      if (r.code === 1) console.log('user said not now');
    } else {
      await AU.openAppStore();                       // the Play listing
    }
  } catch (e) {
    console.log('Play update check failed:', e.message);  // e.g. no Play services
  }
}
```

**Flexible update** - download in the background, then restart when the user agrees:

```js
async function flexibleUpdate() {
  if (!AU) return;
  var info = await AU.getAppUpdateInfo();
  if (info.updateAvailability !== 2 || !info.flexibleUpdateAllowed) return;
  await AU.addListener('onFlexibleUpdateStateChange', function (s) {
    if (s.installStatus === 2) console.log(s.bytesDownloaded + ' / ' + s.totalBytesToDownload);
    if (s.installStatus === 11) showRestartButton();   // 11 = DOWNLOADED
  });
  await AU.startFlexibleUpdate();
}
function restartNow() { if (AU) AU.completeFlexibleUpdate(); }
```

**In an AI-built app:**

```ts
import { appUpdate } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

const info = await appUpdate.check();          // null on the web / without Play
if (info?.inPlace) await appUpdate.start();    // Android: immediate update
```

**Notes:** Use `updateAvailability === 2` as the only "update available" test. The wrapper's `check()` compares `currentVersionName` with `availableVersionCode`, which are never equal on Android, so its `updateAvailable` is not reliable there - test `inPlace` instead. `start()` resolves `true` even when the user cancels.

### `Capacitor.AppwrightDocScanner`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightDocScanner — scan({ pageLimit, pdf, quality }), isSupported()
```

**Example**

Opens the Google ML Kit document scanner: the user photographs one or more pages (or imports them), the edges are found and straightened, and the pages come back as JPEG images. Appwright's own plugin (`AppwrightDocScannerPlugin.kt`).

**Returns:** `scan()` → Promise that always RESOLVES: `{ ok: true, pages: string[] (JPEG data URLs), pdfDataUrl?, pdfPath?, pdfError? }` on success, `{ ok: false, cancelled: true }` when the user backs out, `{ ok: false, error }` when the scanner cannot start. `isSupported()` → `{ value: boolean }` (Google Play services present). **Needs:** nothing to switch on and no camera permission (the scanner runs inside Play services, which downloads its model on first use).

```js
var Scanner = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightDocScanner;

async function scanReceipt() {
  if (!Scanner) { alert('Scanning is not available here'); return; }
  var s = await Scanner.isSupported();
  if (!s.value) { alert('This phone has no Google Play services'); return; }
  var r = await Scanner.scan({ pageLimit: 1, pdf: false, quality: 0.8 });
  if (r.cancelled) return;
  if (!r.ok) { alert('Scanner error: ' + r.error); return; }
  document.getElementById('preview').src = r.pages[0];
}
```

`pageLimit` `0` = no limit. `quality` is 0.1-1 for the JPEG. With `pdf: true` the scanner also writes a PDF: `pdfDataUrl` is it as a `data:application/pdf;base64,…` URL the page can download, upload or show, and `pdfPath` is its copy in the app's cache folder. If the PDF could not be read, the pages still return and `pdfError` says why.

**In an AI-built app** (`null` on cancel, error, or the web):

```ts
import { docScanner, can } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

if (can('docScanner') !== 'none') {
  const res = await docScanner.scan({ pageLimit: 5, pdf: true });
  if (res) setPages(res.pages);          // res.pdfPath when pdf: true
}
```

**Scan several pages and offer the PDF:**

```js
async function scanContract() {
  const Scanner = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightDocScanner;
  if (!Scanner) return;
  const r = await Scanner.scan({ pageLimit: 0, pdf: true, quality: 0.9 });
  if (!r.ok) { if (!r.cancelled) alert('Scanner error: ' + r.error); return; }
  if (r.pdfDataUrl) {
    const a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = r.pdfDataUrl; a.download = 'contract.pdf'; a.click();
  } else if (r.pdfError) console.warn('PDF not made:', r.pdfError);
  console.log(r.pages.length + ' pages scanned');
}
```

**Notes:** Pages are full data URLs and can be large - shrink them before saving many in `localStorage`. Use `pdfDataUrl`, not `pdfPath` - a device file path is not a URL the page can load. A page that cannot be read is skipped; the rest still return.

### `Capacitor.AppwrightGallery`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightGallery — save({ source, fileName, album, kind })
```

**Example**

Saves a photo or a video into the phone's gallery (Pictures/<album> or Movies/<album>). The app shell's own plugin (`AppwrightGalleryPlugin.kt`).

**Returns:** Promise of `{ uri }` of the saved item. Rejects with a `code`: `bad-source`, `download-failed`, `permission-denied` (Android 7-9, storage refused) or `failed`. **Needs:** nothing to switch on; no permission on Android 10+ (Android 7-9 asks for storage the first time).

```js
const Gallery = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightGallery;

async function saveCard(canvas) {
  const dataUrl = canvas.toDataURL('image/png');
  if (!Gallery) { const a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = dataUrl; a.download = 'card.png'; a.click(); return; }
  try {
    await Gallery.save({ source: dataUrl, fileName: 'birthday-card.png', album: 'Cards' });
    toast('Saved to your gallery');
  } catch (e) {
    toast('Could not save: ' + e.message);
  }
}
```

Save a video from your server into its own album, with a message for each failure code:

```js
const Gallery = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightGallery;

async function saveClip(url) {
  if (!Gallery) { window.open(url, '_blank'); return; }
  try {
    await Gallery.save({ source: url, fileName: 'highlight.mp4', album: 'Highlights', kind: 'video' });
    toast('Video saved to Movies/Highlights');
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.code === 'download-failed') toast('Could not download the video. Check your connection.');
    else if (e.code === 'permission-denied') toast('Allow storage access to save videos.');
    else toast('Could not save: ' + e.message);
  }
}
```

Save a photo the user edited as a Blob (for example from `canvas.toBlob`) by turning it into a `data:` URL first:

```js
const Gallery = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightGallery;

function blobToDataUrl(blob) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const r = new FileReader();
    r.onload = () => resolve(r.result);
    r.onerror = () => reject(r.error);
    r.readAsDataURL(blob);
  });
}

async function saveEditedPhoto(canvas) {
  if (!Gallery) return;
  const blob = await new Promise((res) => canvas.toBlob(res, 'image/jpeg', 0.92));
  const { uri } = await Gallery.save({ source: await blobToDataUrl(blob), fileName: 'edit-' + Date.now() + '.jpg', album: 'My Edits' });
  console.log('saved as', uri);
}
```

**Notes:** `source` is a `data:` URL, an http(s) URL or a `content://`/`file://` URI; `kind` (`'image'`/`'video'`) is read from the MIME type when omitted. AI-built apps use `saveToGallery()` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `Capacitor.AppwrightHaptics`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightHaptics
```

**Example**

AppMint's own plugin for rich vibration patterns: a list of beats, each with its own start time, length and strength.

**Returns:** `play({ events })` resolves `{ ok: true }` or `{ ok: false, error }` (`'unsupported'` = no vibrator, `'empty'` = no events, or the system's message). It never rejects. `isSupported()` resolves `{ value: true/false }`. **Needs:** nothing to switch on - every app declares the vibration permission, whether or not **Vibrate** is ticked in Step 4 (Access). `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

Each event is `{ at, duration, intensity, sharpness }`: `at` = start in ms, `duration` = length in ms (under 20 becomes a 30 ms tap), `intensity` = 0-1 (default 0.8). `sharpness` is accepted but ignored on Android.

```js
var AH = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins ? window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightHaptics : null;

async function heartbeat() {
  if (!AH) return false;
  var r = await AH.play({
    events: [
      { at: 0,   intensity: 0.8 },
      { at: 140, intensity: 0.5 },
      { at: 700, intensity: 0.8 },
      { at: 840, intensity: 0.5 }
    ]
  });
  if (!r.ok) console.log('pattern not played:', r.error);
  return r.ok;
}

document.getElementById('like').addEventListener('click', heartbeat);
```

Hide the button on phones with no vibrator:

```js
(async function () {
  var btn = document.getElementById('feel-it');
  var ok = false;
  if (AH) { try { ok = (await AH.isSupported()).value; } catch (e) {} }
  btn.hidden = !ok;
})();
```

Play a quick double tap on a successful action, and report when it cannot play:

```js
async function successBuzz() {
  const AH = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightHaptics;
  if (!AH) return;
  const r = await AH.play({ events: [{ at: 0, duration: 40, intensity: 1 }, { at: 120, duration: 40, intensity: 0.6 }] });
  if (!r.ok && r.error === 'unsupported') console.log('this phone has no vibrator');
}
```

**Notes:** Strength works only on phones with amplitude control; other phones keep the timing at one fixed strength. If the system refuses the vibration, `play` answers `{ ok: false, error: '<the system message>' }`. In AI-built apps use `hapticPlay` from `@/lib/appmintNative`, which also has named patterns.

### `Capacitor.AppwrightLiveProgress`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightLiveProgress — start / update / end
```

**Example**

AppMint's own Android plugin (its JS name is `AppwrightLiveProgress`) for a sticky, silent, live-updating status notification (progress bar, spinner or running clock) that opens a route when tapped.

**Returns:** `start(opts)` / `update(opts)` → `Promise<{ ok: true, id }>`, or `{ ok: false, error }` with nothing posted - `'permission'` when notifications are not allowed (Android 13+: not granted yet, or switched off for the app), `'channel_disabled'` when the user turned off the "Live status" category; `end({ id })` → `Promise<void>`. **Needs:** the Android app and the notification permission (Android 13+). Not available on the web.

**In an AI-built app** use the wrapper `liveProgress` from `@/lib/appmintNative`:

```ts
import { liveProgress } from '@/lib/appmintNative';
await liveProgress.start({ id: 'order', title: 'Order #42', text: 'Being prepared', indeterminate: true });
await liveProgress.update({ id: 'order', title: 'Order #42', text: 'On the way', progress: 0.6, route: '/orders/42' });
await liveProgress.end('order');
```

**In a hand-written page:**

```js
async function showDelivery(step, total) {
  const P = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightLiveProgress;
  if (!P) return;                                   // not in the Android app
  if (window.Notification && Notification.permission !== 'granted') {
    if (await Notification.requestPermission() !== 'granted') return;
  }
  const r = await P.update({
    id: 'delivery',
    title: 'Your delivery',
    text: 'Stop ' + step + ' of ' + total,
    progress: step / total,                         // 0–1; or indeterminate: true
    route: '/track'                                 // opened when the card is tapped
  });
  if (!r.ok) console.warn('live card not posted:', r.error);
}

async function deliveryDone() {
  const P = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightLiveProgress;
  if (P) await P.end({ id: 'delivery' });
}
```

A workout timer: `startedAt` makes the card count up on its own, so it is posted once and ended when the workout stops:

```js
const Live = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightLiveProgress;
let workoutStart = 0;

async function startWorkout(name) {
  workoutStart = Date.now();
  if (!Live) return;
  const r = await Live.start({ id: 'workout', title: name, text: 'Workout in progress', startedAt: workoutStart, route: '/workout' });
  if (!r.ok && r.error === 'channel_disabled') {
    showHint('Turn on "Live status" in this app\'s notification settings to see the timer.');
  }
}

async function stopWorkout() {
  if (Live) await Live.end({ id: 'workout' });
  saveWorkout({ durationMs: Date.now() - workoutStart });
}
```

**Options:** `id` (default `'live'`), `title`, `text`, `progress` (0-1, omit for no bar), `indeterminate`, `startedAt` (epoch ms, shows a running clock), `route`.

**Notes:** `start` and `update` do the same thing (post or replace the card with that id). The card cannot be swiped away - always call `end`. Ask for the permission first: on Android 13+ without it `start` answers `error: 'permission'` and posts nothing.

### `Capacitor.AppwrightSystemPalette`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightSystemPalette — get()
```

**Example**

Returns the phone's Material You colours (the palette Android 12+ builds from the wallpaper), so the app can match the system apps. AppMint's own plugin (`AppwrightSystemPalettePlugin.kt`).

**Returns:** Promise `{ available: false }` below Android 12, else `{ available: true, accent1, accent2, accent3, neutral1, neutral2 }` - each an object from tone to hex colour, with tones `'0'`, `'10'`, `'50'`, `'100'` … `'900'`, `'1000'` (e.g. `accent1['600'] === '#3F5F90'`). **Needs:** nothing to switch on - every app hosts the plugin. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
var Palette = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightSystemPalette;

async function useWallpaperColours() {
  if (!Palette) return;
  var p = await Palette.get();
  if (!p.available) return;                 // keep the app's own colours
  var root = document.documentElement.style;
  root.setProperty('--accent', p.accent1['600']);
  root.setProperty('--surface', p.neutral1['50']);
}
useWallpaperColours();
```

**In an AI-built app:**

```ts
import { systemPalette } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

const p = await systemPalette();
if (p.available && p.accent1) document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--accent', p.accent1['600']);
```

Pick light or dark tones to match the system theme, and read the palette again when the user comes back from changing the wallpaper:

```js
var Palette = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightSystemPalette;
var darkQuery = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)');

async function applyPalette() {
  if (!Palette) return;
  var p = await Palette.get();
  if (!p.available) return;
  var dark = darkQuery.matches;
  var s = document.documentElement.style;
  s.setProperty('--accent', p.accent1[dark ? '200' : '600']);
  s.setProperty('--on-accent', p.accent1[dark ? '800' : '0']);
  s.setProperty('--bg', p.neutral1[dark ? '900' : '10']);
  s.setProperty('--text', p.neutral1[dark ? '100' : '900']);
}

darkQuery.addEventListener('change', applyPalette);
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function () {
  if (document.visibilityState === 'visible') applyPalette();
});
applyPalette();
```

**Notes:** Check text contrast before you apply palette colours - a wallpaper tone is not guaranteed to read well on your background. Browsers expose no wallpaper colours: on the web the wrapper answers `{ available: false }`. The colours change when the user changes the wallpaper; call `get()` again on resume.

### `Capacitor.AppwrightWidget`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightWidget — set(card), clear(), placedCount(), requestPin()
```

**Example**

Fills the app's home-screen widget: one card with a title, a big value, up to twelve lines, your colours and a tap route - the same card `AppMint.widget.set()` takes, every key included. The card is saved on the phone and shown even after a reboot. AppMint's own plugin (`AppwrightWidgetPlugin.kt`).

**Returns:** `set({ title?, value?, caption?, lines?, route?, bg?, ink?, accent?, textSize?, align?, wrap?, … })` → Promise `{ ok: true, placed }`, rejected with the reason for a bad card (`placed` = widgets currently on the home screen). `clear()` → `void`. `placedCount()` → `{ value }`. `requestPin()` → `{ value: boolean }` (`true` when the launcher's "add widget" sheet was opened). **Needs:** nothing to switch on - every app declares the widget. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
var Widget = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.AppwrightWidget;

async function updateWidget(tasks) {
  if (!Widget) return;
  await Widget.set({
    title: 'Today',
    value: tasks.length + ' tasks',
    lines: tasks.slice(0, 6).map(function (t) { return t.title; }),
    route: '/today',                 // opened when the widget is tapped
    bg: '#0B0F1A', ink: '#FFFFFF', accent: '#22D3EE'
  });
}
```

**Offer to place it** (only when none is placed yet):

```js
async function offerWidget() {
  if (!Widget) return;
  var n = (await Widget.placedCount()).value;
  if (n > 0) return;
  var r = await Widget.requestPin();
  if (!r.value) alert('Long-press the home screen, tap Widgets and pick this app.');
}
```

**In an AI-built app:**

```ts
import { widget } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

await widget.set({ title: 'Today', value: '3 tasks', lines: ['Gym', 'Call mum'], route: '/today' });
if ((await widget.placedCount()) === 0) await widget.requestPin();
```

**Notes:** Colours are `#RRGGBB`, `#AARRGGBB` (alpha first) or `rgba()`; empty ones use a dark card with a cyan value. See `AppMint.widget` for styled lines, `caption`, `textSize`, `align`, `wrap` and `font` (your own .ttf/.otf file, given as a path in your app). The tap opens the app at `route` as a deep link (read it with `WebToApk.getLaunchUrl()` or the `appmint:deep-link` event). Before any `set()` the widget says "Nothing to show yet"; `clear()` returns it to that state. In a browser `can('widget')` is `'none'`.

### `Capacitor.Badge`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.Badge — the launcher-icon count
```

**Example**

The Badge plugin (capawesome) that sets the number on the app's launcher icon.

**Returns:** Promises: `set({ count })`, `clear()`, `increase()`, `decrease()` → `void`; `get()` → `{ count }`; `isSupported()` → `{ isSupported }`. The Android plugin has no permission methods. **Needs:** nothing on Android. Not available on the web.

**In an AI-built app** use the wrapper `badge` from `@/lib/appmintNative`:

```ts
import { badge } from '@/lib/appmintNative';
await badge.set(3);
await badge.clear();
```

**In a hand-written page:**

```js
async function setUnread(count) {
  const B = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Badge;
  if (!B) return false;                       // not inside the app
  try {
    const s = await B.isSupported();
    if (!s.isSupported) return false;         // this launcher shows no badges
    if (count > 0) await B.set({ count: count });
    else await B.clear();
    return true;
  } catch (e) {
    return false;
  }
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:push', function () {
  const inbox = JSON.parse(window.WebToApk ? WebToApk.getPushInbox() : '[]');
  setUnread(inbox.filter(function (m) { return !m.read; }).length);
});
```

**Count up and down as items arrive and are read:**

```js
const B = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Badge;
async function onNewMessage() { if (B) await B.increase(); }
async function onMessageRead() { if (B) await B.decrease(); }
async function showCurrent() {
  if (!B) return;
  const { count } = await B.get();
  console.log('badge shows', count);
}
```

**Notes:** on Android the look depends on the launcher (a number, a dot, or nothing). `navigator.setAppBadge(n)` in the app writes to the same badge (it exists only on launchers that can show a count).

### `Capacitor.BarcodeScanner`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.BarcodeScanner — scan, startScan, readBarcodesFromImage, isSupported
```

**Example**

QR and barcode scanning with the `@capacitor-mlkit/barcode-scanning` API - the app shell's own plugin (`BarcodeScannerPlugin.kt`) over the same Google code scanner as `AppMint.scanCode()`. The older `@capacitor-community/barcode-scanner` calls (`startScan()` resolving `{ hasContent, content }`, `checkPermission`, `prepare`, `hideBackground`) share this name and work too.

**Returns:** `scan({ formats?, autoZoom? })` → `{ barcodes: [{ rawValue, displayValue, format, valueType, bytes?, cornerPoints?, urlBookmark?, wifi?, email?, phone?, sms?, geoPoint?, contactInfo?, calendarEvent?, driverLicense? }] }` (rejects `"scan canceled."` when the user backs out); `readBarcodesFromImage({ path, formats? })` → `{ barcodes }`; `isSupported()` → `{ supported }`; `isGoogleBarcodeScannerModuleAvailable()` → `{ available }`; `installGoogleBarcodeScannerModule()` (progress as `googleBarcodeScannerModuleInstallProgress`); `checkPermissions()` / `requestPermissions()` → `{ camera }`; `openSettings()`. `format` is `'QR_CODE'`, `'EAN_13'`, `'CODE_128'`… **Needs:** nothing to switch on and no camera permission - Google's scanner draws its own screen (Play services downloads it on first use). `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
const Scanner = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.BarcodeScanner;

scanBtn.onclick = async () => {
  if (!Scanner) return;
  try {
    const { barcodes } = await Scanner.scan({ formats: ['QR_CODE'] });
    const code = barcodes[0];
    if (code.valueType === 'URL') location.href = code.urlBookmark.url;
    else resultBox.textContent = code.displayValue;
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.message !== 'scan canceled.') alert(e.message);
  }
};
```

Price lookup from a product barcode, with the listener style (`startScan` + `barcodesScanned`) that ML Kit apps already use:

```js
const Scanner = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.BarcodeScanner;

async function scanProduct() {
  const listener = await Scanner.addListener('barcodesScanned', async ({ barcodes }) => {
    await listener.remove();
    await Scanner.stopScan();
    const ean = barcodes[0].rawValue;
    const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products/' + encodeURIComponent(ean));
    priceBox.textContent = res.ok ? (await res.json()).price : 'Not found';
  });
  await Scanner.startScan({ formats: ['EAN_13', 'EAN_8', 'UPC_A', 'UPC_E'] });
}
```

Read a QR code from a photo the user already has:

```js
const Scanner = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.BarcodeScanner;
const Camera = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Camera;

async function qrFromGallery() {
  const photo = await Camera.getPhoto({ source: 'PHOTOS', resultType: 'uri', quality: 90 });
  const { barcodes } = await Scanner.readBarcodesFromImage({ path: photo.path, formats: ['QR_CODE'] });
  return barcodes.length ? barcodes[0].rawValue : null;
}
```

**Notes:** Upstream's `startScan()` shows a live camera preview behind a see-through page and keeps scanning until `stopScan()`; here it opens the scanner screen, the first code fires `barcodeScanned` / `barcodesScanned`, and the session ends (the call then resolves `{ hasContent, content, format }` for community code; a closed scanner resolves `{ hasContent: false }`). Torch and zoom belong to that preview, so `isTorchAvailable()` is `false` and the torch/zoom setters reject - the scanner screen has its own flashlight button. `checkPermissions()` answers `granted` when the app has no camera permission at all (the scanner needs none); an app that also uses the camera gets its real state. AI-built apps use `scanCode()` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `Capacitor.Browser`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.Browser — open({ url, toolbarColor }), close(), addListener('browserFinished')
```

**Example**

Opens a web page in an in-app browser tab (Chrome Custom Tabs), so the user reads terms, docs or a sign-in page and comes back with one gesture (`@capacitor/browser` 8.0.3).

**Returns:** `open()` / `close()` → Promise `void`. Events: `browserFinished` (the user closed the tab) and `browserPageLoaded`. **Needs:** nothing - every app hosts the plugin (a browser that supports Custom Tabs, such as Chrome, must be installed). `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
var Browser = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Browser;

async function openTerms() {
  if (!Browser) return;
  var h = await Browser.addListener('browserFinished', function () {
    console.log('user closed the terms');
    h.remove();
  });
  await Browser.open({ url: 'https://example.com/terms', toolbarColor: '#0B0F1A' });
}
```

**In an AI-built app** (a new tab on the web):

```ts
import { browser } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

const off = browser.onClosed(() => refreshAccount());
await browser.open('https://example.com/terms', { toolbarColor: '#0B0F1A' });
// call off() when you no longer care
```

Open a link, and close the tab when a sign-in return reaches the page:

```js
var Browser = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Browser;

async function openHelp() {
  if (!Browser) { window.open('https://example.com/help', '_blank'); return; }
  try {
    await Browser.open({ url: 'https://example.com/help' });
  } catch (e) {
    alert('Could not open the page: ' + e.message);
  }
}

window.addEventListener('appmint:deep-link', function () {
  if (Browser) Browser.close().catch(function () {});
});
```

**Notes:** `url` must not be empty. `toolbarColor` is a hex colour; an invalid one is ignored. `close()` also works on Android in this plugin version (it finishes the tab's host activity) - useful after a sign-in link returns to the app. The tab is a separate browser: it does not share the app's cookies or `localStorage`.

### `Capacitor.Calendar`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.Calendar — createEvent, findEvents, deleteEvent, listCalendars, openCalendar
```

**Example**

Adds, finds and deletes events in the phone's own calendar (Android CalendarContract), and opens the calendar app at a date. Vendored `@capacitor/calendar` (`template/plugins/calendar`).

**Returns:** `createEvent()` → `{ id }`; `findEvents()` → `{ events: [{ id, title, location?, notes?, startDate, endDate, isAllDay, calendarId, calendarName?, attendees? }] }`; `listCalendars()` → `{ calendars: [{ id, name, displayName?, isPrimary }] }`; `deleteEvent()`, `openCalendar()` → `void`. Dates are epoch milliseconds. **Needs:** tick **Calendar** in Step 4 (Access) when you build. For HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps the build also adds the calendar permission by itself when your files contain a `Calendar.<method>(` call written exactly so (as below) or the wrapper's `calendar.createEvent(`. The plugin asks the user for calendar access on first use. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
var Calendar = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Calendar;

async function addDentist() {
  if (!Calendar) return;
  var start = new Date('2026-10-02T10:00:00').getTime();
  try {
    var r = await Calendar.createEvent({
      title: 'Dentist', startDate: start, endDate: start + 60 * 60 * 1000,
      location: 'Main St 5', notes: 'Bring the card', isAllDay: false,
      firstReminderMinutes: 30
    });
    console.log('event id', r.id);
  } catch (e) {
    // e.code: OS-PLUG-CLDR-0020 permission denied, -0001 bad arguments
    alert('Could not add the event: ' + e.message);
  }
}
```

**Read this week, delete one, open the calendar:**

```js
async function thisWeek() {
  if (!Calendar) return;
  var now = Date.now();
  var found = await Calendar.findEvents({ startDate: now, endDate: now + 7 * 864e5 });
  found.events.forEach(function (ev) { console.log(ev.title, new Date(ev.startDate)); });
  if (found.events.length) await Calendar.deleteEvent({ id: found.events[0].id });
  await Calendar.openCalendar({ date: now });
}
```

**In an AI-built app** (on the web `createEvent` downloads an `.ics` file; reading returns `[]`):

```ts
import { calendar } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

if ((await calendar.requestPermission()) === 'granted') {
  const id = await calendar.createEvent({ title: 'Dentist', start: new Date('2026-10-02T10:00'), end: new Date('2026-10-02T11:00') });
  const week = await calendar.listEvents({ from: Date.now(), to: Date.now() + 7 * 864e5 });
  if (id) await calendar.deleteEvent(id);
  await calendar.openCalendar(new Date());
}
```

**Notes:** Without the calendar permission in the app, no dialog appears and every event call rejects (missing permission); a user who says no gets `OS-PLUG-CLDR-0020`. `recurrence: { frequency: 'daily' | 'weekly' | 'monthly' | 'yearly', interval?, count?, endDate? }` makes a repeating event. `createEventInteractively({ title, startDate, endDate })` opens the calendar app's own editor instead: it resolves `{ id }` of the saved event, and rejects `OS-PLUG-CLDR-0006` when the user closes the editor without saving (it needs read as well as write access to tell the two apart). `deleteEvent({ id, fromDate })` ends a repeating event before `fromDate` and keeps the earlier occurrences. The wrapper returns `null` / `[]` / `false` instead of throwing.

### `Capacitor.Camera`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.Camera
```

**Example**

The official Capacitor Camera plugin, built into the app: take a photo with the camera or choose photos from the gallery.

**Returns:** Promises. `getPhoto(opts)` → `{ dataUrl | base64String | webPath, format, saved }` (which field depends on `resultType`), and REJECTS when the user cancels; `pickImages(opts)` → `{ photos: [{ webPath, format }] }`; `checkPermissions()` / `requestPermissions({ permissions })` → `{ camera, photos }`. **Needs:** tick **Camera** in Step 4 (Access). For HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps the build also adds the camera permission by itself when your files contain `Camera.getPhoto(` written exactly so (as below), `getUserMedia` with video, or `<input capture>`. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

**Take a photo and show it.**

```js
async function takePhoto() {
  var Camera = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Camera;
  if (!Camera) { showMessage('Open the app to use the camera.'); return; }
  try {
    var perm = await Camera.requestPermissions({ permissions: ['camera'] });
    if (perm.camera !== 'granted') { showMessage('Camera permission was refused.'); return; }

    var photo = await Camera.getPhoto({
      source: 'CAMERA',          // 'CAMERA' | 'PHOTOS' | 'PROMPT'
      resultType: 'dataUrl',     // 'dataUrl' | 'base64' | 'uri'
      quality: 80,
      direction: 'REAR',         // 'REAR' | 'FRONT'
      correctOrientation: true,
      saveToGallery: false
    });
    document.getElementById('photo').src = photo.dataUrl;
  } catch (err) {
    // The user closed the camera (or no camera app). Nothing to do.
  }
}
```

**Choose up to 5 photos from the gallery.**

```js
async function choosePhotos() {
  var Camera = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Camera;
  if (!Camera) return;
  try {
    var result = await Camera.pickImages({ quality: 80, limit: 5 });
    result.photos.forEach(function (p) {
      var img = document.createElement('img');
      img.src = p.webPath;       // a URL the page can load
      document.getElementById('gallery').appendChild(img);
    });
  } catch (err) { /* cancelled */ }
}
```

**In an AI-built app** use the wrapper, which also works on the web (and resolves `null` instead of throwing on cancel):

```ts
import { camera } from '@/lib/appmintNative';
const photo = await camera.take({ source: 'camera' });
```

**Notes:** `pickImages` needs no camera permission. If the camera permission is not in the app (the box was off and the build found no camera call), the camera permission is refused with no prompt. An `<input type="file" accept="image/*" capture>` also opens the camera. Camera is sensitive: declare it in your Play Data safety form.

### `Capacitor.CapacitorBarcodeScanner`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.CapacitorBarcodeScanner — scanBarcode({ hint })
```

**Example**

One-call QR / barcode scanning with the official `@capacitor/barcode-scanner` API - the app shell's own plugin (`CapacitorBarcodeScannerPlugin.kt`) over the same Google code scanner as `AppMint.scanCode()`. Code written for the npm package (`CapacitorBarcodeScanner.scanBarcode({ hint: CapacitorBarcodeScannerTypeHint.ALL })`) works unchanged.

**Returns:** `scanBarcode({ hint, scanInstructions?, cameraDirection?, scanOrientation? })` → `{ ScanResult, format }`. `hint` / `format` are the package's numbers: `0` QR_CODE, `1` AZTEC, `2` CODABAR, `3` CODE_39, `4` CODE_93, `5` CODE_128, `6` DATA_MATRIX, `8` ITF, `9` EAN_13, `10` EAN_8, `11` PDF_417, `14` UPC_A, `15` UPC_E, `17` ALL. Rejects with code `OS-PLUG-BARC-0006` when the user closes the scanner. **Needs:** nothing to switch on and no camera permission - Google's scanner draws its own screen (Play services downloads it on first use). `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
const Scanner = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.CapacitorBarcodeScanner;

ticketBtn.onclick = async () => {
  if (!Scanner) return;
  try {
    const { ScanResult } = await Scanner.scanBarcode({ hint: 0 });   // QR codes only
    const ok = await fetch('/api/tickets/check?code=' + encodeURIComponent(ScanResult)).then((r) => r.ok);
    statusBox.textContent = ok ? 'Valid ticket' : 'Unknown ticket';
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.code !== 'OS-PLUG-BARC-0006') alert(e.message);
  }
};
```

Accept any code, and tell the user which kind it was:

```js
const Scanner = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.CapacitorBarcodeScanner;
const NAMES = { 0: 'QR code', 5: 'Code 128', 9: 'EAN-13', 10: 'EAN-8', 14: 'UPC-A', 15: 'UPC-E' };

async function scanAnything() {
  const { ScanResult, format } = await Scanner.scanBarcode({ hint: 17 });
  return (NAMES[format] || 'Barcode') + ': ' + ScanResult;
}
```

Handle a rejection that is not the user closing the scanner:

```js
const Scanner = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.CapacitorBarcodeScanner;

async function scanProduct() {
  if (!Scanner) { alert('Scanning works only inside the app'); return null; }
  try {
    const { ScanResult } = await Scanner.scanBarcode({ hint: 9 });   // EAN-13
    return ScanResult;
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.code === 'OS-PLUG-BARC-0006') return null;                 // user closed the scanner
    alert('Scan failed: ' + e.message);
    return null;
  }
}
```

**Notes:** `scanInstructions`, `scanButton`, `cameraDirection` and `scanOrientation` style upstream's own camera screen and have no effect on Google's scanner (always the back camera). MAXICODE, RSS_14, RSS_EXPANDED and UPC_EAN_EXTENSION are not supported as a `hint` (rejects `OS-PLUG-BARC-0008`); `17` (ALL) scans every supported type. AI-built apps use `scanCode()` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `Capacitor.CapacitorCookies`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.CapacitorCookies — getCookies / setCookie / deleteCookie / clearCookies / clearAllCookies
```

**Example**

Reads and writes the app's cookies, including those of another host your page talks to (Capacitor core's `CapacitorCookies`).

**Returns:** `getCookies({ url? })` → `{ [name]: value }` - with a `url`, the cookies that URL (host and path) would send; without one, the page's own `document.cookie`. It rejects a `url` that is not `http(s)`. `setCookie({ key, value, url?, path?, expires? })`, `deleteCookie({ key, url? })`, `clearCookies({ url? })`, `clearAllCookies()` → Promise `void`; `setCookie` / `deleteCookie` reject without a string `key` (and `value`) and then write nothing. **Needs:** nothing to switch on - every app hosts the plugin. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
var Cookies = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.CapacitorCookies;

// Read the session cookie your API host set — not the page's own cookies.
async function apiSession() {
  if (!Cookies) return null;          // not inside the app
  var jar = await Cookies.getCookies({ url: 'https://api.example.com/' });
  return jar.session || null;
}

// Remember a choice for the API host, for 30 days, on one path only.
async function rememberRegion(region) {
  if (!Cookies) return;
  var expires = new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 864e5).toUTCString();
  await Cookies.setCookie({ url: 'https://api.example.com', path: '/v2', key: 'region', value: region, expires: expires });
}
```

Sign out: drop that host's cookies, or every cookie the app holds.

```js
async function signOut(everything) {
  if (!Cookies) return;
  if (everything) await Cookies.clearAllCookies();
  else await Cookies.clearCookies({ url: 'https://api.example.com' });
}
```

**Notes:** A cookie set with a `path` is only returned for a `url` under that path. Values are URL-decoded when read. Cookies are shared by every page the app shows, so never keep secrets in one a foreign page could read - they belong in `Preferences` or the app's secure storage.

### `Capacitor.CapacitorSQLite`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.CapacitorSQLite — createConnection, open, execute, query, run, executeSet, close
```

**Example**

A real SQLite database on the phone, with the `@capacitor-community/sqlite` API. Vendored `@capacitor-community/sqlite` (`template/plugins/sqlite`), running on Android's own SQLite. Code written for the npm package (`new SQLiteConnection(CapacitorSQLite)`) works unchanged; a hand-written page calls the plugin object directly, as below.

**Returns:** `createConnection({ database, version, encrypted: false, mode: 'no-encryption', readonly: false })`, `open({ database })`, `close({ database })`, `closeConnection({ database })` → `void`; `execute({ database, statements })` → `{ changes: { changes } }`; `run({ database, statement, values })` → `{ changes: { changes, lastId } }`; `query({ database, statement, values })` → `{ values: [rows] }`; `executeSet({ database, set: [{ statement, values }] })` → `{ changes }`; `isDBExists({ database })` / `isDBOpen({ database })` → `{ result }`; `beginTransaction`, `commitTransaction`, `rollbackTransaction`, `isTransactionActive({ database })`; `deleteDatabase({ database })`; `exportToJson` / `importFromJson` for backups. **Needs:** nothing to switch on and no permission. The database lives in the app's private storage and survives app updates. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
const DB = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.CapacitorSQLite;
const database = 'notes';

async function openNotes() {
  if (!DB) return false;
  await DB.createConnection({ database, version: 1, encrypted: false, mode: 'no-encryption', readonly: false });
  await DB.open({ database, readonly: false });
  await DB.execute({ database, statements:
    'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, text TEXT NOT NULL, at INTEGER);' });
  return true;
}

async function addNote(text) {
  const r = await DB.run({ database, statement: 'INSERT INTO notes (text, at) VALUES (?, ?);', values: [text, Date.now()] });
  return r.changes.lastId;
}

async function listNotes() {
  const r = await DB.query({ database, statement: 'SELECT id, text, at FROM notes ORDER BY at DESC;', values: [] });
  return r.values || [];
}
```

Several writes that must all land or none - one transaction with `executeSet`:

```js
const DB = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.CapacitorSQLite;

async function moveMoney(database, fromId, toId, amount) {
  await DB.executeSet({ database, transaction: true, set: [
    { statement: 'UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - ? WHERE id = ?;', values: [amount, fromId] },
    { statement: 'UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + ? WHERE id = ?;', values: [amount, toId] },
    { statement: 'INSERT INTO ledger (from_id, to_id, amount, at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?);', values: [fromId, toId, amount, Date.now()] },
  ] });
}
```

Open the database only once per app start, even when two screens ask at the same time:

```js
const DB = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.CapacitorSQLite;
let ready = null;

function db(database) {
  if (!ready) ready = (async () => {
    try {
      await DB.createConnection({ database, version: 1, encrypted: false, mode: 'no-encryption', readonly: false });
    } catch (e) {
      if (!/already exists/i.test(e.message)) throw e;   // a page reload keeps the native connection
    }
    if (!(await DB.isDBOpen({ database, readonly: false })).result) await DB.open({ database, readonly: false });
    return database;
  })();
  return ready;
}
```

**Notes:** The app is built **without SQLCipher**, so databases are not encrypted: `encrypted: true`, `setEncryptionSecret`, `changeEncryptionSecret`, `isSecretStored` and the other encryption calls reject with "Encryption is not available in this app". `isInConfigEncryption()` answers `false`. Everything else (queries, bound values, transactions, versioned upgrades with `addUpgradeStatement`, JSON import/export) is the plugin's own code. Rejections carry the SQLite error text.

### `Capacitor.Clipboard`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.Clipboard — write(options), read()
```

**Example**

Copies text (or a link) to the system clipboard and reads it back (`@capacitor/clipboard` 8.0.1).

**Returns:** `write({ string?, url?, image?, label? })` → Promise `void`. `read()` → Promise `{ value, type }` (`type` is `'text/plain'` for text). **Needs:** nothing to switch on - every app hosts the plugin. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
async function copyCode(code) {
  var Clipboard = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Clipboard;
  if (!Clipboard) { alert('Copy is not available here'); return; }
  await Clipboard.write({ string: code, label: 'Invite code' });
}

async function pasteCode(input) {
  var Clipboard = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Clipboard;
  if (!Clipboard) return;
  try {
    var r = await Clipboard.read();
    input.value = r.value;
  } catch (e) {
    // An EMPTY clipboard is a rejection: "There is no data on the clipboard".
    if (/no data/i.test(e.message)) input.value = '';
    else alert('Could not read the clipboard: ' + e.message);
  }
}
```

**In an AI-built app** the Capacitor-shaped wrapper turns an empty clipboard into `''`:

```ts
import { Clipboard } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

await Clipboard.write({ string: 'ABC-123' });
const { value } = await Clipboard.read();   // '' when the clipboard is empty
```

Copy a link and confirm it with a tap of feedback:

```js
async function copyLink(url) {
  var P = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins;
  if (!P || !P.Clipboard) { alert('Copy is not available here'); return; }
  await P.Clipboard.write({ url: url });
  if (P.Haptics) P.Haptics.impact({ style: 'LIGHT' });
  copiedToast.hidden = false;
}
```

**Notes:** `write` needs one of `string`, `url` or `image` (a data URL), else it rejects "No data provided". Android 12+ shows its own "pasted from…" notice on read - that is the OS, not the app. The wrapper's `write` sends only `string || url`.

### `Capacitor.Contacts`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.Contacts — getContacts, getContact, pickContact, createContact, deleteContact
```

**Example**

The phone's address book with the `@capacitor-community/contacts` API. Vendored `@capacitor-community/contacts` (`template/plugins/contacts`). Code written for the npm package works unchanged.

**Returns:** `checkPermissions()` / `requestPermissions()` → `{ contacts, contactsWrite }` (each `'granted' | 'denied' | 'prompt'`; `contacts` is reading, `contactsWrite` is adding and deleting); `getContacts({ projection })` → `{ contacts: [ContactPayload] }`; `getContact({ contactId, projection })` and `pickContact({ projection })` → `{ contact }`; `createContact({ contact })` → `{ contactId }`; `deleteContact({ contactId })` → `void`. `projection` picks the fields: `{ name, phones, emails, organization, birthday, note, urls, postalAddresses, image }` (each `true`). **Needs:** tick **Contacts** in Step 4 (Access) to read, and **Edit Contacts** as well to add or delete. HTML, ZIP and AI-Studio builds tick them by themselves when the code calls `Contacts.getContacts(` / `getContact(` / `pickContact(` (reading) or `Contacts.createContact(` / `deleteContact(` (both). The plugin asks the user on first use; without the box ticked the call rejects "Permission is required to access contacts." - and in an app with none of Contacts, SMS or Call log ticked the plugin is not in the app at all (Capacitor rejects "not implemented"). `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

```js
const Contacts = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Contacts;

async function friendsWithPhones() {
  if (!Contacts) return [];
  const { contacts } = await Contacts.requestPermissions();
  if (contacts !== 'granted') return [];
  const res = await Contacts.getContacts({ projection: { name: true, phones: true } });
  return res.contacts
    .filter((c) => c.phones && c.phones.length)
    .map((c) => ({ id: c.contactId, name: (c.name && c.name.display) || '', phone: c.phones[0].number }));
}
```

Let the user choose one person from the system picker:

```js
const Contacts = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Contacts;

inviteBtn.onclick = async () => {
  if (!Contacts) return;
  try {
    const { contact } = await Contacts.pickContact({ projection: { name: true, phones: true, emails: true } });
    inviteField.value = (contact.emails && contact.emails[0] && contact.emails[0].address) || '';
  } catch (e) {
    // The user closed the picker, or refused access.
  }
};
```

Save a business card from the app into the address book:

```js
const Contacts = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Contacts;

async function saveCard(card) {
  const perm = await Contacts.requestPermissions();
  if (perm.contactsWrite !== 'granted') return null;
  const { contactId } = await Contacts.createContact({ contact: {
    name: { given: card.first, family: card.last },
    organization: { company: card.company, jobTitle: card.title },
    phones: [{ type: 'work', label: 'work', number: card.phone }],
    emails: [{ type: 'work', label: 'work', address: card.email }],
  } });
  return contactId;
}
```

**Notes:** `pickContact()` rejects with code `CANCELLED` when the user backs out of the picker. Android only fills `contactId`, `name`, `phones`, `emails`, `organization`, `birthday`, `note`, `urls`, `postalAddresses` and `image` when the projection asks for them - ask only for what you show. Reading contacts is a sensitive permission on Google Play: describe why in the listing's data-safety form. AI-built apps use `listContacts()`, `pickContact()` and `addContact()` from `@/lib/appmintNative`.

### `Capacitor.Device`

```js
Capacitor.Plugins.Device
```

**Example**

The official Capacitor Device plugin, built into the app: phone model, OS version, battery, a stable ID and the language.

**Returns:** Promises. `getInfo()` → `{ model, platform, operatingSystem, osVersion, androidSDKVersion, manufacturer, isVirtual, webViewVersion, … }`; `getId()` → `{ identifier }`; `getBatteryInfo()` → `{ batteryLevel (0-1), isCharging }`; `getLanguageCode()` → `{ value }`. **Needs:** nothing to switch on. `window.Capacitor` exists on pages the app serves itself (HTML, ZIP and AI-built apps) and, in a **Website** mode app, on your own site (its domain and sub-domains) - never on other sites the app opens. Feature-detect.

**Show the phone and battery.**

```js
async function showDevice() {
  var cap = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Device;
  if (!cap) { document.getElementById('out').textContent = navigator.userAgent; return; }
  try {
    var info = await cap.getInfo();

    document.getElementById('out').textContent =
      info.manufacturer + ' ' + info.model + ' - ' + info.operatingSystem + ' ' + info.osVersion +

  } catch (err) {
    document.getElementById('out').textContent = 'Could not read device info';
  }
}
```

**A stable ID and the language.**

```js
async function helloServer() {
  var cap = window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.Device;
  if (!cap) return;
  var id = (await cap.getId()).identifier;
  var lang = (await cap.getLanguageCode()).value;     // e.g. "en"
  await fetch('https://api.example.com/hello?lang=' + encodeURIComponent(lang), {
    method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ device: id })
  });
}
```

**In an AI-built app** use the wrapper, which also works on the web:
