### `appmintNative.setOneSignalUser`

```js
import { setOneSignalUser } from '@/lib/appmintNative'
```

**Example**

OneSignal builds: links this install to your own user (OneSignal's External ID, the same as `OneSignal.login(id)`), so the OneSignal dashboard or its REST API can send to that one user on every phone they use. Pass your stable account id after sign-in and `''` on sign-out (`OneSignal.logout()`).

**Returns:** `boolean` synchronously - `true` when accepted (applied as soon as OneSignal has started); `false` on the web, in an app built without OneSignal, or for an id over 128 characters. **Needs:** Android: **OneSignal** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) with your OneSignal App ID; AppMint 1.11.63 and newer.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { setOneSignalUser } from '@/lib/appmintNative';
import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';

// Keeps OneSignal's External ID in step with the signed-in account.
export function useOneSignalUser() {
  useEffect(() => {
    const { data } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((_event, session) => {
      setOneSignalUser(session ? session.user.id : '');
    });
    return () => data.subscription.unsubscribe();
  }, []);
}
```

**Sending to that user** happens on your own server with OneSignal's REST API (`include_aliases: { external_id: ['<user id>'] }`); never put the OneSignal REST key in the app. With **AppMint Push** instead of OneSignal, use `setPushUser` and `notifyUser`.

### `appmintNative.setPushPresentation`

```js
import { setPushPresentation } from '@/lib/appmintNative'
```

**Example**

Chooses who draws an AppMint Push message you sent with an in-app style (banner, pop-up, bottom sheet or full screen) while the app is open: the app shell (`'auto'`, the default) or your own code (`'none'`).

**Returns:** `boolean` synchronously - `true` when the mode was saved. Always `false` on the web. **Needs:** Android: **AppMint Push** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { setPushPresentation, pushInbox } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

// Option A — keep the shell's banner, and never draw a second one on top of it.
export function usePushBanner(show: (title: string) => void) {
  useEffect(() => {
    const onPush = (e: Event) => {
      const d = (e as CustomEvent).detail;
      // { type: 'received', message, presented } — presented = the shell already showed it
      if (d.type === 'received' && !d.presented) show(d.message.title);
    };
    window.addEventListener('appmint:push', onPush);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('appmint:push', onPush);
  }, [show]);
}

// Option B — the app draws every message itself.
export function takeOverPushBanners() {
  setPushPresentation('none');   // saved on the phone; 'auto' gives it back to the shell
  return pushInbox();
}
```

Check the answer, since it is `false` on the web or when AppMint Push is off:

```ts
import { setPushPresentation } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useOwnBanners(on: boolean): boolean {
  const saved = setPushPresentation(on ? 'none' : 'auto');
  if (!saved) console.info('Push banners are not controllable here');
  return saved;
}
```

Draw your own banner for each message and keep the inbox in step:

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { setPushPresentation, markPushRead, pushInbox, type PushMessage } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useCustomBanner() {
  const [msg, setMsg] = useState<PushMessage | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    setPushPresentation('none');                  // the shell draws nothing; the page does
    const onPush = (e: Event) => {
      const d = (e as CustomEvent).detail;
      if (d.type === 'received') setMsg(d.message);
      if (d.type === 'revoked') setMsg((m) => (m?.id === d.id ? null : m));
    };
    window.addEventListener('appmint:push', onPush);
    return () => { window.removeEventListener('appmint:push', onPush); setPushPresentation('auto'); };
  }, []);
  return { msg, unread: pushInbox().filter((m) => !m.read).length, dismiss: () => { if (msg) markPushRead(msg.id); setMsg(null); } };
}
```

**Notes:** the inbox and the `appmint:push` event work the same in both modes. Setting `'none'` also closes a message the shell is showing right now.

### `appmintNative.setPushTag`

```js
import { setPushTag } from '@/lib/appmintNative'
```

**Example**

Sets one AppMint Push tag on this install. The send center can send to everyone with a tag, and a tag automation can send a message a set time after the tag is set. `''` removes the tag.

**Returns:** `boolean` synchronously - `true` when saved; `false` when the key is not 1-32 letters, digits or `_`, the value is over 128 characters or the install would pass 50 tags. Always `false` on the web. **Needs:** Android: **AppMint Push** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build; tag targeting and automations reach apps built from 30 Sep 2026 on.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { setPushTag } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

// Abandoned cart: a tag automation on "cart" (say 60 minutes) reminds only phones whose cart is
// still open when the time is up. Setting 'open' again does not restart the clock.
export function useCartPushTag(itemCount: number) {
  const hasItems = itemCount > 0;
  useEffect(() => {
    setPushTag('cart', hasItems ? 'open' : '');
  }, [hasItems]);
}

export function onCheckoutComplete() {
  setPushTag('cart', '');
}
```

Check the result: `false` means the tag was refused (bad key, value over 128 characters, more than 50 tags) or this is the web, so keep your own record of the state.

```ts
import { setPushTag } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function markNewsletterChoice(subscribed: boolean) {
  const saved = setPushTag('newsletter', subscribed ? 'yes' : '');
  if (!saved) console.warn('Push tag not saved (web, Push off, or invalid key/value)');
  return saved;
}
```

Tag a phone once it reaches a milestone, so the send center can target everyone at that level.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { setPushTag } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useLevelTag(level: number) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (level >= 10) setPushTag('veteran', 'yes');
    setPushTag('level', String(level));
  }, [level]);
}
```

**Notes:** tags belong to the install, not the signed-in user. Never put private data in a tag.

### `appmintNative.setPushTags`

```js
import { setPushTags } from '@/lib/appmintNative'
```

**Example**

Sets several AppMint Push tags in one change; a `''` value removes that tag, tags you do not name are kept.

**Returns:** `boolean` synchronously - `true` when saved; `false` when any key or value breaks the `setPushTag` rules (then nothing is saved). Always `false` on the web. **Needs:** Android: **AppMint Push** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build; tag targeting and automations reach apps built from 30 Sep 2026 on.

```ts
import { setPushTags, getPushTags, setPushUser } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function tagProfile(profile: { plan: 'free' | 'pro'; level: number; team?: string }) {
  return setPushTags({
    plan: profile.plan,
    level: String(profile.level),   // values are text
    team: profile.team ?? '',       // '' removes the tag
  });
}

// Sign-out: clear every tag and the user id.
export function signOutOfPush() {
  const cleared = Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(getPushTags()).map((k) => [k, '']));
  setPushTags(cleared);
  setPushUser('');
}
```

Tag a phone with its chosen language and topics when the user saves their settings, and check that every tag was accepted.

```ts
import { setPushTags } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function savePreferences(prefs: { lang: string; topics: string[] }) {
  const ok = setPushTags({
    lang: prefs.lang,
    topics: prefs.topics.join(',').slice(0, 128),   // a value is at most 128 characters
    onboarded: 'yes',
  });
  if (!ok) console.warn('Push tags not saved: nothing was changed');
  return ok;
}
```

Keep tags in step with the signed-in account in a React effect, removing the ones that no longer apply.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { setPushTags, setPushUser } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function usePushProfile(user: { id: string; plan: 'free' | 'pro'; trialEnds?: string } | null) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!user) return;
    setPushUser(user.id);
    setPushTags({ plan: user.plan, trial: user.plan === 'pro' ? '' : (user.trialEnds ?? '') });
  }, [user?.id, user?.plan, user?.trialEnds]);
}
```

**Notes:** all of one call is saved or none of it.

### `appmintNative.setPushUser`

```js
import { setPushUser } from '@/lib/appmintNative'
```

**Example**

Tells AppMint Push which of your users is signed in on this install, so the send center can send a message to that one user. Pass your own stable account id after sign-in and `''` on sign-out.

**Returns:** `boolean` synchronously - `true` when the id was saved; `false` for an id with anything other than letters, digits and `_ @ . : + -` (up to 128). Always `false` on the web. **Needs:** Android: **AppMint Push** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build; sending to a user reaches apps built from 30 Sep 2026 on.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { setPushUser, getPushUser } from '@/lib/appmintNative';
import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';

// Keeps AppMint Push in step with the signed-in account: the auth user id, never the email.
export function usePushUser() {
  useEffect(() => {
    const { data } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((_event, session) => {
      const id = session?.user.id ?? '';
      if (getPushUser() !== id) setPushUser(id);
    });
    return () => data.subscription.unsubscribe();
  }, []);
}
```

Handle a refused id: `setPushUser` answers `false` for an email address or any id with characters outside the allowed set, so send a stable id instead.

```ts
import { setPushUser } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function linkPushToAccount(account: { id: string; email: string }) {
  const ok = setPushUser(account.id);   // the id, never the email
  if (!ok) console.warn('Push user id not saved (web, Push off, or invalid characters)');
  return ok;
}
```

Clear the id when the user signs out, in a plain click handler.

```tsx
import { setPushUser, getPushUser } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function SignOutButton({ signOut }: { signOut: () => Promise<void> }) {
  return (
    <button
      onClick={async () => {
        await signOut();
        if (getPushUser()) setPushUser('');   // this install stops receiving "send to this user" messages
      }}
    >
      Sign out
    </button>
  );
}
```

Combine it with a tag so one sign-in step identifies the user and their plan together.

```ts
import { setPushUser, setPushTag } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function onSignedIn(userId: string, plan: 'free' | 'pro') {
  setPushUser(userId);
  setPushTag('plan', plan);
}
```

**Notes:** the id belongs to the install, so sign-out must clear it. It does not clear tags - call `setPushTags` with `''` values for user-specific ones.

### `appmintNative.setStatusBar`

```js
setStatusBar(backgroundColor: string | null, style?: 'light' | 'dark' | null): void
```

**Example**

Paints the system status bar to match the screen, and picks light or dark icons for it.

**Returns:** nothing. **Needs:** nothing.

`style` is the colour of the ICONS: `'light'` = light icons for a dark bar (the default), `'dark'` = dark icons for a light bar. Call it once at startup with the app's `--bg`, and again on any screen with a different background:

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { setStatusBar } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function App() {
  useEffect(() => { setStatusBar('#0B0F1A', 'light'); }, []);   // dark app, light icons
  return <main>{/* … */}</main>;
}

export function PhotoViewer() {
  useEffect(() => {
    setStatusBar('#000000', 'light');
    return () => setStatusBar('#0B0F1A', 'light');                // restore on leave
  }, []);
  return null;
}
```

A light screen:

```ts
import { setStatusBar } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

setStatusBar('#FFFFFF', 'dark');
```

The Capacitor-shaped form (the style is named after the BACKGROUND: `'DARK'` = light icons):

```ts
import { StatusBar } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

await StatusBar.setBackgroundColor({ color: '#0B0F1A' });
await StatusBar.setStyle({ style: 'DARK' });
```

**Notes:**
- In the Android app the shell paints the bar itself, which also works on Android 15 edge-to-edge; an unparseable colour is ignored - pass `#RRGGBB`. A style-only call (`backgroundColor = null`) keeps the colour this page last set and flips the icons; before the page set any colour it flips the icons through the StatusBar plugin and the bar keeps the colour chosen at build time.
- On the web it sets `<meta name="theme-color">`; the browser picks the icon colour itself.

### `appmintNative.setVolume`

```js
setVolume(stream, percent, showUi?) — @/lib/appmintNative
```

**Example**

Sets the phone's own volume level for one stream, 0-100. `showUi` shows the phone's volume slider as it moves.

**Returns:** `{ ok, stream?, current?, max?, percent?, error? }` - error is `unknown_stream`, `bad_percent`, `fixed_volume`, `dnd_access_required` (Do Not Disturb blocks ring / notification - call `requestDndAccess()`), `muted` (Do Not Disturb "Total silence" mutes the stream, so the level did not change), `not_applied`, `foreign_origin`, `failed`, or `unavailable` on the web. **Needs:** nothing for media, alarm and call.

```ts
import { useState } from 'react';
import { getVolume, setVolume, requestDndAccess } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function RingVolume() {
  const [level, setLevel] = useState(() => getVolume('ring')?.percent ?? null);
  if (level === null) return null;                   // web: no phone volume to set
  return (
    <input
      type="range" min={0} max={100} value={level}
      onChange={(e) => {
        const r = setVolume('ring', Number(e.target.value));
        if (r.ok) setLevel(r.percent ?? level);
        else if (r.error === 'dnd_access_required') requestDndAccess();
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Show the media volume as a slider that follows the hardware keys, using `onVolumeChange`.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { getVolume, setVolume, onVolumeChange } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function MediaVolume() {
  const [pct, setPct] = useState<number | null>(() => getVolume('media')?.percent ?? null);
  useEffect(() => onVolumeChange((l) => { if (l.stream === 'media') setPct(l.percent); }), []);
  if (pct === null) return null;   // web: no phone volume
  return <input type="range" min={0} max={100} value={pct} onChange={(e) => setVolume('media', Number(e.target.value))} />;
}
```

Turn the alarm stream up before an alarm screen rings, and report why it did not change.

```ts
import { setVolume } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function louderAlarm() {
  const r = setVolume('alarm', 90, true);   // true shows the phone's volume slider
  if (!r.ok) {
    switch (r.error) {
      case 'fixed_volume': return 'This phone has a fixed volume.';
      case 'unavailable': return 'Volume control needs the Android app.';
      default: return `Could not change the volume (${r.error}).`;
    }
  }
  return `Alarm volume is now ${r.percent}%`;
}
```

### `appmintNative.share`

```js
share(input: { title?, text?, url?, files? }): Promise<boolean>
```

**Example**

Opens the system share sheet in the app, and the Web Share API in a browser.

**Returns:** `Promise<boolean>` - `true` when the sheet opened; `false` when the user dismissed it or sharing is not available. It rejects when the share itself is invalid (for example an unsupported url) or another share is still open. **Needs:** nothing.

```ts
import { can, share, toast } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function ShareRecipe({ recipe }: { recipe: { title: string; url: string } }) {
  if (can('share') === 'none') return null;
  return (
    <button
      onClick={async () => {
        const ok = await share({ title: recipe.title, text: 'Try this recipe', url: recipe.url });
        if (ok) toast('Shared');           // false = the user closed the sheet; say nothing
      }}
    >
      Share
    </button>
  );
}
```

Text only (no link) is fine too:

```ts
import { share } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

await share({ text: 'My score today: 42' });
```

The Capacitor-shaped form `Share.share(opts)` calls the same code but REJECTS when the user cancels (Capacitor's contract) and resolves `{ activityType: '' }` otherwise; `Share.canShare()` resolves `{ value: can('share') !== 'none' }`:

```ts
import { Share } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

if ((await Share.canShare()).value) {
  try {
    await Share.share({ title: 'Invite', url: 'https://example.com/join' });
  } catch {
    /* cancelled or unavailable — never report success here */
  }
}
```

**Notes:**
- Pass only the fields you have. In the app, text and links go through the Capacitor Share plugin.
- `files` works in the Android app (the files go to the share sheet as real attachments; a `url` is added to the text) and on the web where the browser can share files (`navigator.canShare({ files })`). Keep files small - they are passed to the app in memory.
- On the web, call it from a tap; browsers refuse a share that no user action started.

### `appmintNative.sharedText`

```js
sharedText(): { text, subject, url, receivedAt } | null
```

**Example**

Gives the text or link another app shared INTO this app ("Share → your app"), for example a link shared from a browser or YouTube.

**Returns:** synchronously, `{ text, subject, url, receivedAt }` or `null` when nothing is waiting. `url` is the first `http(s)` link found in `text` (`''` if none); `receivedAt` is milliseconds since 1970. **Needs:** the build's **Receive Shares From Other Apps** option with "Text and links" - switched on automatically when your code calls `sharedText(` or `onShared(`.

Check on mount, save it, then clear it:

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { can, sharedText, clearShared, toast } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useSaveSharedLink(save: (item: { title: string; url: string; text: string }) => Promise<void>) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (can('shareTarget') === 'none') return;     // on the web
    const p = sharedText();
    if (!p) return;
    void save({ title: p.subject || p.url || 'Shared note', url: p.url, text: p.text })
      .then(() => { clearShared(); toast('Saved'); });
  }, [save]);
}
```

Listen for a share that arrives while the app is already open with `onShared`, and clear it after it is used.

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { sharedText, onShared, clearShared } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useIncomingShare() {
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => sharedText()?.text ?? '');
  useEffect(() => onShared((p) => setText(p.text)), []);
  return { text, done: () => { clearShared(); setText(''); } };
}
```

Prefill a form from a shared link and show nothing on the web, where `sharedText()` is `null`.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { can, sharedText } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function NewBookmark() {
  const [url, setUrl] = useState('');
  useEffect(() => {
    if (can('shareTarget') === 'none') return;   // web: nobody can share into the page
    const p = sharedText();
    if (p?.url) setUrl(p.url);
  }, []);
  return <input value={url} onChange={(e) => setUrl(e.target.value)} placeholder="Paste a link" />;
}
```

**Notes:**
- The share is KEPT until you call `clearShared()`, so an app that mounts after the share still sees it. Clear it after saving, or the next mount saves it again.
- For a share that arrives while the app is open, use `onShared()`.
- A photo or video shared WITH a caption: the caption arrives here, the file through the opened-file API.
- Android app only. `can('shareTarget')` is `'none'` on the web, and `sharedText()` returns `null` there.

### `appmintNative.sheet`

```js
sheet(opts: { title?, content, dismissible? }): { close(), element, closed }
```

**Example**

Opens a modal bottom sheet with real sheet behaviour - for a filter panel, a composer or a detail preview.

**Returns:** a handle: `close()` closes it, `element` is the body element (fill or update it), `closed` is a `Promise<void>` that resolves when the sheet has closed, however it closed. **Needs:** nothing.

**Options:** `title` (optional heading), `content` - an element, plain text (not HTML), or a function `(host) => { … }` that fills the body; `dismissible` (default `true`: backdrop tap, drag down, Escape and the back gesture close it).

Plain DOM content:

```ts
import { sheet } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

const h = sheet({
  title: 'About this list',
  content: (host) => {
    const p = document.createElement('p');
    p.textContent = 'Items sync to all your devices.';
    host.appendChild(p);
  },
});
await h.closed;
```

React content, rendered into the sheet with a portal:

```ts
import { useState } from 'react';
import { createPortal } from 'react-dom';
import { sheet } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function FiltersButton() {
  const [host, setHost] = useState<HTMLElement | null>(null);
  const [close, setClose] = useState<() => void>(() => () => {});

  const open = () => {
    const h = sheet({ title: 'Filters', content: () => {} });
    setHost(h.element);
    setClose(() => h.close);
    void h.closed.then(() => setHost(null));      // unmount the portal after any close
  };

  return (
    <>
      <button onClick={open}>Filters</button>
      {host && createPortal(
        <form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); close(); }}>
          <label><input type="checkbox" name="open" /> Open now</label>
          <button type="submit">Apply</button>
        </form>,
        host,
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

A sheet that stays open until the user chooses, using `dismissible: false` and the `closed` promise.

```ts
import { sheet } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export async function confirmDelete(name: string): Promise<boolean> {
  let answer = false;
  const h = sheet({
    title: 'Delete this item?',
    dismissible: false,                       // only the buttons below close it
    content: (host) => {
      const p = document.createElement('p');
      p.textContent = `"${name}" will be removed.`;
      const yes = document.createElement('button');
      yes.textContent = 'Delete';
      yes.onclick = () => { answer = true; h.close(); };
      const no = document.createElement('button');
      no.textContent = 'Keep it';
      no.onclick = () => h.close();
      host.append(p, yes, no);
    },
  });
  await h.closed;                             // resolves however the sheet closed
  return answer;
}
```

**Notes:**
- Drawn in the app's tokens (`--surface`, `--ink`, `--muted`, `--border`), above the safe area, with a light haptic on open.
- Drag down closes it when dragged past 120 px or flicked; the body scrolls first when it is not at the top.
- With `dismissible: false` only your own `close()` closes it - give the user a button.
- For a plain list of actions use `actionSheet()`.

### `appmintNative.shortcuts`

```js
shortcuts.set(items: { id?, title, route }[]) / shortcuts.clear()
```

**Example**

Adds shortcuts to the app icon's long-press menu (Android dynamic shortcuts). A tap opens the app at that route.

**Returns:** `set()` returns `Promise<boolean>` - `true` when the shortcuts were handed to the system, `false` where there are none (the web). `clear()` returns `Promise<void>`. **Needs:** nothing.

Set them once at start, and route on the launch link:

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';
import { can, shortcuts, launchUrl } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useAppShortcuts() {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  useEffect(() => {
    if (can('shortcuts') !== 'none') {
      void shortcuts.set([
        { id: 'new', title: 'New note', route: '/new' },
        { id: 'search', title: 'Search', route: '/search' },
      ]);
    }
    void launchUrl().then((u) => { if (u) navigate(new URL(u).pathname); });
  }, [navigate]);
}
```

Remove them (for example after sign-out):

```ts
import { shortcuts } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

await shortcuts.clear();
```

Open the matching screen when a shortcut is tapped while the app is already running, with `onDeepLink`.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';
import { onDeepLink } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useShortcutRouting() {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  useEffect(() => onDeepLink((url) => navigate(new URL(url).pathname)), [navigate]);
}
```

Show shortcuts only for a signed-in user, and handle the web, where `set()` answers `false`.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { shortcuts } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useAccountShortcuts(signedIn: boolean) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!signedIn) { void shortcuts.clear(); return; }
    void shortcuts.set([
      { id: 'inbox', title: 'Inbox', route: '/inbox' },
      { id: 'compose', title: 'Write a message', route: 'compose' },   // gets a leading "/"
    ]).then((handed) => { if (!handed) console.info('No launcher shortcuts on this platform'); });
  }, [signedIn]);
}
```

**Notes:**
- At most 4 items; extra items are dropped. A `route` without a leading `/` gets one. `id` is optional.
- Android 7.1+; on older Android the call does nothing. Titles are cut to 25 characters (short label) and 50 (long label).
- A tap opens the app with the launch link `appmint-shortcut://<package><route>`, so `new URL(u).pathname` is your route. Read it with `launchUrl()` on mount and `onDeepLink()` while the app runs.
- `can('shortcuts')` is `'none'` on the web: a browser has no app icon.

### `appmintNative.snoozeAlarm`

```js
snoozeAlarm(id?, minutes?) — @/lib/appmintNative
```

**Example**

Stops the ringing alarm and rings it again after `minutes` (0 or omitted = the alarm's own `snoozeMinutes`, default 10). Tomorrow's ring of a repeating alarm does not move.

**Returns:** `boolean` - `true` when it was ringing and is snoozed. **Needs:** **🔔 Alarm clock** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

```ts
import { isAlarmRinging, snoozeAlarm } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

// A shake-to-snooze handler:
window.addEventListener('devicemotion', (e) => {
  const a = e.accelerationIncludingGravity;
  if (a && Math.abs(a.x ?? 0) > 25 && isAlarmRinging()) snoozeAlarm('', 5);
});
```

Snooze from a button on your own alarm screen, using `onAlarm` to know when it is ringing.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { onAlarm, snoozeAlarm, stopAlarm } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function RingingScreen() {
  const [ringing, setRinging] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => onAlarm((e) => setRinging(e.action === 'open' && e.ringing === true)), []);
  if (!ringing) return null;
  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={() => { if (snoozeAlarm('', 10)) setRinging(false); }}>Snooze 10 min</button>
      <button onClick={() => { stopAlarm(); setRinging(false); }}>Stop</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`snoozeAlarm` answers `false` when nothing is ringing, so check before you promise the user a second ring.

```ts
import { snoozeAlarm } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function snoozeOrExplain(minutes = 0) {
  return snoozeAlarm('', minutes)
    ? `Ringing again in ${minutes || 'a few'} minutes`
    : 'No alarm is ringing right now.';
}
```

### `appmintNative.speak`

```js
speak(text, opts?) — @/lib/appmintNative
```

**Example**

Reads text aloud with the phone's text-to-speech engine.

**Returns:** `void` - it starts speaking (or queues after the current speech) and gives no "finished" signal. `opts`: `{ lang?: string; rate?: number; pitch?: number }` (defaults: engine language, 1, 1). **Needs:** nothing.

```ts
import { speak, stopSpeaking } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function ReadAloud({ text }: { text: string }) {
  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={() => speak(text, { lang: 'en-IN', rate: 0.9 })}>Read aloud</button>
      <button onClick={() => stopSpeaking()}>Stop</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Different languages and speeds:

```ts
import { speak } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

speak('வணக்கம்', { lang: 'ta-IN' });          // Tamil
speak('Slow and clear', { rate: 0.7 });       // rate 0.1..4, 1 = normal
speak('High voice', { pitch: 1.5 });          // pitch 0.1..4, 1 = normal
```

Speak a short confirmation after an action, and tell the user in text too.

```ts
import { speak, toast } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function announceSaved(title: string) {
  toast('Saved');
  speak(`${title} saved`, { rate: 1.1 });
}
```

Read a list one item after another; `speak()` queues, so call it in a loop and stop everything with `stopSpeaking()` when the screen closes.

```tsx
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { speak, stopSpeaking } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function ReadHeadlines({ items }: { items: string[] }) {
  useEffect(() => () => stopSpeaking(), []);   // leaving the screen stops the voice
  return <button onClick={() => items.forEach((t) => speak(t))}>Read all</button>;
}
```

**Notes:** In the Android app: the app's native engine. On the web: `speechSynthesis`. Several `speak()` calls play one after another. If you need to know when speech ends (to highlight words or move on), use `window.speechSynthesis` with an utterance's `onend` directly; it works in the Android app too.

### `appmintNative.speech`

```js
speech — @/lib/appmintNative
```

**Example**

Dictation: turns the user's speech into text. Android's speech recognizer in the Android app, the Web Speech API in Chrome.

**Returns:** `speech.isAvailable()` → `Promise<boolean>`. `speech.start(onResult, opts?)` → `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when listening started, `false` when the microphone permission was refused or dictation is not available. `onResult(text, isFinal)` is called with the text. `speech.stop()` → `Promise<void>`. `opts`: `{ lang?: string; partial?: boolean; prompt?: string }`. **Needs:** **Mic** in Step 4 (Access); AI builds switch it on for you when the code uses speech recognition.

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { speech } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function VoiceNote() {
  const [ok, setOk] = useState(false);
  const [text, setText] = useState('');
  const [msg, setMsg] = useState('');

  useEffect(() => { void speech.isAvailable().then(setOk); }, []);
  if (!ok) return null;                      // no dictation here: hide the mic button

  const listen = async () => {
    setMsg('Listening...');
    const started = await speech.start(
      (t, isFinal) => { setText(t); if (isFinal) setMsg(''); },
      { lang: 'en-US' },                     // partial results by default
    );
    if (!started) setMsg('Microphone permission is needed for voice input.');
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <button aria-label="Speak" onClick={listen}>🎤</button>
      <button onClick={() => { void speech.stop(); setMsg(''); }}>Stop</button>
      <p>{text}</p>
      <p role="status">{msg}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Dictate into a text field and say so when the microphone was refused, since `start()` answers `false`.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { speech } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function DictateField() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('');
  const [error, setError] = useState('');

  const dictate = async () => {
    setError('');
    const started = await speech.start((text, isFinal) => { if (isFinal) setValue((v) => (v ? `${v} ${text}` : text)); }, { partial: false });
    if (!started) setError('Voice input is not available. Check the microphone permission.');
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <textarea value={value} onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)} />
      <button onClick={dictate}>Dictate</button>
      {error && <p role="alert">{error}</p>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Stop listening when the screen closes, and read the result back with `speak`.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { speech, speak } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function VoiceCommand() {
  const [heard, setHeard] = useState('');
  useEffect(() => () => { void speech.stop(); }, []);

  return (
    <button
      onClick={() => void speech.start((t, isFinal) => {
        setHeard(t);
        if (isFinal) speak(`You said ${t}`);
      }, { lang: 'en-US' })}
    >
      {heard || 'Say something'}
    </button>
  );
}
```

**Notes:**
- With `partial` on (the default) `onResult(text, false)` arrives as words come in, then once `onResult(text, true)` with the final text. With `partial: false` you get only the final one, when the user stops talking.
- The permission prompt is shown on the first `start()`.
- If the user says nothing, `onResult` is not called; listening just ends. Keep a Stop button or a timeout in your UI.
- Listening stops by itself after a pause. `lang` defaults to the phone's language.

### `appmintNative.splash`

```js
splash.hold() / splash.ready()
```

**Example**

Keeps the launch splash on screen until the first real screen is ready, instead of showing "splash, then a spinner".

**Returns:** nothing (both are synchronous). **Needs:** nothing.

By default the splash hides by itself at the app's first paint - you need nothing. When the first screen needs data, hold the splash at module top and release it when that screen is on:

```ts
// main.tsx
import { splash } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

splash.hold();   // at import time, before the first render
```

```ts
// Home.tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { splash } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function Home({ load }: { load: () => Promise<string[]> }) {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<string[] | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    load()
      .then(setItems)
      .catch(() => setItems([]))
      .finally(() => splash.ready());     // ALWAYS release, also when loading failed
  }, [load]);

  if (!items) return null;
  return <ul>{items.map((t) => <li key={t}>{t}</li>)}</ul>;
}
```

Hold the splash while a signed-in session is restored, and release it in a `finally` so a failure cannot keep it up.

```ts
// main.tsx
import { splash } from '@/lib/appmintNative';
import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';

splash.hold();
supabase.auth.getSession().finally(() => splash.ready());
```

Release it once, from a hook, after the first screen's data is on screen.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { splash } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useReleaseSplash(loaded: boolean) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (loaded) splash.ready();   // calling it again later does nothing harmful
  }, [loaded]);
}
```

**Notes:**
- In the Android app `hold()` tells the shell to keep its splash; `ready()` hides it (the creator's minimum splash time still applies).
- On the web both do nothing - there is no splash.
- The shell caps the hold at about 6 seconds, so a page that never calls `ready()` still opens.

### `appmintNative.StatusBar`

```js
StatusBar.setBackgroundColor({ color }) / StatusBar.setStyle({ style })
```

**Example**

The status bar in the shape of Capacitor's StatusBar plugin, built on `setStatusBar()`.

**Returns:** `Promise<void>` for both. **Needs:** nothing.

```ts
import { StatusBar } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

// Colour only — the icon style is left alone (the shell picks readable icons on Android).
await StatusBar.setBackgroundColor({ color: '#0B0F1A' });
```

**Colour and icons together** - prefer `setStatusBar()`, which sets both in one call:

```ts
import { setStatusBar } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

setStatusBar('#0B0F1A', 'light');   // dark bar, light icons
setStatusBar('#FFFFFF', 'dark');    // light bar, dark icons
```

Switch the bar with the app's own light and dark theme, using the Capacitor-shaped calls together.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { StatusBar } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useStatusBarForTheme(dark: boolean) {
  useEffect(() => {
    void StatusBar.setBackgroundColor({ color: dark ? '#0B0F1A' : '#FFFFFF' });
    void StatusBar.setStyle({ style: dark ? 'DARK' : 'LIGHT' });   // 'DARK' = dark bar, light icons
  }, [dark]);
}
```

**Notes:** `style` follows Capacitor: `'DARK'` means a dark background (light icons), anything else means dark icons. In the Android app the shell bridge paints the bar (the plugin's colour call does nothing on Android 15+), and `setStyle()` flips the icons on the bar's current colour. On the web the colour becomes `<meta name="theme-color">`.

### `appmintNative.stopAlarm`

```js
stopAlarm(id?) — @/lib/appmintNative
```

**Example**

Stops the ringing alarm clock, like its Dismiss button. A repeating alarm stays set for its next time.

**Returns:** `boolean` - `true` when it was ringing and is now stopped. `id` omitted = whichever is ringing. **Needs:** **🔔 Alarm clock** in the Access step (Step 4) when you build.

```ts
import { stopAlarm, snoozeAlarm } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function RingScreen({ id, onClose }: { id: string; onClose: () => void }) {
  return (
    <div className="ring">
      <button onClick={() => { snoozeAlarm(id, 10); onClose(); }}>Snooze 10 min</button>
      <button onClick={() => { stopAlarm(id); onClose(); }}>Stop</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Stop the alarm from the screen the app opens when the alarm rings, and react to every way it ends:

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { onAlarm, isAlarmRinging, stopAlarm } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useRingingAlarm() {
  const [ringingId, setRingingId] = useState<string | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => onAlarm((e) => {
    if (e.action === 'open' && e.ringing) setRingingId(e.id);
    else setRingingId(null);   // dismiss, snooze, missed or error: it is no longer ringing
  }), []);
  return {
    ringingId,
    stop: () => { if (isAlarmRinging()) stopAlarm(ringingId ?? ''); },
  };
}
```

Check the answer: `false` means nothing was ringing (or this is the web), so do not claim it stopped:

```ts
import { stopAlarm, alarmSupport } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function stopWithFeedback(id: string, say: (m: string) => void) {
  if (alarmSupport() === 'unavailable') return say('Alarms only work in the Android app');
  say(stopAlarm(id) ? 'Alarm stopped' : 'That alarm is not ringing');
}
```

### `appmintNative.stopSpeaking`

```js
stopSpeaking() — @/lib/appmintNative
```

**Example**

Stops text-to-speech now and drops anything still waiting to be spoken.

**Returns:** `void`. **Needs:** nothing.

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { speak, stopSpeaking } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function StoryPage({ story }: { story: string }) {
  // Stop reading when the user leaves the page.
  useEffect(() => () => stopSpeaking(), []);

  return (
    <article>
      <p>{story}</p>
      <button onClick={() => { stopSpeaking(); speak(story); }}>Read from the start</button>
      <button onClick={stopSpeaking}>Stop</button>
    </article>
  );
}
```

Read a long text aloud with the language and speed the user picked, and stop it from one button:

```ts
import { useState } from 'react';
import { speak, stopSpeaking } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function ReadAloud({ text, lang }: { text: string; lang: string }) {
  const [rate, setRate] = useState(1);
  return (
    <div>
      <input type="range" min={0.5} max={2} step={0.1} value={rate} onChange={(e) => setRate(Number(e.target.value))} />
      <button onClick={() => { stopSpeaking(); speak(text, { lang, rate }); }}>Read aloud</button>
      <button onClick={() => stopSpeaking()}>Stop</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Cut the voice off when the user starts typing a reply:

```ts
import { stopSpeaking } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function ReplyBox({ onSend }: { onSend: (text: string) => void }) {
  return <textarea onFocus={() => stopSpeaking()} onBlur={(e) => onSend(e.currentTarget.value)} />;
}
```

**Notes:** Safe to call when nothing is speaking. In the Android app: the native engine's stop. On the web: `speechSynthesis.cancel()`.

### `appmintNative.swipeable`

```js
swipeable(el: HTMLElement, opts: SwipeOptions): () => void
```

**Example**

Adds swipe gestures to an element - swipe-to-delete rows, paging, dismissing a card.

**Returns:** an unsubscribe function that also restores the element's original `touch-action`. **Needs:** nothing.

**Options:** `onLeft`, `onRight`, `onUp`, `onDown` (at least one), `threshold` (px of travel, default `56`), `edgeGuard` (px from the left/right screen edge where horizontal swipes are ignored, default `24`), `haptics` (selection haptic on a swipe, default `true`).

Swipe left to delete, with a visible button for the same action:

```ts
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { swipeable, toast } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function MessageRow({ id, text, onDelete, onUndo }: {
  id: string; text: string; onDelete(id: string): void; onUndo(id: string): void;
}) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLLIElement>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!ref.current) return;
    return swipeable(ref.current, {
      onLeft: () => { onDelete(id); toast('Deleted'); },
    });
  }, [id, onDelete]);

  return (
    <li ref={ref} className="flex items-center justify-between p-4">
      <span>{text}</span>
      <button onClick={() => onDelete(id)}>Delete</button>
      {/* swipe is never the only way to an action */}
    </li>
  );
}
```

Page between tabs with left / right:

```ts
import { swipeable } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

declare const panel: HTMLElement;
declare let tab: number;
const off = swipeable(panel, { onLeft: () => { tab += 1; }, onRight: () => { tab -= 1; }, threshold: 72 });
// later: off();
```

Dismiss a card by swiping it up, with the handler removed on unmount:

```ts
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { swipeable } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function Banner({ onClose, children }: { onClose: () => void; children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  useEffect(() => (ref.current ? swipeable(ref.current, { onUp: onClose, threshold: 40 }) : undefined), [onClose]);
  return <div ref={ref} className="banner">{children}</div>;
}
```

**Notes:**
- Built on Pointer Events, so the same code works with touch, pen and a mouse drag.
- It sets `touch-action` for you: `pan-y` for horizontal handlers (vertical scrolling still works), `pan-x` for vertical ones, `none` for both.
- A swipe must be clearly one direction (1.5 times more on one axis); diagonal scrolls do not fire. A second finger cancels the gesture.
- The edge guard exists because Android's system back gesture owns the screen edges.

### `appmintNative.systemPalette`

```js
systemPalette(): Promise<SystemPalette>
```

**Example**

Reads the phone's Material You colours (built from the wallpaper on Android 12+), so the app's accent can follow the user's wallpaper like the system apps.

**Returns:** `Promise<{ available: boolean; accent1?, accent2?, accent3?, neutral1?, neutral2? }>` - each swatch maps a tone (`'0'`, `'10'`, `'50'`, `'100'` … `'900'`, `'1000'`) to a hex colour. `{ available: false }` below Android 12 and on the web. **Needs:** nothing.

```ts
import { systemPalette } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export async function applyWallpaperAccent() {
  const p = await systemPalette();
  if (!p.available || !p.accent1) return;          // keep the app's own palette
  const root = document.documentElement.style;
  root.setProperty('--accent', p.accent1['600']);
  root.setProperty('--accent-soft', p.accent1['100']);
}
```

Use the wallpaper colours only when the phone offers them, and re-read them when the app comes back to the screen:

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { systemPalette } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useWallpaperAccent(enabled: boolean) {
  const [accent, setAccent] = useState<string | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!enabled) { setAccent(null); return; }
    const read = () => systemPalette().then((p) => setAccent(p.available ? p.accent1?.['600'] ?? null : null));
    void read();
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', read);
    return () => document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', read);
  }, [enabled]);
  return accent;   // null = no wallpaper palette on this device (Android 11 and older, or the web)
}
```

Show the "Match my wallpaper" switch only when a palette exists, using `{ available: false }` as the answer to "not here":

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { can, systemPalette } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function WallpaperToggle({ value, onChange }: { value: boolean; onChange: (v: boolean) => void }) {
  const [ok, setOk] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => { if (can('systemPalette') !== 'none') systemPalette().then((p) => setOk(p.available)); }, []);
  if (!ok) return null;
  return <label><input type="checkbox" checked={value} onChange={(e) => onChange(e.target.checked)} /> Match my wallpaper</label>;
}
```

**Notes:** Check contrast before you use a wallpaper tone for text or buttons - `--accent` must still reach 3:1 on your background. Offer it as an option ("Match my wallpaper"), not a forced theme. Call it again when the app resumes; the user may have changed the wallpaper.

### `appmintNative.TextToSpeech`

```js
TextToSpeech — @/lib/appmintNative
```

**Example**

The Capacitor-style `TextToSpeech` object (`speak` / `stop`), running on the same code as `speak()` and `stopSpeaking()`.

**Returns:** `speak({ text, lang?, rate?, pitch? })` → `Promise<void>` that resolves once the text has been spoken (or `stop()` cut it short) and rejects when it could not be spoken. `stop()` → `Promise<void>`. **Needs:** nothing.

```ts
import { TextToSpeech } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

async function announce(orderNo: number) {
  await TextToSpeech.speak({ text: `Order ${orderNo} is ready`, lang: 'en-US', rate: 1, pitch: 1 });
  // Here the text is queued; it may still be speaking.
}

async function silence() {
  await TextToSpeech.stop();
}
```

Read out a list of lines one after the other; each `speak` resolves when queued, so the engine plays them in order:

```ts
import { TextToSpeech } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export async function readSteps(steps: string[]) {
  await TextToSpeech.stop();   // drop anything still waiting from before
  for (const [i, s] of steps.entries()) {
    await TextToSpeech.speak({ text: `Step ${i + 1}. ${s}`, lang: 'en-US' });
  }
}
```

A read-aloud button that stops speaking when the screen is left:

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { TextToSpeech } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function ArticleReader({ text }: { text: string }) {
  useEffect(() => () => { void TextToSpeech.stop(); }, []);
  return <button onClick={() => void TextToSpeech.speak({ text, rate: 0.9 })}>Listen</button>;
}
```

**Notes:** `await TextToSpeech.speak(…)` is the end signal: the next step after speaking can follow it directly. In the app: the shell's native Android text-to-speech engine; on the web: `speechSynthesis`.

### `appmintNative.textZoom`

```js
textZoom.get() / textZoom.getPreferred() / textZoom.set(value)
```

**Example**

An in-app text-size control. In the app it changes the page's text zoom (`1` = 100%); on the web it changes the root font size, which scales every `rem`-based layout.

**Returns:** `get()` → `Promise<number>`. `getPreferred()` → `Promise<number>` - the size the user chose in the phone's settings (`1` on the web). `set(value)` → `Promise<void>`; the value is clamped to 0.5-3, and it rejects for a value that is not a number. **Needs:** nothing.

```ts
import { textZoom } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

async function bigger() { await textZoom.set((await textZoom.get()) + 0.1); }
async function smaller() { await textZoom.set((await textZoom.get()) - 0.1); }
async function reset() { await textZoom.set(await textZoom.getPreferred()); }
```

**Remember the choice** across launches:

```ts
import { textZoom } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

const saved = Number(localStorage.getItem('textZoom'));
if (saved) await textZoom.set(saved);

export async function setSize(v: number) {
  await textZoom.set(v);
  localStorage.setItem('textZoom', String(v));
}
```

A text-size stepper that reads the current value, keeps it inside the allowed range, and shows it in percent:

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { textZoom } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function TextSizeStepper() {
  const [z, setZ] = useState(1);
  useEffect(() => { textZoom.get().then(setZ); }, []);
  const change = async (d: number) => {
    const next = Math.min(3, Math.max(0.5, Math.round((z + d) * 10) / 10));
    await textZoom.set(next);
    setZ(next);
  };
  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={() => change(-0.1)}>A-</button>
      <span>{Math.round(z * 100)}%</span>
      <button onClick={() => change(0.1)}>A+</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

**Notes:** The app already follows the phone's font-size setting; this is an extra, in-app control. Test the layout at large sizes - fixed heights on text controls clip.

### `appmintNative.toast`

```js
toast(message: string, opts?: { duration?: 'short' | 'long' }): void
```

**Example**

Shows a brief message that needs no answer - "Copied", "Saved", "Added to list".

**Returns:** nothing (fire and forget). **Needs:** nothing.

```ts
import { toast, haptic } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function SaveButton({ onSave }: { onSave: () => Promise<void> }) {
  return (
    <button
      onClick={async () => {
        await onSave();
        haptic('success');
        toast('Saved');                              // 'short' ≈ 2 s
      }}
    >
      Save
    </button>
  );
}
```

A longer message stays about 3.5 seconds:

```ts
import { toast } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

toast('Your export will be ready in a minute', { duration: 'long' });
```

The Capacitor-shaped form `Toast.show({ text, duration? })` does the same and resolves `Promise<void>`:

```ts
import { Toast } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

await Toast.show({ text: 'Added to list' });
```

For a message the user MUST see, use a dialog instead:

```ts
import { Dialog } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

await Dialog.alert({ title: 'Payment failed', message: 'Your card was declined.' });
```

**Notes:**
- In the Android app the Capacitor Toast plugin shows it at the bottom of the screen.
- Everywhere else it is a small snackbar drawn over the page in the app's own colours (`--ink` on `--bg`), above the safe-area inset, with `role="status"` so screen readers announce it.
- Only one is shown at a time; a new toast replaces the old one.
- A toast is easy to miss by design. Never use it for an error the user has to act on.

### `appmintNative.torch`

```js
import { torch } from '@/lib/appmintNative'
```

**Example**

The phone's flashlight: `torch.on()`, `off()`, `toggle()`, `isOn()`, `isAvailable()`. `can('torch')` is `'none'` on the web.

**Returns:** `on()`/`off()` → Promise (rejects with `code` `'unavailable'` or `'CAMERA_IN_USE'`); `toggle()` → the new state; `isOn()` / `isAvailable()` → boolean. **Needs:** nothing, no permission.

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { can, torch } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function LightButton() {
  const [on, setOn] = useState(false);
  const [ok, setOk] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => { if (can('torch') !== 'none') torch.isAvailable().then(setOk); }, []);
  if (!ok) return null;
  return (
    <button aria-pressed={on} aria-label="Flashlight" onClick={async () => setOn(await torch.toggle())}>
      {on ? 'Light off' : 'Light on'}
    </button>
  );
}
```

Switch the light off when the user leaves the screen and show the error the phone reports when it cannot be switched:

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { torch } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function LightSwitch() {
  const [on, setOn] = useState(false);
  const [err, setErr] = useState('');
  useEffect(() => () => { void torch.off().catch(() => {}); }, []);
  const flip = async () => {
    try { setOn(await torch.toggle()); setErr(''); }
    catch (e) {
      const code = (e as { code?: string }).code;
      setErr(code === 'CAMERA_IN_USE' ? 'Close the camera first' : 'No flashlight on this device');
    }
  };
  return <div><button onClick={flip}>{on ? 'Off' : 'On'}</button>{err && <p role="alert">{err}</p>}</div>;
}
```

Blink the light as a signal, then leave it off:

```ts
import { can, torch } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export async function blink(times = 3) {
  if (can('torch') === 'none') return;
  for (let i = 0; i < times; i++) {
    await torch.on();
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 200));
    await torch.off();
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 200));
  }
}
```

**Notes:** switched off when the app closes. While the app's own camera stream is open, light it with the track's `torch` constraint instead.

### `appmintNative.trackEvent`

```js
import { trackEvent } from '@/lib/appmintNative'
```

**Example**

Reports a moment in your app so the creator's in-app messages with the trigger **"When an event happens"** (same name) show. The app downloads the creator's campaigns from the AppMint Push send center and shows them itself.

**Returns:** `boolean` synchronously: `false` for an invalid name (letters, digits and `_ . : -`, up to 64), on the web, and in apps built without AppMint Push. **Needs:** Android: **AppMint Push** turned on in the Integrate step (Step 3) when you build.

```ts
import { trackEvent } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export async function completeCheckout(cart: { total: number }) {
  await saveOrder(cart);
  trackEvent('checkout_done', { total: cart.total });   // props are optional and not stored
}
```

Report a view change the URL does not show, so **"On a page"** messages see it:

```ts
import { trackEvent } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function selectTab(tab: 'home' | 'cart' | 'profile') {
  setActiveTab(tab);
  trackEvent('appmint:route', { path: '/' + tab });
}
```

A hook that tracks the first time a screen is opened:

```ts
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { can, trackEvent } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useTrackOnce(name: string) {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (can('inAppMessages') === 'none') return;
    const key = 'tracked:' + name;
    if (localStorage.getItem(key)) return;
    if (trackEvent(name)) localStorage.setItem(key, '1');
  }, [name]);
}
```

**Notes:** URL changes (page loads, pushState, #hash routes) are already seen; only report what the address does not change.

### `appmintNative.transition`

```js
transition(update: () => void | Promise<void>, opts?: { type?: 'push' | 'pop' | 'fade' }): Promise<void>
```

**Example**

Runs a screen change with a native-feeling animation: `push` slides the new screen in from the right, `pop` slides back, `fade` cross-fades.

**Returns:** `Promise<void>` that settles after the change and its animation. `update` is your state change (a router `navigate`, a `setState`) and is always applied. **Needs:** nothing.

```ts
import { useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';
import { transition, haptic } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function NoteRow({ id, title }: { id: string; title: string }) {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  return (
    <button
      onClick={() => { haptic('light'); void transition(() => navigate(`/note/${id}`)); }}   // push
    >
      {title}
    </button>
  );
}

export function BackButton() {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  return <button onClick={() => void transition(() => navigate(-1), { type: 'pop' })}>Back</button>;
}
```

Fade between two tabs:

```ts
import { transition } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

declare function setTab(t: 'list' | 'map'): void;
await transition(() => setTab('map'), { type: 'fade' });
```

Use a fade for a tab change, in one handler per tab:

```ts
import { transition } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function Tabs({ tab, setTab }: { tab: 'home' | 'stats'; setTab: (t: 'home' | 'stats') => void }) {
  return (
    <nav>
      <button onClick={() => void transition(() => setTab('home'), { type: 'fade' })} aria-current={tab === 'home'}>Home</button>
      <button onClick={() => void transition(() => setTab('stats'), { type: 'fade' })} aria-current={tab === 'stats'}>Stats</button>
    </nav>
  );
}
```

**Notes:**
- It uses the View Transitions API when the WebView has it. Otherwise it applies the update and plays a short enter animation on `#root` (or the first child of `<body>`).
- When the user asked the system for reduced motion, it only applies the update - no animation.
- Animations are about 240 ms.

### `appmintNative.unlock`

```js
unlock(title?, subtitle?) — from '@/lib/appmintNative'
```

**Example**

Asks the phone's owner to prove they are present - fingerprint, face, or the device PIN/passcode - and tells you whether they did.

**Returns:** `Promise<boolean>` - `true` when unlocked; `false` when cancelled, failed, locked out, or nothing can check on this device. It never throws. **Needs:** in the app, **Fingerprint** in Step 4 (Access) when you build. On the web: the browser's platform authenticator (WebAuthn).

```ts
import { unlock, can } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export async function openPrivateNotes(show: () => void) {
  if (can('unlock') === 'none') {
    alert('This device has no fingerprint, face or PIN check.');
    return;
  }
  const ok = await unlock('Unlock notes', 'Use your fingerprint or PIN');
  if (ok) show();
}
```

Hide the button where there is nothing to unlock with:

```ts
import { can } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

const showLockButton = can('unlock') !== 'none';   // 'native' | 'web' | 'none'
```

Guard a delete with a fresh unlock, then confirm with a haptic and a toast:

```ts
import { unlock, haptic, toast } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export async function deleteAccountData(wipe: () => Promise<void>) {
  const ok = await unlock('Confirm delete', 'This removes your saved data');
  if (!ok) { haptic('warning'); toast('Not unlocked, nothing was deleted'); return; }
  await wipe();
  haptic('success');
  toast('Data deleted');
}
```

**Notes:** In the app the device PIN, pattern or password is allowed as the second way in. On the web, the first call enrols the browser's platform authenticator and counts as unlocked. This proves the device owner is present; it is NOT a login - never use it as the only guard on data that lives on a server. On Android 11 and newer the prompt opens on any phone with a screen lock - a PIN-only phone gets it too, and unlocks with the PIN; on Android 10 and older a fingerprint must be saved first, otherwise it answers `false` without a prompt.

### `appmintNative.updates`

```js
updates.supported() / download() / stage() / confirm() / revertIfUnconfirmed() / current()
```

**Example**

A page-side updater for web-bundle updates. Page code does not need it: in an AppMint app, Remote Update is done natively by the Android app, and `updates.supported()` returns `false` everywhere.

**Returns:** `supported()` → `boolean` (currently always `false`); `download(url, sha256, version, binaryVersion)` → `Promise<boolean>` (`false` while unsupported); `stage(dir, version, binaryVersion)` → `Promise<boolean>`; `confirm()` → `void`; `revertIfUnconfirmed(binaryVersion)` → `Promise<boolean>`; `current()` → `{ path, version, binaryVersion } | null`. **Needs:** nothing for your app - updates are published from Remote Update in AppMint.

The only safe use in app code is to check, and do nothing when it is off:

```ts
import { updates } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

if (updates.supported()) {
  // Not reached today: the Android app's own updater owns the whole update lane.
  const staged = await updates.download(
    'https://example.com/bundle-1.2.0.zip',
    'e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855',  // sha256, required
    '1.2.0',
    '1',
  );
  console.log('update staged:', staged);
}
```

Show which bundle is running (a settings "About" row):

```ts
import { updates } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

const active = updates.current();          // null = no page-staged bundle (always, today)
const label = active ? `Content ${active.version}` : 'Built-in content';
```

Show the running content version in a settings row, with the built-in label when the page has no staged bundle:

```ts
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { updates } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function AboutRow() {
  const label = useMemo(() => {
    const c = updates.current();
    return c ? `Content ${c.version} (app ${c.binaryVersion})` : 'Built-in content';
  }, []);
  return <p>{label}</p>;
}
```

**Notes:**
- In the Android app the shell's Remote Update manager downloads, verifies and serves updates, and rolls back a bundle that fails to load. The page is served by the shell itself, so a bundle staged from page code would never be shown - that is why `supported()` is `false`.
- On the web there is nothing to update; the page is whatever the server sends.
- Updates can change HTML, CSS and JavaScript only; a new native feature still needs a new app build.

### `appmintNative.watchIdle`

```js
import { watchIdle } from '@/lib/appmintNative'
```

**Example**

Tells the app when the user goes idle or locks the screen, and when they are back (`can('idle')`). Start it from a tap the first time - the permission request needs one.

**Returns:** Promise of the stop function. The callback gets `{ user: 'active' | 'idle', screen: 'locked' | 'unlocked' }` at start and on every change. Rejects with `code` `'permission-denied'` or `'unavailable'`. **Needs:** nothing, no Android permission.

```ts
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { can, watchIdle } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function AwayStatus({ setAway }: { setAway: (away: boolean) => void }) {
  const stop = useRef<(() => void) | null>(null);
  if (can('idle') === 'none') return null;
  return (
    <button onClick={async () => {
      stop.current?.();
      stop.current = await watchIdle((s) => setAway(s.user === 'idle' || s.screen === 'locked'), { thresholdMs: 5 * 60000 });
    }}>Show me as away when idle</button>
  );
}
```

Show an away state and stop watching on unmount; a refused permission is reported with its `code`:

```ts
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { can, watchIdle } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function useIdleWatch() {
  const stop = useRef<(() => void) | null>(null);
  const [state, setState] = useState<'off' | 'active' | 'idle' | 'denied'>('off');
  useEffect(() => () => stop.current?.(), []);
  // Call this from a tap: the first permission request needs a gesture.
  const start = async () => {
    if (can('idle') === 'none') return;
    try {
      stop.current = await watchIdle((s) => setState(s.user === 'idle' || s.screen === 'locked' ? 'idle' : 'active'));
    } catch (e) {
      if ((e as { code?: string }).code === 'permission-denied') setState('denied');
    }
  };
  return { state, start };
}
```

Pause a polling timer while the user is away and refresh when they are back:

```ts
import { watchIdle } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export async function pausePollingWhenIdle(refresh: () => void) {
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | undefined = setInterval(refresh, 30000);
  const stop = await watchIdle((s) => {
    const away = s.user === 'idle' || s.screen === 'locked';
    if (away && timer) { clearInterval(timer); timer = undefined; }
    if (!away && !timer) { refresh(); timer = setInterval(refresh, 30000); }
  });
  return () => { stop(); if (timer) clearInterval(timer); };
}
```

**Notes:** the threshold is at least one minute (the spec's floor).

### `appmintNative.widget`

```js
widget.set(card) / widget.clear() / widget.placedCount() / widget.requestPin()
```

**Example**

Fills the app's home-screen widget - one card with a title, a big value, a caption, up to twelve lines (each with an optional colour, marker and route), and a tap that opens the app at a route.

**Returns:** `set(card)` → `Promise<boolean>` (`true` when saved); `clear()` → `Promise<void>`; `placedCount()` → `Promise<number>` (how many copies the user placed); `requestPin()` → `Promise<boolean>` (`true` when the launcher's "add widget" flow opened). None of them reject. **Needs:** nothing in the Android app (the widget is always part of the build).

Update the card after every change the user would want to see on the home screen:

```ts
import { can, widget } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export async function updateTodayWidget(tasks: { title: string; done: boolean }[]) {
  if (can('widget') === 'none') return;          // on the web
  const open = tasks.filter((t) => !t.done);
  await widget.set({
    title: 'Today',
    value: `${open.length} left`,
    lines: open.slice(0, 6).map((t) => '• ' + t.title),
    route: '/today',                              // a tap opens the app here
  });
}
```

An agenda that fills a resized widget, with a see-through background and an overdue line in red:

```ts
import { widget, type WidgetLine } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export async function updateAgendaWidget(events: { day: string; time: string; title: string; overdue: boolean }[]) {
  const lines: WidgetLine[] = events.slice(0, 12).map((e) => e.overdue
    ? { text: `Overdue: ${e.title}`, color: '#FF5252', marker: '#FF5252', bold: true, route: `/day/${e.day}` }
    : { text: `${e.time} ${e.title}`, marker: '#29B6F6', route: `/day/${e.day}` });
  await widget.set({
    title: 'Agenda', value: 'Today', caption: `${events.length} events`,
    bg: 'rgba(20, 38, 74, 0.6)', textSize: 'auto', lines, route: '/agenda',
  });
}
```

An "Add to home screen" button:

```ts
import { can, widget, toast } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function AddWidgetButton() {
  if (can('widget') === 'none') return null;
  return (
    <button
      onClick={async () => {
        if (!(await widget.requestPin())) toast('Long-press your home screen, tap Widgets, and pick this app');
      }}
    >
      Add widget to home screen
    </button>
  );
}
```

Empty the card when the user signs out, and show how many copies are on the home screen:

```ts
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { can, widget } from '@/lib/appmintNative';

export function WidgetStatus({ signedIn }: { signedIn: boolean }) {
  const [placed, setPlaced] = useState(0);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (can('widget') === 'none') return;
    if (!signedIn) void widget.clear();
    widget.placedCount().then(setPlaced);
  }, [signedIn]);
  return <p>{placed === 0 ? 'Not on your home screen yet' : `On your home screen (${placed})`}</p>;
}
```

**Notes:**
- The card is saved on the device, survives a reboot, and every placed copy is refreshed. `placedCount()` of `0` means no copy is on the home screen yet.
- Card fields: `title` (empty = the app name), `value` (shown large in `accent`, hidden when empty), `caption` (small text under the value), `lines` (max 12; six always show, more when the widget is tall enough; a line is a string or `{ text, color?, marker?, bold?, wrap?, route? }`), `route` (default `/`), `textSize` (`'auto'` grows the text with the widget as far as every line still fits, wrapping long lines to two rows; `'small' | 'normal' | 'large' | 'xl'` or a number 0.6-3), `align` (`'start' | 'center' | 'end'`), `wrap` (long lines take two rows), and `bg` / `ink` / `accent`. The colours default to the CSS tokens `--bg`, `--ink`, `--accent`; they must be `#RRGGBB`, `#AARRGGBB` (alpha FIRST: `#9914264A` is 60 % opaque), `#RGB`, `rgb()`/`rgba()` or a colour name - an `hsl()`/`oklch()` value falls back to the default colours. `set()` returns `false` for an unknown `textSize`/`align` or a bad line colour.
- A tap opens the app with `appmint-shortcut://<package><route>`; read it with `launchUrl()` / `onDeepLink()`.
- `requestPin()` needs Android 8+ and a launcher that supports it. `clear()` shows the empty "Nothing to show yet" card.
- Android app only: `can('widget')` is `'none'` on the web, where `set()` and `requestPin()` return `false`.
